title: 2027: Peter Agada predicts sharp drop in Obi’s votes
description:
The presidential candidate of the Young Peoples Party (YPP), Peter Agada, has predicted that Peter Obi will receive far fewer votes in the 2027 general election than he did in 2023.
Agada said Obi, who secured nearly six million votes in the last presidential election, would not get up to 30 per cen
content:
The presidential candidate of the Young Peoples Party (YPP), Peter Agada, has predicted that Peter Obi will receive far fewer votes in the 2027 general election than he did in 2023.

Agada said Obi, who secured nearly six million votes in the last presidential election, would not get up to 30 per cent of that figure in the next poll.

He made the prediction on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

“I definitely know he won’t get that number. He will not even get up to 20 or 30 per cent of that number. I can tell you for sure,” Agada said.

Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party (LP) before joining the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).

Agada attributed Obi’s victory in Lagos State during the last election to the support he received from different groups, including members of the #EndSARS movement, youths and workers.

However, the YPP candidate said he did not expect Obi to win Lagos in the 2027 presidential election.

Speaking on President Bola Tinubu’s administration, Agada said he supported the removal of the petrol subsidy but faulted the government’s approach to its implementation.

He argued that the government had failed to properly target the actual end users of the subsidy.

Agada also claimed that Nigeria was losing about 70 per cent of its revenue to inflated contracts.

He described the reported ₦1 trillion budget for the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as excessive, saying he could construct one kilometre of the road for between ₦750 million and ₦800 million.

Asked whether he was part of the proposed opposition coalition seeking to unseat Tinubu in 2027, Agada said nobody had approached him.

title: Newly wedded couple die in fire disaster, as gunmen kill fresh Operation Rainbow graduate in Plateau
description:
Tragedy  struck in Anguwan Miyango, Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State when a newly married couple, Sikiru Habib and his wife, Ramlat Lawan, were killed died in a fire out that engulfed their residence
The incident came as two men were killed in an ambush by gunmen in Bokkos lo
content:
Tragedy  struck in Anguwan Miyango, Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State when a newly married couple, Sikiru Habib and his wife, Ramlat Lawan, were killed died in a fire out that engulfed their residence

The incident came as two men were killed in an ambush by gunmen in Bokkos local council. One of them was a commander of the state security outfit, Operation Rainbow.

The fire was said to have started on Saturday at about 2:30 a.m. while they asleep and was believed to have been triggered by a high-voltage power surge.

Though the real cause of the fire has not been confirmed, the incident had kept residents bewildered.

A neighbour of the deceased, Lawal Suleiman, said they woke up to a raging inferno and by the time any help could be rendered, the whole house was up in flames.

According to him, the situation became more dangerous when the room’s door failed to open, trapping the couple inside as young men in the neighbourhood made desperate efforts to rescue them.

Suleiman said that the rescuers eventually broke the room’s window and managed to bring the couple out before firefighters arrived to provide emergency assistance.

Though they managed to drag them out of the fire, they suffered severe burns leading to their death  The husband died on Sunday while the wife died on Monday after being rushed to the Jos University Teaching Hospital (JUTH).

In a related development, two men two men have been killed in an ambush by gunmen in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State.

Among the victims was an operative fof the state security outfit,  Operation Rainbow, who recently passed out of training

Our correspondent gathered that the victims were  killed at about 3pm on Monday while returning from a condolence visit to Hurti village to their community in Tadai, Manguna District of Bokkos Local Government Area.

Machief Pau,l community leader, , who confirmed the incident to newsmen, said both victims were members of his community.

“He confirmed that the victims met their deaths unexpectedly in broad daylight

Paul said,  “One of the victims was a newly graduated commander of Operation Rainbow who had recently completed a refresher training programme for unit commanders in Jos. He was agile and ready for the job, but unfortunately his career has been cut short.”

title: Mongolia President Announces Resignation After Graft Accusations
description: Mongolia’s President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh announced his resignation on Tuesday following corruption allegations and impeachment threats from the country’s opposition party.His resignation announcement comes a day after the opposition Democratic Party issued a statement accusing him of graft
content:
Mongolia’s President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh announced his resignation on Tuesday following corruption allegations and impeachment threats from the country’s opposition party.

His resignation announcement comes a day after the opposition Democratic Party issued a statement accusing him of graft and calling for him to step down or face impeachment in parliament.

Khurelsukh told a press conference he was being “falsely accused and defamed with allegations of extremely serious crimes” and would resign in order to “restore my good name”.

“I believe that it is in the interests of justice for the Head of State to relinquish his duties and establish the truth,” he said.

“Therefore, I officially announce that I will relinquish the honorable duties of the president of Mongolia. I will refer those who have defamed my reputation to the relevant authorities and seek to restore my good name,” he added.

The Democratic Party had said on Monday that “this country has become deeply corrupt”, and called for senior government officials, including Khurelsukh, with links to graft allegations to resign and face investigation.

Khurelsukh denied wrongdoing, telling the press briefing that “I am someone who has never stolen from the people or the state during my time as president.”

“I have never lied or stolen. I have never deceived anyone,” he added.

Mongolia has grappled with months-long political turbulence, as well as infighting within the ruling Mongolian People’s Party (MPP).

Lawmakers appointed in March the country’s third prime minister in under 12 months, following weeks of anti-corruption protests.

Thousands of young people demonstrated in the capital Ulaanbaatar, angry at wealthy elites and what they see as pervasive injustice.

Under Mongolian law, the parliament’s speaker — Sandag Byambatsogt of the MPP — will assume presidential duties, and a presidential election must be organised within four months.

AFP

title: Nigeria not poor, held hostage by corruption, selfish ambitions – Utomi
description:
Renowned political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi has enjoined Nigerians to vote wisely in the 2027 general election, noting that the nation needed to replace self-serving leadership with men and women who understand the meaning of public service.
Utomi stated this in a musing posted on Facebook on Tues
content:
Renowned political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi has enjoined Nigerians to vote wisely in the 2027 general election, noting that the nation needed to replace self-serving leadership with men and women who understand the meaning of public service.

Utomi stated this in a musing posted on Facebook on Tuesday.

He said Nigeria is not a poor country, but a country whose immense possibilities have been held hostage by corruption, greed and the selfish ambitions of those entrusted with its leadership.

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain said, “Nigeria is not a poor country. It is a country whose immense possibilities have been held hostage by corruption, greed and the selfish ambitions of those entrusted with its leadership. We possess the land, the natural resources, the human talent and the economic potential to stand among the greatest nations on earth.

“Remove corruption and replace self-serving leadership with men and women who understand the meaning of public service, and we would have overcome half the battle.”

Utomi explained that nations do not change by wishing for a better tomorrow, but when their people find the courage to make different choices.

“But nations do not change by wishing for a better tomorrow. They change when their people find the courage to make different choices. The 2027 elections present us with another opportunity to rescue our country from the cycle of wasted potential and put it on a path worthy of its greatness,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to vote wisely, saying they deserve a country where hard work is rewarded and opportunities are not reserved for the privileged.

“Please, vote wisely. You deserve a country where hard work is rewarded, where opportunities are not reserved for the privileged, and where ordinary people can live with dignity and hope. Nigeria has been blessed with more than enough to make this possible. What we must now demand is leadership capable of turning those blessings into prosperity for all,” Utomi added.

Nigerians will head to the polls for the presidential and National Assembly elections on Saturday, January 16, 2027, and for the governorship and state house of assembly elections on Saturday, February 6, 2027, according to the revised timetable released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

The post Nigeria not poor, held hostage by corruption, selfish ambitions – Utomi appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Police train 10,000 commanders ahead of elections – Iniedu
description:
The Nigeria Police Force has commenced training for more than 10,000 election commanders as part of preparations to secure the forthcoming elections across the country.
The Force Police Relations Officer, CSP Anietie Iniedu, disclosed this during an interview on ARISE News, where he assured Nigerian
content:
The Nigeria Police Force has commenced training for more than 10,000 election commanders as part of preparations to secure the forthcoming elections across the country.

The Force Police Relations Officer, CSP Anietie Iniedu, disclosed this during an interview on ARISE News, where he assured Nigerians that the police were adequately prepared to maintain security during the electoral process.

Iniedu said the police had also begun distributing election security materials nationwide ahead of the polls.

According to him, the force has the personnel and resources required to manage election security, noting that it has demonstrated its capacity to handle elections over the years.

“The Nigerian police force is well empowered to handle the elections. We have started the distribution of our election security materials across the nation and have commenced election security training for over 10,000 election commanders nationwide,” he said.

He also warned that the police would not tolerate political violence, stressing that anyone involved in such acts would face the law.

Iniedu disclosed that the police had arrested more than 397 suspects across the country within the past three months over incidents linked to political violence.

He said the Inspector-General of Police had directed that investigations into the cases be concluded promptly and that those found culpable be charged to court without delay.

“In the past 3 months, we have made over 397 arrests nationwide. The IG has asked that the investigations be quickly concluded, and these actors be charged to court immediately,” he said.

The police spokesman maintained that incidents of political violence would not be allowed to go unpunished, as the force intensified preparations to ensure security before, during and after elections.

title: Apple to face trial over alleged iPhone repair restrictions in France
description:
Apple is to stand trial in Paris in June 2027 on suspicion of having organised the planned obsolescence of various iPhone models by preventing repairs outside official outlets, a source close to the case told AFP on Tuesday.
The case brought by French prosecutors against the US tech giant on charges
content:
Apple is to stand trial in Paris in June 2027 on suspicion of having organised the planned obsolescence of various iPhone models by preventing repairs outside official outlets, a source close to the case told AFP on Tuesday.

The case brought by French prosecutors against the US tech giant on charges of “obstructing repair and refurbishment” is a first, campaign group Stop Planned Obsolescence said, welcoming the move after filing a complaint on December 7, 2022.

“We strongly contest these unfounded allegations,” Apple said when contacted by AFP.

Planned obsolescence refers to techniques used by manufacturers to deliberately shorten the lifespan of their products, generally electronic devices, thereby encouraging consumers to discard and replace them more frequently.

According to the source close to the case, Apple Distribution International and parent company Apple Inc are due to appear in court for a four-day trial starting on June 17.

They are accused of preventing repairs to a range of iPhone models for more than two and a half years, from November 2021 to July 2024.

Apple is accused of configuring its smartphone software to “make it impossible to repair or refurbish” devices outside its authorised network, the source added.

The alleged aim was to boost sales of Apple’s flagship product and increase the revenue of the multinational, which now generates more than $400 billion a year, about half of that from iPhone sales.

AFP

The post Apple to face trial over alleged iPhone repair restrictions in France appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Singing ‘Arise, O Compatriots’ not a criminal offence – Josef Onoh
description:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Josef Onoh, has said that neither the 1999 Constitution nor the National Anthem Act 2024 criminalises the singing of Nigeria’s former national anthem, ‘Arise, O Compatriots’.
Onoh made the clarification during an interview on Arise News on Monda
content:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Josef Onoh, has said that neither the 1999 Constitution nor the National Anthem Act 2024 criminalises the singing of Nigeria’s former national anthem, ‘Arise, O Compatriots’.

Onoh made the clarification during an interview on Arise News on Monday, describing the controversy over the decision by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and other party members to sing the old anthem at a gathering as a trivial issue.

He argued that although the National Anthem Act 2024 restored ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’ as the country’s official anthem, it did not prohibit citizens from singing the former anthem or prescribe punishment for failing to recite the current one.

“Why I think it’s a trivial matter is, one, we have the old national anthem, which is the Arise, O Compatriots, and we have the new national anthem,” he said.

Onoh said both anthems symbolised Nigerians’ allegiance and historical connection to the country, adding that the 2024 law did not criminalise the use of the former anthem.

“And these two national anthems symbolise our allegiance, our deep-rooted and historical affiliation to our nation,” he added.

He noted that the National Anthem Act, signed by President Bola Tinubu in May 2024, contained no provision making it an offence to sing the former anthem.

“And when the National Anthem Act of 2024 was created, they did not in any way, even in the Constitution, criminalise any part of the old national anthem that says, ‘Ok, if you do not recite the old national anthem, if you ever recite the old national anthem, it becomes a crime’,” Onoh said.

The APC chieftain also questioned whether the NDC gathering was legally required to render the current anthem, referring to Section 3 of the Act, which specifies occasions when its performance is mandatory.

He said the provision covered official government, legislative and political gatherings but did not expressly include private political town hall meetings.

“But one particular part of this section, it’s like a loophole in the whole essence, is that when you look at the whole section, it never in any way made it, listed private political town hall gathering as mandatory, as mandatory requiring you to cite the national anthem,” he said.

Onoh further cited Section 24(a) of the 1999 Constitution, which identifies respect for the national anthem as one of the civic duties of citizens.

He argued that while the Constitution recognises respect for the anthem as a civic responsibility, it does not prescribe criminal punishment for failing to sing or recite it.

“Then when you look at Section 24A of the 1999 Constitution as amended, it listed respecting the national anthem, which basically we all know, as a civic duty,” he said.

“But neither the Constitution nor the National Anthem Act of 2024 criminalised the not reciting the national anthem,” he added.

The controversy followed an NDC town hall meeting in Lagos last week, attended by Obi and the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Funso Doherty.

At the event, the former anthem, ‘Arise, O Compatriots’, was sung after attendees did not join in rendering ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’, triggering political reactions.

The incident drew criticism from government officials and supporters of the ruling party, including the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo.

Wike accused Obi of disrespecting national symbols, while Keyamo described the incident as an indication of secessionist tendencies.

However, some NDC figures dismissed the criticism, saying the singing of the former anthem was a spontaneous response by attendees and not a deliberate rejection of the country’s official anthem.

Nigeria adopted ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’ as its national anthem at independence in 1960 but replaced it with ‘Arise, O Compatriots’ in 1978. Tinubu signed the National Anthem Bill into law on May 29, 2024, restoring the original anthem after 46 years.

The post Singing ‘Arise, O Compatriots’ not a criminal offence – Josef Onoh appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: ‘If elected Governor, Teachers, Doctors will not pay taxes’ – Doherty
description:
Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Adedeji Doherty, has promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes if elected governor.
Doherty said his administration would channel increased federal allocations towards improving healthcare, education and the ge
content:
Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Adedeji Doherty, has promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes if elected governor.

Doherty said his administration would channel increased federal allocations towards improving healthcare, education and the general welfare of Lagos residents.

He made the pledge on Tuesday during an interview on a Channels Television programme, where he outlined some of his proposed policies.

The PDP candidate also promised to introduce a tax card that would allow residents struggling with the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually.

According to him, holders of the proposed tax card would also enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation as part of measures to reduce the cost of living.

He said: “When I am governor, I will transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two groups will not pay tax.

“Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation.

“This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you.”

The PDP candidate also promised free education, saying the funds available to the state would enable him to implement the policy.

Justifying the proposed tax exemption for doctors, he said: “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break.”

He described teachers as critical to the state’s future, arguing that they must receive proper training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities.

Doherty further condemned attacks on political activities and disclosed that some people he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge.

He said his Director-General had reported the incident to the police, adding that he would visit the Department of State Services, DSS.

The post 2027: ‘If elected Governor, Teachers, Doctors will not pay taxes’ – Doherty appeared first on Very Nigerian.

Doherty, who made the promise during an interview on a Channels Television programme, said he would also introduce a tax card that would enable residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation.

He said: “When I am governor, I will transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two groups will not pay tax.

“Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation.

The PDP candidate also promised free education, saying the funds available to the state would enable him to implement the policy.

Justifying the proposed tax exemption for doctors, he said: “We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break.”

He described teachers as critical to the state’s future, arguing that they must receive proper training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities.

title: NNPC probes Lagos filling station fire
description:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited has commenced an investigation into a fire outbreak at an affiliated filling station along Ekoro-Ajasa Road in the Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State.
The company said the fire, which occurred on Monday, November 16, 2026, had been brought u
content:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited has commenced an investigation into a fire outbreak at an affiliated filling station along Ekoro-Ajasa Road in the Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State.

The company said the fire, which occurred on Monday, November 16, 2026, had been brought under control by emergency responders, adding that no deaths or injuries had been reported.

NNPC Limited disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh.

The incident affected seven classrooms at St Lawrence Greater Height School, located beside the filling station, as well as two vehicles and three fuel dispensing pumps.

A DAF truck and a Toyota Camry were also reportedly destroyed in the fire.

The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency said preliminary investigations indicated that the fire started while a tanker was discharging diesel at the filling station before spreading to the dispensing pumps and the adjoining school.

Confirming that the fire had been contained, NNPC said its retail, health, safety and environment teams, alongside the management of the affiliated station, were reviewing the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The statement read, “NNPC Limited confirms that the fire at an NNPC-affiliated filling station on Ekoro-Ajasa Road in Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos earlier today, 16 November 2026, has been contained.

“Based on preliminary information, no fatalities or injuries have been reported.

“We understand the fear and distress this incident has caused residents, customers and businesses in the area. Our thoughts are with everyone affected, particularly those whose property or livelihoods may have been impacted.”

The company commended the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and other emergency responders for containing the fire and limiting further damage.

It said, “NNPC Limited commends the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA), the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and other emergency responders for bringing the fire under control and limiting further damage.”

The oil firm said the safety of customers, employees and neighbouring communities remained a priority, assuring residents that it would cooperate with relevant authorities and the station’s management in investigating the incident.

“NNPC Retail, Health, Safety and Environment teams and management of the affiliate filling station are reviewing the cause of the fire.

“The safety of customers, employees and neighbouring communities remains a priority. NNPC Limited will support the relevant authorities and management of the affiliate filling station and provide further updates as verified information becomes available,” it stated.

The incident has renewed attention on fire safety at petroleum retail outlets, particularly during fuel offloading operations, when flammable products are transferred from tankers into storage facilities.

NNPC said it would provide further information after its review and investigations by the relevant authorities.

The post NNPC probes Lagos filling station fire appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fayose: Makinde will flee Nigeria after 2027 elections over his actions
description:
Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has claimed that Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, will leave Nigeria after the 2027 general elections.
Fayose made the allegation on Monday during an interview on TVC, saying Makinde would flee the country because of his actions while in office.
Accordin
content:
Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has claimed that Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, will leave Nigeria after the 2027 general elections.

Fayose made the allegation on Monday during an interview on TVC, saying Makinde would flee the country because of his actions while in office.

According to the former governor, Makinde would not remain in Nigeria to face the consequences of his actions after leaving office.

Fayose further claimed that the Oyo governor would leave the country between January and March 2027, adding that he would not wait to receive the April 2027 allocation from the Federal Government before departing.

He said Makinde will be giving directives from exile.

Fayose asked Nigerians to write down his words. He said he has said many things in the past and they later happened exactly as he said them.

He recalled that he was the one who first spoke about the crisis involving Rivers State Governor, Sim Fubara, before it happened. He also said he predicted the case of former Edo State Governor, Godwin Obaseki.

“Write my words down. After this election, Governor Makinde will run from Nigeria between January and March. I’ve said so many things in Nigeria. I was the one who spoke about this Fubara thing.

“Between March and April, let me be precise: Makinde will run. He won’t take April allocation. He will be directing from exile,” Fayose said.

content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has alleged a plot to deploy suspected thugs to cause mayhem in the name of its members ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s visit to Kebbi State.

The party said it had uncovered a plan to distribute ADC-branded shirts to some unscrupulous elements, who would allegedly be used to create disturbances and portray the party in a negative light.

The allegation was contained in a press briefing addressed by the party’s Deputy Publicity Secretary, Atiku Abubakar.

According to Atiku, the alleged plot was aimed at creating the impression that ADC members were responsible for any disruption during the President’s visit.

He said the party was alerting members of the public and security agencies to the development, insisting that anyone caught engaging in such activities under the guise of being an ADC member should not be regarded as representing the party.

“We therefore call on the general public and security agencies to take note that our party has uncovered this alleged plot. Anyone caught engaging in such acts is not our member and should be dealt with in accordance with the law,” Atiku said.

He maintained that the ADC was a party of credible and peace-loving individuals and urged its members to remain peaceful before, during and after the President’s visit.

title: Nafiu Bala resumes as ADC national chairman, notifies INEC

In a letter dated November 16, 2026, and received by INEC
content:
Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe has formally notified the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of his resumption as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following a court declaration delivered on November 5, 2026.

In a letter dated November 16, 2026, and received by INEC on the same day, Bala Gombe informed the commission that he had officially resumed duty in compliance with the declaration issued by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja Division.

The letter, with reference number ADC/NHQ/CH/2026/001, cited Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, instituted by Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe against the African Democratic Congress and four others.

The notification formally communicates his resumption to the electoral commission in line with the court declaration.

According to the letter, the court affirmed his position as the party’s National Chairman, prompting his decision to resume office with immediate effect.

“In obedience to the said valid and subsisting judgment of the Honourable Court, I have resumed duty as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress with immediate effect,” he stated.

Bala Gombe asked INEC to formally acknowledge his resumption, recognise him as the party’s National Chairman for official correspondence and filings, and update its records and portal accordingly.

He also attached a certified true copy of the court’s judgment and declaration for the commission’s records and necessary action.

In a subsequent statement shared on his Facebook account, Bala Gombe reiterated his position and directed that all official communications concerning the party should henceforth be channelled through his office.

“In strict obedience to the valid and subsisting judgment of the Honourable Court, I have, with immediate effect, resumed duty as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress,” he said.

“Accordingly, all official correspondence, communications, and filings relating to the Party should henceforth be directed to my office at the Party Secretariat, located at No. 4, Miriam Ikejiani Clarke Crescent, Guzape, Abuja.”

He further assured the electoral commission of his commitment to constitutional order, due process and a harmonious working relationship in the interest of democracy.

title: Singing old national anthem not a crime – APC chieftain
description:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Dr Josef Onoh, has said that neither the 1999 Constitution nor the National Anthem Act 2024 criminalises the singing of Nigeria’s former national anthem, ‘Arise, O Compatriots’.
Onoh stated this during an interview on Arise News on Monday, describing the
content:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Dr Josef Onoh, has said that neither the 1999 Constitution nor the National Anthem Act 2024 criminalises the singing of Nigeria’s former national anthem, ‘Arise, O Compatriots’.

Onoh stated this during an interview on Arise News on Monday, describing the controversy surrounding Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate Peter Obi and members of the party for singing the old anthem at a party gathering as a trivial matter.

He argued that although the National Anthem Act 2024 reinstated ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’ as the country’s official anthem, it did not prohibit citizens from singing the previous anthem or prescribe punishment for failing to recite the current one.

“Why I think it’s a trivial matter is, one, we have the old national anthem, which is the Arise, O Compatriots, and we have the new national anthem,” he said.

Onoh said both anthems represented Nigerians’ allegiance and historical connection to the country, adding that the 2024 legislation did not criminalise the use of the former anthem.

“And these two national anthems symbolise our allegiance, our deep-rooted and historical affiliation to our nation,” he added.

He explained that the National Anthem Act, signed by President Bola Tinubu in May 2024, did not contain any provision making it an offence to sing the former anthem.

“And when the National Anthem Act of 2024 was created, they did not in any way, even in the Constitution, criminalise any part of the old national anthem that says, ‘Ok, if you do not recite the old national anthem, if you ever recite the old national anthem, it becomes a crime’,” Onoh said.

The APC chieftain also questioned the argument that the NDC gathering was legally required to render the new anthem, citing Section 3 of the Act, which outlines occasions when its performance is mandatory.

According to him, the provision covers official government and legislative gatherings as well as political gatherings but does not specifically list private political town hall meetings as occasions requiring the rendition of the anthem.

“And you have to also understand that Section 3 of the Act mandates the performance of the new anthem in official government places and official legislative holdings and gatherings and political gatherings too,” he said.

He, however, pointed to what he described as a loophole in the provision, arguing that private political town hall meetings were not expressly included among the gatherings where the anthem must be performed.

“But one particular part of this section, it’s like a loophole in the whole essence, is that when you look at the whole section, it never in any way made it, listed private political town hall gathering as mandatory, as mandatory requiring you to cite the national anthem,” he added.

Onoh further cited Section 24(a) of the 1999 Constitution, which lists respect for the national anthem among the civic duties of citizens.

He argued that although the Constitution recognises respect for the anthem as a civic responsibility, it does not provide criminal punishment for failing to sing or recite it.

“Then when you look at Section 24A of the 1999 Constitution as amended, it listed respecting the national anthem, which basically we all know, as a civic duty,” he said.

“But neither the Constitution nor the National Anthem Act of 2024 criminalised the not reciting the national anthem,” he added.

The controversy followed a town hall meeting organised by the NDC in Lagos last week, which featured Obi and the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Funso Doherty.

During the event, the former anthem, ‘Arise, O Compatriots’, was rendered after the gathering did not join in singing ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’, prompting political reactions.

The incident attracted criticism from several supporters of the ruling party and government officials, including the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo.

Wike accused Obi of disrespecting national symbols, while Keyamo described the incident as an indication of secessionist tendencies.

However, some NDC figures dismissed the criticism, arguing that the singing of the former anthem was a spontaneous reaction by attendees rather than a deliberate rejection of the official national anthem.

Nigeria adopted ‘Nigeria, We Hail Thee’ as its national anthem at independence in 1960 before replacing it with ‘Arise, O Compatriots’ in 1978.

Tinubu signed the National Anthem Bill into law on May 29, 2024, restoring the original anthem after 46 years.

The legislation followed its passage by the National Assembly and generated public debate, with critics questioning the decision amid the country’s economic challenges.

The post Singing old national anthem not a crime – APC chieftain appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Lagos police declare war on political thugs, trouble makers
description:
By Christopher Oji
The Lagos State Police Command has placed its personnel on heightened alert ahead of the 2027 General Elections, warning troublemakers, political thugs and other criminal elements against activities capable of disrupting public peace.
The Commissioner of Police, Lagos State Comman
content:
By Christopher Oji

The Lagos State Police Command has placed its personnel on heightened alert ahead of the 2027 General Elections, warning troublemakers, political thugs and other criminal elements against activities capable of disrupting public peace.

The Commissioner of Police, Lagos State Command, Tijani Fatai, gave the warning while charging Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers (DPOs), Tactical Commanders and heads of strategic departments to strengthen proactive security measures and ensure heightened operational vigilance ahead of the elections.

The CP gave the charge while conveying the directives of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, during a strategic briefing with senior officers of the Command.

He emphasised the need for effective supervision, strict compliance with operational directives and sustained vigilance across all formations of the Command.

Tijani directed officers to strengthen intelligence gathering, identify potential flashpoints and implement preventive security measures to forestall political violence, thuggery, cultism and other criminal activities capable of threatening public peace and disrupting the electoral process.

He further stressed the importance of supervision and accountability, charging senior officers to closely monitor personnel under their command and ensure strict adherence to operational directives, discipline and professional standards.

The CP warned that any supervisory failure, dereliction of duty or misconduct would attract appropriate sanctions.

In a statement, the Police Public Relations Officer in the state, SP Abimbola Adebisi, said the strategic briefing also featured the decoration of 71 newly promoted officers of the Command.

The promoted officers comprise six Chief Superintendents of Police (CSPs), 15 Superintendents of Police (SPs) and 50 Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs).

Congratulating the newly promoted officers, the CP described their elevation as recognition of their dedication, commitment and contributions to the Force.

He urged them to regard their new ranks as a call to greater responsibility and higher standards of service, charging them to justify the confidence reposed in them through exemplary conduct, professionalism and improved service delivery.

The post 2027: Lagos police declare war on political thugs, trouble makers appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Inflation rate drops year-on-year, rises month-on-month
description:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan



The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, has disclosed that Nigeria’s headline inflation rate dropped to 14.06 percent in October 2026 from 14.63 percent in the previous month.



NBS stated this in its latest Consumer Price Index, CPI, Report noting that food inflation also
content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, has disclosed that Nigeria’s headline inflation rate dropped to 14.06 percent in October 2026 from 14.63 percent in the previous month.

NBS stated this in its latest Consumer Price Index, CPI, Report noting that food inflation also declined to 19.13 percent from 19.59 percent in September.

However, Month-on-Month, MoM, inflation rate rose by 0.43% in October, up by 0.38 percentage point from 0.06 percent recorded in September 2026.

This increase also reflected in the MoM trend in food inflation for October.

NBS stated: “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06 percent, down from 14.63 percent in September 2026 and stood at 18.97 percent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025).

“Looking at the movement, the October 2026 Headline inflation rate showed a decrease of 4.9 percent compared to the October 2025 (18.97 percent) Headline inflation rate.

“On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43 percent, which was 0.38 percent higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06 percent).

“This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026.”

On food inflation, NBS, said: “The Food inflation rate in October 2026 was 19.13 per cent on a year-on-year basis and stood at 16.3 per ent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025). “However, on a MoM basis, the Food inflation rate in October 2026 was -0.75 percent , up by 0.80 percent points from September 2026 (-1.55 per cent).

“This can be attributed to the rate of change in the average prices of the following products: vegetable oil (75cl), Titus sardines (125g), green peas (Prepacked), mackerel frozen, croakers (apo), rice local, catfish fresh, beef tripes, palm oil (75cl), millet flour (sold loose), etc”

In October 2026, food inflation on a year-on-year basis was highest in Ondo (31.74 percent), Lagos (31.43 percent), and Imo (29.75 percent), while Nasarawa (3.7 percent), Bayelsa (7.11 percent) and Kano (7.13 percent) recorded the slowest rise in food inflation on a Year-on-Year basis.

“On a MoM basis, however, October 2026 food inflation was highest in Yobe (18.41 percent), Kebbi (16.45 percent), and Borno (13.96 percent), while Lagos (-5.93 percent), Plateau (-5.83 percent), and Benue (-5.49 percent) recorded the slowest rise in Food inflation on a Month-on-Month basis.”

Vanguard News

title: Kano govt, Kwankwasiyya Movement clash over attack on Kwankwaso’s convoy
description:
*Alleged attack fictitiuos – Kano State govt *Kano belongs to all, not those in power, Kwankwasiyya blasts govt



By Hadiza Yusuf



KANO — Kano State government and the Kwankwasiyyah Movement were, yesterday, locked in a verbal war over alleged attack on the convoy of the vice presidential candida
content:
*Alleged attack fictitiuos – Kano State govt *Kano belongs to all, not those in power, Kwankwasiyya blasts govt

By Hadiza Yusuf

KANO — Kano State government and the Kwankwasiyyah Movement were, yesterday, locked in a verbal war over alleged attack on the convoy of the vice presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in the state, weekend.

NDC governorship candidate in Kano, Aminu Gwarzo, had alleged that during a campaign visit to Bichi on Sunday, the convoy of the vice presidential candidate of the party was attacked by thugs allegedly sent by the state government.

The spokesperson for Gwarzo’s campaign, Ibrahim Shu’aibu, said the team had earlier visited Tofa, Rimingado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono and Bagwai local government areas without disruption before proceeding to Bichi where they were attcked.

But reacting to the attack, yesterday, the Commissioner for Information in Kano State, Sanusi Tofa, dismissed the fact that there was an attack on the convoy of Kwankwaso in Bichi Local Government Area, describing the incident as fictitious.

Tofa, who accused the Kwankwasiyya Movement of fabricating the reported attack in Bichi said: “In an attempt to generate public sympathy, the Kwankwasiyya team has framed itself a fictitious attack in Bichi, no pictures, no videos.’’

Kano belongs to all, not those in power — Kwankwasiyya tells govt

Replying the state government, the Kwankwasiyya Movement said Kano State belonged to all residents, regardless of their political affiliations.

The movement said the government had a responsibility to protect everyone in the state and should not allow political differences to affect the safety and rights of citizens.

In a statement by its spokesperson, Dr Habibu Mohammed, yesterday, the movement also criticised the state government for dismissing the incident as fictitious and accusing the Kwankwasiyya Movement of making up the allegation to gain public sympathy.

The statement specifically faulted the Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Tofa, for demanding pictures and videos of the incident, rather than allowing security agencies to investigate the matter.

It questioned why victims should be expected to provide evidence before the government could show concern over their safety.

“Kano belongs to all its people, not exclusively to those occupying government offices. Its security, peace and democratic freedoms are collective responsibilities that must never be sacrificed on the altar of partisan politics,” the statement said.

The movement argued that the responsibility for investigating allegations of criminal activities rested with security agencies, not the victims, accusing the commissioner of making premature conclusions without presenting the findings of any police investigation.

The group called on Kano State police command to investigate the incident, establish what happened in Bichi and ensure that anyone found responsible was brought to justice.

It further demanded an investigation into the reported destruction of vehicles and injuries sustained by members of Kwankwaso’s delegation.

The movement urged Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf to rise above political considerations and guarantee the safety of all political parties, candidates, campaign officials and supporters across the state.

It also warned against political intimidation, insisting that opposition members should be allowed to participate in lawful political activities without fear of harassment or violence.

“Political competition is not warfare, and opposition politics is not a criminal offence,” the statement added.

The Kwankwasiyya Movement said it would remain committed to peaceful political participation but warned that its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for acceptance of intimidation or impunity.

The presidential candidate of the party, Peter Obi, in a post on his X handle yesterday, condemned the attack, describing Kwankwaso as his brother and running mate, expressing sadness over the incident.

He said: “I am deeply saddened by reports of the attack on the convoy of my brother and running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and members of his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

“I strongly condemn this unfortunate incident. Reports indicate that several members of the entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised. This is unacceptable and must not be allowed to become part of our political culture.”

Vanguard News

title: War on terror: Over 2,000 suspected terrorists facing prosecution — Tinubu
description:
*Says more than 1,000 terrorists convicted in war against terror networks *Notes: Nigeria has killed, arrested 4 of 8 global terrorist leaders



By Kingsley Omonobi



ABUJA – President Bola Tinubu has said over 2,000 suspected terrorists were currently undergoing prosecution, while more than 1,000
content:
*Says more than 1,000 terrorists convicted in war against terror networks *Notes: Nigeria has killed, arrested 4 of 8 global terrorist leaders

By Kingsley Omonobi

ABUJA – President Bola Tinubu has said over 2,000 suspected terrorists were currently undergoing prosecution, while more than 1,000 terrorist suspects have been convicted.

According to him, this makes Nigeria one of the countries with the highest rate of prosecution of terrorists elements in the world.

He also said Nigerian security forces had killed or arrested four of eight identified senior global terrorist leaders, describing the feat as evidence of the country’s growing capacity to dismantle terrorist networks.

Tinubu, who was represented by the National Security Adviser, NSA, Malam Nuhu Ribadu, disclosed these at the opening of the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence, CDI, Annual Conference in Abuja yesterday.

Detailing that the operational successes reflected sustained and coordinated pressure on terrorist organisations, the President pointed out the elimination of senior Islamic State leader, Abu Bilal al-Minuki, in May 2026, and the arrest of Omar Hassan Ma’adou as notable examples of the gains recorded.

He said: “Recent operational successes demonstrate our growing capacity to dismantle terrorist leadership, disrupt expansion networks and deny violent groups freedom of action.

“Under this administration, four of eight identified senior terrorist leaders have been killed or arrested. These gains include action against Ahmed Ohida’s ISWAP southern expansion network, the elimination of senior Islamic State leader, Abu Bilal Mainuki, in May 2026, and the arrests of Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa in 2025.

“Together, they reflect sustained and coordinated pressure on terrorist command structures. Our immediate task is to convert these gains into lasting security.

“Operations remain focused on the remaining identified leaders: Ba Shuwa of ISWAP; Abdullahi Oro of IS-Sahel; Sadiku of JAS in the North Central region; and Bakura Doro in the Lake Chad Basin.

“The security services have also killed senior bandit leaders, including Halilu Sububu, and many of their fighters, sustaining pressure on the networks threatening our communities.

“In the Niger Delta, recorded incidents of illegal oil bunkering and vandalism of critical oil and gas installations fell from 32 in the first quarter of 2026 to 21 in the second and 17 in the third: a 46.88 per cent reduction between the first and third quarters.

“Alongside these security gains, oil production has improved, with crude oil and condensate output averaging about 1.68 million barrels per day in August 2026. We must sustain the protection of our energy assets and national revenues.

“Through closer intelligence sharing and coordinated action among the DSS, Armed Forces, Police and other security agencies, we will consolidate these gains, sustain pressure on criminal and terrorist networks, protect vulnerable communities and strengthen security ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“Every Nigerian must be able to live, work and exercise their democratic rights in safety. The contemporary intelligence landscape is being reshaped by rapid technological advancement and the exponential growth of information.

‘’Artificial intelligence, machine learning, cyber capabilities and unmanned systems offer powerful tools to detect patterns, map criminal networks and generate early warning.

“Strategic partnerships allow us to pool insights and resources to address complex security challenges. Nigeria’s security realities, therefore, demand that we optimise our intelligence architecture through technology and deep collaboration. This is a mission in which the Defence Intelligence Agency, DIA, plays a central role.

“To realise these benefits, we must connect AI-assisted analysis, geospatial intelligence and unmanned surveillance through secure, interoperable systems that turn information into timely action. We must also invest in Nigerian technical expertise and partnerships with research institutions and technology companies.

“AI outputs require verification and accountable human judgement. Data protection and cybersecurity must be built into these systems, alongside the capacity to detect deepfakes and other AI-enabled deception. Technology must strengthen the trusted human intelligence on which effective security depends.

“It is within this context that my administration has embarked on comprehensive reforms to strengthen national security, protect our citizens and modernise our intelligence apparatus. We have continued to upgrade operational readiness, strengthen data protection and cybersecurity, and prioritise the protection of critical national infrastructure.

“I have directed the Special Adviser on Homeland Security, Major General A. A. Famadewa, retd, to coordinate preparation of a Comprehensive National Threat Assessment and Five-Year Rolling Strategic Defence Operations Plan. This will place accurate, integrated and anticipatory intelligence at the foundation of capability-based defence planning.

“Strategic partnerships are equally central to achieving these objectives. No single institution possesses all the information, technology, expertise and operational capacity required to address contemporary security threats.

“Effective intelligence requires purposeful collaboration among the Armed Forces, Defence Intelligence Agency, Department of State Services, National Intelligence Agency, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other relevant stakeholders.

‘It must also extend to regional and international partners, sub-national entities, technology companies and research institutions, within appropriate legal and security frameworks. The objective is to establish trusted mechanisms through which information is shared, fused and converted into actionable intelligence.

‘Under this administration, we have strengthened security relationships with the United States, France, the United Kingdom, China, the United Arab Emirates, Türkiye and our African neighbours. We will continue to deepen intelligence sharing, training and technological cooperation, guided by Nigeria’s sovereignty and national interest.

“Accordingly, I encourage our Defence Advisers and Attachés to continue to bolster Nigeria’s strategic intelligence and defence relationships abroad. Developments beyond our immediate borders can rapidly shape our national security. I, therefore, urge you to strengthen bilateral and multilateral engagements with host nations and international partners.

“In the same vein, our state office coordinators should intensify collaboration with local security agencies to ensure effective intelligence fusion. The integration of strategic external awareness with granular domestic intelligence is essential to developing a comprehensive national threat picture.’’

President Tinubu commended the Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lt. Gen. Emmanuel Undiandeye, and his team for their leadership and service in strengthening defence intelligence and strategic cooperation.

In his remarks, the Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Musa, retd, commended intelligence personnel for their professionalism and contributions to national security.

Musa urged them to remain proactive, stressing that credible, timely and actionable intelligence was critical to successful military operations.

He also reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to indigenous defence production, describing local manufacturing as essential to achieving sustainable military capabilities.

The Chief of Defence Staff, CDS, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, said intelligence remained fundamental to operational planning, strategic decision-making and effective military response.

Oluyede called for increased investment in artificial intelligence, advanced data analytics, geospatial intelligence and unmanned systems.

He said the armed forces would continue to prioritise intelligence integration, capacity development and technological innovation.

The CDS stressed the need to transform security operations from largely reactive responses to proactive, intelligence-led engagements capable of anticipating and disrupting threats before they materialised

The post War on terror: Over 2,000 suspected terrorists facing prosecution — Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Inflation drops to 14.05% – NBS report
description:
Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent in September, marking the fifth consecutive month of moderation, although food inflation remained elevated at 19.13 per cent.
The latest figure represents a decline of 0.57 percentage points from Septemb
content:
Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent in September, marking the fifth consecutive month of moderation, although food inflation remained elevated at 19.13 per cent.

The latest figure represents a decline of 0.57 percentage points from September and 4.91 percentage points from the 18.97 per cent recorded in October 2025.

This was disclosed in the October 2026 Consumer Price Index report released on Monday by the National Bureau of Statistics.

The report read, “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06 per cent, down from 14.63 per cent in September 2026 and stood at 18.97 per cent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025).”

Despite the moderation in annual inflation, the report showed that consumer prices increased faster on a monthly basis, indicating that inflationary pressures persisted.

Month-on-month headline inflation rose to 0.43 per cent in October from 0.06 per cent in September, an increase of approximately 0.37 percentage points.

The NBS explained, “This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026.”

The Consumer Price Index increased to 147.0 points in October from 146.4 points in September, reflecting a continued rise in the general price level.

Further analysis showed that food and non-alcoholic beverages remained the largest contributors to annual headline inflation, accounting for 5.63 percentage points.

Restaurants and accommodation services followed with 1.82 percentage points, transportation contributed 1.50 percentage points, while housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels accounted for 1.18 percentage points.

Education and health services contributed 0.87 and 0.85 percentage points, respectively.

Food inflation stood at 19.13 per cent year-on-year in October, compared with 16.30 per cent in October 2025, representing an increase of 2.83 percentage points.

However, on a month-on-month basis, food inflation stood at -0.75 per cent, compared with -1.55 per cent in September, indicating that average food prices declined for the second consecutive month, although at a slower pace.

The bureau explained, “This can be attributed to the rate of change in the average prices of the following products: Vegetable Oil (75cl), Titus Sardines (125g), Green Peas (Prepacked), Mackerel Frozen, Croakers (Apo), Rice Local, Catfish Fresh, Beef tripes, Palm oil (75cl), Millet Flour (sold loose), etc.”

The average annual food inflation rate for the 12 months ending October stood at 15.98 per cent, compared with 26.47 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025.

Core inflation, which excludes volatile agricultural produce and energy prices, declined to 10.78 per cent from 21.25 per cent in October 2025.

On a monthly basis, core inflation fell by 0.53 per cent, reversing the 1.11 per cent increase recorded in September.

Other inflation indicators showed that farm produce prices increased by 18.38 per cent year-on-year, while energy inflation stood at 12.30 per cent. Services inflation was 11.73 per cent, goods inflation reached 13.58 per cent, and imported food inflation stood at 8.39 per cent.

Urban inflation stood at 14.84 per cent year-on-year, compared with 12.17 per cent in rural areas.

On a monthly basis, urban inflation moderated to 0.43 per cent from 0.53 per cent, while rural inflation increased to 0.18 per cent from minus 0.89 per cent.

Across the states, Imo recorded the highest annual headline inflation at 28.66 per cent, followed by Enugu at 22.81 per cent and Kaduna at 21.55 per cent.

Taraba recorded the lowest rate at 6.12 per cent, followed by Sokoto at 6.68 per cent and Ekiti at 7.64 per cent.

For food inflation, Ondo recorded the highest annual rate at 31.74 per cent, followed by Lagos at 31.43 per cent and Imo at 29.75 per cent. Nasarawa recorded the lowest at 3.70 per cent.

The NBS cautioned, “The CPI is weighted by consumption expenditure patterns that vary across States and locations,” adding that differences in consumption baskets could make interstate comparisons misleading.

An analysis of inflation trends in 2026 showed that headline inflation declined from 15.15 per cent in December 2025 to 15.10 per cent in January and 15.06 per cent in February.

However, it increased to 15.38 per cent in March, 15.69 per cent in April and 15.93 per cent in May, before easing to 15.91 per cent in June.

The downward trend continued in July at 15.43 per cent, August at 15.39 per cent and September at 14.63 per cent, before reaching 14.06 per cent in October.

Consequently, inflation has declined by 1.87 percentage points from its May peak, although the continued increase in the general price level means households still face higher living costs.

The latest figures come ahead of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Monetary Policy Committee meeting scheduled for November 24, following its decision in September to reduce the benchmark interest rate to 23 per cent.

The sustained moderation in annual inflation could strengthen expectations of further monetary easing, although persistent food price pressures and the acceleration in monthly headline inflation remain concerns for policymakers.

title: US to close AI chip loophole after Nvidia scandal
description:
The United States announced tougher export controls on AI chips on Monday after a scandal involving Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang exposed a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.
The news came the day before Californian chip titan Nvidia reports its first earnings since Huang’s departur
content:
The United States announced tougher export controls on AI chips on Monday after a scandal involving Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang exposed a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

The news came the day before Californian chip titan Nvidia reports its first earnings since Huang’s departure as CEO, with investors questioning if the artificial intelligence boom can hold strong.

Under Washington’s new rules, data centres anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips.

These changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

While this loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Nvidia co-founder Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in violation of export controls.

Jensen Huang, 63, stepped down last week after at least two extramarital affairs were revealed in media reports.

Facing criticism, the US Commerce Department said Monday it would close a loophole that had drawn concern from US authorities.

The move “is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries,” the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) said in a statement.

It weighed on Nvidia’s shares, which shed four percent on Monday, extending a slide since the scandal erupted.

• ‘Business-as-usual’ unlikely –

Nvidia stock has lost more than a quarter of its value over the past month, as doubts grow about the health of the AI investment boom.

Tuesday’s results will be the first presented under chief financial officer, Colette Kress, who is serving as interim CEO.

“If they try to keep a business-as-usual tone in the call, I think that it probably wouldn’t be well received,” said Jacob Bourne of Emarketer, describing the company as in turmoil.

Investors will be watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.

Analysts said they would also be eyeing Nvidia’s guidance on future sales, along with its chip sales in Asia, particularly Singapore.

That could ripple across the AI investments propping up the US economy — with Nvidia backing major labs including Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, which is expected to begin trading on Wall Street on Thursday.

Tech firms dragged Asian stock markets down again Tuesday as the fallout from the Nvidia crisis rattles trading floors, with the new US moves on chip controls adding to uncertainty.

• ‘Trusted access’ –

On Tuesday, Singapore said it was engaging with affected companies and talking to US authorities to ascertain the scope and implementation of the new measures.

The city-state is also “exploring how to facilitate trusted access (to AI chips) for Singapore companies”, a government statement said.

Indonesia said it was reviewing the measure “and seeking industry input on its potential impact on operations and investment, including in the data centre sector”.

The scandal has exposed a rift within the Trump administration.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for an investigation into Jensen Huang’s dealings with Megaspeed, and accuses the Commerce Department of ignoring widespread reports that Megaspeed was shifting Nvidia technology to China.

Tech tycoon Elon Musk and other major AI investors are meanwhile gathering signatures for an open letter calling for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement.

“The most important time to help someone is when they’re down,” investor Bill Ackman said at a Semafor tech conference.

Before leaving for summits in Asia, President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, waving off the security concerns.

But given the legal cloud over him, most Wall Street analysts doubt that the AI rock star can return anytime soon.

Kress, a non-engineer, is not expected to stay in the role permanently, leaving Nvidia facing a high-stakes search for a successor.

AFP

The post US to close AI chip loophole after Nvidia scandal appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: US confirms probing Singapore-based firm over chip exports
description:
The US government confirmed Monday it was investigating Singapore-based firm Megaspeed over chip exports, following the scandal that has rocked tech giant Nvidia.
Data centre company Megaspeed is suspected of helping to shift Nvidia’s most powerful technology to China in circumvention of US rules.
T
content:
The US government confirmed Monday it was investigating Singapore-based firm Megaspeed over chip exports, following the scandal that has rocked tech giant Nvidia.

Data centre company Megaspeed is suspected of helping to shift Nvidia’s most powerful technology to China in circumvention of US rules.

Those concerns emerged publicly after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang revealed an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a Chinese former executive from Megaspeed whom US authorities also suspect of spying for Beijing.

Huang, a pivotal figure in the AI boom, stepped down last week after at least two affairs were revealed, including the one with Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old.

The US Commerce and Justice departments said in a joint statement they were working together to “bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.”

China is in a race for tech dominance against the United States, which restricts the export to China of cutting-edge silicon chips crucial for artificial intelligence.

Washington has announced tougher export control measures on AI chips in the wake of the scandal.

The Commerce Department began a probe into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations, the statement said.

The department requested records from Nvidia “concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed” in May 2025.

The following month, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on a “no sell” list, while US federal agents conducted an “on-site, in-person” check at the Singapore-based firm and interviewed Alice Huang.

“Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed,” the statement added.

The scandal has exposed a rift within the administration of US President Donald Trump, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accusing the Commerce Department of ignoring reports that Megaspeed was shifting Nvidia technology to China.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate on the matter.

Jensen Huang has agreed to testify behind closed doors in the House of Representatives before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.

He has led Nvidia since its founding in 1993, acknowledged an extramarital affair in a letter to the firm’s employees that did not name the woman involved.

title: Stay away from tomorrow’s APC campaign rally, Itsekiri youths warn Oborevwori
description:
By Jimitota Onoyume



Some youths under the aegis of Itsekiri ethnic nationality have advised Itsekiri political leaders and governor of the state, Sheriff Oborevwori to stay away from the forthcoming campaign rally of the All Progressives Congress, APC, scheduled to hold at Nana College on Wednesd
content:
By Jimitota Onoyume

Some youths under the aegis of Itsekiri ethnic nationality have advised Itsekiri political leaders and governor of the state, Sheriff Oborevwori to stay away from the forthcoming campaign rally of the All Progressives Congress, APC, scheduled to hold at Nana College on Wednesday.


In a statement online by Appearance Efejuku and Joseph Okotie, the youths said their position was necessitated by the rejection of what they described as the alleged fraudulent ward structure delineation in Warri South Local Government Area, adding that Itsekiri political leaders who choose to attend the rally would be labeled enemies of the ethnic nation.
The statement further advised Governor Oborevwori and his political allies to stay away from the campaign until the legitimate concern raised by the Itsekiri people on the issues were addressed.
The statemtnt said: The general youths of Warri Kingdom and the Itsekiri people hereby advise all Itsekiri political leaders, elected and appointed office holders, and stakeholders to boycott the forthcoming APC campaign scheduled to hold at Nana College on Wednesday.
According to the statement, “This position is necessitated by the rejection of the fraudulent ward structure delineation in Warri South council.
“We further advise the state governor and his political allies to stay away from the said campaign until this legitimate concern is addressed.
“For the avoidance of doubt, any Itsekiri son or daughter who chooses to participate in the campaign against this collective position will be treated as an enemy of Itsekiri Nation. Our position is clear: No legitimate ward structure, no political participation.”
