title: NGX Group acquires 10% stake in Kenya’s NSE
description:
Nigerian Exchange Group Plc has acquired a 10 per cent equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, a strategic investment that extends the Group’s participation in East Africa and advances its pan-African growth strategy.
According to a statement issued by the Group, the move aligns with its pr
content:
Nigerian Exchange Group Plc has acquired a 10 per cent equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, a strategic investment that extends the Group’s participation in East Africa and advances its pan-African growth strategy.

According to a statement issued by the Group, the move aligns with its priority of building regional leadership through partnerships and African market integration, while strengthening its investment presence across West and East Africa.

The latest development builds on NGX Group’s earlier strategic investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange, further demonstrating the company’s long-term commitment to participating in the development and growth of African capital market infrastructure.

The acquisition provides NGX Group with exposure to one of East Africa’s most established capital markets, broadening its investment portfolio beyond Nigeria and positioning it to benefit from the long-term growth of the region’s capital markets and increasing financial integration across the continent.

The Group noted that the transaction reflects a disciplined approach to capital allocation, balancing strategic growth opportunities with its commitment to sustainable shareholder returns.

It added that the investment is anchored on three core priorities, namely: deepening regional integration by strengthening connections between African capital markets and supporting cross-border investment opportunities; driving portfolio diversification by expanding investment exposure beyond Nigeria; and enhancing long-term shareholder value.

Commenting on the investment, the Group Chairman, NGX Group, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, said, “African capital markets are at an inflection point, where integration is moving from aspiration to architecture. Exchange groups that commit patient capital to market infrastructure will help shape how capital flows across the continent. Our investment in the Nairobi Securities Exchange is a disciplined, long-term step in that direction, strengthening the financial linkages between West and East Africa while creating opportunities for sustainable shareholder value.”

Also speaking, the Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, NGX Group, Temi Popoola, explained that the acquisition underscores the Group’s drive to build a more diversified and resilient exchange with a stronger continental footprint.

He said, “This investment reflects our strategy to build a more diversified and resilient exchange group with a stronger presence across African markets. Kenya is a cornerstone of East Africa’s financial ecosystem, and our investment in NSE provides exposure to its long-term growth potential while broadening our sources of investment returns beyond Nigeria.

“Both markets have already shown what closer collaboration can achieve for issuers and investors, and a shareholding relationship gives that collaboration permanence. We remain focused on disciplined capital allocation and investments that deliver sustainable value to our shareholders over the long term.”

Through these cross-border investments, NGX Group stated that it would continue to pursue opportunities that enhance its regional participation, diversify its sources of investment returns, and support the development of more connected and competitive African capital markets.

Nigerian Exchange Group Plc operates as an integrated market infrastructure group with interests across Nigeria’s capital market ecosystem, supporting capital formation, investment access, market development, and the provision of financial market infrastructure through its subsidiaries and strategic investments.

The post NGX Group acquires 10% stake in Kenya’s NSE appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Plateau newlyweds die in fire, probe begins
description:
The Plateau State Police Command has begun an investigation into a fire incident that claimed the lives of a newly married couple, Sikiru Habib and his wife, Ramlat Lawan, in Anguwan Miyango, Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of the state.
The couple reportedly died from injuries sustained aft
content:
The Plateau State Police Command has begun an investigation into a fire incident that claimed the lives of a newly married couple, Sikiru Habib and his wife, Ramlat Lawan, in Anguwan Miyango, Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of the state.

The couple reportedly died from injuries sustained after a fire engulfed their residence at about 2:30am on Saturday while they were asleep.

Confirming the incident, the spokesman for the state police command, SP Alabo Alfred, said the matter had been reported to the police, and an investigation had commenced to establish the cause of the fire.

“Yes, it is actually a fire incident. The incident has been reported to us, and we are investigating the cause of the fire incident,” Alfred said when contacted.

Residents of the community, who confirmed the incident to journalists in Jos on Monday, described it as tragic, saying the couple became trapped inside their room as the fire spread.

A neighbour, Lawal Suleiman, said the fire was suspected to have been triggered by a high-voltage power surge, although there was no official confirmation of the cause.

“The incident was terrifying. The groom died on Sunday, while the bride died on Monday after both were admitted to hospital,” Suleiman said.

He said the situation became more dangerous when the room’s door reportedly failed to open, leaving the couple trapped inside.

According to him, young men in the neighbourhood rushed to the scene and made desperate efforts to rescue the victims.

“They eventually broke the room’s window and managed to bring the couple out before firefighters arrived to provide emergency assistance,” he added.

Suleiman said the victims were subsequently rushed to the Jos University Teaching Hospital, where they received medical attention.

“Despite efforts to save their lives, the couple died,” he said.

He added that their deaths had thrown their families, relatives, friends and residents of Anguwan Miyango into mourning, particularly as the tragedy occurred shortly after their marriage.

The post Plateau newlyweds die in fire, probe begins appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Five killed as fresh attacks hit three Plateau communities
description:
Fresh violence has again hit Plateau State, with five persons killed in coordinated attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi Local Government Areas between Sunday night and the early hours of Monday.
One of the attacks occurred at about 9 pm on Sunday in the Zwagal community, Jipal Dis
content:
Fresh violence has again hit Plateau State, with five persons killed in coordinated attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi Local Government Areas between Sunday night and the early hours of Monday.

One of the attacks occurred at about 9 pm on Sunday in the Zwagal community, Jipal District of Mangu LGA, where suspected terrorists killed three people. Several others were reported missing after the raid.

PUNCH Metro learnt on Monday that two more persons were killed in separate attacks in Riyom and Barkin Ladi LGAs within hours.

A resident of Zwagal, Silas Nanfwang, disclosed the attack and appealed to security agencies to track down the killers.

“It is a very sad incident. Security operatives should intensify efforts and go after those responsible for this attack to ensure they are brought to justice,” Nanfwang said.

The Berom Youth Moulders-Association, in a statement issued on Monday by its National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, gave details of the attacks in Riyom and Barkin Ladi.

According to the association, armed attackers invaded Sho village in Barkin Ladi LGA at about 5:20 pm on Sunday and killed 79-year-old Da Ishaku Pam Vwos.

Earlier, at about 1:57am on Sunday, the attackers invaded the Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, killing 42-year-old Dauda John Davou.

“The Jol community was attacked around 12:10am the same day. However, the attackers encountered resistance as alert local vigilantes responded to the threats,” the statement said.

The BYM said the weekend attacks followed earlier violence on Wednesday, when Joshua Doro Dafwel was shot in Jol and was currently receiving medical attention.

On the same day, Ina Arin was killed when he and his friend, Abok Gyang, were ambushed on their way home to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang narrowly escaped.

While commending local vigilantes for responding to the attacks, the association warned that communities should not be left to defend themselves.

“Communities should not be left to defend themselves against armed attacks without adequate and sustained support from security personnel,” the BYM said.

The association called on President Bola Tinubu, Governor Caleb Mutfwang and relevant security agencies to urgently strengthen security deployments in vulnerable communities, investigate the killings and bring the perpetrators to justice.

“We are particularly concerned that these attacks continue despite repeated security assurances and high-profile political engagements in Plateau State.

“The killing of a 79-year-old man in his community further underscores the vulnerability of innocent residents, including the elderly, who deserve protection and the right to live without fear.

The people of Plateau deserve more than promises; they deserve concrete action and the assurance that their lives and communities are protected.

“Behind every casualty is a grieving family and a traumatised community. Our people deserve to sleep peacefully, return home safely and go about their daily activities without the constant fear of being attacked or killed,” the statement noted.

The spokesperson for the Plateau State Police Command, Alabo Alfred, had yet to respond to inquiries from our correspondent about the incident as of the time of filing this report.

Meanwhile, the Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council of Plateau State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Doemak District following heightened tension after suspected gunmen burnt down seven houses in the Bong community.

The curfew, which runs from 6pm to 6am daily, was imposed on Monday evening amid reports that residents were fleeing their homes, shops had closed and commercial activities had been disrupted over fears of further attacks.

The Director of Press and Publicity to the Executive Chairman of the council, Danaan Sylvanus, announced the restriction in a public notice issued on Monday.

He said, “In view of the security tension, Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council has imposed a curfew in Doemak.

“The curfew shall be observed from 6pm to 6am. By this notice, any person found moving during this period will be treated as a security threat by the security agencies.”

The council urged residents to comply strictly with the directive and cooperate with security agencies to maintain peace in the area.

The post Five killed as fresh attacks hit three Plateau communities appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Waste Crisis: Lagos trains sanitation workers on safety
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



The Lagos State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to improving the capacity, efficiency and professionalism of sanitation workers as part of efforts to address the state’s waste management challenges and ensure a cleaner environment.



The government gave the assuranc
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to improving the capacity, efficiency and professionalism of sanitation workers as part of efforts to address the state’s waste management challenges and ensure a cleaner environment.

The government gave the assurance on Monday at a capacity-building workshop for selected sanitation workers held in Alausa, Ikeja.

The Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Omobolaji Gaji, represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Dr Hassan Sanuth, said the workshop was designed to equip participants with the knowledge, practical skills and safety measures required to improve sanitation operations.

He said the initiative was also aimed at promoting a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable Lagos.

Gaji described sanitation workers as indispensable partners in the state’s efforts to maintain a clean and liveable environment, noting that their daily responsibilities, including street sweeping, drainage clearing and waste collection, were critical to protecting public health and preventing flooding.

He commended the workers for their dedication, observing that many of them commence their duties early in the morning, long before most residents begin their daily activities.

According to him, their contributions remain essential to maintaining environmental orderliness and ensuring that Lagos remains a city residents can be proud of.

The Permanent Secretary explained that the selected workers were identified in recognition of their commitment and dedication to duty, adding that the training represented a deliberate government investment in improving their welfare, competence and productivity.

He said participants would be exposed to safer working practices, the appropriate use of personal protective equipment, modern waste-handling techniques and improved approaches to sanitation service delivery.

Gaji added that the workshop would provide an opportunity for the workers to exchange experiences, discuss challenges encountered in the field and learn from one another.

He urged participants to actively engage with facilitators, ask questions and contribute ideas that could enhance their professional capacity and performance.

“This capacity-building programme underscores the Lagos State Government’s commitment to developing a more skilled, safety-conscious and efficient sanitation workforce capable of responding effectively to the environmental challenges of a rapidly growing metropolis,” he said.

He also appreciated the facilitators, partners and stakeholders whose expertise and support contributed to the programme, urging continued collaboration to strengthen environmental sanitation and public health in the state.

Gaji said a clean and sustainable Lagos required collective responsibility, stressing that sanitation workers remained at the centre of the state’s environmental management efforts.

He assured the workers that their contributions were valued, their dignity respected and their professional development remained important to the government.

In a lecture titled, “Safety Culture: A Need to Prevent Occupational Accidents,” the guest lecturer, Mr Adeyinka Adebiyi, urged sanitation workers to prioritise workplace safety in the discharge of their daily responsibilities.

Adebiyi noted that their duties exposed them to various occupational hazards capable of causing injuries, illnesses and, in severe cases, loss of lives.

He emphasised the need for strict compliance with safety procedures, proper use of personal protective equipment, effective risk assessment and responsible handling of waste materials.

He also urged the workers to remain vigilant, avoid unsafe practices and promptly report potential hazards to prevent avoidable accidents and health complications.

The capacity-building initiative is expected to improve sanitation service delivery, promote safer working conditions and contribute to a cleaner environment across Lagos State.

The post Waste Crisis: Lagos trains sanitation workers on safety appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Eight arrested as APC, NDC supporters clash in Kano
description:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested eight suspects following a clash between supporters of the All Progressives Congress and the Nigeria Democratic Congress in the Bichi Local Government Area of the state.
The police said five people sustained injuries while 13 vehicles were vandalised during
content:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested eight suspects following a clash between supporters of the All Progressives Congress and the Nigeria Democratic Congress in the Bichi Local Government Area of the state.

The police said five people sustained injuries while 13 vehicles were vandalised during the violence, which occurred at about 4:45 pm on Sunday.

The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa.

“The clash also led to the destruction of campaign banners and billboards belonging to the political parties,” the statement said.

It said police teams were immediately deployed to the area after receiving a report of the incident, adding that their intervention restored calm.

“Items recovered from the suspects included one Gariyo, two cutlasses, two hard sticks, a bottle of solution and a substance locally known as ‘Suck and Die’,” the police said.

The five injured persons were taken to hospital, where they were receiving treatment, the statement added.

The Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, condemned the violence and destruction of campaign materials by political supporters, warning that the command would not tolerate activities capable of threatening public peace.

“I’m urging political parties and their supporters to conduct their activities peacefully and in accordance with the law,” the commissioner said.

The statement said the suspects had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, Bompai, Kano, for investigation and would be charged in court upon its conclusion.

The command urged political leaders, party supporters and residents to shun violence and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station.

It added that the area remained relatively calm, while security monitoring continued.

PUNCH Metro earlier on Monday reported that suspected thugs had attacked the convoy of former Kano State Governor Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

In a post on his verified X account on Monday, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, confirmed the incident and said several members of Kwankwaso’s entourage had sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised.

He described Kwankwaso as his brother and running mate in the 2027 presidential election under the Nigeria Democratic Congress.

“I am deeply saddened by reports of the attack on the convoy of my brother and running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and members of his entourage in the Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

“I strongly condemn this unfortunate incident. Reports indicate that several members of the entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised. This is unacceptable and must not be allowed to become part of our political culture,” Obi said.

The former Anambra State governor warned against using political differences as justification for violence, intimidation and destruction of property.

He stressed that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to participate in the democratic process without fear of attack, regardless of political affiliation.

Obi urged the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate the incident, identify those responsible, including alleged sponsors, and ensure they were brought to justice.

He also expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State leadership of the NDC and others affected by the incident, while wishing the injured a speedy recovery.

“Our commitment to building a new Nigeria remains unwavering. We believe that change must come through peaceful engagement, persuasion, ideas and the ballot, not violence.

“Nigeria belongs to all of us. We may belong to different political parties, but we remain one people with a common destiny. No political ambition is worth the life of any Nigerian,” he added.

The post Eight arrested as APC, NDC supporters clash in Kano appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Two suspected kidnappers killed in Delta shootout
description:
Two suspected kidnappers have been shot dead in a gun duel with operatives of the Delta State Police Command.
PUNCH Metro learnt that the incident followed the abduction of a 30-year-old man (name withheld) on November 12, 2026, in Edo-Ogwashi.
Operatives of the Special Anti-Kidnapping Unit, Sector
content:
Two suspected kidnappers have been shot dead in a gun duel with operatives of the Delta State Police Command.

PUNCH Metro learnt that the incident followed the abduction of a 30-year-old man (name withheld) on November 12, 2026, in Edo-Ogwashi.

Operatives of the Special Anti-Kidnapping Unit, Sector III, Ubulu-Uku, in collaboration with a human rights activist and members of the Ubulu-Uku community vigilante group, acting on intelligence, trailed the suspected kidnappers to their hideout in the Edo-Ogwashi forest on November 15, 2026, at about 7am.

The hoodlums, on sighting the security team, immediately opened fire on them.

The team, however, engaged the suspected kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. In the ensuing exchange of gunfire, two of the suspects sustained gunshot injuries, while others escaped.

The state Police Public Relations Officer for the Delta State Command, SP Bright Edafe, confirmed the incident, saying that “one locally fabricated single-barrel gun, three live cartridges and part of the ransom paid were recovered.”

The PPRO added that “the injured suspects were taken to the hospital, where they were confirmed dead by the doctor.”

According to the police spokesman, “a manhunt for the other fleeing suspects is ongoing.”

In another development, on Sunday, at about 3:30pm, operatives of the Agbor Division, while conducting a stop-and-search operation along Baleke Street, Agbor, intercepted one Lucky Rechard, aged 31.

A search of the suspect led to the recovery of one English pistol, one locally made cut-to-size gun and three live cartridges.

The PPRO confirmed that the suspect was in custody, while investigations were ongoing.

Meanwhile, the State Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Erale, commended members of the public “for volunteering credible information” and appreciated the continued collaboration of community vigilante groups, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in combating crime.

The CP reiterated the importance of community policing and urged citizens to “sustain this partnership with the police in the collective interest of peace and security across the State.”

title: Nile University of Nigeria holds 14th convocation, unveils new investments in skills, innovation
description:
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja



Nile University of Nigeria will hold its 14th Convocation from November 17 to 19, 2026, with the three-day programme featuring a Convocation Lecture on education and security, the conferment of first degrees and prizes, and the conferment of honorary degrees, postgraduate
content:
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

Nile University of Nigeria will hold its 14th Convocation from November 17 to 19, 2026, with the three-day programme featuring a Convocation Lecture on education and security, the conferment of first degrees and prizes, and the conferment of honorary degrees, postgraduate diplomas and higher degrees.

The Convocation Lecture, titled “Nexus Between Education and Security: Implications and Lessons for Sub-Saharan Africa,” will take place on Tuesday, November 17, and will be delivered by the former Chief of Army Staff, Gen. Tukur Yusuf Buratai (Rtd).

The conferment of first degrees and presentation of prizes will follow on Wednesday, November 18, while honorary degrees, postgraduate diplomas and higher degrees will be conferred on Thursday, November 19.

Speaking ahead of the convocation, Vice-Chancellor, Nile University of Nigeria, Prof. Dilli Dogo, FNAMed,, said the University was increasingly focused on ensuring that graduates leave with practical competencies that complement their academic qualifications.

“We believe education in the 21st century must go beyond certificates. The industry, public and private sectors expect more than certificates from graduates. They want skills,” the Vice-Chancellor said.

He said this approach was driving investments in technology-enabled teaching, professional development, entrepreneurship, healthcare training and infrastructure across the University.

As part of its technology-driven learning strategy, Nile University has deployed 100 AI-enabled digital interactive boards across its classrooms to support interactive teaching, research, student engagement and the use of AI tools in learning.

The University is also preparing to commission its Medical Simulation Centre, which will provide simulated clinical environments where medical students and healthcare trainees can develop practical competencies, clinical judgement and decision-making skills before working with patients in real-life settings.

Beyond the classroom, the University is expanding its entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystem. At the 2026 Collective Lab Demo Day, 30 student-led startups graduated from an initial cohort of 45 teams, providing students with opportunities to develop and test businesses alongside their academic training.

The institution has also strengthened its focus on cybersecurity through engagement with the Nigeria Police Force around cybersecurity, research and professional development, while its wider professional education ecosystem continues to connect academic training with industry needs.

Infrastructure development is another part of the expansion. Construction has commenced on a 4,500-seat multipurpose hall and convocation centre designed to host major academic events, conferences, research dissemination and wider institutional engagements.

The 14th Convocation will also feature the conferment of an honorary degree on Alhaji Mahmud Yayale Ahmed, former Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, former Secretary to the Government of the Federation and former Minister of Defence, in recognition of his distinguished public service and contribution to national institutional development.

The University’s recent healthcare milestones include the induction of 75 newly qualified medical doctors at its fifth MBBS attestation ceremony, reflecting the continued development of its health sciences training.

The Vice-Chancellor said the University’s ambition extends beyond producing graduates to contributing through skills development, research, innovation and solutions relevant to Nigeria and the wider African continent.

The 14th Convocation consequently serves not only as a celebration of the graduating class, but also as a reflection of the University’s broader direction: connecting academic knowledge with practical experience, technology, innovation and professional readiness.

title: Kano woman, three others arrested over co-wife’s son’s murder
description:
Police operatives in Kano have arrested four suspects, including a 20-year-old woman, over the alleged abduction and murder of a 14-year-old boy, Mahmoud Auwal, in Kano State.
The woman, identified as Hadiya Rukayya Auwal, was accused of hiring three men for N4.5m to kill her husband’s children, inc
content:
Police operatives in Kano have arrested four suspects, including a 20-year-old woman, over the alleged abduction and murder of a 14-year-old boy, Mahmoud Auwal, in Kano State.

The woman, identified as Hadiya Rukayya Auwal, was accused of hiring three men for N4.5m to kill her husband’s children, including the deceased.

The Force Public Relations Officer, Ani Iniedu, disclosed this in a police operational success release on Monday.

Iniedu stated that operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad, Kano, with support from the Technical Intelligence Unit, unravelled the killing.

Iniedu identified the three other suspects as Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20; Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27; and Auwal Muhammad, 26.

He noted that the suspects allegedly lured and abducted the teenager before killing him, adding that the victim’s corpse was recovered and identified by his parents.

The FPRO wrote, “In a major investigative breakthrough, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad Kano, assisted by the Technical Intelligence Unit, successfully unravelled the abduction and murder of 14-year-old Mahmoud Auwal.

“Three suspects, Muhammad Musa Isma’il (20), Abubakar Muhammad Isah (27), and Auwal Muhammad (26), were arrested and confessed to luring the victim and snatching him.

“The mastermind, Hadiya Rukayya Auwal (20), a co-wife to the victim’s mother, was identified for hiring the syndicate for N4,500,000 to eliminate her husband’s children. The victim’s corpse was recovered and positively identified by his parents.

The police spokesperson concluded that the case had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, Bompai, Kano, for further investigation.

In a separate operation, Iniedu noted that the Kano operatives arrested three men and recovered a Hyundai Elantra, valued at N14m, which had allegedly been stolen in Kano State.

He added that the operation followed a complaint lodged on November 12 by one Stephanie Patrick Ogedoh over the theft of her light-blue Hyundai Elantra.

The FPRO identified the suspects as Mansur Khalil, 32; Nuhu Garba, 45; and Hussaini Aminu, 55, saying operatives of the Special Intervention Squad intercepted them along Zaria Road, near Kwanar Dangora, in the Kiru Local Government Area.

He noted that the vehicle was recovered and the suspects allegedly confessed to the crime.

He added that the suspects implicated a receiver of the stolen vehicle, while efforts were ongoing to arrest the fleeing suspect and recover more exhibits.

Iniedu concluded that the case was under investigation by the State Criminal Investigation Department, Bompai.

The post Kano woman, three others arrested over co-wife’s son’s murder appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UNIBEN student collapses, dies playing football
description:
The University of Benin has been thrown into mourning following the death of a 100-level Engineering student, identified as Omorodion Japheth, who reportedly collapsed while playing football at the university’s Sports Complex.
Japheth was said to have slumped during a football match on Friday, Novem
content:
The University of Benin has been thrown into mourning following the death of a 100-level Engineering student, identified as Omorodion Japheth, who reportedly collapsed while playing football at the university’s Sports Complex.

Japheth was said to have slumped during a football match on Friday, November 13, 2026, prompting efforts by fellow students and others at the facility to revive him.

According to an eyewitness, who pleaded anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the incident, first aid was administered before the deceased was rushed to the university’s health centre, where he was subsequently confirmed dead.

The eyewitness said heatstroke, resulting from intense heat and physical exertion, might have caused the deceased’s death.

The source said, “Japheth collapsed while playing football, and I think it was due to the intense heat. The other players tried to revive him, but he was pronounced dead when he was taken to the school’s medical centre.”

While the exact circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear, no official medical confirmation of the cause of death had been made public as of the time of filing this report.

In honour of the deceased, the Nigerian Universities Engineering Students’ Association, UNIBEN Chapter, has announced plans to organise a candlelight procession in his memory.

The procession is scheduled for Monday at 6pm at the Engineering Car Park. Members of the university community attending the event have been encouraged to wear black in tribute to the deceased.

Japheth’s death has thrown his family, friends, fellow students and the university community into mourning.

title: LASG spends N120.8bn on ‘professional fees’
description:
The Lagos State Government recorded N120.8bn in expenditure on a single budget item classified as “Professional Fees Expenses” between January and September 2026, with more than N56.5bn incurred in the third quarter.
According to the state’s third-quarter budget performance report, released by the M
content:
The Lagos State Government recorded N120.8bn in expenditure on a single budget item classified as “Professional Fees Expenses” between January and September 2026, with more than N56.5bn incurred in the third quarter.

According to the state’s third-quarter budget performance report, released by the Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget and obtained and reviewed by The PUNCH, “Professional Fees Expenses” is listed as a distinct expenditure item with an annual allocation of N227.3bn.

The report’s cumulative expenditure of approximately N120.8bn represents about 53.1 per cent of the allocation, accounting for almost a quarter of the state’s total overhead spending of N498.9bn during the nine-month period.

The scale of this spending is more than 15 times the reported primary healthcare expenditure and over 11 times the basic education figure. Primary healthcare expenditure was approximately N7.8bn against an annual allocation of N19.2bn, while basic education recorded expenditure of about N10.5bn against a budget of N14.1bn.

The Lagos State Government’s third-quarter budget performance report does not provide a breakdown of the N120.8bn by recipient, assignment, contract, procurement process, or approving authority, leaving the specific services covered by the expenditure unclear and raising concerns about transparency and accountability.

The figures reveal a sharp acceleration in the third quarter, when expenditure on professional fees rose to N56.5bn from N32.2bn in the preceding quarter, an increase of approximately 75.5 per cent based on the reported figures.

The third-quarter figure represents nearly half of the total professional fees expenditure for the first nine months of 2026. The increase came at a time of heightened political activity ahead of the next electoral cycle, raising questions about the nature and timing of the expenditure, particularly as overall overhead spending declined during the same period.

According to the documents reviewed, Lagos recorded overhead expenditure of approximately N191bn in the second quarter, compared with N173.4bn in the third quarter, representing a decline of about 9.2 per cent.

The disparity becomes more pronounced when the professional fees item is excluded. Overhead expenditure on all other items fell from approximately N158.8bn in the second quarter to N116.9bn in the third quarter, a decline of about 26.4 per cent.

The figures show that the professional fees item moved sharply against the broader spending trend, accounting for a substantially larger proportion of the state’s recurrent expenditure in the third quarter.

The scale of the expenditure, its sharp quarterly increase and the absence of a corresponding breakdown raise questions about the nature of the services procured, the agencies responsible for the commitments, and the approval and accountability mechanisms governing the expenditure.

The PUNCH made repeated attempts over several days to obtain clarification from the relevant government offices on the expenditure, its beneficiaries and the circumstances surrounding the sharp increase in the third quarter.

After reviewing the newspaper’s enquiry, the Public Affairs Officer at the Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget, Busola Fatinukun-Aroloye, directed The PUNCH to the Office of the Accountant-General at the State Treasury Office, suggesting that the office was better placed to provide the requested information.

“Please reach out to the Accountant-General at the State Treasury Office (STO) or get in touch with their PAO,” Fatinukun-Aroloye said on Monday morning.

However, when contacted, the Public Affairs Officer at the Office of the Accountant-General, Olawunmi Ajala, redirected the newspaper to the Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget, saying the office was not in a position to respond to the questions.

“We are not in a position to respond. Please, you need to reach out to them at the Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget for responses to your questions. They are in charge,” Ajala said.

The exchange left The PUNCH without a substantive response from either office on the specific engagements covered by the N120.8bn expenditure, the identities of the recipients or the approvals authorising the spending.

Additional requests for comments sent to the Governor’s Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Gboyega Akosile, also remained unanswered as of the time this report was filed.

The N120.8bn expenditure represents almost one in every four naira recorded as overhead spending by the Babajide Sanwo-Olu administration in the first nine months of 2026, although the report does not provide details of the recipients or establish the specific beneficiaries of the payments.

The amount is also substantially higher than spending on any other individual overhead category identified in the report. The next largest item was “Welfare Package and Special Services to the Public”, which recorded expenditure of approximately N44.1bn.

This means the professional fees expenditure was about 2.7 times the amount recorded for providing welfare packages and special services to the public.

“The government cannot establish the legitimacy of this expenditure merely by pointing to its inclusion in the approved budget. Budgetary approval is only one part of public financial accountability.

“Lagos should publish a detailed breakdown showing which ministries and agencies incurred the expenditure, the consultants and firms engaged, the procurement processes followed, the approving authorities and the specific deliverables for which payments were made,” Senior Researcher at Good Governance Africa, Kabir Adejumo, told The PUNCH.

“The most significant governance concern is not simply that Lagos State spent such billions of naira on professional fees, but that such a substantial amount of public money is recorded under a broad expenditure heading without sufficient information about the services procured, the beneficiaries, the contracts involved and the outcomes delivered,” he added.

A further examination of the state’s consulting and professional services classification reveals the extent to which expenditure is concentrated in the broadly named professional fees category. The report records approximately N162.8bn under consulting and professional services during the period. Of this amount, the generic professional fees item accounted for approximately N120.8bn, representing about 74 per cent of the total.

All the other consulting and professional services categories combined accounted for approximately N42bn. The disparity is particularly pronounced when the professional fees expenditure is compared with four identifiable professional service categories.

The state recorded approximately N1.2bn for legal services, N2.3bn for engineering consultancy, N2bn for architectural services and N1.4bn for financial consulting. Together, these four categories amounted to about N6.9bn. The expenditure on the generic professional fees item was therefore approximately 17.5 times the combined amount recorded for the four categories.

Other consulting and professional services categories collectively recorded expenditure of approximately N20.4bn in the second quarter, compared with about N12.4bn in the third quarter, representing a decline of roughly 39 per cent. Within that period, management consultancy fees fell from approximately N8bn to N2bn. Professional fees, by contrast, increased by about N24.3bn.

Beyond the size of the allocation, the absence of a transaction-level breakdown weakens public scrutiny of how the money was committed and what value the state received in return, raising concerns about accountability.

For a state with extensive responsibilities in healthcare, education, transport, infrastructure and social protection, the accountability standard for an expenditure of this magnitude cannot end with its appearance in a budget performance table.

“The issue is about the public’s right to know how its money is being spent. A government that seeks public trust must make its expenditure traceable, verifiable and open to independent scrutiny. Transparency should not depend on investigative reporting uncovering unusual spending patterns; it should be built into the way public finances are managed and reported,” Adejumo said.

The post LASG spends N120.8bn on ‘professional fees’ appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Court joins Gwarzo as defendant in Kano NDC ticket suit
description:
The Federal High Court in Kano has joined the governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Aminu Gwarzo, as a defendant in a suit seeking to stop the party from fielding a candidate in the state.
Justice Simon Amobeda granted the application on Monday following a request by Gwarzo’s co
content:
The Federal High Court in Kano has joined the governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Aminu Gwarzo, as a defendant in a suit seeking to stop the party from fielding a candidate in the state.

Justice Simon Amobeda granted the application on Monday following a request by Gwarzo’s counsel, Sagir Gezawa (SAN), seeking to join him as a necessary party to the suit.

The suit was instituted by three NDC members in Kano, who are seeking an order restraining the party from submitting the name of its governorship candidate to the Independent National Electoral Commission.

The plaintiffs, Garba Umar Isa, Yau Abubakar and another party member, are also asking the court to restrain INEC from publishing Gwarzo’s name as the NDC governorship candidate, citing the Supreme Court judgment in the Zenith Labour Party case.

Gwarzo secured the NDC governorship ticket and is contesting the election with Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate.

However, INEC excluded the duo from its published list of governorship candidates for Kano State, citing a court order.

At Monday’s proceedings, counsel for the plaintiffs, Moses Falana, initially opposed the joinder application filed by Gezawa but later withdrew his counter-affidavit.

“My Lord, having reviewed the application, we are no longer opposing the joinder of the governorship candidate as a necessary party,” Falana told the court.

Counsel for INEC, Hassan Aminu, and the NDC, Dahiru Ibrahim, did not oppose the application.

In his ruling, Justice Amobeda granted the application and formally joined Gwarzo as the third defendant in the suit.

“The application for joinder is hereby granted. The applicant is joined as the third defendant in this suit,” the judge ruled.

Justice Amobeda directed all parties to file their processes reflecting Gwarzo’s inclusion in the case and adjourned the matter until September 23 for hearing of the pending preliminary applications.

title: 2027: Ogun PDP optimistic, chieftain commends judiciary
description:
The Peoples Democratic Party in Ogun State has expressed confidence in its chances in the 2027 governorship election, with its campaign spokesperson, Wale Adedayo, predicting that the party’s candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, will win between 18 and 19 of the state’s 20 local government areas.
Similarly
content:
The Peoples Democratic Party in Ogun State has expressed confidence in its chances in the 2027 governorship election, with its campaign spokesperson, Wale Adedayo, predicting that the party’s candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, will win between 18 and 19 of the state’s 20 local government areas.

Similarly, a party chieftain in the state, Alhaji Fasiu Bakene, commended the Federal High Court judgment directing the Independent National Electoral Commission to restore Adebutu’s candidacy, describing it as a boost to confidence in the judiciary and an opportunity for the PDP to participate in the 2027 election.

The Federal High Court in Abuja had, on Friday, ordered INEC to restore Adebutu’s name as the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, paving the way for his participation in the 2027 election.

Speaking during an appearance on Arise Television, monitored on Sunday, Adedayo dismissed the influence of federal might in the election, insisting that it would not prevent the PDP from securing victory.

He said the APC’s federal might would be defeated hands down in Ogun, the same way it happened in Osun State.

“The federal might was there in 2023, it didn’t work. The federal might was there in Osun State, and it didn’t work, and it won’t work again this time,” he declared.

According to Adedayo, the party had the support of voters across the state, including some people currently associated with the All Progressives Congress.

He said that “The PDP actually won in 2023, but the poll was manipulated. The PDP will clear between 18 and 19 local government areas in Ogun. I can assure you of that. Adebutu will win Ogun East, Adebutu will win the six LGAs of Ogun Central and a minimum of two in Ogun West.

“It is not the noise that makes things happen. When it comes to the real show, those who are following them know the party they will vote for.”

He added that the hardship across the country had been rejected by all, saying most of those being paid to attend APC campaigns would eventually cast their ballots for Adebutu.

Adedayo equally hailed the Judiciary for allowing democracy to thrive by returning Adebutu to INEC’s list of candidates.

He said the APC was jittery and already realising the landslide defeat it would suffer in the poll next year, which was why the party was plotting to edge out Adebutu in the contest.

Faulting Adebutu’s initial removal from the list, he said, “You can’t mention PDP in Ogun without talking about Ladi Adebutu. The electoral umpire made itself a laughing stock by coming out to say his name was not on the list. INEC brought a hard copy to court while the list of names submitted was in soft copy.

“The PDP submitted the register and not INEC. It is the party that can prove who is a member and who is not a member. It is not INEC.

“The judgment of the court was very sound. INEC should have written to the party that submitted the list rather than removing his name from the list.

“INEC monitored the primary that the same Ladi Adebutu won, and INEC updated Adebutu’s name as the winner of the primary.”

He said the removal of Adebutu’s name did not stop the campaign activities of the party, as Adebutu and his running mate, Hajia Lateefat Sowunmi-Kolapo, continued to tour villages and towns, canvassing for votes and selling their manifesto.

“Those who orchestrated the thing wanted to demoralise members, but Ladi Adebutu continued with his campaign, and that is how he has been going round all villages and towns in Ogun State, meeting with the people.

“It didn’t stop our programme; we have been moving around. Seeing the leaders coming out to campaign boosted the morale of PDP members and supporters. There won’t be any battle in Ogun State,” he said.

Adedayo said the people were craving for grassroots development, which Adebutu had promised, including local government autonomy.

“Ogun State is on a true path for real development because all our health centres must work. The farm settlement must be revived by all means; their output in terms of food production must increase, and there will be potable water in all villages.

“This will be easily achieved through the local government autonomy. Once the local government and councillors do their work, the people won’t have any problem,” he said.

On the ancestry issue raised against the APC candidate, Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, Adedayo said the people of the state were still expecting the APC candidate to clear himself and tell them his real identity and origin.

In a separate statement, Alahaji Bakene commended the Federal High Court judgment, describing it as a development that had restored confidence in the judiciary.

Bakene, therefore, urged the INEC to uphold the rule of law and ensure fairness in its preparations and conduct of the 2027 elections.

“We thank God for the landmark judgment, and we use this occasion to appreciate all citizens of Ogun State and lovers of true democracy who showed concern in the matter before the judgment,” he said.

He added that the restoration of Adebutu’s name had renewed confidence in the judiciary, which he described as a source of hope for ordinary citizens.

He also urged the APC-led government in Ogun State to allow opposition parties to campaign freely without intimidation, attacks or denial of access to public facilities.

Bakene said residents should be allowed to exercise their democratic rights and vote for candidates of their choice.

The post 2027: Ogun PDP optimistic, chieftain commends judiciary appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: A’Ibom gov seeks 80,000 LG votes for Tinubu, APC
description:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has tasked voters in Mkpat Enin Local Government Area with delivering 80,000 votes for President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress candidates in the 2027 general elections.
Eno, who is seeking re-election on the APC platform, made the demand on Monday
content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has tasked voters in Mkpat Enin Local Government Area with delivering 80,000 votes for President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress candidates in the 2027 general elections.

Eno, who is seeking re-election on the APC platform, made the demand on Monday at the kick-off of the party’s campaign tour of the local government, where he urged residents to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and mobilise support for the party.

The governor’s vote target came alongside promises of fresh development projects, including the reconstruction of the abandoned Ikot Akata Technical College and Ukam Market, for which he said he had directed the constitution of an emergency implementation committee.

According to a statement issued by the Akwa Ibom APC Campaign Council’s Media Directorate on Monday, Eno said his administration had undertaken several infrastructure and empowerment projects in Mkpat Enin and would consolidate the interventions if returned to office.

He listed about 94 kilometres of roads, bridges, a model primary school at Ikot Ebak, a model primary healthcare centre at Ikot Ekpe, renovated and newly constructed classroom blocks, and a solar-powered water facility at Ukpom Minya among projects executed in the area.

The governor also cited the ARISE Youth Friendly Centre, which is nearing completion, 13 ARISE Compassionate Homes and empowerment programmes for farmers, traders and small business owners.

He said beneficiaries of the administration’s empowerment schemes included recipients of ₦5m grants, while 210 residents had benefited from the mega empowerment programme. Two minibuses and a car had also been distributed.

Eno further announced plans to distribute 50 bags of rice to every village in the local government for Christmas, amounting to more than 5,000 bags.

He urged residents to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the National Assembly elections scheduled for January 16 and the governorship and state House of Assembly elections on February 6.

The Deputy Governor, Akon Eyakenyi, described the state as united under Eno and urged the people to sustain their engagement with the administration.

The Coordinator of the Office of the First Lady, Helen Obareki, said the governor had fulfilled commitments to his late wife’s community.

Also, the wife of the Senate President, Ekaette-Unoama Akpabio, who represented her husband, Godswill Akpabio, urged voters to identify with the APC during the elections.

The Director-General of the campaign council, Assam Assam, said Mkpat Enin had an estimated 80,000 registered voters and called on them to support APC candidates at all levels.

The rally marked the beginning of the APC campaign council’s tour of the state’s 31 local government areas.

title: NDC loses Bauchi gov candidate, Kano executives to APC
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress governorship candidate in Bauchi State, Ibrahim Kashim, has dumped the party for the All Progressives Congress, ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Also, the vice-chairman of the NDC in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State, Haladu Sa’adu, and five ward chairmen
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress governorship candidate in Bauchi State, Ibrahim Kashim, has dumped the party for the All Progressives Congress, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Also, the vice-chairman of the NDC in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State, Haladu Sa’adu, and five ward chairmen have defected to the APC.

The defections are coming also three months to the February 6, 2027 governorship election, with the list of candidates, including that of Kashim, already released by the Independent National Electoral Commission.

Kashim, a former Secretary to the State Government, announced his defection on Monday at a ceremony held at the Explaining his decision, the ex-SSG said he joined the APC because it offered Bauchi a stronger opportunity to participate in national governance and attract development.

He described the APC as the governing party at the federal level, with an overwhelming presence across Northern Nigeria, as well as the political structure and institutional capacity to advance the state’s interests.

Kashim said, “The APC is currently the governing party at the federal level and has an overwhelming presence across Northern Nigeria.

“It is also the party with the political structure, national reach and institutional capacity to provide a viable platform for the political and developmental aspirations we seek for Bauchi.

“I believe that Bauchi must be strategically positioned within this political reality.

“We cannot afford to gamble with the future of our state by placing our developmental aspirations on a platform that lacks comparable national reach and institutional influence.

“Our decision must be guided by the interests of Bauchi, not sentiment, political nostalgia or the convenience of individuals.”

The former SSG added, “The question is not simply which party can put forward a candidate. The question is which party has the organisational strength, national reach, political influence and institutional capacity to advance Bauchi’s interests. I am convinced that the APC offers the stronger platform.”

Kashim said his decision to leave the NDC followed his resignation from the party on October 16, 2026, adding that his commitment to the political struggle for a better Bauchi remained unchanged.

He appealed to his supporters, political associates and other stakeholders to join him in the APC, insisting that his political ambition was driven by the desire to improve governance and development in the state.

“Our ultimate objective is not the triumph of one political party over another. It is the triumph of good governance over poor governance, development over stagnation, opportunity over deprivation and hope over despair.

“I have chosen strategic engagement over political isolation. I have chosen a broader national platform over limited political reach.

“Above all, I have chosen what I sincerely believe offers Bauchi State a better opportunity for development and prosperity,” he said.

In Kano, the NDC vice-chairman in Bichi Local Government Area, Sa’adu, and five ward chairmen, including the party’s treasurer, Mannir Umar, ward secretaries, women and youth leaders and other members of the Kwankwasiyya movement, announced their decision to dump the party on Monday during a visit to the member representing Bichi Federal Constituency, Kabir Abubakar, at his office in Kano.

The PUNCH gathered that the five ward chairmen are from Waire, Danzabuwa, Kaukau, Muntsira and Bichi wards of the local government area.

Speaking on behalf of the defectors, the Danzabuwa Ward Chairman, Abdulkadir Lawan, said the lawmaker’s developmental projects and commitment to the people influenced their decision to join the APC.

“I want to inform you that we are all from Bichi, and we have decided to announce our defection from the NDC to the APC because we have recognised your dedication and the developmental projects you have executed in the Bichi Local Government,” Abdulkadir said.

He also commended the lawmaker for providing educational opportunities, saying he benefited from a scholarship programme facilitated by the Abubakar Kabir Foundation.

“I was previously a member of the opposition, but I benefited from your scholarship programme, which enabled me to pursue my master’s degree.

“Through your foundation, the Abubakar Kabir Foundation, I am now pursuing my PhD without any form of harassment or intimidation,” he said.

Abdulkadir also cited what he described as a lack of proper coordination and respect for members by the NDC leadership in Kano State, including issues surrounding the party’s leadership under Rabiu Kwankwaso, as reasons for their defection.

Speaking while receiving the defectors, the lawmaker welcomed them into the APC.

“I heartily welcome you all into the All Progressives Congress. Your decision to join us will further strengthen our grassroots structure in Bichi and the entire federal constituency,” he said.

He highlighted some of his interventions in Danzabuwa Ward, including the construction of a primary school, ongoing road projects and the provision of boreholes.

“We have continued to deliver projects that directly touch the lives of our people, and we will not relent. I urge you to work hard towards strengthening party unity and grassroots mobilisation ahead of the forthcoming elections,” Abubakar stated.

He also called for support for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Abba Yusuf and other APC candidates in the next elections.

“I urge all of you to continue to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and all our candidates. Together, we will consolidate the gains of this administration,” he added.

The event was attended by the APC member representing Bichi Constituency in the Kano State House of Assembly, Lawan Bichi; the Director-General of the campaign council, Sani Bichi; the Vice-Chairman of Bichi Local Government, Babangida Danzabuwa; the APC State Secretary, Yusuf Sabo; and the Special Adviser on Publicity, Ahmad Aruwa, among other party leaders.

title: A’Court vows sanctions for corrupt election tribunal
description:
The President of the Court of Appeal, Monica Dongban-Mensem, has warned secretaries and registry staff of election petition tribunals against accepting bribes or compromising judicial processes ahead of the 2027 general elections.
She warned that any staff found engaging in corrupt practices would b
content:
The President of the Court of Appeal, Monica Dongban-Mensem, has warned secretaries and registry staff of election petition tribunals against accepting bribes or compromising judicial processes ahead of the 2027 general elections.

She warned that any staff found engaging in corrupt practices would be sanctioned, stressing that the assignment was a call to national service and not an opportunity for personal enrichment.

Dongban-Mensem gave the warning on Monday at the opening of a two-day capacity-building workshop on the theme: “Modern Registry Practices for Effective Election Petition Tribunal Administration”, in Abuja.

The PCA said the exercise was designed to prepare tribunal staff for the administrative demands of handling electoral disputes, particularly as the presidential and National Assembly elections approach on January 16, 2027.

She described the registry as the engine room of every tribunal, noting that its efficiency, integrity and transparency were critical to the timely administration of electoral justice.

According to her, the responsibilities of registry staff include receiving and filing petitions, serving processes on parties, issuing hearing notices, preparing records of proceedings and orders, preserving tribunal documents and compiling records.

She said the performance of the registry directly affected the efficiency of tribunals and public confidence in the judicial process.

Citing Sections 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, Dongban-Mensem said the PCA was empowered to constitute election petition tribunals in every state of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory.

She also cited Section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act 2026, which provides that the tribunals must be constituted not later than 30 days before an election and open their registries for business not later than seven days before the poll.

The PCA stressed the need for confidentiality, professionalism and strict adherence to the timelines governing election petitions.

Dongban-Mensem charged the tribunal secretaries to familiarise themselves with the Electoral Act 2026 and the Election Petition Tribunal Proceedings Practice Direction 2026, warning that ignorance of the relevant provisions could expose them to manipulation and costly administrative errors.

“As tribunal secretaries, as prescribed by the Electoral Act 2026 and the Election Petition Tribunal Proceedings Practice Direction 2026, you must know the Practice Directions and have them at your fingertips. If you do not know them, you will be intimidated, you will be misled, and you will permit serious errors, and that will fetch serious consequences,” she said.

“There is no room for that now. You have been given a good chance to equip yourselves now, and we are giving you materials, so there will be no excuses. And we shall be constantly monitoring every aspect of your conduct,” she added.

Addressing the issue of integrity among tribunal staff, the PCA warned against allowing financial inducements to influence their conduct, saying their activities would be subjected to intense public scrutiny.

“Let me be clear that you must discharge your duties with utmost good faith and not be swayed by pecuniary inducements. Your conduct, and indeed that of the tribunal, will be under intense public scrutiny.

“You must not allow yourselves to be used as instruments to truncate the judicial process. You must live above board and protect the reputation of the judiciary,” she said.

Describing the assignment as an opportunity to serve the country, she said the court would not hesitate to sanction erring officials.

“This assignment is not an opportunity for self-enrichment, but a call to national service, which is also an opportunity to build a good name. It is said that a good name is better than silver and gold. We will not hesitate to sanction any staff found wanting,” she added.

She further urged the secretaries to ensure prompt service of processes and maintain regular communication with the Election Petition Tribunal Unit at the Court of Appeal headquarters.

She said the presiding justice of each tribunal was the immediate supervisor of its administrative staff and should be approached whenever they encountered difficulties.

The PCA described the participants’ selection as a demonstration of the confidence reposed in them by the court, urging them not to betray the trust.

Also speaking, the Chief Registrar of the Court of Appeal, Umar Bangari, said the integrity of Nigeria’s democratic process depended on the efficient, transparent and timely resolution of electoral disputes.

He recalled that the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, inaugurated 375 judicial officers from different jurisdictions across the country last week to serve on election petition tribunals ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He described Monday’s workshop as an administrative continuation of the training, designed to equip tribunal staff with the technical knowledge required for the assignment.

The Chief Registrar said the presidential and National Assembly elections would be held on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections were scheduled for February 6, 2027.

He warned that the success of the tribunals rested significantly on registry staff, who were responsible for managing court processes, statutory timelines and administrative communication between the bench and litigants.

He identified integrity, timeliness, communication and professionalism as the key pillars of their assignment.

On corruption, the Chief Registrar warned that the court would not tolerate misconduct, compromise or dereliction of duty, noting that election petitions were high-stakes matters that could expose staff to financial inducements.

“Election petitions are high-stakes matters, and you will, inevitably, face pressure and temptations. I urge you to live strictly above board.

“Remember that your personal integrity, and of course, your career, and the institutional reputation of the court, as well as the Nigerian judiciary in general, are permanently in the public searchlight.

“Let me therefore reiterate the stern warning of the Honourable President that the court will show zero tolerance for any form of corruption, misconduct, compromise or dereliction of duty on your part, and advise that you take this warning very seriously,” he said.

The Chief Registrar further warned that the court would sanction staff found colluding with parties or lawyers, manipulating court processes, altering records for personal or political advantage, or leaking confidential internal communications.

However, he said the court had also resolved to reward secretaries and registry officials who demonstrated “outstanding commitment and diligence in the exercise of this assignment.”

He urged the participants to take advantage of the two-day workshop, which would cover the Electoral Act, the Judicial Electoral Manual, the 2026 Electoral Case Management System, record-keeping and compliance with filing and service deadlines.

Earlier, the acting Deputy Chief Registrar of the Election Petition Tribunal, Maitumbi Altine, disclosed that 655 staff and chief registrars were attending the workshop.

She said 223 of the participants had previously served in election petition tribunals, while 432 were first-timers.

Altine also disclosed that the Court of Appeal was working to update its Case Management System to “forestall the incidence of conflicting judgments which the tribunals had experienced in times past.”

She added that the court would upload judgments delivered by election petition tribunals since 1999 into the system to serve as judicial precedents on legal issues that might arise during the proceedings.

The Acting Deputy Chief Registrar also warned participants against granting interviews without express authorisation, cautioning them against any activity capable of undermining the neutrality of the tribunals and the Court of Appeal.

The post A’Court vows sanctions for corrupt election tribunal appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG pushes regional deal to prevent internet disruptions
description:
The Federal Government is seeking a regional agreement among West African countries to protect submarine telecommunications cables, coordinate repairs, and prevent prolonged internet disruptions that could affect businesses and digital services.
The proposed agreement would establish common procedur
content:
The Federal Government is seeking a regional agreement among West African countries to protect submarine telecommunications cables, coordinate repairs, and prevent prolonged internet disruptions that could affect businesses and digital services.

The proposed agreement would establish common procedures for rerouting internet traffic during cable failures, strengthen cross-border telecommunications infrastructure and reduce dependence on limited international connectivity routes.

The Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Bosun Tijani, advanced the proposal during engagements with member states of the International Telecommunication Union at its 2026 Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, Qatar.

According to a statement issued by the ministry on Monday, Tijani “advocated for a shared regional protocol for digital infrastructure resilience, including mechanisms for rerouting network traffic and coordinating repairs when subsea cables fail.”

The ministry said the initiative formed part of Nigeria’s efforts to strengthen regional digital infrastructure and improve the reliability and affordability of internet services across West Africa.

It disclosed that Nigeria was collaborating with Chad, Burkina Faso and the Republic of Benin to improve cross-border connectivity, with plans to extend the cooperation to Cameroon.

Nigeria is also working with Togo on plans to establish a regional data park to expand access to computing capacity for researchers and businesses across West Africa.

The ministry said the initiatives would strengthen regional economic integration and reduce vulnerabilities arising from dependence on limited international telecommunications infrastructure.

It noted that submarine cables carry more than 99 per cent of international data traffic, making their protection essential to the functioning of the global digital economy.

Nigeria’s involvement in submarine cable protection gained prominence in 2024 when Tijani was appointed Co-Chair of the ITU International Advisory Body for Submarine Cable Resilience, established in partnership with the International Cable Protection Committee.

The country subsequently hosted the International Submarine Cable Resilience Summit in Abuja in February 2025, bringing together government officials, industry leaders and technical experts to address vulnerabilities affecting critical subsea infrastructure.

The advisory body’s work culminated in the adoption of recommendations in July 2026, following further international engagements, including a summit in Porto, Portugal.

The recommendations addressed cable protection, risk mitigation, infrastructure redundancy, timely deployment and repairs, and diversification of submarine cable routes.

Meanwhile, the ministry announced that Nigeria had secured re-election to the ITU Council for the 2027–2030 term.

Nigeria emerged among 13 African countries elected to the 48-member council, extending its participation in international telecommunications governance, which dates back to 1973.

The statement read, “The Federal Republic of Nigeria has secured re-election to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union for the 2027–2030 term, reaffirming the country’s growing influence in global telecommunications governance and its commitment to advancing inclusive digital development.

“The re-election was secured at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26), holding in Doha, Qatar, where Nigeria emerged among the 13 African countries elected to serve on the 48-member Council.

“The victory represents another important milestone in Nigeria’s longstanding engagement with the ITU and strengthens its voice in shaping international policies and decisions that will influence the future of global connectivity and digital development.”

Reacting to the development, Tijani said, “Nigeria’s re-election to the ITU Council is a strong affirmation of the confidence the international community has in our country’s leadership and contribution to the global digital agenda.”

He added, “Under the visionary leadership of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, we are positioning Nigeria to play an increasingly influential role in shaping the policies, partnerships and innovations that will define the future of telecommunications.”

“We will use this renewed mandate to advance meaningful connectivity, strengthen Africa’s voice and ensure that emerging technologies create opportunities for our people.”

The minister was elected Vice-Chair of the ITU Council in June 2025 and subsequently chaired its 2026 session in Geneva. During his chairmanship, the council considered emerging technologies, stakeholder engagement, sustainable funding arrangements and institutional reforms.

It also endorsed a revised draft strategic plan for consideration at the Doha conference and approved the union’s operational plan for 2027. Beyond telecommunications infrastructure, the ministry highlighted Nigeria’s participation in international efforts to strengthen child online protection.

It disclosed that Stella Chubiyo Erebor served as the African regional Vice-Chair of the ITU Council Working Group on Child Online Protection, contributing to discussions on online safety policies and regulatory practices.

The ministry linked these efforts to domestic initiatives, including the Nigerian Communications Commission’s establishment of a multi-stakeholder technical working group and the development of the Nigerian Child Online Protection Policy in 2014.

Tijani also called for inclusive access to artificial intelligence, arguing that people across different countries and communities should be able to develop technologies that reflect their languages and address local challenges.

The ministry credited the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, led by Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, and Nigerian diplomatic representatives in Qatar and Geneva with supporting the country’s re-election campaign.

Other participating institutions included the Nigerian Communications Commission, Nigerian Communications Satellite Limited, National Space Research and Development Agency, Defence Space Administration and National Emergency Management Agency.

The Federal Government said Nigeria would use its renewed ITU mandate to strengthen international cooperation on affordable connectivity, cybersecurity, digital skills, technology transfer and responsible innovation.

The post FG pushes regional deal to prevent internet disruptions appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ’Public sector reforms need citizens’ trust’
description:
A former permanent secretary and Nigerian businesswoman, Dr Dere Awosika, has said public sector reforms must reflect the needs and realities of citizens to achieve their intended objectives.
Awosika said governments should consult affected communities and public servants before implementing reforms
content:
A former permanent secretary and Nigerian businesswoman, Dr Dere Awosika, has said public sector reforms must reflect the needs and realities of citizens to achieve their intended objectives.

Awosika said governments should consult affected communities and public servants before implementing reforms rather than impose policies without understanding the challenges they face.

She spoke recently on the Aig-Imoukhuede Foundation podcast, Reform Is Not a Guessing Game.

According to her, consultation would help reformers identify institutional weaknesses, understand stakeholders’ interests and develop implementation strategies suited to local realities.

“Reforms are not supposed to be a pass down of instructions. It’s supposed to be a discussion on the weaknesses, identify them, and see that the goals that you set to meet are not being met,” she said.

The Chief Executive Officer of Josephine Consulting Ltd said her experience leading polio eradication efforts in Nigeria demonstrated the importance of engaging communities in public programmes.

She explained that working with traditional and religious leaders helped address concerns and build acceptance of vaccination. “We need to build trust with the citizenry. They cannot believe us unless we trust them,” she said.

Also speaking, an economist and policy strategist, Dr Akin Olusoji-Akinyele, said governments must obtain feedback from beneficiaries throughout the reform process to determine whether policies were meeting their needs.

“The reform itself is not complete until the beneficiary has given you some form of feedback as to whether this is working,” he said.

The discussion was moderated by Ofovwe Aig-Imoukhuede, Executive Vice Chair of the Foundation, ahead of the launch of its Public Sector Reform Playbook in Abuja on November 19.
