title: 28 shops razed in Abuja market fire
description:
About 45 traders have been affected by a fire outbreak at the Gwagwalada International Market in the Federal Capital Territory, with 28 open stalls and two lock-up shops damaged.
The FCT Emergency Management Department disclosed this in a statement on Monday, following a post-incident assessment con
content:
About 45 traders have been affected by a fire outbreak at the Gwagwalada International Market in the Federal Capital Territory, with 28 open stalls and two lock-up shops damaged.

The FCT Emergency Management Department disclosed this in a statement on Monday, following a post-incident assessment conducted by its Director, Muhammad Dikko, alongside officials of the National Emergency Management Agency.

The fire occurred last Saturday, with an eyewitness video showing flames engulfing parts of the market at about 7pm. The footage, shared on Facebook, showed the fire still burning as the eyewitness called on emergency responders to intervene.

PUNCH had reported on Sunday that the fire ravaged the market, with the cause yet to be established at the time.

However, during the post-incident assessment, the Chairman of the Market Association, Aminu Lawal Bakinruwa, told the delegation that security personnel on duty noticed smoke coming from one of the shops about 20 minutes after electricity supply was restored to the market by the Abuja Electricity Distribution Company.

Some of the affected traders expressed distress over their losses, describing the incident as a major setback to their businesses and livelihoods.

One of the victims, Salome Israel, said, “She lost goods worth about N400,000, including yams, tomatoes and peppers,” the statement said.

Other items destroyed in the fire included clothing, herbal medicines and beverages.

Addressing the traders, Dikko “urged market operators to prioritise fire safety by ensuring that all electrical appliances were switched off before leaving their shops”, the statement said.

He also stressed the importance of insurance coverage for businesses, noting that traders with insurance policies would be better positioned to recover from losses arising from disasters.

The FEMD director further called for the provision of adequate firefighting equipment in the market to ensure prompt intervention during emergencies.

He appealed to the Market Board of Trustees and the leadership of the traders’ union to explore ways of supporting the victims and alleviating their hardship.

Speaking on behalf of NEMA, Mariam Dantanko explained that the agency’s disaster response assistance was primarily provided through relief materials rather than direct cash payments.

She said such interventions could include food and building materials, but would depend on the outcome of the assessment and approval by the agency’s headquarters.

The statement added that FEMD’s Relief and Rehabilitation Division was also at the scene to conduct a needs assessment to determine the immediate requirements of the affected traders.

The department reiterated the need for regular inspection of electrical installations, fire safety awareness and functional firefighting equipment in markets and other public facilities to prevent avoidable fire outbreaks.

title: IGP urged to play role in Lagos property demolition
description: The Nigeria Policy Group has condemned the reported demolition and alleged unlawful seizure of a private property located at No. 12 Tumbuli Road, Ikoyi, Lagos State and called on the Inspector-General of Police to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly the alleged invol
content:
The Nigeria Policy Group has condemned the reported demolition and alleged unlawful seizure of a private property located at No. 12 Tumbuli Road, Ikoyi, Lagos State and called on the Inspector-General of Police to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly the alleged involvement of some police officers.

The group expressed concern over the allegations that officials and individuals linked to Lagos State property development agency, alongside members of the Nigeria Police, were involved in the action.

This was contained in a statement by Prince Ike Onuoha yesterday.
According to the group, the allegations raised serious questions about respect for private property rights, the rule of law and the proper conduct of public institutions.

It expressed concern about the reported presence and involvement of police personnel, calling on the Inspector-General of Police to urgently establish the identities of the officers involved, the authority under which they acted, the purpose of their visit and whether their conduct complied with the established police procedures and the law.

“The Nigeria Police Force exists to protect lives, property and the rights of citizens. It must never be perceived as an instrument for intimidation, unlawful dispossession or the enforcement of private interests. Any officer found to have abused the authority of the office must be held accountable in accordance with the law,” the group stated.

It also called on the Lagos State Government and the relevant property development agency to publicly clarify the legal basis for the reported demolition and any subsequent activities on the property.

“If due process was followed, the relevant authorities should provide clear explanations and supporting documentation. If it was not, appropriate steps must be taken to address the alleged violations and ensure accountability,” it stated.

The group, among other things called for an immediate and impartial investigation by the Inspector-General of Police into the alleged involvement of police officers; the identification of all officers and other individuals involved in the incident, including the authority under which they acted; a clear explanation from the Lagos State Government and the relevant property development agency regarding the legal basis for the demolition and subsequent activities at the property; appropriate action against any individual or officer found to have acted unlawfully or abused public office and measures to prevent further interference with the property while the matter is being properly investigated.

The group also urged President Bola Tinubu to ensure that the matter receives the attention it deserves, insisting that the protection of citizens’ property rights and the enforcement of the rule of law must not depend on an individual’s political influence, financial standing or social connections.

“Nigeria must remain a country where public institutions serve the people, where the law applies equally to everyone and where no citizen is left without protection against alleged abuses of power. The law must protect every citizen and nobody should be above it,” the group submitted.

title: Defamation Charges: DSS Asks Appeal Court To Uphold ₦100m Fine Against SERAP
description: The Department of State Services (DSS) is asking the Court of Appeal in Abuja to uphold the ₦100m fine imposed on the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) for defaming two of its operatives through false publications.At the day’s proceedings, the DSS argued that the appeal
content:
The Department of State Services (DSS) is asking the Court of Appeal in Abuja to uphold the ₦100m fine imposed on the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) for defaming two of its operatives through false publications.

At the day’s proceedings, the DSS argued that the appeal by SERAP against the judgment of the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory that awarded the fine did substantial justice to the complaints of defamation.

Counsel to the DSS, Oluwaleke Kehinde, asked a special panel of the Court of Appeal to uphold the findings of Justice Halilu Yusuf and the judgment that led to the award of the damages.

The legal team was led by Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN.

On its part, Counsel to SERAP, Oluwatosin Adesioye, urged the appellate court to set aside the judgment and the ₦100m fine imposed on it by the High Court.

However, after taking arguments for and against, the court reserved its judgment to a date that would be communicated to the parties involved.

The three-member panel, led by Justice Danlami Senchi, reserved the appeal for judgment after all parties adopted their final briefs of argument.

The two appeals were filed by SERAP and its Deputy Director, Mr. Kolawole Oluwadare, respectively.

While the appellants, represented by Mr. Paul Mgbenwa and Mr. Oluwatosin Adesioye, prayed for the appeals to be upheld and the High Court’s order set aside, the respondents’ legal team, led by Mr. Oluwaleke Samuel Kehinde, sought the dismissal of the appeals for want of merit.

The Justice Senchi-led panel said it would communicate the judgment date to the parties.

A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), in a judgment delivered on May 5, awarded damages against SERAP and Mr. Oluwadare, who were sued as the first and second defendants.

The trial judge, Justice Yusuf Halilu, held that he was satisfied that the non-governmental organisation had, on September 9, 2024, tarnished the reputations of two DSS personnel, Sarah John and Gabriel Ogundele, when it falsely alleged that they had invaded its office in Abuja.

The court held that the defendants had unjustly defamed the operatives when they published on SERAP’s website and X (formerly Twitter) handle that the operatives had invaded the office and harassed a staff member.

According to the court, the publication was in bad taste.

Therefore, in addition to the ₦100m damages, the court ordered SERAP to tender a public apology to the defamed DSS operatives in two national newspapers, on two television stations, and on its website.

It also ordered the defendants to pay the two operatives ₦1 million to cover the cost of the litigation, as well as 10 per cent annual interest on the judgment sum until it is fully liquidated.

The judgment followed Suit No. CV/4547/2024, which the two operatives filed before the court to challenge what they regarded as SERAP’s false claim, which had negatively affected both their reputations and the corporate image of the DSS.

content:
…challenges Atiku, Obi to clarify education policies ahead of 2027

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

Former Edo State Governor Adams Oshiomhole has taken a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar over his advocacy for the privatisation of tertiary education, declaring that Nigeria cannot afford to surrender its public education system to private interests when millions of children are still denied access to schooling.

Oshiomhole argued that privatising tertiary education would further deepen inequality and undermine access to learning in a country still battling a huge out-of-school population, inadequate educational infrastructure and unequal opportunities.

The former governor spoke on Monday in Abuja at the unveiling of the Renewed Hope Education A+Z Scorecard by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa.

He questioned the rationale behind Atiku’s renewed push for private-sector control of tertiary education, recalling that the former Vice-President had pursued a privatisation agenda during his time in office.

Oshiomhole also challenged Atiku and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi to tell Nigerians whether they would sustain or dismantle the education policies introduced by the President Bola Tinubu administration if allowed to govern the country.

He insisted that Nigerians deserved clarity on the opposition politicians’ education agenda, particularly on policies designed to expand access to tertiary education and provide financial assistance to students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Taking a further swipe at Atiku, Oshiomhole criticised what he described as the former Vice-President’s position on using public resources to enrich friends, warning that such an approach could undermine critical social investments, particularly education.

He maintained that government resources were limited and that decisions on public spending must reflect national priorities rather than personal interests.

“If the money he wishes to use to enrich his friends is not diverted to paying student grants, remember that resources are limited at any point in time. That is why economics is about priorities. What is given to those students will not be available to be used to assist friends,” he said.

Nigeria’s education crisis remains a major national concern, with millions of children still excluded from formal schooling despite successive government interventions.

A 2024 UNICEF estimate put the country’s out-of-school children population at 18.3 million, comprising 10.2 million primary school-age children and 8.1 million children of junior secondary school age, although the Federal Ministry of Education has more recently cited an estimate of about 15 million.

Against this backdrop, the federal government has introduced several interventions aimed at expanding access, improving learning outcomes and equipping young Nigerians with employable skills.

Among them are the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, the Technical and Vocational Education and Training, TVET, programme, the Nigerian Education Data Infrastructure, NEDI, and targeted interventions to return out-of-school children to classrooms.

According to the Federal Ministry of Education’s Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative 2026 report, NELFUND had processed more than 1.65 million applications and disbursed N372.62bn in student loans, covering tuition and upkeep allowances across 319 tertiary institutions.

The government also reported that 156,446 verified trainees had benefited from its TVET programme, which offers free vocational training, monthly stipends and start-up support.

In a related development, the Federal Government unveiled a National Education Technology Strategy on Monday, aimed at addressing teacher shortages, expanding access to learning and improving education data management through digital platforms.

The strategy is expected to bring 26 government initiatives under a coordinated framework covering digital learning, teacher development, education financing and interventions for out-of-school children.

Earlier, Alausa disclosed that the federal government had put funding arrangements in place for its education data infrastructure, while introducing a three-year renegotiation window in its agreement with the Academic Staff Union of Universities and other university-based unions.

He explained that the provision would allow the agreements to be reviewed every three years, providing a mechanism for addressing staff welfare and remuneration concerns before they escalate into prolonged industrial disputes.

The federal government had in October unveiled fresh agreements with academic and non-academic staff unions in tertiary institutions, featuring improved welfare packages, allowances and a monitoring framework to ensure implementation.

The three-year review arrangement is also expected to strengthen regular engagement between the government and university unions and minimise recurring strikes that have repeatedly disrupted academic calendars.

The Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’id Ahmad, said the ministry was also pursuing reforms to strengthen governance and discipline in educational institutions.

She listed the introduction of guidelines for appointing vice-chancellors, rectors and provosts, alongside policies addressing bullying in schools, among measures being implemented to improve standards across the education sector.

title: Tinubu’s education reforms reach 3m tertiary students, Alausa tells opposition
description:
…Accuses opposition of misleading Nigerians, says government prioritising results over promises



By Joseph Erunke, Abuja



Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has challenged opposition politicians, particularly former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to familiarise themselves w
content:
…Accuses opposition of misleading Nigerians, says government prioritising results over promises

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has challenged opposition politicians, particularly former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to familiarise themselves with Nigeria’s education laws before criticising the Federal Government’s policies, insisting that nearly three million tertiary students are benefiting from President Bola Tinubu’s reforms.

Alausa, who accused the opposition of deliberately misrepresenting the administration’s interventions, said criticisms of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and other education policies were misplaced and failed to acknowledge the benefits Nigerians were already enjoying.

The minister fired back at Obi on Monday during a briefing at the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council headquarters in Abuja, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s record in education ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a direct response to Obi’s criticisms, Alausa said the former presidential candidate needed to study the relevant legislation before making public statements about the government’s education financing arrangements.

“What Mr Obi is saying is borne out of ignorance. He needs to read the law. This is the law of Nigeria,” the minister declared.

He further accused Obi of misleading Nigerians, saying: “If Mr Obi wants to blame me and mislead the public and Nigerians, that tells you the kind of person he is.”

At the centre of the disagreement is the four per cent development levy introduced under the Nigeria Tax Act, which Alausa said was designed to guarantee sustainable funding for the student loan scheme.

He explained that 15 per cent of the proceeds from the levy was earmarked for NELFUND, insisting that the allocation was expressly provided for in the law and not an arbitrary government arrangement.

The minister challenged Obi to examine the relevant provisions of the legislation rather than cast doubts on the funding structure of the scheme.

Defending the broader education reforms, Alausa said the administration’s interventions had expanded access to tertiary education through student loans, improved infrastructure, increased funding and efforts to address the shortage of academic personnel in universities and other higher institutions.

He disclosed that nearly three million students in tertiary institutions and another 200,000 students in secondary schools had benefited from the administration’s interventions.

“We have almost three million Nigerian students in tertiary education and another 200,000 in secondary education. Today, students in every single section of our country have benefited the most from President Tinubu’s transformative agenda,” he said.

Rejecting what he described as an opposition fixation on policy announcements, Alausa argued that the real measure of government performance should be the tangible benefits reaching Nigerians rather than promises and political rhetoric.

“We have enough policies in Nigeria. We want tangible benefits for Nigerians. So, every single thing about today is not about policies. What I am trying to tell you is how Nigerians are benefiting,” he said.

Beyond student financing, the minister disclosed that the Federal Government had developed guidelines to strengthen governance in universities, particularly in the appointment of vice-chancellors, while committees had been established to monitor compliance.

He also identified efforts to tackle bullying in schools and ensure that recommendations from previous education review panels were implemented before another round of policy reviews commenced.

Alausa’s defence comes amid mounting opposition criticism of the administration’s education spending and reform priorities.

Obi had in July faulted the Federal Government’s decision to phase out the policy separating junior and senior secondary schools, arguing that Nigeria’s education challenges were rooted in inadequate funding, poor management and weak leadership rather than the structure of the school system.

The former Anambra governor also criticised the 2026 education budget, claiming that the sector received only 6.17 per cent of total expenditure, far below UNESCO’s recommended 15 to 20 per cent benchmark.

However, the Tinubu administration has continued to defend its education agenda, pointing to interventions in basic education, technical and vocational training, digital learning, teacher development and tertiary education financing.

Figures released by the Federal Government showed that NELFUND had disbursed N372.62bn in student loans across 319 tertiary institutions, covering tuition and upkeep allowances.

The administration has also introduced programmes targeting out-of-school children, expanded technical education opportunities and pursued digital initiatives to improve education planning and service delivery.

With the 2027 general elections approaching, education has increasingly become a battleground between the ruling APC and opposition politicians, with the government relying on its reform record to justify its quest for another mandate.

title: 2027: Atiku takes jab at APC following ADC rally in Yobe
description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of using artificial intelligence (AI) to create the impression of massive attendance at its political rallies, insisting that the crowds at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign in Yobe State were genuine.
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of using artificial intelligence (AI) to create the impression of massive attendance at its political rallies, insisting that the crowds at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign in Yobe State were genuine.

Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, made the allegation while thanking residents of Potiskum and other parts of Yobe for the reception accorded him and his entourage during the party’s campaign rally.

In a statement issued on Monday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku also commended Governor Mai Mala Buni for allowing the opposition party to hold its campaign without interference.

He described the reception from the moment his entourage entered Potiskum from Azare as overwhelming, saying the large turnout and enthusiasm of residents would remain memorable.

“The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart,” he said.

Atiku said Buni’s decision to provide a level playing field for the ADC demonstrated the importance of allowing all political parties to engage voters and present their programmes freely.

He, however, took a swipe at the ruling party, alleging that it relied on AI-generated images to exaggerate attendance at its rallies.

“The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate,” Atiku said.

“Our Affordable Life campaign needs no artificial crowd; the people’s presence and their voices speak for themselves.”

The former Vice-President continued his criticism, mocking what he described as unrealistic AI-generated depictions of supporters at APC rallies.

“The Presidency’s AI must have forgotten that crowds need seats and that people do not fly. Perhaps in Tinubu’s imaginary rally, the supporters were expected to hover through the speech,” he said.

Atiku also interpreted chants of “Tinubu Must Go” at ADC rallies as a reflection of public dissatisfaction with the current administration and growing demands for improved living conditions.

“The ADC’s Affordable Life campaign is not mere sloganeering. When I hear the crowd chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ at our rallies, I take those words personally,” he said.

He pledged to prioritise measures to reduce the cost of living and improve the welfare of Nigerians if elected President, promising to begin implementing his plans immediately after assuming office.

“When President Tinubu leaves office on 29 May 2027, good governance and an affordable life must follow. I solemnly pledge to take immediate steps to make life affordable again when elected president at the January 16 presidential election. That is my promise to our teeming supporters,” he said.

Atiku said the reception in Yobe had strengthened his confidence in the ADC’s campaign, adding that Nigerians were willing to support political programmes that addressed their economic difficulties and aspirations.

title: Plateau LG imposes 12-hour curfew after gunmen burn seven houses
description:

The curfew, which runs from 6pm to 6am daily, was imposed on Monday evening amid reports that r
content:
The Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council of Plateau State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Doemak District following heightened tension after suspected gunmen burnt down seven houses in Bong community.

The curfew, which runs from 6pm to 6am daily, was imposed on Monday evening amid reports that residents were fleeing their homes, shops had closed and commercial activities had been disrupted over fears of further attacks.

The Director of Press and Publicity to the Executive Chairman of the council, Danaan Sylvanus, announced the restriction in a public notice issued on Monday.

He said, “In view of the security tension, Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council has imposed a curfew in Doemak.

“The curfew shall be observed from 6pm to 6am. By this notice, any person found moving during this period will be treated as a security threat by the security agencies.”

The council urged residents to comply strictly with the directive and cooperate with security agencies to maintain peace in the area.

The curfew followed Sunday’s attack on Bong community in Doemak District, where suspected gunmen reportedly stormed the village around 9pm and set seven houses ablaze.

A community source, Silas Bishop, who confirmed the attack, lamented the destruction and called on security operatives to intensify efforts to track down and arrest those responsible.

He also urged security agencies to strengthen surveillance and deploy more personnel to the affected communities to prevent further attacks.

Meanwhile, tension has reportedly gripped Doemak, the headquarters of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area, with residents said to be packing their belongings and relocating to safer places over fears for their lives and property.

As of Monday evening, shops were reportedly shut, while commercial activities had been disrupted as residents expressed concern over the security situation.

Confirming the attack, the Executive Chairman of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council, Christopher Audu Manship, condemned the incident and assured residents that the government would not abandon them.

Manship, who visited Bong community to assess the destruction, said the government would support efforts to rebuild the houses destroyed by the attackers.

He said, “Government will not abandon the people of Bong community. We will support efforts towards the restoration of the houses destroyed and sustain measures to secure the community against further attacks.”

The chairman urged youths in the affected communities to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies.

The attack on Bong community occurred around the same time suspected terrorists invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District of neighbouring Mangu Local Government Area, where several residents were killed.

Manship, who visited Zwagal alongside the Executive Chairman of Mangu Local Government Council, Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, described the attack as barbaric and inhuman.

He said, “The government will intensify efforts to secure lives and property, which remains the primary responsibility of every government.”

The Qua’an-Pan chairman also conveyed Governor Caleb Mutfwang’s condolences to the bereaved families in Zwagal, saying the governor remained determined to tackle insecurity in the state.

Also speaking, Mwolpun assured residents that efforts were being made to improve network services in the affected communities to enhance security surveillance and communication.

Earlier, the Long Zwagal, Miskagam Jonathan Wadong, thanked the two council chairmen for their prompt response and mobilisation of security personnel following the attack.

He said gunshots suddenly rang out in the community at about 8pm before the attackers invaded, throwing residents into panic.

Wadong appealed to the government to deploy more security personnel to the area to prevent a recurrence of the attacks.

The post Plateau LG imposes 12-hour curfew after gunmen burn seven houses appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
A few weeks after the death of Spanish footballer Jesús de Miguel, Argentine footballer Abel Núñez has died after suffering a head injury during a match while representing Ezeiza FC, a club statement announced on Sunday.

The National Pension Commission also disclosed that only 14 out of Nigeria’s 36 states are paying pensions regularly,

It also noted that the ₦400 billion provided by the Federal Government and the pension industry for the Pension Protection Fund could sustain the minimum monthly pension initiative for at least 10 years, based on current projections.

In other news, President Bola Tinubu has ordered the release of  78 suspects arrested over the attack on his motorcade in Abuja last Friday after Jumu’ah prayers.

The recap in full:

1. Argentine footballer Abel Núñez dies after head injury during match

An Argentine footballer, Abel Núñez, has died days after suffering a head injury during a match while representing Ezeiza Football Club.

The club announced his death in a statement released on Sunday, expressing sadness over the loss of the young player, who had undergone surgery after the incident.

“After suffering a hard blow during a match, proudly wearing our Ezeiza shirt, we deeply regret his departure,” the club said.

Read more details here.

2. Only 14 states pay pensions regularly – PenCom

The National Pension Commission has disclosed that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states are paying pensions regularly, acknowledging that some state governments are performing poorly in meeting their obligations to retirees.

The Director-General of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, made this known during an interview with ARISE NEWS on Monday, describing pension payments as a continuing challenge in several states.

“We have 14 states that are paying up. But 14 out of 36 states is a lot. And some states are doing very badly,” she said.

Read more details here.

3. Tinubu grants clemency to 78 suspects arrested over convoy attack

The Federal Capital Territory Police Command has said 78 suspects arrested over the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade in Abuja are to be released following the President’s extension of clemency to them.

In a statement released on Monday by the command spokesperson, Josephine Adeh, the suspects were arrested after the attack on the President’s convoy on Friday, November 13, at a mosque in Garki District.

The incident happened shortly after Tinubu observed Jumu’ah prayer

Read more details here.

4. Nigeria cannot afford Atiku’s tertiary education privatisation plan — Oshiomhole

Former Edo State Governor, Adams Oshiomhole, has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s advocacy for the privatisation of tertiary education, saying Nigeria cannot afford such a policy when millions of children are still out of school.

Oshiomhole spoke on Monday in Abuja at the unveiling of the Renewed Hope Education A+Z Scorecard by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa.

He recalled that Atiku pursued a privatisation agenda while serving as Vice-President, questioning the rationale behind his advocacy for private-sector control of tertiary education in a country where access to basic education remains a major challenge.

Read more details here.

5. VIDEO: Explosion sparks fire at Lagos NNPC filling station

A gas explosion at an NNPC filling station near Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ipaja, Lagos State, on Monday sparked a fire, raising concerns among residents.

The fire reportedly spread to nearby buildings, while emergency responders were said to have arrived at the scene.

title: 2,500 Akwa Ibom widows, PWDs benefit from First Lady’s food intervention
description:
• hails ASR Africa, anonymous donor for sustained food supplies
No fewer than 2,500 widows, persons with disabilities (PWDs) and other vulnerable persons across Akwa Ibom State have received food assistance under the Renewed Hope Initiative (RHI), led by Nigeria’s First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu.
The int
content:
• hails ASR Africa, anonymous donor for sustained food supplies

No fewer than 2,500 widows, persons with disabilities (PWDs) and other vulnerable persons across Akwa Ibom State have received food assistance under the Renewed Hope Initiative (RHI), led by Nigeria’s First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu.

The intervention, which targets households struggling to meet basic nutritional needs, has now extended the initiative’s Food Outreach Scheme to 33 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), since its launch in March 2024.

According to a statement by her media aide, Busola Kukoyi, the latest distribution took place at the Banquet Hall of the Government House, Uyo, on Monday, with the wife of the Vice President, Hajiya Nana Shettima, representing the First Lady at the event.

She handed over the food items to the Coordinator of the Office of the First Lady of Akwa Ibom State, Lady Helen Eno-Obareki, for distribution to the identified beneficiaries.

Speaking at the event, Mrs. Shettima disclosed that the programme had been sustained through the contributions of two partners who provide two truckloads of food items monthly, enabling the initiative to support two states every month.

She identified the Abdul Samad Rabiu Africa Initiative (ASR Africa) and an anonymous donor as the partners, explaining that the food consignment for Akwa Ibom was provided by ASR Africa.

Nigeria’s First Lady expressed appreciation to the donors for their sustained contributions, saying their generosity had enabled the initiative to extend humanitarian assistance to vulnerable communities across the country.

She said the RHI remained committed to complementing President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda by translating its vision of inclusive development into practical interventions that improve lives.

Tinubu also acknowledged the support of Governor Umo Eno and commended Obareki for her commitment to advancing the objectives of the initiative in the state.

Governor Eno, represented by his deputy, Akon Eyakenyi, described the intervention as a demonstration of compassion and commitment to caring for the less privileged.

He noted that the initiative had consistently supported vulnerable groups, particularly women, older persons and people in need, through various humanitarian and empowerment programmes.

The governor recalled that the First Lady had, barely two weeks earlier, sent a delegation to the state to provide financial assistance to women.

“I recall barely two weeks ago, on November 5 precisely, the First Lady sent a delegation to empower our women with cash. This further demonstrates the RHI’s commitment to improving livelihoods,” he said.

Obareki, in her remarks, commended the First Lady for what she described as a sustained commitment to improving the welfare of vulnerable Nigerians.

She said the First Lady’s return to the state for the second time within a month underscored her dedication to the welfare of the people.

Obareki highlighted the initiative’s interventions in Akwa Ibom, particularly programmes focused on women’s empowerment and inclusion across the state’s 31 local government areas.

She added that the interventions were designed to ensure that assistance reached those who needed it most, making a tangible difference in vulnerable households.

Also speaking, the Managing Director of ASR Africa, Dr Ubon Udoh, assured the initiative of the organisation’s continued support and collaboration.

He said the organisation was ready to partner with the RHI on further interventions aimed at improving citizens’ welfare, strengthening social protection and providing meaningful assistance to disadvantaged groups.

In a separate interview, the Governor’s Special Adviser on Persons with Disabilities, Mrs Nnene Bassey, said the First Lady had consistently supported the disability community through financial assistance, food distribution and skills acquisition programmes.

She disclosed that 100 persons with disabilities had previously received N100,000 each, while another 100 beneficiaries received N200,000 each under the initiative.

According to her, the programme had also provided skills acquisition opportunities to promote financial independence, improve livelihoods and discourage street begging among persons with disabilities.

Bassey added that new beneficiaries were introduced annually to ensure that more members of the disability community benefited from the interventions.

The 2,500 beneficiaries were drawn from the state’s 31 local government areas, with Uyo accounting for the highest allocation of 500 beneficiaries.

title: US military intervention must respect Nigeria’s sovereignty – Veritas varsity
description: The Centre for Peace and Development, Veritas University, Abuja, has called on the Federal Government to place human rights, civilian protection and national sovereignty at the centre of Nigeria’s counter-terrorism operations, warning against foreign military intervention without clear legal safegua
content:
The Centre for Peace and Development, Veritas University, Abuja, has called on the Federal Government to place human rights, civilian protection and national sovereignty at the centre of Nigeria’s counter-terrorism operations, warning against foreign military intervention without clear legal safeguards.

The centre also urged Nigeria and the United States to strengthen their security partnership through intelligence sharing, technical assistance and institutional capacity-building, rather than relying largely on military operations to tackle terrorism.

The recommendations were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of a roundtable and mini-conference organised by CEPAD in collaboration with the Rosa Luxemburg Foundation, West Africa, at Veritas University, Abuja.

The communiqué was released on Monday.

The conference, themed, ‘Counter-terrorism in Nigeria and United States Military Intervention: Rethinking the Responsibility to Protect’, brought together academics, researchers, security practitioners and students to examine Nigeria’s security challenges and the implications of possible United States military engagement.

According to the communiqué, terrorism remains a major threat to Nigeria’s national security, human security, social cohesion and sustainable development, requiring responses beyond military action.

It stated that counter-terrorism strategies must address the political, socioeconomic, ideological and institutional conditions sustaining violent extremism.

The conference noted that although United States security assistance had strengthened Nigeria’s counter-terrorism capacity through intelligence, training, surveillance and logistics, it had not decisively defeated insurgent groups, including Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province.

It also identified human rights violations, weak intelligence, corruption and governance deficits as factors undermining the effectiveness of counter-terrorism operations.

On the Responsibility to Protect framework, the participants warned against interpreting it as an unrestricted justification for unilateral military intervention.

The communiqué stated, “The Responsibility to Protect should not be interpreted as an unrestricted justification for unilateral military intervention. Its application must remain consistent with the principles and procedures of international law and the United Nations Charter.”

It further stressed that Nigeria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity must be respected in all forms of international security engagement, while recognising the government’s responsibility to protect citizens against terrorism and mass atrocities.

The conference called for stronger mechanisms to protect religious minorities, vulnerable communities and places of worship, warning that counter-terrorism policies must avoid religious profiling, discrimination and the stigmatisation of particular religious groups.

On civilian protection, the participants recommended independent monitoring of military operations, credible investigations into allegations of civilian casualties and accountability procedures for human rights violations. They also called for greater community participation in intelligence gathering, early warning and the prevention of violent extremism.

Presenting a paper on Nigeria-US counter-terrorism cooperation, a lecturer in the Departments of Political Science and Diplomacy, and Peace and Conflict Studies at Veritas University, Emmanuella Onota, argued that the partnership should be assessed not only by its military achievements but also by its contribution to civilian protection.

She identified security coordination gaps, civilian casualties, weak accountability and inadequate community participation as challenges undermining security operations. Onota also emphasised the importance of community knowledge and participation in preventing violent extremism, cautioning against arming local communities without effective oversight or treating civil society organisations merely as intelligence sources.

Similarly, Dr Roberts Anya Nkata, in his presentation on civilian protection and US military engagement in Nigeria, argued that military assistance alone could not guarantee effective counter-terrorism or civilian protection.

He identified institutional weaknesses, poor intelligence coordination, corruption, operational failures and declining civilian trust as factors limiting the success of counter-terrorism efforts.

Nkata proposed what he described as “protection-conditioned security assistance”, linking military support to accountability, lawful operations, civilian protection and institutional learning. He recommended stronger monitoring of US security assistance, improved target verification, credible investigations of civilian harm and joint assessments of security operations by Nigeria and the United States.

Also speaking, Rev. Fr. Dr Isaac Vasumu Augustine, who examined religious freedom and counter-terrorism, identified terrorism, religious intolerance, weak governance, poverty and socioeconomic exclusion as interconnected drivers of insecurity.

He said the activities of Boko Haram, ISWAP and other violent groups had contributed to killings, displacement, abductions and violations of religious freedom. Augustine called for stronger intelligence cooperation, human rights accountability, interreligious dialogue, good governance and socioeconomic development to address the underlying causes of insecurity.

In his presentation on the international legal basis of US military engagement in Nigeria, Dr Chukwudi Victor Odoeme examined the tension between national sovereignty and international counter-terrorism obligations.

He argued that Nigeria’s consent to joint military operations could provide a potential legal justification for US military engagement, but noted that the absence of publicly available details concerning such consent left aspects of the intervention’s legality unresolved.

Odoeme stressed that any foreign military intervention must comply with the principles of valid state consent, necessity, proportionality and international law.

The communiqué further recommended strengthening Nigeria’s security institutions, institutionalising the participation of religious leaders and faith-based organisations in peacebuilding, and deepening regional cooperation through the Economic Community of West African States and the African Union.

It also called on universities, research institutions and policy organisations to intensify research and sustained dialogue on terrorism, religious freedom, human security, international law and national sovereignty.

The roundtable was chaired by the Director of CEPAD, Rev. Fr. Dr Innocent T. Jooji, who also presented a paper on counter-terrorism in Nigeria and the question of US military intervention.

Jooji highlighted concerns about national sovereignty, weak oversight, external dependency, human rights and the potential use of foreign military involvement as propaganda by insurgent groups.

He recommended recalibrating Nigeria’s security partnership with the United States by strengthening domestic security capacity, improving parliamentary oversight, expanding deradicalisation and development programmes, and enhancing regional cooperation.

The event also featured two thematic roundtable sessions examining religious freedom, security and defence, as well as international relations and law.

The communiqué was signed by Jooji; the Programme Manager of Rosa Luxemburg Foundation, Nigeria, Comrade Angela Odah; and Dr Ikechukwu Maxwell Ukandu of the conference secretariat.

Background: Nigeria has sustained military operations against Boko Haram and ISWAP, particularly in the North-East, while insecurity involving armed groups, banditry, kidnappings and other forms of violence has continued to challenge security agencies.

The debate over US involvement has also drawn attention to the balance between international security assistance, Nigeria’s sovereignty and civilian protection.

The Responsibility to Protect (R2P), endorsed by United Nations member states in 2005, places responsibility on states to protect their populations from genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity, while providing for international assistance and collective action through established UN mechanisms.

title: Oshiomhole challenges Obi: Come to Edo, I’ll show you my achievements one by one
description:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja
Former Edo State Governor, Adams Oshiomhole, has challenged former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, to visit Edo State for an inspection of his administration’s projects, saying he is ready to take him round to showcase his achievements.
Oshiomhole threw the challenge on Mond
content:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

Former Edo State Governor, Adams Oshiomhole, has challenged former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, to visit Edo State for an inspection of his administration’s projects, saying he is ready to take him round to showcase his achievements.

Oshiomhole threw the challenge on Monday in Abuja at the launch of A-Z of Education Reforms Scorecard by the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, while responding to the renewed political debate over the performance of former governors following President Bola Tinubu’s criticism of Obi’s record in Anambra State.

Obi had announced plans to publish his achievements as governor on a daily basis over the next few days, following Tinubu’s allegation that he failed to address the persistent erosion menace in Anambra before leaving office.

But Oshiomhole, who defended Tinubu’s position, said he was prepared to lead Obi round Edo State to show him the projects executed during his administration before both of them proceeded to Anambra to assess the former governor’s record.

“I offer through the media. I will take you to Edo and I will show my landmark achievement. And then Peter will follow me. We will go to Anambra. Let him point to all those things,” he said.

The former governor said the inspection would provide an opportunity to examine the erosion problem in Anambra and the complaints of residents whose homes were allegedly threatened or destroyed by gully erosion.

“When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu talks about his failure to fix erosion, we will go and see that this erosion were there and all the cries of the people. We will check it out. Give me station and see how the people were crying that their homes were being swept away,” Oshiomhole said.

He also used the occasion to defend the Tinubu administration’s education reforms, particularly the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), arguing that the student financing initiative had expanded access to tertiary education for children from economically disadvantaged families.

According to him, the opposition to the scheme by some political figures was misplaced, insisting that the policy was providing opportunities for gifted Nigerian students whose parents could not afford university education.

He specifically argued that the policy was a departure from the privatisation approach he attributed to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, whom he accused of promoting private tertiary education while serving in government.

Oshiomhole said the Tinubu administration’s intervention in the education sector went beyond providing financial assistance to students, noting that improved remuneration for university lecturers was also critical to restoring stability in the academic calendar.

He described the improved conditions of service for academic staff as a strategic investment that would encourage brilliant Nigerians to pursue careers in universities rather than seek better-paying opportunities elsewhere.

The former governor recalled that successive administrations had failed to implement agreements with the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), despite repeated industrial disputes, but said the Tinubu administration had taken steps to address the outstanding issues.

Oshiomhole, who said he was appointed by former President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua in 2009 to mediate between ASUU and the Federal Government, argued that better remuneration would help prevent avoidable strikes and strengthen the university system.

He maintained that the sustainability of the education reforms depended largely on continuity in government, urging Nigerians to support Tinubu for another term to prevent policy reversal.

“Keep President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on the job. That is the answer,” he said, arguing that the reforms needed time to become firmly established.

He likened the policies to a tree that required time to develop deep roots, warning that a change in government could threaten initiatives that were beginning to deliver results.

Oshiomhole further argued that education reforms must be linked to industrial development and job creation, saying Nigeria needed to invest in local manufacturing rather than depend excessively on imported goods.

He maintained that education should equip young Nigerians with the skills required to drive the economy, create employment and strengthen domestic industries.

The former governor thus urged the media to interrogate the records and policy positions of political leaders, saying Nigerians deserved evidence-based explanations of their achievements and promises.

title: Truck Crash Kills 31 Youth Party Members In Burundi
description: At least 31 members of the youth wing of Burundi’s ruling party died in a truck crash over the weekend, the police said on Monday.The accident took place in the northern Busoni commune at around 6:50 pm (1650 GMT) on Sunday after the driver lost control thanks to a brake failure, police colone
content:
At least 31 members of the youth wing of Burundi’s ruling party died in a truck crash over the weekend, the police said on Monday.

The accident took place in the northern Busoni commune at around 6:50 pm (1650 GMT) on Sunday after the driver lost control thanks to a brake failure, police colonel Pierre Nkurikiye said.

He said in a statement that 25 people were killed instantly, while six others later died of their injuries in the hospital.

The members of the ruling party’s powerful youth wing, known as the Imbonerakure, were returning from a day of “moralisation” training ahead of the presidential polls in 2027, the Interior Ministry said in a statement.

The group is described as a militia by the United Nations and rights organisations.

A police source confirmed the goods truck — which is frequently used to ferry Imbonerakure despite doing so being illegal — was travelling at high speed down a steep slope when the incident occurred.

“The driver was unable to brake in time to make a turn and slammed violently into two houses on the side of the road,” the police officer said, requesting anonymity.

“The impact was so severe that the truck was completely crushed, reduced to a mangled heap of scrap metal,” he said.

“Many died instantly, while the injured were taken to various hospitals in the region… Dozens remain in critical condition, their lives hanging in the balance.”

He added that officers were often “forced to turn a blind eye” to the illegal use of trucks for fear of reprisals.

Several rights groups, including Human Rights Watch, have accused the Imbonerakure of killing and torturing dozens of people, particularly under the authoritarian rule of former president Pierre Nkurunziza, in power from 2005 until 2020.

Burundi’s presidential election will see Evariste Ndayishimiye seek a second term and is scheduled to take place on May 3 next year.

Last week, the president submitted his candidacy papers, paying a deposit of 100 million Burundian francs ($33,000).

Opposition parties argue the huge sum imposed by the authorities is designed to prevent them from participating in the election.

AFP

title: Seven things to know about the next James Bond film
description:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, taking over the iconic role previously played by Daniel Craig in the long-running film franchise.
Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson’s casting on Monday, November 16, 2026, in a statement published on its official website.
content:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, taking over the iconic role previously played by Daniel Craig in the long-running film franchise.

Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson’s casting on Monday, November 16, 2026, in a statement published on its official website.

The announcement was also confirmed on the official James Bond social media accounts on Instagram and X, as verified by our correspondent.

The upcoming film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Amy Pascal and David Heyman will serve as producers, while Tanya Lapointe will be executive producer.

Pattinson described his appointment as the honour of a lifetime, while the studio said his casting marked a new chapter for the franchise.

Following the announcement, here are seven things to know about the upcoming James Bond film, as curated in a separate release on the MGM website on Monday.

1. Robert Pattinson takes over as James Bond

Pattinson has been officially cast as the next actor to portray James Bond, the fictional British secret agent also known as 007.

The actor, whose career spans more than two decades, has appeared in independent films and major studio productions, including The Twilight Saga, Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Tenet, The Lighthouse, Mickey 17 and The Batman.

He also starred in A24’s The Drama and Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey in 2026.

Reacting to his appointment, Pattinson said, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

2. Denis Villeneuve to direct the film

Canadian filmmaker Denis Villeneuve will direct the upcoming James Bond production.

Villeneuve is known for directing films including Dune, Blade Runner 2049, Arrival, Sicario, Prisoners, Enemy and Incendies.

Amazon MGM Studios announced his appointment as director on June 25, 2025, alongside the announcement that Tanya Lapointe would serve as executive producer.

Speaking about taking on the project, Villeneuve said: “Some of my earliest movie-going memories are connected to 007. I grew up watching James Bond films with my father, ever since Dr. No with Sean Connery. I’m a die-hard Bond fan. To me, he’s sacred territory. I intend to honor the tradition and open the path for many new missions to come.

“This is a massive responsibility, but also incredibly exciting for me and a huge honor. Amy, David, and I are absolutely thrilled to bring him back to the screen. Thank you to Amazon MGM Studios for their trust.”

3. Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight writes the screenplay

Steven Knight, the creator of the television series Peaky Blinders, is writing the screenplay for the upcoming James Bond film.

Amazon MGM Studios announced his appointment on July 31, 2025.

The British screenwriter, producer and director is also known for creating Taboo, SAS: Rogue Heroes, See and A Thousand Blows.

His film credits include Dirty Pretty Things, Eastern Promises, Spencer, Hummingbird, Locke and Serenity.

Knight also co-created the international television game show Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

4. Spider-Man and Harry Potter producers join the project

Amy Pascal and David Heyman will produce the upcoming film through their respective production companies, Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films.

Amazon MGM Studios announced their appointment on March 25, 2025.

Pascal is known for her work on the Spider-Man franchise, including the four films starring Tom Holland and the three animated Spider-Verse productions.

Her other production credits include Project Hail Mary, Challengers and Spider-Noir.

Heyman, on the other hand, produced all eight film adaptations of J.K. Rowling’s Harry Potter books, as well as the three Fantastic Beasts films.

His other credits include Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood, Marriage Story, Gravity and Barbie.

5. Tanya Lapointe named executive producer

Tanya Lapointe will serve as executive producer of the upcoming James Bond film.

Her appointment was announced by Amazon MGM Studios on June 25, 2025, alongside Villeneuve’s selection as director.

Lapointe is known for her work with Villeneuve, including their collaboration on the Dune films.

Amazon MGM Studios also named her as executive producer in its November 16, 2026 announcement confirming Pattinson’s casting.

6. Amazon MGM Studios has creative control of James Bond

Amazon MGM Studios’ involvement in the franchise follows its acquisition of MGM in 2022, which brought a catalogue of more than 4,000 films and 17,000 television shows under its ownership.

In March 2025, Amazon MGM Studios concluded a new joint venture with Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, under which the studio gained creative control of the James Bond intellectual property rights.

The arrangement gave Amazon MGM Studios control over the creative direction of the franchise.

7. All 25 previous James Bond films are on Prime Video

Amazon says all 25 previous official James Bond films are streaming on Prime Video worldwide.

The collection features the different actors who have portrayed the British secret agent over the decades, including Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig.

Pattinson’s appointment makes him the next actor to take on the role in the official film series, following Craig’s final appearance in No Time to Die, released in 2021.

The post Seven things to know about the next James Bond film appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to cybercrimes after hospital release
description:
A hacker who stole dozens of unfinished clips of Grand Theft Auto 6 and attempted to extort the game’s developers has pleaded guilty to a series of cybercrimes after being released from a secure hospital.
Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, United Kingdom, pleaded guilty on Monday at Woolwich Crown Court
content:
A hacker who stole dozens of unfinished clips of Grand Theft Auto 6 and attempted to extort the game’s developers has pleaded guilty to a series of cybercrimes after being released from a secure hospital.

Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, United Kingdom, pleaded guilty on Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to hacking Rockstar Games in 2022 and several other offences committed when he was 16 and 17 years old as a member of the hacking group Lapsus$`.

According to the BBC on Monday, Kurtaj was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital because of the severity of his autism. However, following a routine assessment late last year, he was deemed fit to stand trial and transferred to a normal prison in January.

Kurtaj hacked Rockstar Games while on bail for multiple other hacking offences and under police protection.

He was staying at a Travelodge hotel in Bicester, where he had been accommodated to protect him from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him over his stolen Bitcoin holdings.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj carried out the attack using an Amazon Fire Stick connected to his hotel television, alongside a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

He stole internal company data, including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished Grand Theft Auto 6.

He subsequently accessed the company’s internal Slack messaging system and issued an ultimatum, declaring: “If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code.”

When the company refused to cooperate, he published the clips and source code on an online forum using the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said the breach cost the company `$5m (£3.79m) to recover from, in addition to thousands of hours of staff time.

The company also said the hack exposed for the first time that one of the game’s playable characters was a woman, a detail it had been closely guarding for marketing purposes.

Kurtaj was initially considered unfit to stand a traditional trial because of the severity of his autism and was instead subjected to what is known as a trial of the facts.

Under the procedure, the jury was required to determine whether he committed the alleged acts rather than whether he did so with criminal intent.

In December 2023, the court ruled that he would remain in a secure hospital indefinitely unless doctors determined that he was no longer a danger.

However, a routine assessment late last year found him fit to face a criminal trial, which was scheduled to take place at Woolwich Crown Court.

Kurtaj subsequently pleaded guilty to all the offences.

The BBC reported that he appeared in court with short hair and an unkempt beard, wearing a suit and buttoned-up white shirt without a tie.

He reportedly blinked frequently during the hearing and stood to confirm his identity before entering his guilty pleas without visible emotion.

Other companies targeted

The offences to which Kurtaj pleaded guilty also included cyberattacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber, where he used social engineering techniques to gain access to internal systems.

The court heard that during his attack on Uber, he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His attacks on the companies were estimated to have caused about £10m in damage.

Using data stolen from the firms, Kurtaj and other members of Lapsus$` also targeted cryptocurrency investors.

The prosecution argued that the group stole at least `$300,000 from individual victims.

Kurtaj also admitted physically assaulting workers while in custody, including multiple biting incidents.

While in prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

He will be sentenced at a later date.

The prosecution described Kurtaj as a “leading light” in the teenage hacking group Lapsus$`.

Lapsus`$ member jailed for five years

Another member of the group, who was 17 at the time, was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court during Kurtaj’s original trial in 2023.

The teenager, whose identity could not be disclosed at the time because of his age, received an 18-month Youth Rehabilitation Order, including intensive supervision and a ban on using virtual private networks online.

Earlier in 2026, the same hacker, identified as Thalha Jubair, was sentenced to five years and six months in prison after continuing his cybercrime activities with another group known as Scattered Spider.

Among the victims of the group’s subsequent activities was Transport for London, which suffered a disruptive cyberattack that caused an estimated £39m in damage and significant disruption within the organisation.

The post GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to cybercrimes after hospital release appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
Faith-based film, ‘Agbara Nla: The Return,’ has grossed over N513.4m at the Nigerian box office, becoming the second highest-grossing Nollywood title of 2026.

The film also emerged as the highest-grossing faith-based title of all time and the ninth highest-grossing Nollywood title ever.

The distributor, Nile Entertainment, announced the milestone on Monday in an Instagram post, stating that the film had grossed over N513.4m in Nigeria.

“Agbara Nla: The Return is now the second highest-grossing Nollywood title of 2026, the highest-grossing faith-based film of all time and the 9th highest-grossing Nollywood title ever,” the distributor said.

The distributor added, “We’re proud to celebrate this moment with everyone who made it happen.”

The distributor had earlier described the film’s opening as the biggest non-December Nollywood opening weekend, the biggest October opening weekend and the biggest opening weekend for a faith-based film.

The film, a remake of the 1993 Christian production created by filmmaker Mike Bamiloye, returned to cinemas on October 1, 2026, more than three decades after the original was released.

The new production was directed by Bamiloye’s sons, Damilola Mike-Bamiloye and Joshua “Jay Mikee” Mike-Bamiloye.

The distributor also said the film’s single-day preview earnings had surpassed N71m.

Agbara Nla: The Return is a modern reimagining of the original film, which was later released in English as The Ultimate Power in 1994.

The story follows Muwonleru, a village controlled by a powerful herbalist, Isawuru, as two believers, Olaboye and Olatomi, leave their city lives to take the Christian message to the community, leading to a conflict between their faith and Isawuru’s spiritual power.

Mike Bamiloye reprises his role as Isawuru, while the cast also includes Aanu Kolade Abiodun, Remilekun Mosiko, Philip Olubakin, Gloria Mike-Bamiloye and David Kola Okeowo.

title: Beyoncé becomes first artiste to earn 100 Grammy nominations
description:
Beyoncé has become the first artist in Grammy history to receive 100 career nominations after earning a nod at the 2027 Grammy Awards.
The singer reached the milestone on Monday following the announcement of nominees for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with her song, “Morning Dew (Donk),” nominated i
content:
Beyoncé has become the first artist in Grammy history to receive 100 career nominations after earning a nod at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

The singer reached the milestone on Monday following the announcement of nominees for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with her song, “Morning Dew (Donk),” nominated in the Best R&B Solo Performance category.

The latest nomination takes her career tally to 100, extending her record as the most-nominated artist in the history of the awards.

Despite receiving only one nomination for the 2027 edition, Beyoncé remains the most-awarded artist in Grammy history, with 35 wins.

“Morning Dew (Donk)” is among the nominees alongside “Out the Window” by Kehlani, “Let Me” by Victoria Monét, “Pressha” by Jill Scott and “What You Need” by Nigerian singer Tems.

The nomination adds another milestone to Beyoncé’s Grammy record, having previously received 11 nominations for her album, Cowboy Carter, at the 2025 ceremony.

The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States.

The three laws presented to the governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, are the 2026 Revised Appro
content:
Ekiti State Governor, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, on Monday signed three new laws following their passage by the State House of Assembly.

The three laws presented to the governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, are the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law; Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 (No. 4 of 2026); and Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026 (No. 5 of 2026).

The Special Adviser to the Governor on Media, Yinka Oyebode, said in a statement in Ado Ekiti, “The signing of the three laws underscores the Oyebanji administration’s commitment to strengthening public institutions, improving the regulatory environment for infrastructure development and ensuring effective management of public resources in the interest of the people”.

According to the statement, the legislation on the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law retains the state’s total budget size at ₦415,572,070,139.44, while adjusting the allocation between recurrent and capital expenditure. Under the revised budget, recurrent expenditure increases from ₦221,872,839,071.84 to ₦268,765,546,864.66, while capital expenditure decreases from ₦193,699,231,067.60 to ₦146,806,523,274.78.

It stated, “The adjustment represents a reallocation of resources from capital expenditure to recurrent expenditure to accommodate the state’s financial and operational obligations without increasing the overall budget size originally approved in December 2025.

“The revised appropriation is expected to sustain government operations while maintaining funding for infrastructure, social development, economic growth and institutional efficiency,” Oyebode stated.

He added that the Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 “is an amendment of the existing Pension Reform Law No. 3 of 2022 to formally accommodate the designation of a Director-General alongside the Permanent Secretary in the administrative and governance structure of the Commission responsible for the Contributory Pension Scheme in the state.

“The amendment also makes consequential adjustments to relevant provisions of the principal law, including the composition of the Commission’s Board, staff administration, remuneration and allowances among others,” he said.

He added that the Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026, established a regulatory framework for the approval and administration of permits for the installation and maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure in the state.

Oyebode stated, “The legislation fixes the maximum Right of Way fee at ₦145 per linear metre for ducts and cables and ₦700,000 per site for a Base Transceiver Station.

“It also requires telecommunications operators to comply with approved engineering standards, protect public safety and the environment, minimise damage to roads and public utilities, and restore affected infrastructure after installation.”

title: Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa
description:
By Juliet Umeh, Agency Report



At least 17 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, with police yet to establish the motives behind the attacks, which occurred about 530 kilometres apart on Sunday.



Eight people were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle in Sw
content:
By Juliet Umeh, Agency Report

At least 17 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, with police yet to establish the motives behind the attacks, which occurred about 530 kilometres apart on Sunday.

Eight people were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg, while nine others were killed in a shack in Jeffsville, near the capital, Pretoria.

Police spokesperson, Robert Netshiunda, said the identities of the eight victims in Sweetwaters were yet to be confirmed, although some families had approached authorities to assist.

“It’s still too early to tell what the motive could have been and who could be behind the shooting because we are yet to identify the victims,” he said.

In Jeffsville, six males and three females were found with gunshot wounds inside a four-room shack. Police spokesperson, Brenda Muridili, said officers were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Monday, although the shooting reportedly occurred between 10 p.m. and 11 p.m. on Sunday.

No arrests had been made as investigations continued.

Gauteng Police Commissioner, Tommy Mthombeni, said the killings could be linked to a shooting in nearby Saulsville last year, which claimed 12 lives and left 13 others injured.

He disclosed that one of Sunday’s victims was a person of interest in the previous attack, adding that police could not rule out retaliation.

South Africa has recorded several deadly mass shootings in the past year. In September, 11 people, including a pregnant woman, were killed in an attack on a house near Durban, while another shooting at a tavern claimed 17 lives.

Two separate shootings in Johannesburg in June also left 24 people dead, with police linking one to rival illegal mining gangs.

Two other mass shootings in December last year claimed 21 lives.

Police investigations into Sunday’s attacks are ongoing.

The post Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Nigeria’s inflation rate drops to 14.06% in October
description:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan



Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent recorded in September, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) has said.



The NBS disclosed this in its latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report released on Monday, also showi
content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent recorded in September, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) has said.

The NBS disclosed this in its latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report released on Monday, also showing a decline in food inflation to 19.13 per cent in October from 19.59 per cent in the preceding month.

According to the report, headline inflation stood at 18.97 per cent in October 2025, indicating a 4.91 percentage-point decline in the annual rate between October 2025 and October 2026.

The statistics agency, however, reported an increase in the month-on-month headline inflation rate, which rose to 0.43 per cent in October from 0.06 per cent in September.

It explained that the development indicated that the average price level increased at a faster rate in October than in the preceding month.

“In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06%, down from 14.63% in September 2026 and stood at 18.97% in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025),” the NBS stated.

The report added that the October 2026 headline inflation rate represented a 4.91 percentage-point decline compared with the corresponding period of the previous year.

“On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43%, which was 0.38% higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06%).

“This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026,” the agency said.

In a statement issued on Monday in Benin by the commission’s Head of
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Edo has disowned the author of a viral video, claiming to have recruited ad-hoc personnel for the commission and directing them to work for a particular political interest.

In a statement issued on Monday in Benin by the commission’s Head of Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Samuel Sunday, on behalf of the Resident Electoral Commissioner, the commission stated that the man was not its staff member.

“INEC Edo declares that no one named Osayi Israel Omoroduwa is among its staff in Edo, and that no one has the power or access to recruit ad-hoc staff for the commission,” Sunday explained.

He further explained that the recruitment of ad-hoc personnel was conducted exclusively through the online INECPRES platform, administered by INEC Headquarters.

“The path to being an ad-hoc staff of INEC is by online application through the INECPRES platform and whoever has internet access can do so by themselves or support others so qualified to apply,” he added.

He emphasised that staff members in its state offices could not influence the recruitment process, adding that the person named in the video had no special access to the platform.

According to Sunday, successful applicants will undergo scrutiny by the commission and receive training on the conduct and ethics of elections.

The INEC Spokesman described the online video as “an irresponsible and targeted attack” on the commission and its processes.

He argued that the video was intended to undermine public confidence in the electoral process through misinformation.

He, however, reaffirmed the commitment of the commission to conducting credible elections and urged the public to disregard what it described as “falsehood contained in the video”. (NAN)

The post INEC disowns ‘staff’ behind report of partisan recruitment in Edo appeared first on Vanguard News.
