title: Budget 2027: FG moves to cut overhead, orders MDAs to share facilities
description:
…Targets spending on hotels, private venues for official meetings



By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief



The Federal Government has directed Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other pr
content:
…Targets spending on hotels, private venues for official meetings

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Federal Government has directed Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings, as part of efforts to reduce overhead expenditure in the 2027 Budget.

The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations.

The Head of the Ministry’s Information and Public Relations Unit, Efe Ovuakporie, disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Monday.

She said the Efficiency Office was working towards establishing a coordinated system that would enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements.

According to her, a major component of the initiative is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide.

The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier for them to locate suitable venues.

Ovuakporie explained that the arrangement would also enable MDAs with underutilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets.

She said the initiative aligned with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions.

In a related development, the Efficiency Office recently inspected shared government facilities across the five South-East states of Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo to identify underutilised public infrastructure and opportunities for cost savings.

The inspection covered selected Federal Secretariats, Federal Polytechnics, Federal Medical Centres and Federal Universities.

According to the statement, the exercise assessed the condition, availability, utilisation and maintenance of the facilities, with particular attention to areas where improved management could enhance productivity and reduce unnecessary government spending.

The inspection teams identified underutilised office spaces and facilities, deteriorating furniture, fittings and equipment, as well as inadequate maintenance of some offices and common areas.

They also identified opportunities to improve the use of conference facilities and strengthen the organisation, storage and preservation of official records.

Ovuakporie said the Efficiency Office engaged the management of the institutions visited on measures to address the identified shortcomings.

These include the introduction of regular maintenance schedules, proper asset inventories, improved records management and more effective arrangements for sharing available facilities.

She said the findings would inform recommendations for strengthening the management of government assets, promoting cooperation among institutions and ensuring that infrastructure acquired with public funds delivered maximum value.

The Office stressed that the inspections were not intended to apportion blame but to identify areas requiring improvement and encourage more responsible management of public resources.

The Federal Ministry of Finance said the interventions underscored the need for government institutions to make better use of existing infrastructure and eliminate avoidable costs through improved planning, coordination and resource sharing.

The initiative is expected to support the Federal Government’s efforts to rein in overhead expenditure by ensuring that public institutions utilise available resources before committing additional funds to facilities and services already provided by government.

title: Tinubu’s education reforms yielding results — Alausa
description:
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, on Monday faulted opposition criticisms of the Federal Government’s education policies, insisting that the administration of President Bola Tinubu has recorded significant achievements in the sector.
Alausa said the opposition, particularly the National De
content:
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, on Monday faulted opposition criticisms of the Federal Government’s education policies, insisting that the administration of President Bola Tinubu has recorded significant achievements in the sector.

Alausa said the opposition, particularly the National Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, had “failed to acknowledge the benefits of the government’s interventions in education, accusing him of misleading Nigerians over some of the policies.”

The minister spoke while defending the administration’s education reforms, including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, infrastructure development in tertiary institutions, improved funding and efforts to address staffing shortages during a briefing at the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council headquarters in Abuja.

Responding to the criticisms, Alausa said, “What Mr Obi is saying is borne out of ignorance. He needs to read the law. This is the law of Nigeria.”
He also accused the former presidential candidate of misleading the public, saying, “If Mr Obi wants to blame me and mislead the public and Nigerians, that tells you the kind of person he is.”

Alausa said the four per cent development levy introduced under the Nigeria Tax Act was designed to provide sustainable funding for the student loan scheme, adding that 15 per cent of the proceeds was allocated to NELFUND.

He explained that the provision was captured in the law and challenged Obi to verify it before criticising the government.

The minister further argued that the administration’s interventions had improved access to tertiary education through student loans and infrastructure upgrades, while efforts were being made to address the shortage of academic staff in universities and other higher institutions.

“We have almost three million Nigerian students in tertiary education and another 200,000 in secondary education. Today, students in every single section of our country have benefited the most from President Tinubu’s transformative agenda,” he said.

Alausa also dismissed what he described as the opposition’s preoccupation with policy promises, insisting that the administration was focused on delivering practical results.

“We have enough policies in Nigeria. We want tangible benefits for Nigerians. So, every single thing about today is not about policies. What I am trying to tell you is how Nigerians are benefiting,” he said.

He also disclosed that the Federal Government had developed guidelines to improve university governance, particularly in the appointment of vice-chancellors, while committees had been established to monitor compliance and address issues such as bullying in schools.

The minister added that the government was monitoring the implementation of recommendations made by previous education panels, insisting that another cycle of reviews would not begin until outstanding recommendations had been implemented.

His comments come amid sustained criticism of the government’s handling of the education sector by opposition figures, including Obi, who has repeatedly questioned the level of public investment in education and the effectiveness of government policies.

In July, Obi faulted the Federal Government’s decision to phase out the policy separating junior and senior secondary schools, arguing that the country’s education crisis was rooted in inadequate funding, poor management and weak leadership rather than the structure of the school system.

He also criticised the 2026 education budget, which he said allocated only 6.17 per cent of total expenditure to the sector, below the 15 to 20 per cent benchmark recommended by UNESCO.

Meanwhile, the Tinubu administration has made education reforms a major part of its policy agenda, with interventions spanning basic education, technical and vocational training, digital learning, teacher development and tertiary education financing.

According to figures released by the Federal Government, NELFUND had disbursed N372.62bn to students across 319 tertiary institutions, while the administration has also reported initiatives aimed at returning out-of-school children to classrooms and improving access to technical education.

The minister’s defence also comes as the ruling All Progressives Congress intensifies its campaign to secure a second term for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections. Alausa had earlier argued that the President’s performance across sectors, including education, justified his re-election.

title: UK Sets Minimum Age Requirement For Foreigners Seeking Skilled Worker Visa - Check Below For Full Details
description: Applicants must have turned 18 before submitting a UK Skilled Worker visa application - underage applications are rejected outright regardless of qualifications or sponsorship.
content:
The United Kingdom has set a clear minimum age requirement for foreign nationals hoping to work in the country through its Skilled Worker visa route: applicants must have turned 18 before submitting their application.

According to the UK government, anyone who has not yet reached that age is ineligible to apply — regardless of any other qualifications or sponsorship arrangements they may hold.

What happens if you apply underage: applications submitted by individuals below the age of 18 are rejected outright, meaning underage applicants face an automatic disqualification from the process, even if a UK employer has offered them a job.

What this means for young applicants: for people approaching adulthood who may already have a job offer or sponsorship lined up, timing becomes a critical factor. Even with every other requirement in place, an application submitted before the applicant’s 18th birthday will not be accepted — prospective applicants in this position must wait until they meet the minimum age before applying.

Full guidance is available on the official UK government Skilled Worker visa page.

title: Romania Releases List Of 372 Occupations With Shortage Of Workers For Foreigners To Apply - Check Below For Full Details
description: Romania published 372 shortage occupations in its Official Gazette under the COR classification - truck drivers, welders, electricians, cooks, farm workers, hotel staff and many more roles foreigners can target.
content:
Romania has published an official list of 372 occupations with shortages of workers in its Official Gazette, Part I, No. 941, dated November 11, 2026, giving foreign nationals a reference for job titles they can target when seeking work in the country.

The list appears under the country’s official Classification of Occupations (COR) and covers both skilled and unskilled roles across construction, manufacturing, agriculture, transport, hospitality, healthcare, food production and administrative services.

Some of the roles on the list include: truck drivers, welders, electricians, cooks, mechanics, carpenters, bricklayers, farm workers, hotel staff, cleaners, childcare workers, nursing assistants, forklift operators, bakers, hairdressers, tailors, solar panel installers, crane operators, receptionists, accountants and many more.

How foreigners can use the list: the publication helps applicants identify occupations that match their qualifications and experience before applying. Romania runs two main employment routes for foreign nationals: one requires a Romanian employer to handle the application, while the other works through an authorised agency and is only available while the annual immigration quota has not been exhausted.

Important caveat: the inclusion of an occupation on the shortage list does not automatically guarantee a job, a work permit or a residence permit. Foreign applicants must still secure the required employment arrangements and meet Romania’s immigration conditions.

The full list is published on the government’s Work in Romania portal (workinromania.gov.ro).

title: British actor Pattinson replaces Daniel Craig as new James Bond
description:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been officially announced as the next James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig in the iconic film franchise.
Amazon MGM Studios announced the casting on Monday, November 16, 2026, through a statement published on its official website, saying Pattinson would take on the
content:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been officially announced as the next James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig in the iconic film franchise.

Amazon MGM Studios announced the casting on Monday, November 16, 2026, through a statement published on its official website, saying Pattinson would take on the role of the legendary British secret agent in its highly anticipated film.

The announcement was also confirmed on the official James Bond social media channels on Instagram and X, as verified by our correspondent.

The upcoming 26th James Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Amy Pascal and David Heyman will produce through Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films, respectively, while Tanya Lapointe will serve as executive producer.

Reacting to his appointment, Pattinson described the opportunity as the honour of a lifetime.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team,” he said.

The head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, Mike Hopkins, described the casting as a defining moment for the studio and a significant milestone in the history of the franchise.

“Today marks a defining moment for our studio and a significant milestone in the history of James Bond as we proudly introduce Robert Pattinson as the next 007,” Hopkins said.

“This iconic character has captivated audiences around the world for more than six decades, and there’s no doubt that Robert’s remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice to carry that legacy forward.

“With Denis Villeneuve at the helm, Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing, Tanya Lapointe executive producing, and a brilliant script from Steven Knight, we have a world-class creative team in place to usher in a new era of Bond, and we couldn’t be more excited about the journey ahead,” he added.

The head of film at Amazon MGM Studios, Courtenay Valenti, also welcomed Pattinson’s appointment, saying the studio was confident he would bring something special to the role.

“Few films carry the kind of anticipation that comes with James Bond, and we have strived to honor the passionate fans, the legacy, and the future of this iconic character. We are thrilled to officially welcome Robert Pattinson as our 007 and are confident he will bring something truly special to this role. Robert, Denis, Amy, David, and Tanya are embarking on an amazing adventure together,” Valenti said.

Villeneuve, who will direct the film, said he was delighted to welcome the actor after considering other talents for the role.

“Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin,” the director said.

Producers Pascal and Heyman also expressed confidence in the actor’s ability to carry on the franchise’s legacy.

“James Bond is one of the most beloved, inspiring, iconic, and yet enigmatic characters in literature and movies. The legacy of this character is in great hands with Robert Pattinson. His fearlessness as an actor, his self-deprecating wit, and his ability to continually reinvent himself make him the perfect Bond for our times,” they said.

Pattinson, who has built a career spanning more than two decades, is known for his roles in major film productions, including the Harry Potter franchise, The Twilight Saga, Tenet, The Lighthouse, Mickey 17 and The Batman.

He is also currently in production on The Batman Part II, the sequel to the 2022 film.

Amazon said its acquisition of MGM in 2022 included a catalogue of more than 4,000 films and 17,000 television shows.

In March 2025, Amazon MGM Studios also concluded a new joint venture with Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, under which the studio gained creative control of the James Bond intellectual property rights.

The post British actor Pattinson replaces Daniel Craig as new James Bond appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027 Grammys: 10 female artistes leading nominations
description:
It’s women o’clock at the 2027 Grammy Awards, as female musicians take centre stage in this year’s nominations, dominating several major categories and emerging as the biggest contenders for some of the music industry’s most prestigious honours.
From British singer-songwriter RAYE, who leads the nom
content:
It’s women o’clock at the 2027 Grammy Awards, as female musicians take centre stage in this year’s nominations, dominating several major categories and emerging as the biggest contenders for some of the music industry’s most prestigious honours.

From British singer-songwriter RAYE, who leads the nominations with an impressive 11 nods, to Spanish sensation Rosalía, American pop star Olivia Rodrigo and Nigerian singer Tems, women are making their presence felt across pop, R&B, country, dance, rock and other musical genres.

The nominations, announced on Monday, have placed several female artistes ahead of their male counterparts, with seven women featuring among the nine leading nominees.

RAYE’s 11 nominations also equal the record for the most Grammy nominations received by a female artiste in a single year, previously set by Beyoncé in 2025.

The Grammy Awards, organised by the Recording Academy, recognise outstanding achievements in the music industry, honouring artistes, songwriters, producers, composers and other music professionals.

The 69th edition of the ceremony is scheduled for February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States.

See full list: here

Key Top Nominations (The “Big Four”)

• Record of the Year: Features tracks from Olivia Dean, Ella Langley, Bruno Mars, RAYE, Olivia Rodrigo, Rosalía with Björk and Yves Tumor, and Taylor Swift.

• Album of the Year: Nominees include projects by Phoebe Bridgers, Olivia Dean, Ella Langley, Bruno Mars, RAYE, Olivia Rodrigo, Rosalía, and Taylor Swift.

• Song of the Year: Recognized songwriters include teams behind tracks by Rosalía, Ella Langley, Olivia Rodrigo, Ariana Grande, Taylor Swift, and Olivia Dean.

Here are 10 female artistes making significant impressions in the 2027 Grammy nominations:

1. RAYE – 11 nominations

British singer-songwriter RAYE leads the 2027 Grammy nominations with 11 nods, becoming the year’s most-nominated artiste.

She earned recognition in some of the awards’ biggest categories, including Album of the Year for This Music May Contain Hope, and Record and Song of the Year for her hit single, Where Is My Husband!

Her other nominations include Best Pop Solo Performance, Best Pop Vocal Album, Best Dance Pop Recording, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance and Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical.

Her 11 nominations equal Beyoncé’s record for the most Grammy nominations received by a female artiste in a single year.

2. Rosalía – Nine nominations

Spanish singer-songwriter Rosalía follows RAYE with nine nominations, making her the second-most-nominated artiste at this year’s awards.

Her album, Lux (Complete Works), earned her a nomination for Album of the Year, while her song Berghain, featuring Björk and Yves Tumor, received recognition in both Record and Song of the Year categories.

She also earned nominations for Best Pop Solo Performance, Best Alternative Performance and Best Alternative Music Album, among others.

3. Ella Langley – Seven nominations

American country singer Ella Langley is among the biggest revelations of this year’s nominations, securing seven nods.

Her song Choosin’ Texas earned her nominations for Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best Country Solo Performance, while her album Dandelion is competing for Album of the Year and Best Contemporary Country Album.

She also earned nominations for Best New Artist and Best Country Song.

Langley is the first country artiste since Bobbie Gentry in 1968 to receive nominations in all four general field categories.

4. Miranda Lambert – Seven nominations

Country music star Miranda Lambert also secured seven nominations, with her contributions as a performer, songwriter and producer earning her recognition across multiple categories.

She received nominations for Producer of the Year, Non-Classical, and Best Country Song for Choosin’ Texas and Hardwired.

Her other songwriting and collaborative contributions also feature in this year’s country nominations.

5. Olivia Rodrigo – Seven nominations

American singer-songwriter Olivia Rodrigo earned seven nominations, continuing her impressive run at the Grammys.

Her song The Cure earned nominations for Record of the Year and Song of the Year, while her album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, is competing for Album of the Year.

She also received nominations for Best Pop Solo Performance, Best Pop Vocal Album, Best Rock Performance and Best Rock Song.

6. Phoebe Bridgers – Seven nominations

American singer-songwriter Phoebe Bridgers received seven nominations, including recognition in some of the awards’ major categories.

Her album, Lost Weekend, is nominated for Album of the Year and Best Alternative Music Album.

She also earned nominations for Best Rock Performance, Best Rock Song and Best Alternative Performance.

7. Olivia Dean – Six nominations

British singer Olivia Dean earned six nominations, placing her among the leading contenders at the 2027 awards.

Her song Man I Need received nominations for Record of the Year and Song of the Year, while her album, The Art of Loving, is competing for Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album.

She also received nominations for Best Pop Solo Performance and Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance.

Earlier in November, Dean was named Apple Music artiste of the year.

8. Taylor Swift – Five nominations

American pop superstar Taylor Swift earned five nominations, including recognition in the three major general field categories.

Her album, The Life of a Showgirl, is nominated for Album of the Year, while The Fate of Ophelia received a Record of the Year nomination.

Her songwriting on I Knew It, I Knew You earned her a Song of the Year nomination, while The Life of a Showgirl, featuring Sabrina Carpenter, is nominated for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance.

She also received recognition in the Best Remixed Recording category.

9. Kehlani – Five nominations

American R&B singer Kehlani secured five nominations, featuring prominently in the R&B categories.

Her self-titled album, Kehlani, received a nomination for Best R&B Album, while her song Out the Window is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song.

She also received nominations for Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance for Sweet Nuthins, featuring Leon Thomas, and Best Melodic Rap Performance for Safe, featuring Cardi B.

10. Lainey Wilson – Five nominations

American country singer Lainey Wilson completes the list with five nominations.

She earned recognition for Best Country Solo Performance for Can’t Sit Still and Best Country Duo/Group Performance for Phone, Keys, Wallet, alongside John Mayer.

She also features in the nominations for Best Country Song, Best Country Duo/Group Performance for Light of a Clear Blue Morning alongside Dolly Parton, Miley Cyrus, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire, and Best Contemporary Christian Music Performance/Song for The Jesus I Know Now, alongside Brandon Lake.

OTHER NOTABLE FEMALE NOMINEES

Beyond the 10 leading artistes, several other women have also made significant impressions in the nominations.

Nigerian singer Tems earned four nominations, including Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for What You Need, Best African Music Performance for Big Daddy and Best Global Music Album for Love Is a Kingdom.

American singer Jill Scott received five nominations, including recognition in the R&B categories, while Ariana Grande earned four nominations.

Other notable female nominees include Madonna, Cardi B, Brandi Carlile, Kacey Musgraves, Tinashe, Zara Larsson, Doechii, Beyoncé, Lisa, Angélique Kidjo and CeCe Winans.

Beyoncé, despite receiving only one nomination this year for Best R&B Solo Performance with Morning Dew (Donk), reached a major career milestone, bringing her total Grammy nominations to 100.

content:
The National Association of Polytechnic Students, Ogun State Liaison Council, has renewed its 48-hour notice to the Ogun State Government, demanding urgent intervention in the ongoing industrial action by the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics in state-owned polytechnics.

The association, which described the prolonged disruption of academic activities as increasingly unbearable for students, called on Governor Dapo Abiodun to personally intervene in the dispute and ensure a peaceful resolution that would facilitate the immediate resumption of academic activities.

Chairman of NAPS, Ogun State Liaison Council, Joshua Opatunmibi, made the appeal on Monday during a press conference at Moshood Abiola Polytechnic, Abeokuta.

Opatunmibi announced that the association had renewed its 48-hour notice, which would commence at 12 noon on Monday, November 16, and expire at 12 noon on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

He explained that the renewed notice was intended to compel the relevant authorities to demonstrate tangible commitment towards resolving the disagreement between the state government and ASUP, stressing that students could no longer afford to lose valuable academic time.

The NAPS chairman lamented that the industrial action had disrupted academic activities across Ogun State-owned polytechnics, leaving students uncertain about their academic futures while affecting institutional calendars and opportunities for learning and personal development.

He said, “We are here today because we can no longer overlook the consequences of the ongoing industrial action by the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP) in our state.

“The academic activities of students across Ogun State-owned polytechnics have been disrupted. Academic calendars are being affected, students are uncertain about their academic future, and the time that should be invested in learning and personal development is gradually being lost.

“As the representative body of polytechnic students in Ogun State, we consider it our responsibility to speak up. Let me state our position clearly: We stand for the interest of the students.

“We are not here to fight ASUP. We are not here to fight the Ogun State Government. We are not here to create political tension or encourage violence. We are here to appeal for a solution.

“We believe lecturers deserve their legitimate welfare and entitlements. We believe our institutions deserve adequate funding. But we equally believe that students deserve uninterrupted education.These interests should not be in conflict. They should be protected together”.

The student leader expressed concern over the increasing financial burden of education on parents, guardians and students, arguing that the growing cost of accessing tertiary education should be accompanied by improved institutional stability and uninterrupted academic activities.

He observed that many political leaders occupying positions of authority today benefited from free or relatively affordable education, which provided them with opportunities to acquire qualifications, build careers and eventually attain positions of leadership.

According to him, it was unfair for the present generation to face increasing educational expenses while continuing to experience disruptions in the public institutions they depend on.

On the issues underlying the industrial dispute, Opatunmibi said the association had engaged with relevant information and ASUP representatives to understand the concerns responsible for the ongoing strike.

He identified the implementation of applicable allowances under the renegotiated 2026 Federal Government-ASUP agreement, improved funding of state-owned polytechnics, and outstanding pension deductions and contributions as some of the issues raised by the union.

The NAPS chairman specifically referenced the renegotiated agreement, reportedly signed on April 8, 2026, noting that the union was concerned about the implementation of relevant provisions, including the Consolidated Academic Teachers Allowance and Earned Academic Allowance.

He also disclosed that among the demands communicated by ASUP was an increase in the monthly subvention to each state-owned polytechnic from N5 million to N100 million.

While acknowledging that state-owned polytechnics might operate under different financial and administrative arrangements from their federal counterparts, he urged the government to clearly communicate its position on the demands and engage the union towards an acceptable resolution.

Addressing the governor, Opatunmibi said that “Your Excellency, we recognise the responsibilities that come with governing a state. We recognise that government must balance competing demands and financial obligations.

“However, education is too important to be left in prolonged uncertainty. Thousands of students across our state-owned polytechnics are looking up to the government for intervention.

title: Lagos PDP candidate promises tax exemption for teachers, doctors
description:
By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo



The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Adedeji Doherty, has promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes if elected governor, saying his administration would deploy increased federal allocations to improve healthc
content:
By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo

The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Adedeji Doherty, has promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes if elected governor, saying his administration would deploy increased federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and residents’ welfare.

Doherty made the pledge during an interview on Channels Television on Monday, where he also proposed a special tax card that would allow residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation.

He said his proposed policy would ensure that increased revenue accruing to the state translated into direct benefits for residents.

“When I am governor, I will definitely transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two people will not pay tax,” he said.

Explaining the proposed tax card, Doherty said residents who could not afford to pay N50,000 annually would be allowed to pay N10,000 and benefit from subsidised medication and transportation.

“Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation.

“This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you,” he said.

The PDP candidate also promised to introduce free education, arguing that the resources available to Lagos State would enable his administration to implement the policy.

He justified his proposed tax exemption for doctors by citing an alleged shortage of medical personnel in the state, claiming that Lagos had about 3,000 doctors against an estimated requirement of 15,000.

“We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break,” he said.

Doherty also promised improved welfare packages, including comfortable accommodation, discounted food and car loans, to encourage medical professionals practising abroad to return to Lagos.

“I want those experts in London, in America, in Germany, in Hungary. I want them to come back to Lagos and feel like they are even special. I will make them special, just like the teachers,” he said.

He described teachers as critical to the future of the state, stressing the need to provide them with adequate training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities.

On his campaign activities, the governorship candidate condemned attacks on political materials, alleging that some individuals he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge.

He said his Director-General had reported the incident to the police, adding that he planned to visit the Department of State Services (DSS) after the television interview.

Doherty also expressed support for President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms but disagreed with the manner in which the Lagos State Government was implementing the President’s agenda.

He urged state governors to ensure that residents benefited from increased federal allocations, while advocating investments in the power and manufacturing sectors to stimulate economic growth.

description:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri



ABUJA: The Supreme Court has fixed Wednesday to hear an appeal over the dispute surrounding the All Progressives Congress (APC) House of Representatives ticket for the Owo/Ose Federal Constituency in Ondo State ahead of the 2027 general elections.







The appeal seeks to
content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA: The Supreme Court has fixed Wednesday to hear an appeal over the dispute surrounding the All Progressives Congress (APC) House of Representatives ticket for the Owo/Ose Federal Constituency in Ondo State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The appeal seeks to set aside the October 9 judgment of the Abuja Division of the Court of Appeal, which directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise Mr. Abdulghani Arobo as the authentic candidate of the APC for the election.

In processes filed before the apex court, the appellant, Mr. Oluwatimehin Adelegbe, insisted that he won the primary election the APC conducted in the constituency on May 16 and was duly nominated as the party’s candidate for the seat.

The appellant faulted the Court of Appeal’s refusal of his application to tender evidence to prove that he won the primary and that his name was uploaded by the APC to INEC’s portal as the party’s candidate for the House of Reps election.

Listed as respondents in the appeal are Arobo, the APC and INEC.

According to the appellant, the appellate court, in deciding the appeal marked CA/ABJ/CV/1235/2026, wrongly affirmed an earlier verdict that Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja delivered on August 5, which recognised Arobo as the APC flag bearer.

In the 18 grounds of appeal filed before the Supreme Court through his team of lawyers led by Mr. Joseph Daudu, SAN, Adelegbe contended that the concurrent judgments of the lower courts occasioned a miscarriage of justice against him.

Alleging that he was denied a fair hearing, the appellant told the apex court that he was not joined as an interested party in the suit that led to his removal as the APC candidate for the election.

The appellant further contended that the refusal of the court to grant a motion on notice, brought pursuant to Order 4 Rule 2 of the Court of Appeal Rules 2021, for leave to adduce fresh or additional evidence, proved fatal to his case.

He identified the additional evidence sought to be tendered as statutory public documents, which included the APC’s official candidate forwarding letter dated 26 June 2026; his Form EC9 affidavit; the INEC Candidate Nomination Portal (ICNP) submission receipt dated 11 July 2026; and a certified true copy (CTC) of the official APC Election Committee result sheet, showing that he polled 13,094 votes.

Adelegbe maintained that the essence of the application was that, had Arobo joined him as a party in the suit leading to the High Court judgment, he would have provided sufficient evidence showing that he was the person declared the winner of the APC primary for the Owo/Ose Federal Constituency.

He argued that, by Order 4 Rule 2 of the Court of Appeal Rules 2021, the appellate court has full discretionary power to receive further evidence on questions of fact, particularly where such evidence could not have been produced at the trial court as a result of his exclusion, through no fault of his, or where special grounds exist.

Besides, while accusing Arobo of deliberately excluding him from the proceedings before the trial court, the appellant contended that unlawful exclusion and non-joinder of a necessary and indispensable party at the lower court constitute the highest threshold of “special grounds” under Order 4 Rule 2, since a party who was unaware of a proceeding cannot be faulted for not tendering documents during a trial from which he was excluded.

On another ground of appeal, he argued that the Court of Appeal erred in law and reached a perverse decision when it affirmed the trial court’s judgment, which was delivered in total breach of Section 36(1) of the 1999 Constitution and without joining him as an indispensable and necessary party, upon the erroneous finding that no final declaration or return had been made in his favour.

He said the appellate court erred in law when it held that he was bound by the trial court’s proceedings under the doctrine of “standing by” and that his interests were adequately represented and defended by the APC.

It was further the position of the appellant that the doctrine of estoppel by “standing by” strictly requires clear proof that the non-party had full, actual notice of the institution and pendency of the suit, possessed a direct interest in the subject matter, and consciously made an informed election to stand by and allow others to fight his cause on his behalf.

Adelegbe noted that he deposed in his uncontroverted affidavits that he was never served with any documents relating to the suit filed by Arobo, on which the trial court’s judgment was based, and hence he “had absolutely no actual or constructive knowledge of the suit until after final judgment was delivered behind his back on 5th August 2026, thereby making it legally impossible to invoke the doctrine of ‘standing by’ against him.”

He added that the Court of Appeal erred in law when it held that Arobo was justified in bypassing the final appellate organ of the APC, the National Working Committee (NWC), after waiting 11 days.

The appellant also faulted the appellate court for holding that Arobo’s suit at the trial court was properly commenced by originating summons under Paragraph 7(1) of the Pre-Election Practice Directions 2026, despite grave, hostile and conflicting factual allegations raised in the suit.

He is, therefore, praying the apex court to issue an order affirming his candidacy and directing INEC to recognise, publish and maintain his name, profile and nomination particulars as the duly nominated candidate of the APC for the constituency.

The post Ondo: Supreme Court fixes Wednesday to hear appeal over APC Reps ticket appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Kaduna varsity unions suspend strike, insist on demands
description:
The Joint Action Committee of Kaduna State University has suspended its one-week warning strike following discussions with key stakeholders in the Kaduna State Government and the university management.
The JAC Chairperson, Sa’adiyya Mustapha, announced the suspension while addressing journalists on
content:
The Joint Action Committee of Kaduna State University has suspended its one-week warning strike following discussions with key stakeholders in the Kaduna State Government and the university management.

The JAC Chairperson, Sa’adiyya Mustapha, announced the suspension while addressing journalists on Monday, saying the decision was taken to allow ongoing negotiations over the unions’ grievances to continue.

The committee comprises the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities, the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions and the National Association of Academic Technologists.

Mustapha stressed that the suspension did not mean the unions had surrendered or abandoned their demands but demonstrated their willingness to resolve the dispute through dialogue.

“We have gone on a one-week strike and have now decided to suspend it, not because we are surrendering, but for the good of this university.

“Several key stakeholders in this administration have made efforts to dialogue with us, and we have seen reason in those discussions. We have therefore decided to suspend the strike to show that we are willing to support the government and give dialogue a chance,” she said.

The JAC chairperson appreciated members for their support and resilience during the industrial action, explaining that the strike was intended to draw the government’s attention to their unresolved grievances.

She reaffirmed the unions’ support for Governor Uba Sani, recalling previous salary-related challenges faced by university workers and the governor’s intervention in clearing outstanding payments.

Mustapha recalled that university workers received half salaries in 2017, while their May 2023 salaries were not paid. She added that the outstanding payments were presented to the governor and subsequently cleared after he assumed office.

“Because of what he has done for us, we cannot say we are not in support of him. We support the governor and are solidly behind him.

“However, what happened to JAC was what we were unhappy with, and that was why we decided to embark on the strike,” she said.

She expressed optimism that the ongoing negotiations would lead to government intervention and a resolution of the dispute, urging the university management, governing council and state government to ensure fairness and equity in their dealings with staff.

PUNCH Online reports that the industrial action followed a seven-day ultimatum issued by the three unions on November 2, 2026, to the Kaduna State Government and the university management over outstanding welfare demands and the alleged failure to implement agreements reached with non-teaching staff unions.

The unions demanded the immediate implementation of the 2026 Federal Government/non-teaching staff agreement, particularly the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance, payment of approved wage awards and the Federal Government’s N70,000 monthly transport support for workers for six months.

Other demands included respect for university autonomy, provision of group life insurance for staff and settlement of outstanding allowances and entitlements.

The unions had warned that failure to address their grievances within seven days would compel them to embark on industrial action.

The warning strike commenced on November 10 after the unions said the ultimatum expired without a response, invitation for dialogue or concrete action from the authorities.

The development came despite an interim order issued by the National Industrial Court in Abuja on November 5 restraining the three unions from embarking on industrial action pending the determination of a suit instituted by the university, its governing council and vice-chancellor.

The court, presided over by Justice E. D. Subilim, adjourned the hearing of the application to November 18, 2026.

The dispute also followed earlier disagreements over the Kaduna State Government’s decision to implement the 2025 Federal Government agreement with university academic staff without extending similar benefits to non-academic workers.

In September, the JAC had protested what it described as discriminatory implementation of the agreement, insisting that non-teaching staff should not be excluded from benefits arising from negotiations with university-based unions.

The unions had also raised concerns over outstanding earned allowances, excess workload allowances, promotion arrears, pension arrears, group life insurance and the implementation of salary adjustments.

title: Only four MDAs score above 50% in fiscal responsibility index
description:
…FRC raises annual surplus remittances from N300m to N2trn



By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief



Only four Federal Government Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) scored above 50 per cent in the 2026 Fiscal Responsibility Index (FRI), raising concerns over compliance with statutory public fi
content:
…FRC raises annual surplus remittances from N300m to N2trn

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

Only four Federal Government Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) scored above 50 per cent in the 2026 Fiscal Responsibility Index (FRI), raising concerns over compliance with statutory public financial management requirements.

The four MDAs are the Federal Ministries of Water Resources; Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy; Finance; and Housing and Urban Development.

The Acting Chairman of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), Mr Charles Abana, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja while presenting the 2026 Fiscal Responsibility Index report.

He called on MDAs to improve compliance with the provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, stressing the need to strengthen accountability and transparency in public financial management.

Under Pillar I of the assessment, which focuses on policy-based budgeting, the Ministry of Finance topped the list with 90 per cent, followed by Water Resources with 75 per cent, Health with 70.1 per cent, Innovation and Science Technology with 70 per cent, and Defence with 68 per cent.

Other ministries recorded lower scores, including Aviation with 28.2 per cent, Information with 36.7 per cent, Justice with 40 per cent, Police Affairs with 40 per cent, Works with 40 per cent, Youth Development with 40 per cent and Education with 48.4 per cent.

Under Pillar II, which assesses budget-policy linkages, comprehensiveness and transparency, only the Ministries of Water Resources and Finance scored above 50 per cent.

The Ministries of Police Affairs and Labour recorded the lowest scores in the category, with 6.7 per cent and 12.8 per cent, respectively.

Presenting the report, Abana described the exercise as a significant milestone in the commission’s efforts to deepen the institutionalisation of fiscal responsibility principles across the Federal Government.

He said the index was designed to assess the performance of MDAs in implementing statutory public financial management requirements and identify areas requiring improvement.

“The Fiscal Responsibility Index is not merely an assessment document or an administrative scorecard.

“It is an empirical, evidence-based benchmarking instrument designed to measure, score and rank Federal Ministries, Departments and Agencies according to their levels of compliance with established public financial management obligations,” he said.

The index assesses institutional compliance with statutory requirements relating to public financial management practices, budgeting thresholds, procurement transparency and revenue remittance guidelines under the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, and other applicable frameworks.

The 2026 edition evaluates the public financial management performance of federal MDAs across three consecutive financial years: 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Abana also disclosed that some ministries failed to complete the assessment process.

They include the Ministries of Transport; Agriculture and Food Security; Foreign Affairs; Petroleum Resources; Environment; and Industry, Trade and Investment.

He said the commission received and verified physical and electronic documentary evidence submitted by participating MDAs up to the September 4, 2026 deadline.

According to him, the final verification process ensured that supporting documents were examined, outstanding information considered and the data used in preparing the report properly validated.

The FRC boss described the presentation as an important accountability exercise, urging MDAs to embrace the findings and demonstrate a genuine commitment to improving their performance.

He said public institutions must move beyond preparing reports and submitting returns to ensuring that compliance was reflected in actual institutional practices and measurable public value.

Abana added that the findings should encourage stronger collaboration among oversight institutions, improve public confidence in government financial management systems and promote best practices across the Federal Public Service.

Meanwhile, the FRC chairman disclosed that the commission had increased annual independent revenue generated through operating surplus remittances and other internally generated revenue from about N300 million in 2010 to over N2 trillion.

He, however, lamented that the commission continued to face challenges, including limited enforcement powers, inadequate funding, staff shortages and insufficient accommodation, despite more than 16 years of operation.

“The commission has been challenged with limited enforcement powers, inadequate funding, staff shortages, lack of adequate accommodation after over 16 years of its establishment.

“Yet the Commission through the payment of Operating surplus and other IGR has increased independent revenue from just about N300M in 2010 to over N2 trillion annually,” he said.

He called on the Federal Government to strengthen the commission’s enforcement powers, amend the Fiscal Responsibility Act and increase its funding to enable it to discharge its responsibilities more effectively.

The post Only four MDAs score above 50% in fiscal responsibility index appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as his National Leader, saying he is contesting against the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to ensure that the President’s Renewed Hope agenda is properly implemented in the state.

Doherty stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, where he explained why he was seeking to become Lagos governor despite his support for Tinubu and his administration’s national agenda.

He said he supported Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda but disagreed with the way the APC-led government in Lagos State was implementing it.

According to him, the failure to translate the President’s vision into reality in Lagos had contributed to political tensions, including alleged thuggery and the destruction of campaign materials.

He said, “I am going against the APC governorship candidate in Lagos because they are not doing what they are supposed to do concerning the APC/Mr President’s agenda for the country.

“When you do not crystallise the dream that is being made by your boss, then definitely all these fallouts of thuggery, removing of banners, tearing of posters and things like that, definitely is what is going to happen because you are trying to cover up your inadequacies in government.”

The PDP candidate further described Tinubu as his National Leader, stressing that his support for the President and the Renewed Hope agenda did not extend to the way the agenda was being implemented in Lagos.

He said, “Basically, you know? I’m going to support what I support fully, what my National Leader is doing. I support fully the Renewed Hope agenda, which is the agenda for the entire country, but I do not support the agenda as it is being materialised and crystallised in Lagos State.”

title: UK actor Robert Pattinson to be new James Bond
description:
British actor Robert Pattinson was Monday named as the new James Bond, stepping into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy.



“Amazon MGM Studios have announced that Robert Pattinson will take on the iconic role of James Bond,” the studio said on the official 007.com website.
content:
British actor Robert Pattinson was Monday named as the new James Bond, stepping into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy.

“Amazon MGM Studios have announced that Robert Pattinson will take on the iconic role of James Bond,” the studio said on the official 007.com website.

Pattinson would succeed Daniel Craig as the super-suave MI6 agent, “ushering in a new era for one of cinema’s most celebrated characters”, the studios added.

It will be the first Bond film since long-term Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson stepped back and Amazon took creative control of the franchise, after acquiring the series’ parent company MGM.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said.

“To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” he added in a statement.

Amazon MGM also announced that Oscar-nominated Canadian director Denis Villeneuve, behind such box-office hits as the “Dune” films, would be directing the next Bond movie from a script by “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight.

Knight said in May that Amazon has given him a licence to play with the legendary secret agent created by author Ian Fleming.

“Bond has been bulletproof. People have been able to make mistakes and variations, and the character has survived,” Knight told Screen magazine at the Cannes Film Festival.

“Because the core of it is like a diamond. You can’t touch it,” he added.

Knight also told reporters that he has done research with “the SAS and even more secret outfits” for his reinvention of the next 007 movie.

Pattinson, 40, started out in amateur dramatics before getting his break in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire” (2005) as Cedric Diggory, a champion for Hogwarts.

But he rocketed to global fame for his part as brooding teen heartthrob in the romantic vampire saga “Twilight”.

– ‘Extremely inventive’ –

He was paid a reported $2 million for his lead in “Twilight” (2008), but by the time the saga wrapped up with the two parts of “Breaking Dawn” in 2011 and 2012, he was reportedly on $12.5 million plus 7.5 percent of the box office take.

One of his first forays into edgier cinema came with 2012 drama “Cosmopolis”, in which he portrayed a self-destructive currency speculator as his life falls apart.

The film was directed by legendary US auteur David Cronenberg, who described the actor as “extremely inventive”.

He received critical acclaim after later switching to more independent films and was nominated for best actor at the Cannes festival in 2017 for neo-grindhouse crime caper “Good Time” by New York-based brothers Josh and Ben Safdie.

In 2022, Amazon bought storied Hollywood studio MGM, which held distribution rights to Bond’s extensive back catalogue.

But it was not until early 2025 that the company struck a deal with longtime Bond producers Wilson and Broccoli to obtain full creative control.

The franchise had been closely guarded by the Broccoli family since 1962’s “Dr. No”.

They famously insisted on preserving the integrity of the Bond character and brand, resisting spin-offs and licensing that many industry experts expect to see following Amazon’s takeover.

The post UK actor Robert Pattinson to be new James Bond appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Argentine footballer Abel Núñez dies after head injury during match
description:
An Argentine footballer, Abel Núñez, has died days after suffering a head injury during a match while representing Ezeiza Football Club.
The club announced his death in a statement released on Sunday, expressing sadness over the loss of the young player, who had undergone surgery after the incident.
content:
An Argentine footballer, Abel Núñez, has died days after suffering a head injury during a match while representing Ezeiza Football Club.

The club announced his death in a statement released on Sunday, expressing sadness over the loss of the young player, who had undergone surgery after the incident.

“After suffering a hard blow during a match, proudly wearing our Ezeiza shirt, we deeply regret his departure,” the club said.

It added, “Today football is in the background. We are overwhelmed by the pain of saying goodbye to a colleague, a young man full of dreams and hopes, who was part of our family.”

Reports said Núñez was playing for Ezeiza’s fifth-division team in the Argentine Football Association’s Juveniles C Copa de Plata competition when he was struck in the head by a ball during a match against Deportivo Muñiz.

The incident reportedly occurred at Club Atlético La Sonia in José C. Paz, where Núñez collapsed on the pitch and received immediate medical attention before being taken to hospital for surgery.

Days before announcing his death, Ezeiza had appealed to its community to support the player as he underwent treatment following the injury.

In an earlier statement, the club said Núñez had suffered a serious blow to the head that required surgery, urging players, families, coaches and supporters to join in prayers for his recovery.

Following his death, the club extended its condolences to his family, friends, teammates and loved ones, saying he would always remain part of its family.

title: Tinubu: 1,000 terrorists convicted, 2,000 prosecuted
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that more than 1,000 terrorists have been convicted, while over 2,000 suspected terrorists are currently undergoing prosecution as part of his administration’s efforts to dismantle terrorist networks across the country.







The President
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that more than 1,000 terrorists have been convicted, while over 2,000 suspected terrorists are currently undergoing prosecution as part of his administration’s efforts to dismantle terrorist networks across the country.

The President also said Nigerian security forces had killed or arrested four of eight identified senior global terrorist leaders, describing the development as evidence of the country’s growing capacity to dismantle terrorist command structures.

Tinubu, who was represented by the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, made the disclosures on Monday at the opening of the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence (CDI) Annual Conference in Abuja.

He said the number of convictions and ongoing prosecutions placed Nigeria among countries with high rates of terrorism-related prosecutions globally.

Highlighting the operational successes recorded by security agencies, the President cited the elimination of senior Islamic State leader, Abu Bilal al-Minuki, in May 2026, as well as the arrests of other prominent terrorist figures.

According to him, the operations also targeted Ahmed Ohida’s ISWAP southern expansion network, while Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa were arrested in 2025.

“Recent operational successes demonstrate our growing capacity to dismantle terrorist leadership, disrupt expansion networks and deny violent groups freedom of action.

“Under this administration, four of eight identified senior terrorist leaders have been killed or arrested. These gains include action against Ahmed Ohida’s ISWAP southern expansion network, the elimination of senior Islamic State leader Abu Bilal al-Minuki in May 2026, and the arrests of Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa in 2025,” he said.

Tinubu, however, identified the remaining four senior terrorist figures as Ba Shuwa of ISWAP, Abdullahi Oro of IS-Sahel, Sadiku of JAS in the North-Central region and Bakura Doro in the Lake Chad Basin.

He said security agencies were sustaining operations against the remaining leaders and their networks, adding that senior bandit leaders, including Halilu Sububu, had also been killed alongside several of their fighters.

On developments in the Niger Delta, the President disclosed that incidents of illegal oil bunkering and vandalism of critical oil and gas installations declined from 32 in the first quarter of 2026 to 21 in the second quarter and 17 in the third quarter.

He said the figures represented a 46.88 per cent reduction between the first and third quarters.

Tinubu added that crude oil and condensate production averaged approximately 1.68 million barrels per day in August 2026, stressing the need to sustain the protection of the country’s energy assets and revenue sources.

He attributed the security gains to improved intelligence sharing and coordinated operations among the Department of State Services (DSS), Armed Forces, Police and other security agencies.

The President said the administration would consolidate the gains and sustain pressure on criminal and terrorist networks, particularly ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“Every Nigerian must be able to live, work and exercise their democratic rights in safety,” he said.

On the changing nature of security threats, Tinubu said technological advancements, particularly artificial intelligence, machine learning, cyber capabilities and unmanned systems, were creating new opportunities for intelligence gathering and security operations.

He said such technologies could help security agencies detect patterns, map criminal networks and generate early warnings of potential threats.

The President called for the integration of AI-assisted analysis, geospatial intelligence and unmanned surveillance through secure and interoperable systems capable of translating information into timely operational decisions.

He, however, cautioned that artificial intelligence outputs must be verified through accountable human judgement, while data protection and cybersecurity safeguards must be incorporated into the systems.

“Technology must strengthen the trusted human intelligence on which effective security depends,” he said.

Tinubu further disclosed that he had directed the Special Adviser on Homeland Security, Major General A.A. Famadewa (rtd), to coordinate the preparation of a Comprehensive National Threat Assessment and a Five-Year Rolling Strategic Defence Operations Plan.

He said the initiative was aimed at placing accurate, integrated and forward-looking intelligence at the centre of Nigeria’s defence planning.

The President also emphasised the importance of collaboration among the Armed Forces, Defence Intelligence Agency, DSS, National Intelligence Agency, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other relevant institutions.

He said intelligence cooperation must extend to regional and international partners, subnational entities, technology companies and research institutions.

Tinubu listed the United States, France, the United Kingdom, China, the United Arab Emirates, Türkiye and Nigeria’s African neighbours among countries with which his administration had strengthened security partnerships.

He pledged to deepen intelligence sharing, training and technological cooperation while safeguarding Nigeria’s sovereignty and national interest.

The President also urged Nigeria’s Defence Advisers and Attachés abroad to strengthen strategic intelligence and defence relationships with their host countries and international partners.

He called on State Office Coordinators to intensify collaboration with local security agencies to improve intelligence gathering and coordination.

Tinubu commended the Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lieutenant General Emmanuel Akomaye Parker Undiandeye, and his team for their leadership and contributions to strengthening defence intelligence and strategic cooperation.

In his remarks, the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, commended intelligence personnel for their professionalism and contributions to national security.

Musa urged them to remain proactive, stressing that credible, timely and actionable intelligence was critical to successful military operations.

He also reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to indigenous defence production, describing local manufacturing as essential to developing sustainable military capabilities.

Similarly, the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, described intelligence as fundamental to operational planning, strategic decision-making and effective military responses.

Oluyede called for increased investment in artificial intelligence, advanced data analytics, geospatial intelligence and unmanned systems.

He said the Armed Forces would continue to prioritise intelligence integration, capacity development and technological innovation.

The CDS stressed the need to shift security operations from largely reactive responses to proactive, intelligence-led engagements capable of anticipating and disrupting threats before they materialise.

The conference, organised by the Defence Intelligence Agency, is themed, “Optimising Intelligence through Technological Innovations for Effective Strategic Operations in a Complex Security Environment.”

Vanguard Newspaper

The post Tinubu: 1,000 terrorists convicted, 2,000 prosecuted appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: UniAbuja land cut approved by Wike’s predecessor – FCTA
description:
The Federal Capital Territory Administration has defended its decision to reduce the land allocated to the University of Abuja, saying the action was based on recommendations made by a joint committee established in 2016 by the administration of former FCT Minister Mohammed Bello.
The FCTA said the
content:
The Federal Capital Territory Administration has defended its decision to reduce the land allocated to the University of Abuja, saying the action was based on recommendations made by a joint committee established in 2016 by the administration of former FCT Minister Mohammed Bello.

The FCTA said the committee, comprising representatives of the administration and the university, had recommended that the institution’s landholding of over 11,000 hectares be reduced to 100 hectares in line with the National Universities Commission’s recommended size for universities.

The administration’s position followed a protest by the university’s academic and non-academic staff, students and alumni on Monday over the reduction of its original 11,824.04 hectares of land to 4,685 hectares by the administration of the incumbent FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike.

In a statement issued on Monday by the minister’s Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, the FCTA described the protest as misplaced, insisting that Wike merely implemented a decision taken by his predecessor.

According to the statement, the joint committee was inaugurated on November 10, 2016, to examine the university’s land size, encroachment by indigenous settlers, illegal developments around its Gwagwalada mini-campus and the issuance of title documents for the institution’s two campuses.

Olayinka disclosed that five of the committee’s 12 members were representatives of the university, namely Prof Otaki Alanana, Prof A. Mallam, Mohamed Kassim, A.E. Ripite and Sadiq O. Shuaibu.

He said the committee subsequently recommended that the university’s landholding of over 11,000 hectares was far beyond the size recommended by the NUC, adding that the 100-hectare recommendation was approved by Bello.

“It is on record that on November 10, 2016, the then FCT Minister inaugurated a Joint Committee of FCTA and UNIABUJA on Land and Sundry Issues. The committee was to look into the UNIABUJA land size vis encroachment by indigenous settlers, encroachment on the Gwagwalada Mini Campus land by illegal developers and issuance of titles for the two campuses of the university with their actual land size.

“The committee recommended, amongst others, that the land area of over 11,000 hectares of the main campus was far beyond the recommended size by the National University Commission (NUC), and that the recommended size of 100 hectares by the NUC be given to the university.

“Report of the committee was approved by the immediate past FCT Minister, Mohammed Musa Bello, and going by the committee’s recommendation, only 100 hectares of land ought to be given to UNIABUJA,” the statement partly read.

Olayinka, however, said Wike approved 4,519.80 hectares for the university, rather than the 100 hectares recommended by the committee.

It added that the retained land could accommodate more than 80,000 buildings, using a plot size of 500 square metres.

The FCTA also accused the university of allocating portions of its land to individuals and corporate organisations without consulting the administration, citing the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission as one of the beneficiaries.

The statement questioned the rationale behind the university’s insistence on retaining more than 11,000 hectares, asking what significant expansion the institution had undertaken in its 38 years of existence to justify such a land requirement.

“Questions to ask the protesters, particularly the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), Students’ Union Government (SUG) and the university’s alumni association are; were they unaware that the university had representatives in the committee that recommended the reduction of the UNIABUJA land to 100 hectares in line with the NUC recommendation?

“Where in the civilised world is a university built on over 11,000 hectares of land, on which over 220,000 houses can be built at 500 square meters per plot?

“If the government that owns a university chooses to reduce the size of its land on which no structure has been built in the school’s 38 years of existence, what effect will that have on ASUU, SSANU and NASU? Will that affect the payment of their salaries? Will it affect the students in terms of their studies?,” Olayinka asked.

The media aide urged the academic unions to be honest and clarify their interest in a land dispute between the administration and the management.

The FCTA’s defence comes amid an escalating dispute between the administration and the university community over the ownership, control and proposed redistribution of portions of the institution’s land in Giri District, Abuja.

The controversy dates back to June 2025, when Wike announced that the administration had reclaimed about 7,000 hectares of land from the university, accusing the institution of laying claim to an extensive portion of government land without adequate documentation.

At the inauguration of access roads in Giri District, the minister directed relevant agencies to carve out about 4,000 hectares for the university, while the remaining portions would be made available for other developments.

Wike had argued that the university could not retain such an extensive landholding without developing it, particularly as the FCTA sought to open up the district for infrastructure and institutional development.

However, the university’s management and ASUU have maintained that the original land allocation was legitimate and necessary for the institution’s long-term development, including academic expansion, agricultural research and other infrastructure.

The university’s Pro-Chancellor, Senator Olanrewaju Tejuoso, had also argued that much of the land left for the institution comprised rocky hills, raising questions about the actual amount of land available for development.

The dispute has also taken a legal dimension, with the university instituting Suit No. FCT/HC/CV/3500/2026 before the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Maitama.

In the suit, Justice F.E. Messiri, on August 18, 2026, reportedly ordered parties to maintain the status quo ante bellum concerning Plot No. 1, Giri District, pending the determination of the substantive matter.

ASUU has subsequently accused the FCTA of violating the court order through alleged allocations of portions of the disputed land to private individuals and companies on September 26, 2026.

The post UniAbuja land cut approved by Wike’s predecessor – FCTA appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed as false and misleading a viral social media video alleging that the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be remotely logged out before the end of voting.







The commission clarified that only the poll official operati
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed as false and misleading a viral social media video alleging that the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be remotely logged out before the end of voting.

The commission clarified that only the poll official operating the device has the authority to log in or log out of the BVAS during voter accreditation and the subsequent result upload process.

INEC disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X platform on Monday, following the circulation of a video on Instagram alleging that voters would be logged out of the system before the conclusion of voting.

Describing the claim as fabricated, the commission said each polling unit was assigned unique login credentials, which were issued to the Presiding Officer on the eve of an election.

According to INEC, the credentials enable the poll official to log into the BVAS for voter accreditation on election day and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet at the close of polls.

“The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated.

It stressed that there was no provision for any external individual or authority to remotely log out the device.

The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost, explaining that the IReV application had been upgraded to accommodate offline uploads.

INEC said the enhancement followed experiences during the 2023 general election, when some poll officials were held hostage at their polling units because they could not upload results due to poor or non-existent network connectivity.

It explained that the offline upload feature allows poll officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload polling unit result sheets in the presence of stakeholders at the polling unit.

According to the commission, such results remain securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

” As Poll Officials proceed from the polling unit to the Ward Collation Centre and the device reconnects to the internet, the result sheet is automatically transmitted to the IReV portal without requiring any further manual intervention,” it said.

INEC assured Nigerians that the BVAS and IReV systems operate in accordance with established procedures designed to protect the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process.

The commission urged members of the public to disregard the video, refrain from creating or sharing unverified information and rely on its official communication channels for accurate information.

It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections.

The post INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends appeared first on Vanguard News.
