title: [PHOTOS] Nigeria Re-Elected To Council Of International Telecommunication Union
description: Nigeria has been re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) at the ongoing conference in Doha, Qatar.With this development, Nigeria retains its seat on the council for the term 2027-2030.As part of Nigeria’s campaign for re-election, the Ambassador to Qatar Ma
content:
Nigeria has been re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) at the ongoing conference in Doha, Qatar.

With this development, Nigeria retains its seat on the council for the term 2027-2030.

Established in 1865 with headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, the ITU is the United Nations specialised agency for information and communication technologies (ICTs).

It brings together 194 member states and over 1,000 sector members, which include companies, universities and international organisations.

Nigeria became a member in 1961.

Nigeria’s participation was coordinated by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu.

The Nigerian delegation was led by the Minister of Communication, Innovation and Digital Economy, Bosun Tijani.

Nigeria’s Ambassador to the State of Qatar, Mahmood Yakubu, served as the Deputy Head of Delegation, supported by the Executive Vice Chairman of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), Aminu Maida; Nigeria’s Permanent Mission to Geneva, led by Innocent Imejuo; officials of the Ministry of Communication (NCC) and staff of the Nigerian Embassy in Doha.

title: Rivers Polytechnic shuts down as ASUP declares indefinite strike over unpaid allowances
description:
Academic activities have been disrupted at Kenule Beeson Saro-Wiwa Polytechnic, Bori, Rivers State, following an indefinite strike declared by the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP) over the state government’s failure to implement agreed academic allowances.
The ASUP chapter of the institut
content:
Academic activities have been disrupted at Kenule Beeson Saro-Wiwa Polytechnic, Bori, Rivers State, following an indefinite strike declared by the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP) over the state government’s failure to implement agreed academic allowances.

The ASUP chapter of the institution announced its participation in the industrial action on Monday, November 16, 2026, in compliance with a directive from the union’s national leadership instructing academic staff in affected state-owned polytechnics to withdraw their services.

In a statement issued on Monday and signed by the chapter’s Chairman, Engr. Dr Bariakawaadoo Bere, the union said the strike was intended to compel the Rivers State Government to implement the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Earned Academic Allowance (EAA).

The union explained that the outstanding allowances were meant for lecturers, instructors and technologists working at the institution.

ASUP recalled that the Federal Government and the union signed an agreement on April 8, 2026, providing for the implementation of CATA and EAA for academic staff in the polytechnic sector, effective January 2026.

According to the union, the Federal Government approved the allowances as a template for academic staff across polytechnics nationwide, adding that the agreement had been fully implemented in federal government-owned institutions.

It noted, however, that state governments were expected to extend the same benefits to academic staff in polytechnics and colleges of technology under their respective control.

The union said its national leadership had made several efforts to secure the Rivers State Government’s compliance through two separate letters dated August 10 and September 21, 2026, addressed to the governor.

In the letters, ASUP appealed to the governor to extend the approved allowances to academic staff of Kenule Beeson Saro-Wiwa Polytechnic and other affected state-owned institutions, arguing that their lecturers, instructors and technologists performed similar professional duties under comparable working conditions as their counterparts in federal institutions.

The union, however, expressed disappointment over what it described as the low level of response from the state government.

It also questioned what it considered unequal treatment of academic staff in the state’s tertiary institutions, noting that the same Rivers State Government had implemented the Federal Government-ASUU agreement for university lecturers in the state.

ASUP argued that both categories of academic workers faced similar economic realities and should therefore receive comparable consideration.

In a further attempt to resolve the disagreement, the union said its National Executive Council, at its 118th meeting held on October 22, 2026, directed the issuance of a 15-day ultimatum to the Rivers State Government.

The ultimatum commenced on October 27 and expired on November 10, 2026.

The union alleged that neither the state government nor any of its agencies contacted or invited its national or state leadership for discussions or negotiations throughout the period.

Following the expiration of the ultimatum without a resolution, the national leadership of ASUP, on November 12, formally notified the Rivers State Governor of its decision to embark on industrial action beginning Monday, November 16.

Consequently, the Kenpoly Bori chapter declared its full participation in the strike, insisting that the action was necessary to secure the implementation of the CATA and EAA provisions of the April 8 agreement.

The development puts pressure on the Rivers State Government to address the demands of the polytechnic workers and engage the union to resolve the dispute.

As of Monday, when the statement was issued, the union had commenced the industrial action, with no agreement announced to resolve the disagreement.

The post Rivers Polytechnic shuts down as ASUP declares indefinite strike over unpaid allowances appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 14 residents remain in captivity as bandits abduct 12 in fresh attack on Kaduna community
description:
Suspected bandits have abducted 12 residents of Kurmin Wali community in Afogo Ward, Kajuru Local Government Area of Kaduna State, in a fresh attack that has left nine people in captivity.
The attack reportedly took place on Sunday, November 15, 2026, when armed men stormed the community at about 9:
content:
Suspected bandits have abducted 12 residents of Kurmin Wali community in Afogo Ward, Kajuru Local Government Area of Kaduna State, in a fresh attack that has left nine people in captivity.

The attack reportedly took place on Sunday, November 15, 2026, when armed men stormed the community at about 9:14am and whisked away 12 residents.

The village head, Isiaku Danazumi, who confirmed the incident on Monday, said three of the abducted residents had escaped from their captors and returned home.

He added that the remaining nine victims were still being held by the kidnappers as of Monday.

He explained that the nine victims, alongside five other residents abducted in two separate attacks in October, brought the total number of people still being held by the bandits to 14.

“Yes, the incident happened on Sunday around 9:14am. Twelve people were abducted by the bandits, but three returned, while the remaining nine are still with them.

“But on October 2, 2026, two people were also abducted during the rainy season. Again, on October 10, three other people were abducted. So, in total, 14 of our people are with the bandits in the bush,” he said.

The traditional ruler expressed concern over the recurring abductions, saying that although the relevant authorities had been notified, no concrete action had been taken to secure the victims’ release.

He further disclosed that some security personnel visited the community on Sunday after the attackers had fled but reportedly left less than an hour after arriving.

The latest attack has heightened concerns over the security situation in Kurmin Wali, which attracted national attention in January 2026 when suspected bandits abducted more than 80 residents during a church service.

The mass abduction sparked widespread outrage and renewed calls for urgent government intervention to protect vulnerable communities in Kaduna State.

As of the time of filing this report, the Kaduna State Police Command and the Ministry of Internal Security and Home Affairs had yet to issue official statements on Sunday’s attack.

title: 2027: Court of Appeal warns elections tribunal staff against bribery
description:
The President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem, has warned secretaries and registry staff of election petition tribunals against accepting bribes or compromising judicial processes ahead of the 2027 general elections.
She warned that any staff found engaging in corrupt practices
content:
The President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem, has warned secretaries and registry staff of election petition tribunals against accepting bribes or compromising judicial processes ahead of the 2027 general elections.

She warned that any staff found engaging in corrupt practices would be sanctioned, stressing that the assignment was a call to national service and not an opportunity for personal enrichment.

Dongban-Mensem gave the warning on Monday at the opening of a two-day capacity-building workshop on the theme, “Modern Registry Practices for Effective Election Petition Tribunal Administration”, in Abuja.

The Court of Appeal President said the exercise was designed to prepare tribunal staff for the administrative demands of handling electoral disputes.

She described the registry as the engine room of every tribunal, noting that its efficiency, integrity and transparency were critical to the timely administration of electoral justice.

The PUNCH reports that the presidential and National Assembly elections would hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections were scheduled for February 6, 2027.

The Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, inaugurated 375 judicial officers from different jurisdictions across the country last week to serve on election petition tribunals ahead of the 2027 general elections.

(https://punchng.com/2027-cjn-swears-in-tribunal-judges-warns-against-pressure/)

According to the PCA, the responsibilities of registry staff include receiving and filing petitions, serving processes on parties, issuing hearing notices, preparing records of proceedings and orders, preserving tribunal documents and compiling records, adding that the registry’s performance directly affects the efficiency of tribunals and public confidence in the judicial process.

Citing Sections 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, Dongban-Mensem said the President of the Court of Appeal was empowered to constitute election petition tribunals in every state of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory, among others.

Dongban-Mensem charged the tribunal secretaries to familiarise themselves with the Electoral Act 2026 and the Election Petition Tribunal Proceedings Practice Direction 2026, warning that ignorance of the relevant provisions could expose them to manipulation and costly administrative errors.

“As tribunal secretaries, as prescribed by the Electoral Act 2026 and the Election Petition Tribunal Proceedings Practice Direction 2026, you must know the Practice Directions and have them on your fingertips. If you do not know them, you will be intimidated, you will be misled, and you will permit serious errors, and that will fetch serious consequences.

“There is no room for that now. You are given a good chance to equip yourself now, and we are giving you materials, so there will be no excuses. And we shall be constantly monitoring every aspect of your conduct,” she added.

Addressing the integrity of tribunal staff, the PCA warned against allowing financial inducements to influence their conduct, saying their activities would be subjected to intense public scrutiny.

“Let me be clear: you must discharge your duties with utmost good faith, and not be swayed by pecuniary inducements. Your conduct, and indeed, that of the tribunal, will be under intense public scrutiny.

“You must not allow yourselves to be used as instruments to truncate the judicial process. You must live above board and protect the reputation of the judiciary,” she said.

Describing the assignment as an opportunity to serve the country, she said the court would not hesitate to sanction erring officials.

“This assignment is not an opportunity for self-enrichment, but a call to national service, which is also an opportunity to build a good name. It is said that a good name is better than silver and gold. We will not hesitate to sanction any staff found wanting,” she added.

She further urged the secretaries to ensure prompt service of processes and maintain regular communication with the Election Petition Tribunal Unit at the Court of Appeal headquarters.

She said the presiding justice of each tribunal was the immediate supervisor of its administrative staff and should be approached whenever they encountered difficulties.

The PCA described the participants’ selection as a demonstration of the confidence reposed in them by the court, urging them not to betray the trust.

Also speaking, the Chief Registrar of the Court of Appeal, Umar Bangari, said the integrity of Nigeria’s democratic process depended on the efficient, transparent and timely resolution of electoral disputes.

He described the workshop as an administrative continuation of the training, designed to equip tribunal staff with the technical knowledge required for the assignment, among others.

Earlier, the Acting Deputy Chief Registrar of the Election Petition Tribunal, Maitumbi Altine, disclosed that 655 staff and chief registrars were attending the workshop.

She said 223 of the participants had previously served in election petition tribunals, while 432 were first-timers.

Altine also disclosed that the Court of Appeal was working to update its Case Management System to “forestall the incidences of conflicting judgments which the tribunals had experienced in time past.”

She added that the court would upload judgments delivered by election petition tribunals since 1999 into the system to serve as judicial precedents on legal issues that might arise during the proceedings.

The Acting Deputy Chief Registrar also warned participants against granting interviews without express authorisation, cautioning them against any activity capable of undermining the neutrality of the tribunals and the Court of Appeal.

The post 2027: Court of Appeal warns elections tribunal staff against bribery appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ex-Togo PM Gilbert Re-Elected UN Labour Agency Chief
description: Former Togolese prime minister Gilbert Houngbo was re-elected Monday as head of the United Nations’ labour agency after the only rival candidate pulled out at the last minute.Houngbo was re-elected for a second, five-year term as director-general of the International Labour Organization, start
content:
Former Togolese prime minister Gilbert Houngbo was re-elected Monday as head of the United Nations’ labour agency after the only rival candidate pulled out at the last minute.

Houngbo was re-elected for a second, five-year term as director-general of the International Labour Organization, starting on October 1 next year, after Spanish Labour Minister Yolanda Perez withdrew.

Houngbo received 51 votes out of 56 at the meeting of the ILO’s governing body, at the UN agency’s Geneva headquarters.

There were five abstentions, an ILO spokeswoman told AFP.

“More than a century after its founding, our organisation remains charged with a mission that is more relevant than ever: to promote social justice as the foundation for universal and lasting peace,” said Houngbo, 65.

“Faced with the uncertainties of the world, we have a duty to defend human dignity, promote social justice and foster dialogue between nations, workers and employers.”

He said that among the challenges shaping the future, “none perhaps is more decisive than artificial intelligence”, saying AI would open up new possibilities but also raise fundamental questions about jobs and skills.

He said the ILO must be at the forefront in “ensuring that technological progress remains at the service of humanity”.

Turbulent Period

Before the vote, Diaz Perez announced that she was pulling out to avoid divisions within the trade union movement.

In a statement on Bluesky, she lamented that the current ILO leadership had “plunged the organisation into the deepest financial crisis in its history”.

She said the general secretary of the International Trade Union Confederation and the spokesperson of the ILO Workers’ Group had chosen to stick with Houngbo, “against the feeling of a large part of the world’s trade union movement, which they have denied the freedom to vote”.

“I will not divide the trade union movement.”

Former Peruvian foreign minister Javier Gonzalez-Olaechea, the only other declared candidate, pulled out of the race on November 4.

The ILO has been going through a turbulent period for several months.

A decline in international funding — particularly from the United States — has forced the organisation to undertake reforms including job cuts.

Founded in 1919, the ILO has 187 member states which, uniquely in the UN system, are represented by governments, employers and workers.

The ILO aims to promote rights at work, encourage good employment opportunities, enhance social protection and strengthen dialogue on work-related issues.

AFP

title: 2027: Bauchi NDC gov candidate defects to APC
description:
The Bauchi State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Ibrahim Kashim, has defected to the All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Kashim, a former Secretary to the Bauchi State Government, announced his defection on Monday at a ceremony held at the APC St
content:
The Bauchi State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Ibrahim Kashim, has defected to the All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Kashim, a former Secretary to the Bauchi State Government, announced his defection on Monday at a ceremony held at the APC State Secretariat in Bauchi.

His defection came despite the publication of his name on the list of governorship candidates released by the Independent National Electoral Commission.

Explaining his decision, the former SSG said he joined the APC because it offered Bauchi a stronger opportunity to participate in national governance and attract development.

He described the APC as the governing party at the federal level, with an overwhelming presence across Northern Nigeria, as well as the political structure and institutional capacity to advance the state’s interests.

Kashim said, “The APC is currently the governing party at the Federal level and has an overwhelming presence across Northern Nigeria. It is also the party with the political structure, national reach and institutional capacity to provide a viable platform for the political and developmental aspirations we seek for Bauchi.

“I believe that Bauchi must be strategically positioned within this political reality.

“We cannot afford to gamble with the future of our state by placing our developmental aspirations on a platform that lacks comparable national reach and institutional influence.

“Our decision must be guided by the interests of Bauchi, not sentiment, political nostalgia or the convenience of individuals.”

He argued that remaining outside the ruling party at the centre could limit the state’s ability to attract federal projects, influence national policies, facilitate investments and secure adequate representation in the corridors of power.

The former SSG said, “The question is not simply which party can put forward a candidate. The question is which party has the organisational strength, national reach, political influence and institutional capacity to advance Bauchi’s interests.

“I am convinced that the APC offers the stronger platform.”

Kashim said his decision to leave the NDC followed his resignation from the party on October 16, 2026, adding that his commitment to the political struggle for a better Bauchi remained unchanged.

He also appealed to his supporters, political associates and other stakeholders to join him in the APC, insisting that his political ambition was driven by the desire to improve governance and development in the state.

According to him, his priorities include creating employment opportunities for youths, empowering women, improving agricultural productivity, providing quality education and strengthening healthcare delivery.

He added, “Our ultimate objective is not the triumph of one political party over another. It is the triumph of good governance over poor governance, development over stagnation, opportunity over deprivation and hope over despair.

“I have chosen strategic engagement over political isolation. I have chosen a broader national platform over limited political reach. Above all, I have chosen what I sincerely believe offers Bauchi State a better opportunity for development and prosperity.”

The former governorship candidate further called on the people of the state to support his decision, saying Bauchi should not be left behind in accessing opportunities available through the federation.

PUNCH Online recalls that Kashim announced his resignation from the NDC on October 16, 2026, in a statement, saying the decision followed careful reflection.

He then stressed that his resignation would not affect his commitment to the political struggle for a better Bauchi State.

The post 2027: Bauchi NDC gov candidate defects to APC appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: COAS, Tinubu seek technology-driven security cooperation
description: The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, on Monday joined President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the opening of the Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja, where participants called for stronger intelligence collaboration and technology-driven security operations.
content:
The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, on Monday joined President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the opening of the Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja, where participants called for stronger intelligence collaboration and technology-driven security operations.

The conference, held on November 16, 2026, at the Armed Forces Officers’ Mess, Asokoro, was themed, “Optimizing Intelligence Through Technological Innovations and Strategic Partnerships in a Complex Security Environment.”

President Tinubu, who was represented by the National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, emphasised the need for stronger intelligence sharing, technological innovation and operational cooperation among security agencies to address emerging security threats.

The President also urged security agencies to deepen partnerships with global technology companies and research institutions to strengthen the country’s intelligence-gathering and security capabilities.

He further charged Nigerian Defence Advisers serving abroad to maximise bilateral and multilateral engagements to advance the country’s national security interests.

The conference attracted top government and military officials, including the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd.); the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede; Service Chiefs; senior government officials and Defence Advisers.

The gathering focused on the role of emerging technologies, intelligence sharing and strategic partnerships in improving the country’s response to evolving security challenges.

The participation of the COAS and other military leaders reaffirmed the Armed Forces’ commitment to strengthening a technology-enabled and intelligence-driven security architecture through inter-agency collaboration and strategic partnerships.

The initiative is aimed at enhancing operational effectiveness and safeguarding Nigeria’s national security.

The post COAS, Tinubu seek technology-driven security cooperation appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: British Singer Raye Tops 2027 Grammy With 11 Nominations
description: Soulful British singer-songwriter Raye on Monday topped the Grammy nominations with 11, and Spanish superstar Rosalía earned nine in a strong showing for female artists across the board.Women have historically been underrepresented at the Grammy Awards held by the Recording Academy, whose 69t
content:
Soulful British singer-songwriter Raye on Monday topped the Grammy nominations with 11, and Spanish superstar Rosalía earned nine in a strong showing for female artists across the board.

Women have historically been underrepresented at the Grammy Awards held by the Recording Academy, whose 69th annual gala will take place on February 7 in Los Angeles.

But recent years have seen women dominate both the industry and the trophies list.

Raye’s whopping 11 nominations included the three most prestigious, recognizing best album, best song, and best record for her jazz-inflected blend of pop and R&B.

She was also recognized for her songwriting for fellow artists with a nomination for the relatively new best songwriter category.

Rosalia’s nine nominations follow a banner night at last week’s Latin Grammys, where her sweeping, avant-garde classical pop album “Lux” reigned supreme.

First-time nominee Ella Langley, the crooner behind the ubiquitous smash hit “Choosin’ Texas,” will enter the evening with seven shots at Grammys gold, as will fellow country star Miranda Lambert, who co-wrote that hit and notably scooped a nomination for producer of the year.

Pop-rock phenom Olivia Rodrigo also earned seven nods, as did the multifaceted musician Phoebe Bridgers, who released her third solo studio album “Lost Weekend” to widespread critical acclaim.

First-timers make waves

Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean — the English singer behind the smash “Man I Need” — earned six nods as did perennial Academy favorite Bruno Mars.

Taylor Swift predictably will be a threat in the top categories for her album “The Life of a Showgirl” as well as the song she penned for the latest film in the “Toy Story” franchise. She has five chances at winning.

But for all the heavyweight glory, it also proved a strong Grammys cycle for first-time nominees.

content:
Soulful British singer-songwriter Raye on Monday topped the Grammy nominations with 11, and Spanish superstar Rosalía earned nine in a strong showing for female artists across the board.

Women have historically been underrepresented at the Grammy Awards held by the Recording Academy, whose 69th annual gala will take place on February 7 in Los Angeles.

But recent years have seen women dominate both the industry and the trophies list.

Raye’s whopping 11 nominations included the three most prestigious, recognizing best album, best song, and best record for her jazz-inflected blend of pop and R&B.

She was also recognized for her songwriting for fellow artists with a nomination for the relatively new best songwriter category.

Rosalia’s nine nominations follow a banner night at last week’s Latin Grammys, where her sweeping, avant-garde classical pop album “Lux” reigned supreme.

First-time nominee Ella Langley, the crooner behind the ubiquitous smash hit “Choosin’ Texas,” will enter the evening with seven shots at Grammys gold, as will fellow country star Miranda Lambert, who co-wrote that hit and notably scooped a nomination for producer of the year.

Pop-rock phenom Olivia Rodrigo also earned seven nods, as did the multifaceted musician Phoebe Bridgers, who released her third solo studio album “Lost Weekend” to widespread critical acclaim.

First-timers make waves

Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean — the English singer behind the smash “Man I Need” — earned six nods as did perennial Academy favorite Bruno Mars.

Taylor Swift predictably will be a threat in the top categories for her album “The Life of a Showgirl” as well as the song she penned for the latest film in the “Toy Story” franchise. She has five chances at winning.

New York indie rockers Geese capped a breakout year with their first-ever nominations, garnering five.

description:

content:
Nigerian music stars Tems, Asake, Wizkid, Ayra Starr, Davido and Burna Boy have been nominated for the 2027 Grammy Awards, alongside international artistes including Raye, Rosalía, Olivia Dean, Bruno Mars and Taylor Swift.

The nominations for the 69th edition of the annual awards were announced on Monday, with British singer-songwriter Raye emerging as the leading nominee with 11 nods.

Rosalía followed with nine nominations, while Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers each received seven. Bruno Mars, Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean secured six nominations apiece.

The 2027 awards feature 100 categories, including five new ones: Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, Best Traditional Folk Album, Best Latin Song and Best Asian Pop Music Performance.

The ceremony is scheduled to hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States. It will be broadcast on ABC and streamed on Hulu and Disney+.

Nigerian artistes featured prominently in the African and global music categories, with Tems also earning recognition in the R&B category.

Tems was nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance for her song, What You Need, and Best R&B Song as a songwriter on the same track. She also received nominations for Best African Music Performance for Big Daddy and Best Global Music Album for Love Is a Kingdom.

Asake received two nominations in the Best African Music Performance category for Gratitude and Jogodo, the latter alongside Wizkid. Wizkid was also nominated in the category for Jogodo.

Ayra Starr earned nominations for Best African Music Performance for Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?), alongside Angélique Kidjo, and Best Global Music Album for Starrgirl.

Davido was nominated for Best Global Music Album for Oriadé, while Burna Boy earned a nomination for Best Global Music Performance for Dai Dai, alongside Shakira.

title: New Zealand Suspends Visa-Free Entry For Citizens Of 1 Country, Gives New Requirements - Check Below For Full Details
description: Kuwait passport holders can no longer use the NZeTA to enter New Zealand. The visa waiver is suspended for three months and a full visa is now required before travel.
content:
New Zealand has suspended visa-free travel for holders of Kuwait passports, effective from 23:59 on Thursday, 12 November 2026 (New Zealand Daylight Time).

The decision was announced by New Zealand’s Minister of Immigration and made under the Immigration Act 2009. It means Kuwaiti nationals can no longer enter New Zealand using the New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority (NZeTA) — the online authorisation that previously let eligible travellers visit without going to an embassy or consulate.

What changed: Kuwait passport holders who wish to travel to New Zealand must now apply for and receive a valid visa before departure. During the suspension period, the NZeTA is no longer available to them, and travellers with urgent plans have been directed to escalation channels within the immigration system to expedite their applications where necessary.

How long it lasts: The suspension is temporary, running for three months until 23:59 on Thursday, 11 February 2027, after which the government will reassess the situation.

Why the suspension happened: The move was triggered by uncertainty surrounding Kuwait’s citizenship revocation programme, which raised concerns for New Zealand immigration authorities about the status and documentation of Kuwaiti travellers.

The scale: At the time of the decision, about 20 Kuwaiti nationals were in New Zealand on visitor visas, while around 370 others held other forms of temporary visas. Immigration New Zealand also noted that roughly 88 Kuwaiti nationals arrive in the country on visitor visas each month.

The suspension applies to Kuwait nationals only — passport holders of all other visa-waiver countries remain eligible to use the NZeTA as before. Travellers affected by the change are advised to check the official Immigration New Zealand notice for the latest requirements before booking travel.

title: 2027: Deny opposition 25% of votes in FCT, Wike tells Tinubu campaign council
description:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has charged members of President Bola Tinubu’s campaign council in the FCT to prevent opposition parties from securing 25 per cent of votes in the territory in the January 16, 2027 general elections.
Wike gave the directive on Monday while inau
content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has charged members of President Bola Tinubu’s campaign council in the FCT to prevent opposition parties from securing 25 per cent of votes in the territory in the January 16, 2027 general elections.

Wike gave the directive on Monday while inaugurating the 466-member All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in Abuja.

He specifically identified the African Democratic Congress and the Nigeria Democratic Congress as opposition parties the campaign team must prevent from securing the required percentage of votes in the FCT.

The minister said the council’s responsibility went beyond winning the election, insisting that it must deliver an overwhelming victory for Tinubu and APC candidates contesting National Assembly seats.

“We’re not talking about winning; we’re talking about winning overwhelmingly.

“We must not allow them to go with 25 per cent. They don’t deserve to get 25 per cent,” Wike told the gathering, which included council members, party supporters and members of the Peoples Democratic Party.

Dismissing claims by opposition figures about their political strength ahead of the election, Wike rejected suggestions that the ADC controlled the political space in northern Nigeria or stood a chance of taking the FCT.

He also challenged former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi, over opposition remarks concerning an APC rally in Port Harcourt, urging him to test his party’s popularity in Rivers State.

“The FCT is for no other party other than the APC,” the minister declared, warning campaign council members that they would be held responsible for the electoral outcome in the territory.

Wike urged the campaign team to sell the achievements of the Tinubu administration rather than make promises, citing changes in the administration of the FCT since 2023.

He listed the appointment of an FCT representative to the Federal Executive Council for the first time since Abuja’s creation in 1976, the establishment of Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth, and the creation of the FCT Civil Service Commission among the administration’s achievements.

He also cited the appointment of the first Head of Service for the FCT and the opportunity for career civil servants in the territory to attain the rank of permanent secretary.

On land administration, Wike said the removal of the FCT from the Treasury Single Account had enabled the territory to access financial markets directly to fund capital projects.

He added that more than 20,000 Certificates of Occupancy had been signed within three years, compared with approximately 8,000 issued between 1999 and 2023.

The minister further listed the elevation of traditional rulers, construction of road networks and police stations, and educational projects, including the proposed University of Science and Technology in Abaji, as part of the administration’s interventions across satellite towns and rural communities.

Wike commended the APC and PDP leadership in the FCT for setting aside their political differences to establish the Rainbow Coalition in support of Tinubu’s re-election and APC National Assembly candidates.

The candidates include Senator Philip Aduda, seeking election to represent the FCT in the Senate; John Gabaya, contesting the AMAC/Bwari Federal Constituency seat; and Danladi Chiya, the Abuja South Federal Constituency candidate.

He urged other states to adopt the alliance model, which he said was also being practised in Rivers and Akwa Ibom states.

The minister directed the campaign council to establish committees across the FCT’s area councils and take its message to markets, suburbs, traditional rulers, indigenes and non-indigene associations, while maintaining peace and complying with electoral laws.

Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Yamawo, commended the party leadership for promoting political cooperation across party lines.

Yamawo described the developmental projects executed under Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda as the party’s major campaign message, saying, “The people can see the transformation taking place.”

He also described Wike’s appointment as coordinator of the FCT Presidential Campaign Council as a strategic decision, citing his grassroots mobilisation capacity.

The FCT PDP Chairman, Mohammed Dogara, also praised Wike for bringing rival political camps together, describing the alliance between APC and PDP leaders in the territory as unprecedented.

Using a local proverb, Dogara commended the minister for “bringing the cat and the rat to build the house and live in the house without any issues.”

He assured Wike that local council chairmen and grassroots leaders could mobilise voters across the territory, expressing confidence that the coalition would deliver victory on January 16, 2027.

“Come 17th of January, we are going to rejoice and celebrate the resounding victory,” he said.

NAN

title: Atiku thanks Yobe people for warm campaign reception
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has thanked the people of Potiskum and Yobe State for the warm reception accorded him and his campaign team during the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign rally in the state.







Atiku also commended Yobe State Governor for providing what he described a
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has thanked the people of Potiskum and Yobe State for the warm reception accorded him and his campaign team during the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign rally in the state.

Atiku also commended Yobe State Governor for providing what he described as a level playing field for the party to present its campaign message to the electorate.

The former vice-president’s appreciation was contained in a statement issued on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, who personally signed and posted it on his X account.

Atiku said the reception he received from the moment his entourage arrived in Potiskum from Azare, Bauchi State, was a testament to the people’s support for the ADC’s campaign promise of an affordable life.

“The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart.

“To the people of Potiskum and to the good people of Yobe State, I say thank you. You opened your doors and your hearts to us, and we are deeply grateful,” he said.

He also thanked the state governor for allowing the ADC to campaign freely, saying democracy was strengthened when political parties were given the opportunity to engage voters and present their programmes.

Atiku, however, used the statement to take a swipe at the Presidency over allegations of the use of artificial intelligence to portray large crowds at political events.

“The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate,” he said.

He added that the ADC’s campaign did not need artificial crowds, insisting that the turnout and chants at its rallies reflected the people’s desire for political change.

Atiku also referred to chants of “Tinubu Must Go” at ADC rallies, describing them as a call for change and a reminder of the responsibility that would accompany a popular mandate.

He pledged that, if elected president in the January 16, 2027 election, he would take immediate steps to make life more affordable for Nigerians.

“When President Tinubu leaves office on 29 May 2027, good governance and an affordable life must follow. I solemnly pledge to take immediate steps to make life affordable again when elected president,” he said.

Atiku said the reception in Yobe had reinforced his campaign’s belief that messages addressing the people’s everyday struggles and aspirations would attract widespread support.

“Yobe has reminded us that when a message speaks to people’s struggles and aspirations, they will come out in their numbers to be heard,” he added.

title: Poland Arrests Three Teens For Planning ‘Terror’ Attacks
description: Polish special services on Monday said they had arrested three minors suspected of preparing “terrorist attacks”, just days after a deadly shooting in the country’s second city.Poland is still in shock over the November 7 killing spree in Krakow, where a 24-year-old Pole randomly k
content:
Polish special services on Monday said they had arrested three minors suspected of preparing “terrorist attacks”, just days after a deadly shooting in the country’s second city.

Poland is still in shock over the November 7 killing spree in Krakow, where a 24-year-old Pole randomly killed six people after murdering his parents and sister.

According to authorities, the perpetrator may have been inspired by Norwegian neo-Nazi Anders Behring Breivik.

The arrested teens — two aged 17 and one 16 –“not only promoted Nazi and fascist ideology, but were already engaging in actions aimed at committing acts that fall under terrorism,” said Tomasz Siemoniak, minister in charge of special services, on X.

The first two were exchanging information online on how to make homemade explosives and firearms, he said.

Substances that could be used to manufacture explosives were found at the home of one of them.

In another incident illustrating the increased vigilance since the Krakow shootings, two Ukrainians aged 18 and 19 were detained last Friday and sent back home after they shouted from a balcony they were terrorists and had a bomb.

title: ASUP declares indefinite strike at Rivers polytechnic
description:
By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt



Academic activities at Kenule Beeson Saro-Wiwa Polytechnic, Bori, Rivers State, have been disrupted following the declaration of an indefinite strike by the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP), over the state government’s failure to implement agreed academic all
content:
By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt

Academic activities at Kenule Beeson Saro-Wiwa Polytechnic, Bori, Rivers State, have been disrupted following the declaration of an indefinite strike by the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP), over the state government’s failure to implement agreed academic allowances.

The ASUP Kenpoly Bori Chapter announced its participation in the industrial action on Monday, November 16, 2026, in compliance with a directive from the union’s national leadership ordering academic staff in affected state-owned polytechnics to withdraw their services.

In a statement issued on Monday and signed by the chapter’s Chairman, Engr. Dr Bariakawaadoo Bere, the union said the strike was aimed at compelling the Rivers State Government to implement the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) for lecturers, instructors and technologists in the institution.

ASUP recalled that the Federal Government and the union signed an agreement on April 8, 2026, providing for the implementation of CATA and EAA for academic staff in the polytechnic sector, effective January 2026.

According to the union, the Federal Government approved the allowances as a template for academic staff across polytechnics nationwide, adding that the agreement had been fully implemented in federal government-owned institutions.

It noted, however, that state governments were expected to extend the same benefits to academic staff in polytechnics and colleges of technology under their respective control.

The union said its national leadership had made several efforts to secure the Rivers State Government’s compliance through two separate letters dated August 10 and September 21, 2026, addressed to the governor.

In the letters, ASUP appealed to the governor to extend the approved allowances to academic staff of Kenule Beeson Saro-Wiwa Polytechnic and other affected state-owned institutions, arguing that their lecturers, instructors and technologists performed similar professional duties under comparable working conditions as their counterparts in federal institutions.

The union, however, expressed disappointment over what it described as the low level of response from the state government.

It also questioned what it considered unequal treatment of academic staff in the state’s tertiary institutions, noting that the same Rivers State Government had implemented the Federal Government-ASUU agreement for university lecturers in the state.

ASUP argued that both categories of academic workers faced similar economic realities and should therefore receive comparable consideration.

In a further attempt to resolve the disagreement, the union said its National Executive Council, at its 118th meeting held on October 22, 2026, directed the issuance of a 15-day ultimatum to the Rivers State Government.

The ultimatum commenced on October 27 and expired on November 10, 2026.

The union alleged that neither the state government nor any of its agencies contacted or invited its national or state leadership for discussions or negotiations throughout the period.

Following the expiration of the ultimatum without a resolution, the national leadership of ASUP, on November 12, formally notified the Rivers State Governor of its decision to embark on industrial action beginning Monday, November 16.

Consequently, the Kenpoly Bori chapter declared its full participation in the strike, insisting that the action was necessary to secure the implementation of the CATA and EAA provisions of the April 8 agreement.

The development puts pressure on the Rivers State Government to address the demands of the polytechnic workers and engage the union to resolve the dispute.

As of Monday, when the statement was issued, the union had commenced the industrial action, with no agreement announced to resolve the disagreement.

title: Plateau: People may forgive Tinubu, but won’t forget absence – Atiku
description:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his recent appeal for forgiveness in Plateau State, saying the people may forgive him but will not forget his alleged failure to visit and stand with them during periods of killings and kidnappings.







Atiku, the pres
content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his recent appeal for forgiveness in Plateau State, saying the people may forgive him but will not forget his alleged failure to visit and stand with them during periods of killings and kidnappings.

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), said no campaign visit or last-minute promise could erase what he described as the President’s absence when Plateau residents needed reassurance and protection.

He spoke through a statement issued on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, who disclosed the position on his X platform.

The statement was issued from Potiskum, Yobe State, where Atiku took his affordable-life campaign message on Sunday.

According to the former Vice President, Plateau residents needed the President’s presence when their communities were under attack and families were grieving over the loss of loved ones.

“The people of Plateau needed their President when they were grieving, when their communities were under attack and when families desperately needed reassurance.

“President Tinubu promised to end the killings and protect them, but he failed to keep those promises. He did not visit to stand with them in their darkest hour,” Atiku said.

He argued that Tinubu’s recent visit to the state to seek political support could not erase the concerns over his response to the security challenges confronting the people.

“Now he has gone to Plateau to campaign and ask for forgiveness. The people may forgive him, but they will never forget the lives lost, the communities left in fear and the absence of their President when they needed him most,” he said.

Atiku added that residents should not be treated as campaign instruments, insisting that their grief should not be used for political purposes.

“President Tinubu cannot abandon Plateau in its hour of agony, then return when he needs its votes and expect a warm welcome.

“The people are not props for his campaign, and their grief is not a slogan to be used when politically convenient. They may forgive him, but they will remember—and they will hold him accountable,” he added.

The ADC presidential candidate also extended his criticism to the Tinubu administration’s handling of the economy, accusing the President of failing to address the cost-of-living crisis confronting Nigerians.

He said the President had failed to meet the expectations of Nigerians who gave him the mandate in the 2023 general election.

Atiku, however, presented the ADC’s Affordable Life campaign as an alternative, saying it was designed to address the country’s economic challenges and restore relief, dignity and hope to households. “Nigerians deserve leadership that stands with them in their moments of greatest hardship,” he said.

title: Obi demands arrest of attackers of Kwankwaso’s convoy in Kano
description: Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has called for an immediate investigation and arrest of those responsible for the attack on the convoy of former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government A
content:
Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has called for an immediate investigation and arrest of those responsible for the attack on the convoy of former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

Obi, who disclosed this in a statement posted on his X platform on Monday, said several members of Kwankwaso’s entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised during the incident.

He condemned the attack, describing it as unacceptable and warning against the growing resort to violence during political activities.

“I am deeply saddened by reports of the attack on the convoy of my brother and running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and members of his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

“I strongly condemn this unfortunate incident. Reports indicate that several members of the entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised. This is unacceptable and must not be allowed to become part of our political culture,” he said.

Obi said political differences should not be used as justification for violence, intimidation or destruction of property, stressing that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to participate in the democratic process without fear of attack.

“Democracy is not warfare. Political differences should never be a reason to resort to violence, intimidation or the destruction of property,” he stated.

He urged Nigerians to embrace dialogue and respect divergent political opinions, warning that violence could undermine democratic participation.

The former governor specifically called on the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate the incident, identify those involved and prosecute anyone found culpable, including alleged sponsors of the attack.

“I therefore call on the Nigeria Police Force and all relevant security agencies to immediately investigate this incident, identify those responsible, including anyone found to have sponsored the attack, and ensure that they are brought to justice.

“No individual should be above the law, regardless of political position or influence,” he said.

Obi also expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and others affected by the incident, while wishing those injured a speedy recovery.

He reaffirmed his commitment to peaceful political engagement, saying the quest for political change should be pursued through dialogue, persuasion, ideas and the ballot rather than violence.

“Our commitment to building a new Nigeria remains unwavering. We believe that change must come through peaceful engagement, persuasion, ideas and the ballot, not violence,” he added.

title: Belgium’s Lukaku Retires From International Football
description: Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku on Monday retired from international football after scoring 94 goals in 135 games for his country, saying he was “at peace” with his decision.Lukaku featured in four World Cups for the Red Devils and helped them reach the quarter-finals of this year’s
content:
Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku on Monday retired from international football after scoring 94 goals in 135 games for his country, saying he was “at peace” with his decision.

Lukaku featured in four World Cups for the Red Devils and helped them reach the quarter-finals of this year’s tournament before losing to eventual winners Spain.

The 33-year-old, who now plays for Turkish club Fenerbahce, made his debut in 2010 as a teenager and was an unused substitute in Sunday’s 4-1 Nations League win over Italy.

“These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. It was a nice ride, and I enjoyed every single moment,” Belgium’s record goal scorer said on Instagram.

“To the Belgium fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.

“I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here,” Lukaku said.

The former Chelsea, Manchester United and Inter Milan forward was part of Belgium’s so-called ‘golden generation’.

Lukaku, alongside Kevin De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, finished third at the 2018 World Cup, a best-ever finish for Belgium in the tournament but they failed to lift a trophy during the period.

“I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for,” Lukaku said.

“I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team,” he added.

‘Legend, my brother’

A host of fellow Belgian players paid tribute to Lukaku.

“Legend, my brother,” midfielder Axel Witsel said on Instagram.

“Thank you for everything, my bro,” Courtois said.

“So many amazing memories,” the Real Madrid goalkeeper added.

Lukaku’s last appearance for his country came in October’s 4-1 loss to France.

“Beyond his exceptional performances on the pitch, he has been a true leader, with a strong personality and an essential role in the dressing room,” Lukaku’s former team-mate and now Belgium’s technical director Simon Mignolet said in a statement from the Belgian football association.

“We respect his decision and are deeply grateful to him for everything he has brought to our national team,” the former Liverpool goalkeeper added.

Belgium’s first game without Lukaku will be a Nations League last-eight fixture in March.

“We must now turn our attention to the future and prepare for the Nations League quarter-finals,” Mignolet said.

“With the ambition of continuing to make progress as a team,” he added.

AFP

The post Belgium’s Lukaku Retires From International Football appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Tinubu’s proximity won’t make me dictate Katsina politics – Masari
description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Political Affairs, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabir Masari, has dismissed suggestions that he is using his closeness to the President to influence or dictate the political direction of Katsina State.







Masari, who spoke in an intervi
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Political Affairs, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabir Masari, has dismissed suggestions that he is using his closeness to the President to influence or dictate the political direction of Katsina State.

Masari, who spoke in an interview with the BBC Hausa Service, also said he had no regrets supporting Dr Dikko Radda’s emergence as governor of Katsina State, despite reported political differences between them.

His comments come amid speculations that the strained relationship between him and Radda could affect the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The presidential aide said President Tinubu and Almighty Allah were witnesses to his contributions towards Radda’s emergence, lamenting what he described as unfair allegations against him.

Asked to assess Radda’s performance in office over the past three years, Masari said even those opposed to the governor would acknowledge that he had made efforts to develop the state.

“I have no regrets helping Dikko Radda to become the Governor of Katsina State,” he declared.

Explaining the origin of the disagreement, Masari alleged that the crisis began when some youths associated with the governor started displaying campaign materials bearing Radda’s photograph without that of President Tinubu.

He said he, alongside a minister and another prominent Katsina politician, Malam Jabiru Tsauri, had mobilised resources to promote the President and other political leaders in the state.

According to him, they sponsored billboards, posters and banners across Katsina featuring photographs of Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima, Governor Radda, former governors Aminu Masari and Ibrahim Shehu Shema, among other prominent political figures.

Masari alleged that some of the billboards were subsequently destroyed at night by individuals he claimed were working with the governor’s aides.

He further claimed that some suspects were arrested by the police in connection with the incident, adding that the development contributed to the misunderstanding between the two camps.

“I don’t have any issue with the governor; perhaps he has one with me. But what I will disagree with is a situation where the President cannot be advertised in Katsina State,” he said.

Masari also alleged that some individuals around the governor were uncomfortable with him and were responsible for creating tension between the two political camps.

He maintained that Radda should not feel threatened by the political activities of Katsina indigenes residing in Abuja, insisting that he and other prominent politicians from the state had no personal or political problem with the governor.

He urged APC stakeholders to ensure that the perceived divisions did not undermine the party’s unity and electoral fortunes in Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: Iran war: Bahrain jails 64 Shias for life over terror links
description:
A Bahraini court sentenced dozens of Shia Muslims, most of them clerics, to life in prison on terror charges on Monday, as authorities crack down on groups it accuses of ties to Iran.
Since the Iran war began with US-Israeli attacks, Gulf states that have borne the brunt of the Islamic Republic’s re
content:
A Bahraini court sentenced dozens of Shia Muslims, most of them clerics, to life in prison on terror charges on Monday, as authorities crack down on groups it accuses of ties to Iran.

Since the Iran war began with US-Israeli attacks, Gulf states that have borne the brunt of the Islamic Republic’s retaliatory strikes have cracked down on what they call cells with links to the Revolutionary Guards.

Bahrain, a Sunni Muslim kingdom, has a large Shia population that has long complained of marginalisation.

Authorities in the country have denied cracking down on citizens based on their religious identity.

On Monday, the criminal court sentenced 64 Shias, 57 of them clerics, to life in prison, a rights group and a Bahraini official said.

It also sentenced five others to 15 years in prison, according to the Britain-based Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy (BIRD), citing a lawyer who attended the court session.

A Bahraini official, speaking to AFP on condition of anonymity, confirmed the figures.

The mass trial involves 69 Bahraini Shias, including 60 clerics — 13 of whom were tried in absentia, including prominent cleric Ayatollah Isa Qassim, according to BIRD.

Bahrain’s official news agency confirmed the sentencing, adding that more than eight million dinars ($21 million) were confiscated from defendants and donated to charitable causes.

“The defendants in the case of the terrorist group linked with the Revolutionary Guards were convicted and handed sentences ranging between life in prison and 15 years,” the Bahrain News Agency said, without specifying the number of defendants or other details.

It said they were convicted of “establishing and managing a terrorist group linked to the Iranian Revolutionary Guards, which advocates for the suspension of the constitution and the overthrow of the ruling system”.

Since the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran in February, Bahrain has cracked down on anyone expressing support or sympathy for Tehran.

It has arrested hundreds of mostly Shia Muslims it accused of espionage, terrorism or links to the Revolutionary Guards, according to activists.

Dozens have also been stripped of their nationality.

– Torture allegations –

The Shias sentenced on Monday had initially been arrested and tried in separate groups earlier this year.

In May, Bahrain said its security services had dismantled an organisation accused of links to the Revolutionary Guards and arrested 41 of its suspected members. It named 11 others it said were in Iran.

In June, 15 more people were arrested in connection with the case, with authorities later saying two more people were on the run.

They had been accused of various crimes, including forming a terrorist group, collaborating with the Revolutionary Guards and plotting to overthrow Bahrain’s system and spread Iran’s ideology.

In an open letter, rights groups including BIRD and Human Rights Watch called on authorities to investigate “serious allegations of torture” in the case.

“Since Bahrain’s judiciary was established in the 1920s, the country has never witnessed persecution of Shia clerics on this scale,” said Sayed Ahmed Alwadae of BIRD.

The rights groups said defendants had reported “being subjected to forced standing, prolonged blindfolding and handcuffing, sleep deprivation, and threats of physical and sexual violence against themselves and their families, as well as citizenship revocation and deportation”.

They had also allegedly been pressured to sign long statements they were not allowed to read, they said.

AFP

title: 2027 Grammys: Davido, Asake, Tems, Burna Boy, Ayra Starr, Wizkid Earn Nominations
description: Afrobeats stars Davido, Asake, Tems, Burna Boy, Ayra Starr and Wizkid have earned nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with Nigerian artistes featuring prominently across several categories.The Recording Academy announced the nominations on Monday, with Nigerian artistes securing multiple
content:
Afrobeats stars Davido, Asake, Tems, Burna Boy, Ayra Starr and Wizkid have earned nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with Nigerian artistes featuring prominently across several categories.

The Recording Academy announced the nominations on Monday, with Nigerian artistes securing multiple nods in the Best African Music Performance and Best Global Music categories.

Tems leads the Nigerian contingent with four nominations, while Asake earned two nominations in the Best African Music Performance category.

Other Nigerian artistes recognised include Davido, Ayra Starr, Burna Boy and Wizkid, who shares a nomination with Asake.

In the Best African Music Performance category, Nigerian artistes account for four of the five nominated entries.

Asake earned nominations for his songs ‘Gratitude’ and ‘Jogodo’, his collaboration with Wizkid.

Tems was nominated for ‘Big Daddy’, while Ayra Starr received a nod alongside Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for their collaboration, ‘Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)’.

The fifth nominee is Ghanaian musician King Ayisoba, whose song ‘No Tradition, No Africa’ features Rocky Dawuni.

Tems also received nominations in three other categories. She was recognised in the Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song categories for ‘What You Need’, as well as Best Global Music Album for her project, Love Is a Kingdom.

Ayra Starr earned another nomination in the Best Global Music Album category for Starrgirl, while Davido’s Oriadé was also nominated in the category.

Burna Boy received a nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category for ‘Dìá Dìá’, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira.

Other International Stars

British singer-songwriter RAYE emerged as the biggest winner among international artistes at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, leading all nominees with 11 nominations. Her recognition includes Album of the Year for ‘This Music May Contain Hope’, as well as Record and Song of the Year for ‘Where Is My Husband!’ and Songwriter of the Year. Spanish singer Rosalía followed with nine nominations, including Album of the Year for ‘Lux (Complete Works)’ and Record and Song of the Year for ‘Berghain’, her collaboration with Björk and Yves Tumor.

Other major international contenders include American singer Olivia Rodrigo and country star Ella Langley, who each earned seven nominations, while British singer Olivia Dean secured six.

Phoebe Bridgers and Miranda Lambert also received seven nominations each, while Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas earned six apiece. Taylor Swift received five nominations, including recognition in the major categories for her album ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ and songs ‘The Fate of Ophelia’ and ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’.

Beyond the major categories, the nominations also highlighted the Grammy Awards’ growing international reach, with Tame Impala and South Korean singer JENNIE recognised for ‘Dracula’, while Thailand’s LISA and South Korea’s IVE earned nominations in the newly introduced Best Asian Pop Music Performance category.

Filipino groups BINI and SB19 also secured nominations, alongside Colombian star Karol G, who featured among the contenders in the inaugural Best Latin Song category.

title: 2027: Kebbi backs Tinubu, rallies LGAs for presidential rally
description:
The Kebbi State Government has intensified mobilisation across its 21 local government areas ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s forthcoming visit for the All Progressives Congress presidential rally, reaffirming its support for his second-term ambition.
The state Commissioner for Information and Cultu
content:
The Kebbi State Government has intensified mobilisation across its 21 local government areas ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s forthcoming visit for the All Progressives Congress presidential rally, reaffirming its support for his second-term ambition.

The state Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed-BK, said the government, APC leadership and various support groups were working together to ensure a massive turnout and a memorable reception for the President.

Ahmed-BK disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Birnin Kebbi, where he said Governor Nasir Idris had inaugurated several sub-committees to coordinate arrangements for the visit.

He described the forthcoming rally as an opportunity for Kebbi to demonstrate its political loyalty to Tinubu and support for the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

“Kebbi State is fully prepared to receive Mr President. Under the purposeful leadership of Governor Nasir Idris, the government, APC leadership and various support groups have continued to mobilise stakeholders across the state to ensure a successful and historic rally,” he said.

The commissioner said the mobilisation had extended to party leaders, elected representatives, women, youths, farmers, labour unions and grassroots supporters.

He linked Kebbi’s support for Tinubu’s re-election bid to the expected economic benefits of ongoing federal infrastructure projects, particularly the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway.

According to him, the project would improve transportation, facilitate trade and strengthen economic activities, particularly in Kebbi, where agriculture remains a major economic activity.

He said improved road connectivity would enable farmers to transport their produce to markets more easily, reduce transportation difficulties and expand commercial opportunities.

Ahmed-BK also identified the Bachaka Road, Malando-Ngaski Road and other federal and state infrastructure projects as critical interventions capable of connecting rural communities and stimulating economic development.

On the political front, the commissioner recalled that Kebbi was among the first states to openly endorse Tinubu for a second term, describing the decision as a reflection of confidence in his leadership and ongoing reforms.

“Our position remains that Nigeria needs sustained leadership, strong partnerships and a government capable of translating policies into tangible benefits for its citizens,” he said.

He attributed the APC’s political strength in Kebbi to what he described as the cordial relationship between Governor Idris’s administration and the people, citing achievements in education, healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure, workers’ welfare and social development.

The commissioner said the administration’s inclusive governance and people-oriented policies had helped strengthen public confidence in the ruling party.

He challenged opposition parties to present credible alternatives, clear policy directions and verifiable records of service rather than relying on political promises.

Ahmed-BK expressed confidence that the APC would maintain its dominance across the state’s 21 local government areas, attributing its strength to party unity, consultation and grassroots engagement.

He urged party members, supporters and residents to participate peacefully in the rally and give the President a rousing welcome.

“Our message is clear: Kebbi is ready, Kebbi is united, and Kebbi stands firmly with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress,” he declared.

description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



Suspected bandits have abducted 12 residents of Kurmin Wali community in Afogo Ward, Kajuru Local Government Area of Kaduna State, in a fresh attack that has left 14 people in captivity.







The attack reportedly occurred on Sunday, November 15, 2026, when armed men inva
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Suspected bandits have abducted 12 residents of Kurmin Wali community in Afogo Ward, Kajuru Local Government Area of Kaduna State, in a fresh attack that has left 14 people in captivity.

The attack reportedly occurred on Sunday, November 15, 2026, when armed men invaded the community at about 9:14am and abducted 12 residents.

The village head, Isiaku Danazumi, who confirmed the incident on Monday, said three of the abducted residents had escaped and returned to the community, while nine others remained in the custody of their abductors.

He explained that the nine victims, alongside five other residents abducted in two separate attacks in October, brought the total number of people still being held by the bandits to 14.

“Yes, the incident happened on Sunday around 9:14am. Twelve people were abducted by the bandits, but three returned, while the remaining nine are still with them.

“But on October 2, 2026, two people were also abducted during the rainy season. Again, on October 10, three other people were abducted. So, in total, 14 of our people are with the bandits in the bush,” he said.

The traditional ruler expressed concern over the recurring abductions, saying that although the relevant authorities had been notified, no concrete action had been taken to secure the victims’ release.

He further disclosed that some security personnel visited the community on Sunday after the attackers had fled but reportedly left less than an hour after arriving.

The latest attack has heightened concerns over the security situation in Kurmin Wali, which attracted national attention in January 2026 when suspected bandits abducted more than 80 residents during a church service.

The mass abduction sparked widespread outrage and renewed calls for urgent government intervention to protect vulnerable communities in Kaduna State.

As of the time of filing this report, the Kaduna State Police Command and the Ministry of Internal Security and Home Affairs had yet to issue official statements on Sunday’s attack.

title: Oyo proposes N1.115trn 2027 budget, targets jobs, infrastructure
description:
By Adeola Badru



The Oyo State Government has proposed a N1.115 trillion budget for 2027, prioritising infrastructure development, job creation, entrepreneurship and the growth of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to accelerate economic expansion and improve residents’ living standards.
content:
By Adeola Badru

The Oyo State Government has proposed a N1.115 trillion budget for 2027, prioritising infrastructure development, job creation, entrepreneurship and the growth of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to accelerate economic expansion and improve residents’ living standards.

The proposed budget, tagged “Budget of Sustained Progress,” is designed to consolidate gains recorded across critical sectors while strengthening the state’s economic competitiveness through investments in infrastructure, agriculture, human capital development and public-private partnerships.

Governor Seyi Makinde presented the proposal to the Oyo State House of Assembly last week, with capital expenditure accounting for 60.1 per cent of the total spending plan.

Speaking during the presentation of the budget breakdown and analysis at the Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning in Ibadan on Monday, the Permanent Secretary, Julius Ayanleke, said the proposal aligned with the administration’s vision of making Oyo State the fastest-growing economy in Nigeria.

He said the government’s spending priorities would focus on completing ongoing projects, strengthening Internally Generated Revenue (IGR), attracting public and private investments, supporting MSMEs, expanding infrastructure and ensuring efficient utilisation of resources through Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs).

According to Ayanleke, the proposed budget comprises N670.03 billion for capital expenditure, representing 60.1 per cent, and N445.31 billion for recurrent expenditure, accounting for the remaining 39.9 per cent.

He explained that the substantial allocation to capital projects was intended to sustain the state’s development drive, particularly through the completion of ongoing projects and execution of critical infrastructure programmes.

Among the projects earmarked for priority funding are the Ibadan Circular Road, Ido-Eruwa Road and several rural road projects, which he said had received adequate provisions to facilitate their timely completion.

Providing an update on the state’s fiscal performance, Ayanleke disclosed that Oyo generated N618.72 billion between January and September 2026.

He said the revenue comprised N401.44 billion in recurrent revenue and N217.28 billion in capital receipts.

The permanent secretary explained that the 2027 budget was developed through the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), sectoral planning processes and consultations with stakeholders across the state’s seven geopolitical zones to ensure that the spending priorities reflected residents’ development needs.

Outlining the government’s fiscal targets, he said the administration would prioritise the completion of ongoing projects, reduce non-essential overhead costs and improve efficiency in personnel and recurrent expenditure.

He added that the government was targeting a minimum annual growth of 10 per cent in IGR between 2027 and 2029, while ensuring that recurrent expenditure was financed through sustainable revenue sources.

Other priorities, according to him, include diversifying the state’s revenue base, accelerating critical capital projects and expanding access to grants, development funding and public-private partnership arrangements.

Ayanleke said maintaining the 60:40 capital-to-recurrent expenditure ratio demonstrated the government’s commitment to development-focused investments and long-term economic growth.

He added that the spending approach would enable the state to channel more resources into productive investments capable of stimulating economic activities, supporting businesses, creating employment opportunities and improving residents’ welfare.

Also speaking, the Executive Assistant to the Governor on Finance, Budget and Economic Planning, Gafar Bello, commended the state’s budget performance since 2019, attributing the progress to transparency, fiscal discipline, efficiency and effective deployment of fiscal management tools.

Bello said the administration’s approach to fiscal management had contributed to improved budget implementation and strengthened the state’s capacity to pursue its development objectives.

In his remarks, the President of the Multi-disciplinary Finance Professionals (MFP), Dr Oyedepo Oyebade, praised the state government and the Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning for what he described as the transparent presentation of the 2027 budget and impressive implementation of the 2026 fiscal proposal.

Oyebade particularly highlighted the state’s 103 per cent performance on statutory allocation on a pro-rata basis, saying it reflected the adoption of prudent and realistic revenue projections.

He also commended the government for sustaining transparency, accountability and the January-to-December budget cycle, describing the consistency as an important feature of sound fiscal management.

According to him, allocating about 60 per cent of the proposed budget to capital projects underscored the administration’s commitment to completing ongoing projects, expanding infrastructure and driving development across the state.

The post Oyo proposes N1.115trn 2027 budget, targets jobs, infrastructure appeared first on Vanguard News.
