title: UniAbuja unions, students protest alleged land reallocation by Wike
description:
…Accuse FCT minister of undermining university’s expansion plans



…Warn move could threaten research, student accommodation and infrastructure



By Joseph Erunke, Abuja



ABUJA — Academic and non-academic staff, students and alumni of the University of Abuja on Monday took to the streets to prot
content:
…Accuse FCT minister of undermining university’s expansion plans

…Warn move could threaten research, student accommodation and infrastructure

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

ABUJA — Academic and non-academic staff, students and alumni of the University of Abuja on Monday took to the streets to protest the alleged reallocation of portions of the institution’s land by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, demanding an immediate reversal of the decision.

The protesters, operating under the Joint Action Committee (JAC), accused the minister of threatening the university’s future, disregarding the rule of law and undermining its capacity to expand academic and research infrastructure.

The demonstration involved members of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), Students’ Union Government (SUG) and the university’s alumni association.

Carrying placards and chanting solidarity songs, the protesters appealed to President Bola Tinubu to intervene and direct Wike to reverse the alleged reallocation.

Chairman of ASUU, University of Abuja branch, Prof. Sylvanus Ugoh, accused the FCT minister of disregarding the rule of law, insisting that the university had been allocated the land in 1988 when it was established.

Ugoh said the land had remained under the university’s ownership despite changes in the FCT administration, questioning why Wike had taken a different position from his predecessors.

He described the development as an attempt to place private interests above public interest, arguing that a public university should not lose land required for its future expansion to accommodate individuals and businesses.

“What the Honourable Minister of the FCT has done is a breach. He has refused to have regard for the rule of law. This land was allocated to the University of Abuja in 1988, when the university was founded, and there have been several FCT Ministers, but none of them has done what he is doing,” he said.

The ASUU chairman maintained that the institution’s land should not be taken away and allocated to private individuals.

“University is a public good. University is a public interest. There is nowhere in the world where you take public interest and sacrifice it for individual interest.

“We say no to the issue of the Honourable Minister taking the land that belongs to the University of Abuja and giving it to his friends and individuals in this nation. We are calling on His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu, to call the Minister to order so that he will reverse this trend,” Ugoh said.

Also speaking, NASU Chairperson in the university, Comrade Sadiya Hassan, said any development agenda being pursued by the FCT administration should also accommodate the institution’s expansion needs.

She noted that the university had several projects requiring additional land and should not be deprived of the space originally allocated to it for future development.

Hassan urged Wike to channel his development initiatives towards strengthening public institutions rather than making land available to private companies.

“The development you intend to bring, Mr Wike, is also needed at the university. If you want to promote development, do so for the university and not for private companies. If you cannot help us, kindly leave our land alone,” she said.

Similarly, SSANU Chairman of the university branch, Comrade Nurudeen Yusuf, warned that any attempt to take over the institution’s land could undermine specialised academic programmes and critical research activities.

He explained that the university required adequate space not only for physical expansion but also for specialised research facilities, particularly in disciplines with specific safety and operational requirements.

Yusuf cited the Department of Nuclear Engineering, explaining that research activities in the field required designated buffer zones, which informed the provision of additional land for the institution.

He also identified Aeronautical Engineering as another programme requiring sufficient space for teaching, research and related activities.

“At the University of Abuja, we have a Department of Nuclear Engineering. For research in nuclear engineering to be conducted, buffer zones are required. That is why those lands were provided. We also have a Department of Aeronautical Engineering, which requires adequate space for its activities,” he said.

The National Publicity Secretary of the University of Abuja Alumni Association, Dr Rauf Olaiya Sarafadeen-Kunle, expressed concern over the possible implications of the alleged reallocation for the safety and security of the university community.

He cautioned against allowing private commercial interests to override the institution’s development priorities and urged the FCT minister to respect the university’s land.

The students also joined the protest, warning that further reduction in the institution’s available land could worsen its existing infrastructural challenges.

President of the Students’ Union Government, Eyamu Oghenenyerovwo Peculiar, appealed to the Federal Government to prioritise the university’s pressing needs, particularly accommodation and basic facilities, rather than support developments that could constrain its expansion.

She said the university currently had more than 55,000 students, with new faculties and departments being established, but continued to grapple with inadequate hostel accommodation and other infrastructural deficits.

According to her, the shortage of on-campus accommodation has forced many students to seek housing outside the university, where rising rental costs have made affordable accommodation increasingly difficult to secure.

The student leader warned that depriving the institution of land needed for expansion could further compound the challenges confronting students and undermine efforts to provide a conducive learning environment.

The protesters insisted that the university’s land was critical to its long-term academic, infrastructural and research ambitions, urging the Federal Government to intervene and address the dispute.

The post UniAbuja unions, students protest alleged land reallocation by Wike appeared first on Vanguard News.

​Describing the minister’s actions as a breach of the rule of law, Ugoh implored President Bola Tinubu to intervene and direct Wike to reverse course.

​“The land has been allocated to the University of Abuja since 1988, when it was founded. There have been several FCT ministers since then, and none of them has done what he is doing,” he said.

​“A university is a public good and serves the public interest. Nowhere in the world do you sacrifice the public interest for individual gain.

​“We say no to the honourable minister taking land that belongs to the university.”
​The ASUU chairman warned that the dispute could undermine the federal government’s commitment to preventing industrial action in universities under the current administration.

​“We reject this, and we call on His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu, to call the honourable minister to order so that he reverses his decision,” he added.

​“This administration has consistently reiterated that ASUU and other university unions will not go on strike, yet the FCT minister’s actions are capable of undermining that peace.

​“The unions in this university will not fold their hands and watch land meant for unborn generations be taken away.

​“We cannot allow property meant for future generations to be handed over to private individuals. University development benefits everyone.”

​Nurudeen Yusuf, chairman of the UniAbuja branch of SSANU, stated that the unions would resist any attempt by the government to seize the university’s land.

​Yusuf emphasized that adequate land is a critical requirement for the growth and development of any higher institution.
​“At the University of Abuja, we have a Department of Nuclear Engineering, which requires strict buffer zones to safely conduct research that is why those lands were provided. We also have a Department of Aeronautical Engineering, which requires vast space for its operations,” he added.

title: AA Leadership Crisis: Udeze urges INEC to recognise him
description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



The National Chairman of the Action Alliance (AA), Chief Kenneth Udeze, has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise his leadership of the party following the withdrawal of a Supreme Court appeal by a rival factional leader, Adekunle Rufai Omo
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

The National Chairman of the Action Alliance (AA), Chief Kenneth Udeze, has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise his leadership of the party following the withdrawal of a Supreme Court appeal by a rival factional leader, Adekunle Rufai Omo-Aje.

Udeze, in a statement on Monday, said the development had brought an end to the prolonged leadership dispute within the party.

He said Omo-Aje had withdrawn his appeal, marked SC/CV/162/2024, which challenged the January 26, 2024 judgment of the Court of Appeal in appeal No. CA/ABJ/CV/955/2022.

According to Udeze, the Court of Appeal had dismissed Omo-Aje’s appeal and awarded N1 million in costs against him in favour of the AA National Chairman.

He said the appellate court found no merit in the appeal and affirmed his leadership of the party.

Udeze further explained that Omo-Aje subsequently approached the Supreme Court to challenge the decision but applied to withdraw the appeal ahead of its scheduled hearing on November 16.

Describing the development as a victory for the rule of law, Udeze congratulated members of the National Executive Committee, state chairmen, local government and ward executives, as well as party supporters across the country.

He urged INEC to recognise his leadership as the authentic national leadership of the Action Alliance and accept candidates nominated by his faction for the 2027 general elections.

The party chairman also cautioned the electoral commission against dealing with any rival faction or accepting candidate lists submitted by individuals outside his leadership, warning that such action could lead to post-election litigation.

He appealed to President Bola Tinubu, the Attorney-General of the Federation, the Department of State Services and the Nigeria Police Force to prevail on INEC to comply with the court’s decision. Udeze maintained that the Action Alliance remained united under his leadership.

title: UK Women Convicted For Having Abortions Granted Automatic Pardons
description: Women in England and Wales convicted of abortion offences under a 19th-century law were granted automatic pardons Monday after landmark legislation decriminalising abortion took effect.Under the new law, voted in by lawmakers last year, it will no longer be a criminal offence for a woman to terminat
content:
Women in England and Wales convicted of abortion offences under a 19th-century law were granted automatic pardons Monday after landmark legislation decriminalising abortion took effect.

Under the new law, voted in by lawmakers last year, it will no longer be a criminal offence for a woman to terminate her pregnancy at any stage.

“Women previously convicted of, or cautioned for, an abortion offence relating to their own pregnancy have been automatically pardoned,” the Ministry of Justice said in a statement.

In June 2025, lawmakers voted to end prosecutions of women in England and Wales for terminating their own pregnancy. Until then, women faced criminal charges for choosing to end a pregnancy after 24 weeks or without appropriate medical approval.

Abortion is legal in England and Wales with an authorised provider up to 24 weeks, with limited circumstances allowing one after that, including when the mother’s life is at risk.

But until last year, an 1861 law criminalised abortions carried out outside the law, with a maximum sentence of life imprisonment.

Campaigners said six women had appeared in court in England charged with attempting to end their own pregnancy outside abortion law between 2022 and 2025.

The lawmaker who put forward the amendment decriminalising termination, Tonia Antoniazzi, previously said police had investigated “more than 100 women for suspected illegal abortion” between 2020 and 2025.

Under the new rules, the legal provision of abortion services, including the time limits, remains the same, and anyone assisting a woman in getting an abortion outside the scope of the law will still be liable for prosecution.

“Today is a momentous and historic day for women and girls in England and Wales,” Antoniazzi said, adding that any women investigated would also have their criminal records deleted.

“No pardon can erase the harm and distress of their experiences, but this is an important recognition that what they faced was an injustice,” the Labour MP added.

She told the PA News Agency she believed more than 100 women who were “unnecessarily harmed” by the old law would benefit from the changes.

Northern Ireland decriminalised abortion for women in 2019. Scotland is currently reviewing its abortion laws.

AFP

title: EXCLUSIVE: Gov Abba Yusuf moves to settle marital crisis, sends Ganduje, Islamic clerics on peace mission to Kwankwaso
description:
Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has reportedly assembled a delegation of prominent political leaders, Islamic clerics, elders and influential stakeholders to intervene in the marital disagreement between him and his wife, Hajiya Zainab Musa Kwankwaso.
The delegation is expected to visit the A
content:
Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has reportedly assembled a delegation of prominent political leaders, Islamic clerics, elders and influential stakeholders to intervene in the marital disagreement between him and his wife, Hajiya Zainab Musa Kwankwaso.

The delegation is expected to visit the Abuja residence of former Kano State Governor and former presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in an effort to resolve the crisis involving his daughter and Governor Yusuf.

A source at the Kano Government House, who spoke exclusively on condition of anonymity, disclosed that the delegation would be led by former Kano State Governor and former National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Dr Abdullahi Umar Ganduje.

Other prominent figures expected to participate in the peace mission include the spiritual leader of the Qadiriyya Islamic movement in Nigeria and West Africa, Khalifa Sheikh Qaribullah Sheikh Muhammad Nasiru Kabara; prominent Islamic scholar and member of the Kano State Shura Council, Sheikh Abdulwahhab Abdallah; and Malam Tijjani Yammota, alongside other respected elders and political leaders.

According to the source, the delegation plans to travel from Kano to Abuja to appeal to Kwankwaso to reconsider his position and allow his daughter to return to the Government House.

The delegation is also expected to encourage both families to resolve the disagreement through dialogue, mutual understanding and respect for the marriage, rather than allowing political differences to worsen the situation.

The source further claimed that Governor Yusuf remained committed to his marriage and wanted to reconcile with his wife, particularly for the sake of their six children.

The couple reportedly married on July 29, 2006, and have been together for more than 20 years.

“Governor Yusuf still loves his wife, who is the mother of his children, and he also continues to regard Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso as his father. This is a family matter that deserves understanding, reconciliation and the intervention of respected elders.

“Politics should not be allowed to come between a husband and wife who love each other, especially after more than 20 years of marriage and six children. The governor wants peace, and we believe that dialogue and the intervention of these respected personalities can help restore understanding between the two families,” the source said.

However, when contacted for confirmation, the Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, said he was unaware of any delegation constituted to intervene in the matter.

He described the issue as a personal family matter that did not require public explanation, warning government officials against commenting on it without approval.

“According to our rules of engagement, personal issues of the Governor can only be discussed with prior approval. I therefore urge all government officials to exercise restraint on this issue.

“No comment is the only official response to this issue,” the commissioner stated.

The post EXCLUSIVE: Gov Abba Yusuf moves to settle marital crisis, sends Ganduje, Islamic clerics on peace mission to Kwankwaso appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: VIDEO: I attempted suicide many times, says Kunle Afolayan’s son
description:
Dieko Afolayan, son of Nollywood filmmaker and producer, Kunle Afolayan, has opened up about his struggles with bullying, sexual assault and multiple suicide attempts, revealing how he has turned his painful experiences into a renewed sense of purpose.
Afolayan made the disclosure during an intervie
content:
Dieko Afolayan, son of Nollywood filmmaker and producer, Kunle Afolayan, has opened up about his struggles with bullying, sexual assault and multiple suicide attempts, revealing how he has turned his painful experiences into a renewed sense of purpose.

Afolayan made the disclosure during an interview on The Morayo Show on Monday, where he spoke about his journey towards healing, self-discovery and finding meaning in his experiences.

Reflecting on his journey from pain to purpose, he described it as challenging, particularly given the traumatic experiences he had endured.

“Moving from pain to purpose has not been easy, especially knowing that you are going to be doing a lot of difficult things, having been through difficult experiences,” he said.

He disclosed that beyond the bullying he experienced, he had attempted suicide several times and was also a survivor of sexual assault.

He, however, stressed that these experiences did not define his identity or determine his future.

“I have tried so many times to commit suicide, and I am also a victim of sexual assault. However, I have realised that these experiences do not define who I am, where I get to or what I do with myself,” he said.

Afolayan emphasised the importance of self-compassion, urging people dealing with difficult experiences to be kinder to themselves.

He said learning to challenge negative thoughts and adopt alternative perspectives played a significant role in changing his outlook on life.

“I feel like if there is anything anyone should practise, it is self-compassion,” he added.

Recalling the depth of his struggles, Afolayan disclosed that he once attempted to ingest broken glass after feeling that he did not belong.

“There were so many times I would cry. I remember a time I tried to ingest broken glass because I felt I did not belong here,” he said.

He, however, said his outlook began to change when he started hosting and presenting programmes in school, an experience that helped him discover his passion and purpose.

According to him, the positive response from people who approached him after his presentations made him realise that he could use his voice to make a difference in society.

“I realised that I came into this world for something. I have a mission on earth, and that is to make people feel something and use my voice for the voiceless,” he said.

Afolayan also acknowledged the support of his family, particularly his mother, whom he described as instrumental to his journey.

He expressed gratitude to her and other family members for their encouragement and support throughout his personal struggles.

title: Stop copying Western cinema, AMAA jury president tells African filmmakers
description:
The President of the 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards jury, Dorothy Wenner, has urged African filmmakers to stop imitating Western cinema and develop original storytelling approaches rooted in their cultures and experiences.
Wenner said filmmakers should resist the pressure to satisfy foreign expect
content:
The President of the 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards jury, Dorothy Wenner, has urged African filmmakers to stop imitating Western cinema and develop original storytelling approaches rooted in their cultures and experiences.

Wenner said filmmakers should resist the pressure to satisfy foreign expectations and instead have confidence in their ability to tell authentic African stories.

Speaking during an interview with ARISE NEWS on Sunday, she said African cinema needed a distinct identity rather than reproducing Western styles and narratives.

“This is a new way of telling a story that is not a spoof of Western cinema, but it comes from storytelling from an African background and culture, So authenticity is something that you don’t create. It is something where, you know, you come to yourself. And it’s not an imitation,” she said.

She advised emerging filmmakers against copying previously successful films, urging them to develop original ideas and explore their individual creative perspectives.

“Don’t imitate the winner from last year. Very often happening. What I think is to really think, what have I to say? And what is my new way of telling my story, not imitating something that was successful earlier,” she stated.

Wenner also encouraged filmmakers to take creative risks and explore subjects that genuinely interest them.

She further stated, “I say, well, surprise the jury. Be courageous. And when it comes to subject matters, do look out, ask your friends and trust, do have a trust in what interests you.”

African films face distribution barriers in Europe

The jury president also raised concerns about the difficulty African films face in securing mainstream distribution in Europe, saying distributors often consider them too risky to release.

Speaking from her experience in Berlin, Germany, she said African films across different genres struggled to gain access to regular distribution channels.

“I’m from Berlin, Germany, and I can only say it’s so tough to have, to bring a film of African descent, no matter if it’s a documentary, if it’s comedy or whatever genre it is, into regular distribution. The distributor says, but this is so old-fashioned.

“Sometimes it drives me nuts. So to say, oh, it’s such a risk. We are in such difficult times. It is too risky to bring an African film into distribution,” she observed.

She said the Africa Movie Academy Awards had a role to play in creating new opportunities for African cinema through strategic efforts to promote its films.

“So here is where I find AMA is really at the fore of fighting for new revenues. And not with aggression, but with clever films and with clever strategies,” Wenner noted.

Wenner further cautioned African filmmakers against tailoring their productions to what they assume European audiences expect from the continent.

She declared, “So sometimes it’s also, and I hope I don’t sound too critical, but sometimes it’s also the African filmmaker thinks, oh, this is what is expected from us by the Europeans.

“And I think this is an outdated thing. This is a trap that I’ve seen. Quite a lot also African filmmakers get into.”

Wenner praises Nigerian, Kenyan films

Assessing entries for this year’s awards, Wenner described the quality of films submitted as exceptional, highlighting the emergence of new filmmakers and artists from across the continent.

“This was an exceptional year. I think overall internationally the film industry is in kind of like where do we move to, what’s happening, who’s coming to the cinemas.

“And so having had the chance of watching all these films I was extremely happy and excited and especially I would say because there were a lot of surprises.

“In a such new names and new names filmmakers also in other artistic departments that really climbed to the top in lightning speed and the films that we got to see were surprising, innovative and they have a kind of, there is an urgency to say something and that we got films from all over the continent I think was making all of us very proud,” Wenner noted.

She singled out Nigeria’s The Herd and Kenya’s One Woman, One Bra as two outstanding entries.

Speaking about The Herd, she said, “This is a film that really, really took me by surprise. And I remember when I was watching it I didn’t know where it would go to.”

On the Kenyan film, she said, “The title is very provocative. It’s a satire. It’s a comedy. But I can’t really remember to having seen a film that would put as a topic international aid and how it affects communities in film, in a feature film. Stunning, stunning actress, lead actress.”

She also called for fresh approaches to documentary filmmaking, noting the growing influence of mobile phones on how people record and present their experiences.

“If you go into documentary, allow the new reality in which everyone is constantly having their phones and has become a director of his and her own film. Life, sorry, not sure. Director of your own film.

“So thereby you have to find new ways of storytelling within documentary. Observe. Observation is very important to create something like authenticity,” she said.

Wenner said filmmakers needed to trust their instincts and draw from their own experiences when developing stories.

Wenner said, “I think we have to find our own voice. As creative people, that’s very important because oftentimes creative people are the lead, you know?

“So you find your own voice and you have confidence in yourself and confidence in your ability to tell that story. And know that what you are telling is based on truth. Not someone else’s truth, but your own truth.”

She added that filmmakers did not necessarily need large budgets to communicate important ideas, but should make creative use of the resources available to them.

“It’s always a big issue, you know, no matter where we are. But how is it that you use the resources that you have in order to tell that story? How do you apply what you have to communicate those ideas that you feel are important and how you do that in a creative way?,” she concluded.

Meanwhile, PUNCH Online reported Monday that Nollywood actors Wale Ojo and Linda Ejiofor were among Nigeria’s biggest winners at the recently concluded 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards.

The 22nd edition of the awards was held on Sunday, November 15, 2026, at the Marriott Hotel in Ikeja, Lagos State.

The post Stop copying Western cinema, AMAA jury president tells African filmmakers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: APC chieftain urges Amaechi to stop criticising Tinubu
description:
…Says delegation of duties reflects leadership, not ineptitude



By Daniel Abia



PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Barrister Princewill Dike, has urged former Minister of Transportation and African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, Rt. Hon. R
content:
…Says delegation of duties reflects leadership, not ineptitude

By Daniel Abia

PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Barrister Princewill Dike, has urged former Minister of Transportation and African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, Rt. Hon. Rotimi Amaechi, to stop criticising President Bola Tinubu over his leadership style.

Dike, a member of the APC Presidential/Rivers Rainbow Coalition Candidates Campaign Council, said the President had the constitutional and administrative discretion to delegate responsibilities to anyone he considered capable.

He argued that delegation of duties was a hallmark of effective leadership rather than evidence of incompetence, as allegedly suggested by Amaechi in his recent remarks.

Amaechi had reportedly spoken about his experience working closely with Tinubu during the 2015 presidential campaign, questioning the President’s capacity based on his approach to assigning responsibilities.

Reacting, Dike described such an interpretation as a misunderstanding of leadership principles.

“To interpret the delegation of responsibilities as a sign of ineptitude shows a misunderstanding of the principles of leadership,” he said.

According to him, the ability to identify competent individuals, assign responsibilities and harness their intellectual capacities is one of the defining attributes of effective leadership.

“No successful leader can personally undertake every responsibility,” he said.

Dike maintained that effective leaders distinguish themselves by building teams of capable and resourceful individuals whose expertise strengthens decision-making and promotes result-oriented governance.

“Leadership is not about being a jack of all trades or attempting to control every aspect of administration, but about building a competent team, providing direction and ensuring accountability in the discharge of assigned duties,” he added.

To support his argument, the APC chieftain cited the biblical account of Moses and his father-in-law, Jethro, in Exodus 18:14-26, where Jethro advised Moses to appoint capable men to handle disputes among the Israelites rather than bear the entire responsibility alone.

He said Moses accepted the advice and appointed leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, establishing a system of shared responsibility that improved administration and reduced his workload.

Dike also cited Jesus Christ’s delegation of responsibilities to his disciples, as recorded in Luke 9:1-2 and 6, as well as the appointment of Stephen, Philip and five others by the early Apostles to handle administrative responsibilities in Acts 6:1-7.

“Delegation of duties is key in governance,” he said, adding that the examples demonstrated that delegation was a longstanding principle of effective leadership and should not be misconstrued as weakness.

He further referenced renowned neurosurgeon Ben Carson’s 2008 book, Take The Risk, which discusses the Bible as a source of practical wisdom for everyday living.

On the political implications of Amaechi’s comments, Dike challenged opposition politicians to present credible alternative economic policies rather than focus on personal criticism of Tinubu.

He said those seeking to lead the country in 2027 should demonstrate their preparedness through concrete policy proposals capable of addressing Nigeria’s economic and developmental challenges.

Dike also expressed confidence in Tinubu’s political prospects ahead of the 2027 general election, cautioning opposition politicians against underestimating the President’s political experience and mobilisation capacity.

He particularly highlighted the political influence of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, describing him as a significant factor in political calculations ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The APC chieftain maintained that the forthcoming electoral contest would require more than political rhetoric and personal attacks, insisting that opposition candidates must demonstrate an understanding of contemporary political realities and present convincing alternatives to Nigerians.

title: ADC crisis: Keyamo accuses Ojudu of misrepresenting his comments
description:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has accused former lawmaker Senator Babafemi Ojudu of misrepresenting his comments on the leadership crisis in the African Democratic Congress out of what he described as hatred for President Bola Tinubu.

Keyamo, through his Special
content:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has accused former lawmaker Senator Babafemi Ojudu of misrepresenting his comments on the leadership crisis in the African Democratic Congress out of what he described as hatred for President Bola Tinubu.

Keyamo, through his Special Adviser on Media and Research, Gabriel Emameh, said Ojudu’s criticism was part of a sustained campaign against the President, despite his continued claim to membership of the All Progressives Congress.

In a statement issued on Monday, Emameh said the minister’s earlier remarks on the ADC crisis were intended to defend the judiciary and caution opposition figures against making inflammatory statements following a Federal High Court judgment nullifying the party’s leadership.

The court, presided over by Justice Peter Lifu, had ruled against the leadership structure led by former Senate President David Mark, a development that has raised questions about the validity of decisions taken by the affected party leadership, including the process that produced former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate.

Ojudu had criticised Keyamo in a piece titled ‘Festus, Let Us Preserve the Country’, accusing him of taking a position that could heighten political tensions and undermine democratic tolerance.

However, Emameh maintained that the minister did not call for the suppression of opposition voices or advocate violence, but merely explained the implications of court judgments and the need for political actors to respect judicial decisions.

He quoted Keyamo as citing the Supreme Court’s decisions on the 2019 Zamfara governorship and legislative elections, as well as the 2020 Bayelsa governorship election, where the ruling APC lost victories initially secured by its candidates.

According to him, the party accepted those judgments despite their political consequences.

Keyamo was also quoted as saying that the heavens would not fall if Atiku did not appear on the ballot in the 2027 presidential election.

Emameh argued that the minister’s position was that the ADC could remain on the ballot while the eligibility of Atiku to contest under the party’s platform could be affected by the court’s decision on the leadership that conducted the nomination process.

He said there was nothing undemocratic about drawing attention to the possible legal consequences of the judgment.

The presidential politics of 2027 has increasingly brought the ADC into focus as opposition figures seek to build a formidable coalition against the ruling APC. However, the party’s leadership dispute has introduced fresh uncertainty into those efforts, particularly over its internal processes and the authority to conduct party activities.

The statement read in part, “As a senior member of the Bar and indeed a member of the Inner Bar, Mr Keyamo was only discharging a professional duty by clarifying the letter and spirit of the law and defending the sanctity of the courtroom. Whilst cautioning against such threats, he affirmed that court pronouncements are sacrosanct, however unpleasant some might find them.

“On February 13, 2020, when the Supreme Court nullified the victory of the APC governorship candidate in Bayelsa State, David Lyon, a day to his swearing-in (when he was in fact inspecting the stadium to be used), the APC took it with equanimity on the chin. When the Supreme Court in 2019 stripped all the APC victorious candidates from top to bottom (Governor to House of Assembly) of their victories at the polls in Zamfara State and replaced them with the PDP candidates that all lost at the polls, this is what Atiku Abubakar said at the time (JUSTICE HAS PREVAILED IN ZAMFARA). That judgment was against the ruling party. We took it on our chins. You cannot abuse judges and blackmail the judiciary when it doesn’t go your way. Heavens will not fall if a certain Atiku Abubakar is not on the ballot in 2027.”

Taking a swipe at Ojudu, Emameh recalled that the former senator, who served as political adviser to former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, had openly declared in 2022 that he would not support Tinubu if he emerged as the APC presidential candidate.

He also alleged that Ojudu had “repeatedly criticised the President on social media while continuing to identify as an APC member.”

Emameh further argued that Ojudu’s continued political engagement without harassment was “evidence of the administration’s tolerance of dissent.”

He noted that the former senator still held a political appointment in Ekiti State, governed by the APC, “while his daughter is also serving in an appointment under the Tinubu administration.”

The minister’s aide consequently dismissed Ojudu’s allegation of growing intolerance under Tinubu, insisting that “opposition figures have continued to organise, campaign and express their views without state-sponsored intimidation.”

He said the country had not witnessed state-sponsored political assassinations or midnight arrests of political opponents under the current administration.

On Ojudu’s reference to a property transaction involving Keyamo in Wuse, Abuja, Emameh said the minister purchased the property in 2008 from Independent Communications, the company associated with the ownership of TheNEWS and PM News.

He described Keyamo as “a long-standing real estate investor” and accused Ojudu of failing to provide the full context of the transaction.

Emameh, however, concluded by wishing Ojudu well in exercising his freedom of expression, insisting that the former senator remained free to criticise the President without hindrance.

title: ‘You are not going for Grammy’ — Osita Iheme warns politicians against dancing at rallies
description:
Nollywood actor Osita Iheme, popularly known as Pawpaw, has cautioned Nigerian politicians against turning campaign rallies into entertainment events, urging them to focus on presenting their achievements, competence and plans for the country.
Iheme made the remarks in a post on his Instagram page,
content:
Nollywood actor Osita Iheme, popularly known as Pawpaw, has cautioned Nigerian politicians against turning campaign rallies into entertainment events, urging them to focus on presenting their achievements, competence and plans for the country.

Iheme made the remarks in a post on his Instagram page, where he expressed displeasure with politicians who dance on stage during campaign rallies instead of using the platforms to explain their programmes to Nigerians.

The actor urged political leaders to demonstrate what they had achieved, outline what they intended to do if elected and convince voters through their ideas rather than stage performances.

He listed what he considered the priorities Nigerians should demand from political leaders, stressing the need for competence over choreography, good governance over hype and leadership over entertainment.

“Show us what you have done. Tell Nigerians what you will do. You are not going for Grammy,” he said.

Iheme also warned politicians against making dancing a major feature of their campaign appearances.

“I don’t want to see you guys’ dance on stage again. Be careful,” he added.

His comments come as political activities gradually gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections, with political parties and their candidates expected to intensify campaigns and mobilise supporters across the country.

The post ‘You are not going for Grammy’ — Osita Iheme warns politicians against dancing at rallies appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Power Minister Tegbe reaffirms Tinubu administration’s commitment to improved electricity supply
description:
Seeks media partnership to strengthen public trust, highlights progress on power sector reforms


The Minister of Power, Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, has reaffirmed the Tinubu administration’s commitment to transforming Nigeria’s electricity sector through sustained reforms, infrastructure investment a
content:
• Seeks media partnership to strengthen public trust, highlights progress on power sector reforms

The Minister of Power, Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, has reaffirmed the Tinubu administration’s commitment to transforming Nigeria’s electricity sector through sustained reforms, infrastructure investment and improved service delivery.

Speaking at an interactive luncheon with senior editors in Lagos on Friday, Tegbe acknowledged Nigerians’ frustration over unreliable electricity supply, assuring them that the Federal Government was addressing the sector’s longstanding challenges through coordinated, measurable interventions.

He stressed that rebuilding public confidence would require not only improved electricity supply but also transparency, accountability and sustained engagement with the media.

The Minister described the sector’s challenges as systemic, citing gas supply constraints, ageing infrastructure, vandalism, transmission constraints, poor metering and commercial challenges affecting the entire electricity value chain.

According to him, these interconnected problems require disciplined reform implementation rather than isolated interventions or short-term solutions.

Highlighting progress, Tegbe disclosed that the Federal Government had settled ₦1.23 trillion of the ₦3.3 trillion approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for verified legacy debts owed to electricity generation companies.

He further revealed that more than 2.8 million electricity customers had been metered between 2023 and October 2026 under the Presidential Metering Initiative, while recently commissioned substations and equipment had added over 1,300MVA to national transmission capacity.

The transmission improvements cover locations including Apapa, Ijora, Ikeja, Kumbotoso, Dankata, Mashi, Dan-Agundi, Biliri and Walalambe.

Other interventions include building a new National Grid Control Centre in Osogbo to replace the existing facility, which is over 60 years old, alongside efforts to expand generation capacity to 10,000MW.

Looking ahead, Tegbe outlined the Ministry’s corridor-based electricity development strategy, targeting the Lagos-Ogun, Benin-Enugu-Port Harcourt and Abuja-Kaduna-Kano economic corridors as critical energy zones.

He explained that the Lagos-Ogun axis and Abuja franchise area, which together account for more than 50 per cent of national electricity demand, would serve as proposed pilot locations for 24-hour energy zones, subject to technical readiness and commercial viability.

The initiative seeks to align generation, transmission and distribution capacity with demand in major economic centres.

On infrastructure security, the Minister disclosed that the Federal Government had approved a coordinated anti-vandalism campaign involving relevant security agencies, supported by stronger legal measures to protect critical electricity assets.

Addressing the role of the media, Tegbe called for a constructive partnership built on factual reporting, professional scrutiny and transparent communication of government interventions.

He emphasised that Nigerians deserved timely explanations of electricity disruptions, remedial actions and the responsibilities of institutions across the power value chain.

While acknowledging that the sector remained far from meeting national expectations, the Minister expressed confidence that sustained reforms, institutional collaboration and disciplined implementation would progressively improve electricity supply.

He assured the editors that the Ministry would maintain open communication channels, welcome constructive criticism and provide regular updates on reform implementation.

Tegbe reiterated that the ultimate measure of success would not be installed capacity or policy announcements alone, but tangible improvements in electricity supply to Nigerian homes, businesses and industries.

The post Power Minister Tegbe reaffirms Tinubu administration’s commitment to improved electricity supply appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Two killed in fresh attack on Plateau communities
description:
From Jude Owuamanam, Jos
Two persons have been killed and several others wounded in an attack by gunmen on Sho village in Barkin Ladi and Sambak community in Riyom local government areas of Plateau State.
According to the National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), Rw
content:
From Jude Owuamanam, Jos

Two persons have been killed and several others wounded in an attack by gunmen on Sho village in Barkin Ladi and Sambak community in Riyom local government areas of Plateau State.

According to the National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, the first incident occurred at about 1:57 a.m. on Sunday, when the attackers, whom he identified as Fulani terrorists, from the direction of Fass, invaded Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, killing Dauda John Davou, 42.

The same gunmen also attacked Jol community at around 12:10 a.m. but were repelled by vigilantes from the community.

Tengwong, in a statement on Monday, said that later the same day, the same group from the same direction attacked Sho village in Barkin Ladi LGA at about 5:20 p.m., killing Da Ishaku Pam Vwos, aged 79.

The latest round of killings came less than 24 hours after the All Progressives Congress (APC) North Central campaign train berthed in Jos, where President Bola Ahmed Tinubu promised to rebuild villages ravaged by age-long crises in the state.

They also came less than two days after the lifting of the state of emergency by the Plateau State government.

Tengwong said: “BYM, under the leadership of its National President, Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, Esq., is deeply concerned over renewed attacks on Berom communities in Riyom and Barkin Ladi Local Government Areas of Plateau State, which have claimed two lives within hours.

“These incidents followed Wednesday’s shooting of Joshua Doro Dafwel in Jol, who is currently receiving medical attention.

“On the same day, Ina Arin was killed when he and his friend, Abok Gyang, were ambushed on their way home to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang narrowly escaped.

“BYM is particularly concerned by reports from communities of suspicious movements of Fulani individuals from the direction of Fass, which has reportedly been renamed Tafawa. These reports require urgent investigation to establish the facts, determine the circumstances surrounding the movements and identify anyone connected to the attacks.”

While commending the vigilance and courage of local security volunteers, BYM stressed that communities should not be left to defend themselves against armed attacks without adequate and sustained support from security personnel.

Tengwong therefore called on President Tinubu, Governor Caleb Mutfwang and all relevant security agencies to urgently strengthen security deployments in vulnerable communities, investigate the latest killings and ensure that those responsible were identified and brought to justice.

He added: “It is particularly troubling that these attacks continue despite repeated security assurances and high-profile political engagements in Plateau State. The killing of a 79-year-old man in his community further underscores the vulnerability of innocent residents, including the elderly, who deserve protection and the right to live without fear.”

He said that the people of Plateau deserved more than promises, but concrete action and the assurance that their lives and communities were protected.

“Behind every casualty is a grieving family and a traumatised community. Our people deserve to sleep peacefully, return home safely and go about their daily activities without the constant fear of being attacked or killed,” the statement said.

The post Two killed in fresh attack on Plateau communities appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‘Children Are Not Witches’ — Danish worker shares recovery of boy rescued in Akwa Ibom
description:
Danish humanitarian worker Anja Ringgren Loven has shared photographs showing the recovery of a boy identified as Godbless, four months after he was rescued following alleged abuse and abandonment over witchcraft accusations in Akwa Ibom State.
Loven shared a video showing the boy severely malnouris
content:
Danish humanitarian worker Anja Ringgren Loven has shared photographs showing the recovery of a boy identified as Godbless, four months after he was rescued following alleged abuse and abandonment over witchcraft accusations in Akwa Ibom State.

Loven shared a video showing the boy severely malnourished and eating shortly after his rescue, alongside a recent photograph in which he appeared healthy and happy.

The humanitarian worker also disclosed that Godbless was rescued alongside his brother and sister.

In a Facebook post on Friday, Loven reflected on the children’s progress and reiterated her opposition to the stigmatisation of children through witchcraft accusations.

Accompanying the video from the time of the rescue was the caption: “Children are not witches.”

She wrote, “It has been four months since we rescued Godbless and his brother and sister.

“For nearly 14 years, I have rescued children accused of being witches. All of them would have been dead today.

“My eyes cannot stop looking at the first picture.”

Loven’s latest update highlighted the boy’s recovery since he was found in a severely weakened condition.

She also disclosed that Hope, one of the children, had graduated from primary school and was preparing to begin secondary education in September.

The update comes amid continued concerns over the abuse and neglect of children accused of witchcraft, a practice that has exposed vulnerable children to violence, abandonment and other forms of mistreatment.

The post ‘Children Are Not Witches’ — Danish worker shares recovery of boy rescued in Akwa Ibom appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: FG unveils Digital Education Strategy to tackle Out-of-School Children, Teacher shortages
description:
The Federal Government has unveiled a National Education Technology Strategy aimed at tackling the challenges of out-of-school children and teacher shortages through digital learning platforms, improved learner identification and wider access to educational resources.
The National Coordinator of the
content:
The Federal Government has unveiled a National Education Technology Strategy aimed at tackling the challenges of out-of-school children and teacher shortages through digital learning platforms, improved learner identification and wider access to educational resources.

The National Coordinator of the Special Programmes Operation and Implementation Unit at the Federal Ministry of Education, Adebayo Onigbanjo, disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Abuja, where he outlined the strategy designed to integrate 26 government initiatives into a unified digital education system.

Onigbanjo explained that the initiatives were not intended to operate as separate projects but as interconnected interventions to strengthen teaching, learning, education management, skills development and financing.

He said the National Education Verification and Identification initiative would enable the government to identify children outside the formal education system and assign them unique Learner Identification Numbers to support targeted interventions.

According to him, the data would help the government reach out-of-school children, girls and learners enrolled in home education programmes.

He also said the Inspire Live initiative would connect pupils in schools without qualified subject teachers to certified educators through digital platforms.

The programme would be supported by zero-rated data services to remove internet subscription costs as a barrier to accessing online lessons.

“The main message today is that these are not 26 separate projects; they form one connected system. The digital infrastructure is what connects them,” he said.

Onigbanjo said the strategy would also strengthen the connection between education, employment and entrepreneurship through initiatives such as the Digital Training Academy, Technical and Vocational Education and Training programmes, and entrepreneurship schemes.

He identified the NELFund loans, Student Venture Capital Grant and Tertiary Institution Staff Support as interventions intended to ease financial constraints affecting students and educators.

The coordinator added that public portals and dashboards would promote transparency by allowing citizens to monitor government commitments and track the implementation of education programmes.

He said the strategy would be implemented through five pillars, including data and interoperability, digital infrastructure, technology and procurement, and teacher transformation, alongside other measures to improve education delivery.

On data management, Onigbanjo said the government would build on the Nigeria Education Data Infrastructure by introducing common data standards that would enable existing education databases to exchange information automatically while preserving institutional autonomy.

He said priority would be given to information on schools, teachers, enrolment and education financing, while personal records would be protected under the Nigerian Data Protection Act.

On infrastructure, he said the government would prioritise reliable electricity, broadband connectivity and digital devices for schools, particularly in rural and underserved communities.

He added that the strategy would also provide for the maintenance of such facilities and build on existing national connectivity initiatives, including Project BRIDGE and the Universal Service Provision Fund.

The coordinator said the government would adopt vendor-neutral standards and transparent, performance-based procurement systems to encourage Nigerian developers to create technology solutions aligned with the national curriculum.

He further disclosed that the National Teachers’ Digital Competency Framework would establish standards for teachers’ digital skills, certification and career progression, supported by a national teacher professional development portal.

According to him, the strategy aligns with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and the Federal Ministry of Education’s vision of using education to promote national development, innovation and global competitiveness.

Onigbanjo acknowledged the contributions of the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, state governments, development partners, the private sector, academia and civil society to the development of the strategy.

He particularly recognised the roles of the Mastercard Foundation and the World Bank Group.

The announcement comes amid persistent challenges in Nigeria’s education sector, including the large number of children excluded from formal education and shortages of qualified teachers in public schools.

A 2024 UNICEF report estimated that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, comprising 10.2 million primary school-age children and 8.1 million children of junior secondary school age.

However, the Federal Ministry of Education has cited an estimated 15 million out-of-school children in its more recent interventions.

Teacher shortages also remain a major concern. Data reportedly obtained from the ministry’s digital education database showed that 31.8 million learners in public schools were being served by 592,077 teachers, representing an estimated learner-teacher ratio of 54 to one.

The Universal Basic Education Commission has also estimated that the basic education sector requires an additional 194,876 qualified teachers.

The new strategy builds on the Federal Government’s rollout of the Digital National Education Management Information System (DNEMIS), launched in July 2026 to improve education data collection, planning and accountability.

During its initial nationwide rollout, the platform reportedly captured information from 124,548 schools, covering more than 40 million learners and 1.19 million teachers.

The Federal Government says the National Education Technology Strategy will provide a coordinated framework for deploying technology to address these challenges and ensure that investments in digital education translate into improved learning outcomes.

The post FG unveils Digital Education Strategy to tackle Out-of-School Children, Teacher shortages appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: [VIDEO] Doctors, Teachers Won’t Pay Tax When I Become Governor – PDP Lagos Candidate Deji Doherty
description: The Governorship candidate of the People’s Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has vowed that doctors and teachers will not pay tax if he emerges governor of the State. Deji pledged while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Monday.“Whe
content:
The Governorship candidate of the People’s Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has vowed that doctors and teachers will not pay tax if he emerges governor of the State.

Deji pledged while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Monday.

“When I am governor, I will definitely transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two people will not pay tax.”

He promised to employ measures such as a tax holiday and transport subsidy funded from the Federal Government palliative to make life easy for the people of the state.

“You will get a subsidy on your drugs, you will get a subsidy on your transportation. This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it.”

The governorship candidate applauded President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, including increased Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) allocation and lower import duties.


He also noted that private organisations can now plan their operation as a result of the economic stability brought by the President’s economic reforms.

“I support fully what my national leader is doing, the renewed hope agenda which is the agenda for the entire country.”

Commenting on the recent opposition attack in Lagos and across the country, he linked the incidents to the poor performance of state governors, including Lagos State.

He, however, argued that Lagos debt burden remains very high, alleging that Lagos has failed to implement the renewed hope agenda of the President at the state level.

“I do not support the agenda being materialised and crystallised in Lagos state.”

“All these fallouts of thuggery and removing of banners and tearing of posters and things like that definitely is what is going to happen because you are trying to cover up your inadequacies in government.”

The PDP governorship candidate urged the ruling party to create an enabling democratic environment for political activities to thrive. “The ruling party has to take responsibility,” he said.

description:
Nigerian comedian and actor, Adebowale Adedayo, popularly known as Mr Macaroni, has spoken about his reservations concerning marriage and romantic relationships.
The comedian reportedly shared his thoughts during an appearance on the In My Opinion Podcast, where he spoke about relationships and expl
content:
Nigerian comedian and actor, Adebowale Adedayo, popularly known as Mr Macaroni, has spoken about his reservations concerning marriage and romantic relationships.

The comedian reportedly shared his thoughts during an appearance on the In My Opinion Podcast, where he spoke about relationships and explained why he is reluctant to get married.

The episode, titled ‘I’m So Scared to Get Married’, was released on November 15.

His remarks highlight his concerns about marriage and the emotional commitment that comes with it.

In May 2025, the actor disclosed that he was afraid of committing himself deeply to someone who might not reciprocate his love.

He explained that he tends to withdraw whenever he notices himself developing feelings for someone because he fears being hurt.

He said, “I’m not thinking about marriage. I did not say I won’t get married, I’m just saying I’m not thinking about it right now.”

The comedian also admitted that heartbreak could affect his concentration and career, stressing that he was fully committed to his work at the time.

title: NIPR warns: AI making deception cheaper, faster and more convincing
description:
• Says PR professionals must prioritise human judgement, accountability, moral courage
________________________________________________________________________
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
The Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) is making
content:
• Says PR professionals must prioritise human judgement, accountability, moral courage

________________________________________________________________________

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

The Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) is making deception cheaper, faster and increasingly convincing, urging public relations professionals to strengthen ethical standards, accountability and human judgement in an era of technology-driven communication.

Nigeria’s Vice President of NIPR, Emmanuel Dandaura, gave the warning while delivering a presentation titled “Redefining Public Relations: Nigeria’s Gold Proposition for a Changing World” at the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja, themed “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World”.

He said the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, alongside the proliferation of misinformation, disinformation and malinformation, had made it increasingly difficult to establish trust in public communication.

According to him, the growing capacity of machines to generate information and persuasive content meant that public relations professionals must offer more than message production to remain relevant.

“This matters particularly in an age when artificial intelligence makes deception cheaper, faster, and increasingly convincing,” he said.

Dandaura maintained that the enduring value of public relations practitioners must lie in their ability to exercise sound judgement, uphold accountability, demonstrate moral courage and counsel institutions towards responsible conduct.

“Our competitive advantage must remain our ability not just to produce persuasive content, because machines can do that better, but most importantly, our enduring value must lie in judgment, accountability, moral courage and the ability to counsel institutions toward responsible conduct,” he said.

He argued that the challenge confronting the profession went beyond technological disruption, pointing to a widening gap between the growing volume of communication and declining public confidence.

“We communicate so much, yet we struggle so profoundly to trust one another,” he observed.

He questioned why trust had become increasingly fragile despite the availability of more communication platforms, sophisticated technologies and powerful algorithms.

The NIPR Vice President said the development underscored the need to redefine public relations from a profession primarily concerned with publicity and strategic communication to one that exercised strategic leadership and promoted responsible institutional behaviour.

He disclosed that the NIPR Governing Council adopted a new definition of public relations on July 22, 2025, as “a strategic leadership role that builds trust, reputation, relationships and drives inclusive development through ethical, transparent and respectful communication”.

Explaining the new definition, Dandaura identified five key elements: strategic leadership, trust, inclusive development, cultural respect, and ethics and transparency.

He said public relations practitioners should be involved in institutional decision-making processes from the beginning, rather than being invited only after decisions had been taken to manage public reactions.

According to him, involving practitioners at the communication stage after major decisions have been concluded compromises their ability to ensure responsible communication.

He also stressed that institutions must demonstrate responsible conduct rather than rely on favourable publicity to secure public confidence.

“An institution can enjoy visibility without enjoying credibility. It may achieve favourable publicity without public confidence,” he said.

Dandaura further challenged practitioners to make inclusive development a central component of their responsibilities, arguing that organisations must create value beyond their immediate institutional interests.

He said corporations could not claim to enjoy good community relations when host communities bore the costs of their operations without meaningful participation or benefits.

On cultural respect, he said African societies had historically employed consultation, mediation, storytelling and consensus-building to sustain relationships and social confidence, long before public relations became an established profession.

He urged practitioners to respect the cultural contexts through which different communities interpret information and construct meaning.

He emphasised that ethics and transparency must remain central to professional practice, not optional additions, particularly as artificial intelligence increased the sophistication of deceptive communication.

“The future of public relations is not simply about communication and how to communicate better. It is indeed about helping humanity to trust better, relate better and live better,” he said.

The post NIPR warns: AI making deception cheaper, faster and more convincing appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: God’s grace propelling Obi, Kwankwaso to unseat Tinubu – Babachir Lawal
description: A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, will defeat President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election, saying the duo enjoy God’s grace and widespread pu
content:
A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, will defeat President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election, saying the duo enjoy God’s grace and widespread public support.

Lawal, a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), stated this on Sunday during an interview on Arise Television, where he said the reception Obi and Kwankwaso receive from Nigerians showed that they enjoy divine favour.

“I have told everybody that talks to me that both Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have the grace of God upon their lives, which makes people like them,” he said.

“The population likes them. They just show up in the market. They don’t hire people to come to their rallies. People just turn out at their own expense.”

The former SGF said his experience in politics, including his involvement in the Buhari administration and Tinubu’s political campaign before the APC primaries, had helped him recognise signs pointing to a possible opposition victory.

“It’s not the first time I am in the position I am in now in politics. I have been in this position during Buhari’s time. Even this your president, I drove his system up to the primaries,” he said.

“So I am a very skilled and experienced person in the game. I can see the signs and we know the loopholes. And we are working on the loopholes.”

Lawal expressed confidence that the NDC would defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), insisting that the party had put structures and systems in place to achieve its objective.

“We have an inside chance of toppling this government. We are inside and we know we will beat this government,” he said.

“We know they are gone. We have put up structures and systems. I am 100 percent confident.”

He said the responsibility of the party’s technical team was to translate the popularity of Obi and Kwankwaso into electoral success by mobilising support, protecting votes and ensuring they were counted.

“This grace that God has bestowed upon them, it’s our duty, the technical people, to harmonise and crystallise this thing into delivering it at the polling station and protecting the votes and ensuring it’s counted,” he said.

On the recent departure of some prominent figures from Obi’s camp, including former Obidient Movement National Coordinator Yunusa Tanko, Nana Kazaure, Doyin Okupe and a former NDC Deputy National Publicity Secretary, Lawal said politicians were free to leave a party or political movement when their expectations were not met.

He compared the development with the departure of some politicians who had previously been close to Tinubu, including Kashim Imam and Rauf Aregbesola.

“I was with Bola Tinubu, but I left. I can remember Kashim Imam; he has also left. I remember Rauf Aregbesola, who was also with Bola Tinubu.

“But he has left. These are big politicians. But they left Bola Tinubu,” he said.

Lawal described movement between political parties as a normal part of politics, saying individuals joined parties for different reasons and had varying expectations.

He said while some politicians joined to benefit personally, others were motivated by a desire to contribute to the political system.

He added that the Obidient Movement was not driven by financial inducements, noting that some supporters might have left because they expected resources to meet their personal needs.

“Moreover, the Obidient system is not about money. And people have families to feed, bills to pay.

“And if they join the Obidient Movement hoping to get the resources to settle these, they will be disappointed. So, it’s only fair. They have their reasons for leaving,” he said.

The post 2027: God’s grace propelling Obi, Kwankwaso to unseat Tinubu – Babachir Lawal appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Flamingos star Esther Stephen shows off gifts from Sanwo-Olu
description:
Nigeria’s U-17 women’s football team player, Esther Stephen, has shared a video showing the gifts she received during the team’s visit to Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu.
In the video posted on social media, Stephen unboxed several items presented to the players, including an iPhone 17 Pro
content:
Nigeria’s U-17 women’s football team player, Esther Stephen, has shared a video showing the gifts she received during the team’s visit to Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu.

In the video posted on social media, Stephen unboxed several items presented to the players, including an iPhone 17 Pro Max, cash, a Lagos State souvenir, water bottles and other gifts.

She began by revealing the phone, expressing excitement as she showed it to her teammates and social media followers.

“Guess what he gave us, the players? Guess. You cannot guess. You guys cannot know either. It is a 17 Pro Max. It’s a 17 Pro Max,” she said.

Stephen also disclosed that Sanwo-Olu gave specific instructions concerning the phones, asking the players not to give them to anyone else.

“He said, do not dash anybody. Do not give it to anybody. It is a gift from you guys. You have money. You can give your money out, but do not give this gift out. That is his instruction,” she added.

The player subsequently showed the cash and other items she received, including a Lagos State souvenir, which she described as a Lagos State statue.

“Look at what we brought from there. Look at it. This is the Lagos State statue. It’s a Lagos State statue, guys,” she said while displaying the item.

She also unboxed a water bottle and other packages, admitting that she did not know what some of the items were.

Throughout the video, Stephen expressed appreciation for the governor’s gesture and the reception the team received during the visit.

Describing Sanwo-Olu as a father figure, she said, “Guys, this man is wonderful. He’s a father indeed.”

She ended the video by thanking the governor and praying for him, saying, “God bless you. God bless you.”

The post Flamingos star Esther Stephen shows off gifts from Sanwo-Olu appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Danish aid worker shares recovery of boy accused of witchcraft in A’Ibom
description:
Danish aid worker Anja Ringgren Loven has shared pictures showing the recovery of a boy rescued four months ago after he was allegedly branded a witch, starved, abused, and abandoned in Akwa Ibom State.
Loven shared a video showing the boy, identified as Godbless, severely malnourished and eating sh
content:
Danish aid worker Anja Ringgren Loven has shared pictures showing the recovery of a boy rescued four months ago after he was allegedly branded a witch, starved, abused, and abandoned in Akwa Ibom State.

Loven shared a video showing the boy, identified as Godbless, severely malnourished and eating shortly after his rescue, with the caption, “Children are not witches.”

In a Facebook post on Friday, she also shared a recent photograph of the boy looking healthy and happy, four months after he was rescued alongside his brother and sister.

Reflecting on the children’s recovery, Loven wrote, “It has been four months since we rescued Godbless and his brother and sister.

“For nearly 14 years, I have rescued children accused of being witches. All of them would have been dead today.

“My eyes cannot stop looking at the first picture.

“How cute a face is a child allowed to have? I feel like squeezing those little munchkin cheeks.

“Support Land of Hope, and we can save more lives.”
Loven, who runs the child protection organisation Land of Hope, has shared several accounts of children rescued after being accused of witchcraft in parts of Akwa Ibom State.

In October 2025, she shared photographs of a young girl identified as Christiana, who was reportedly rescued from the streets of Akwa Ibom after being accused of witchcraft, beaten and abandoned.

Similarly, in August 2025, she shared the progress of Hope, a Nigerian boy rescued after being branded a witch and abandoned by his family.

Hope had graduated from primary school and was preparing to begin secondary education in September, according to the aid worker.

The post Danish aid worker shares recovery of boy accused of witchcraft in A’Ibom appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG Introduces VPASS To Improve Airline Travel Experience
description: Nigeria’s aviation sector is set for another major digital transformation with the introduction of the Virtual Passenger Processing System (VPASS), aimed at improving passenger processing, enhancing security and making air travel more seamless.Passengers are required to onboard by taking a dig
content:
Nigeria’s aviation sector is set for another major digital transformation with the introduction of the Virtual Passenger Processing System (VPASS), aimed at improving passenger processing, enhancing security and making air travel more seamless.

Passengers are required to onboard by taking a digital picture on the system, input your National Identity Number (NIN), and downloading the VPASS App from the Google Play Store.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, said he has directed all domestic airlines to integrate their operations into the new platform by the end of December, warning that compliance with the directive is mandatory.

The initiative is expected to strengthen data management and deliver a more efficient passenger experience across the country’s airports.
