title: (BREAKING) 2027: Amid convoy attack, Presidency accuses Kwankwaso of telling supporters to improvise weapons
description:
The Presidency has accused former Kano State Governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, of encouraging his supporters to improvise dangerous weapons ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The allegation was raised by President Bola Tinubu’
content:
The Presidency has accused former Kano State Governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, of encouraging his supporters to improvise dangerous weapons ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The allegation was raised by President Bola Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, in a post on his X account following Kwankwaso’s political rally in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State on Sunday.

Onanuga alleged that Kwankwaso made comments capable of encouraging confrontation while addressing supporters at the rally.

The presidential aide quoted the former governor as telling his supporters: “Continue to stay prepared; do not go easy on these shameless people.”

He further alleged that Kwankwaso encouraged his followers to improvise dangerous weapons, expressing concern that such remarks could heighten political tensions and promote violence ahead of the next general elections.

Onanuga argued that prominent political figures should use their influence to encourage restraint, tolerance and peaceful political engagement rather than make statements that could be interpreted as preparing supporters for physical confrontations.

Reacting to the allegation, human rights activist Comrade Musa Bala Gaye called on security agencies to intervene, warning that the development could threaten peace in Kano State if not properly addressed.

Gaye maintained that political campaigns should provide an opportunity for candidates and parties to present their policies and ideas rather than encourage intimidation, political thuggery or the use of dangerous weapons.

The controversy comes amid reports of an attack on Kwankwaso’s convoy in Bichi on Sunday, during which several members of his entourage were reportedly injured and between six and seven vehicles damaged.

According to Ibrahim Garba Shuaibu, spokesperson for the Kano State NDC governorship candidate, Comrade Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, Kwankwaso and his entourage had earlier visited Tofa, Rimin Gado, Kabo, Gwarzo and Shanono before proceeding to Bichi for another political engagement.

Shuaibu said the earlier visits were completed without major security challenges but claimed that tension arose when the delegation arrived in Bichi, as some individuals reportedly began throwing stones.

He explained that Kwankwaso instructed members of the delegation to proceed with their activities despite the disturbance.

“Senator Kwankwaso told us to enter the town without fear or retreat. When we arrived, there was a sign of disturbance and stone-throwing, but we held our meeting peacefully,” Shuaibu said.

However, he alleged that the situation deteriorated as the delegation was preparing to leave, when some individuals emerged from a location and attacked their vehicles, smashing windscreens.

“It was on our way out that some people emerged from a location and started attacking our vehicles, smashing windscreens,” he added.

Shuaibu said between six and seven vehicles were damaged, while some members of the entourage sustained injuries.

Following the incident, NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi condemned the reported attack on his running mate, describing it as unacceptable and calling on the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate the matter.

In a statement issued on Monday, Obi urged the authorities to identify and arrest those responsible, including anyone found to have sponsored the attack.

He stressed that political disagreements should not lead to violence, intimidation or destruction of property, insisting that political competition must be settled through peaceful engagement and the ballot.

Obi also expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State leadership of the NDC and others affected by the incident, while wishing those injured a speedy recovery.

The competing allegations and reports of violence have added to concerns over political tensions in Kano as activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gather momentum.

The post (BREAKING) 2027: Amid convoy attack, Presidency accuses Kwankwaso of telling supporters to improvise weapons appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: FG unveils digital plan to tackle teacher shortage, out-of-school children
description:
The Federal Government says its new National Education Technology Strategy will help address the challenges of out-of-school children and teacher shortages through digital learning platforms, improved learner identification and expanded access to educational resources.
The National Coordinator, Spec
content:
The Federal Government says its new National Education Technology Strategy will help address the challenges of out-of-school children and teacher shortages through digital learning platforms, improved learner identification and expanded access to educational resources.

The National Coordinator, Special Programmes Operation and Implementation Unit at the Federal Ministry of Education, Adebayo Onigbanjo, disclosed this in a press briefing in Abuja on Monday while outlining the strategy, which seeks to integrate 26 government initiatives into a unified digital education system.

Onigbanjo said the initiatives were not designed to operate as separate projects but as interconnected interventions that would strengthen teaching, learning, education management, skills development and financing.

He explained that the National Education Verification and Identification initiative would, “enable the government to map children and assign them unique Learner Identification Numbers, making it easier to identify those outside the education system and direct interventions towards them.”

According to him, the data would support targeted programmes for out-of-school children, girls and learners enrolled in home education programmes.

He said the Inspire Live initiative would connect pupils in schools without qualified subject teachers to certified teachers through digital platforms, while zero-rated data would remove internet subscription costs as a barrier to accessing online lessons.

“The main message today is that these are not 26 separate projects; they form one connected system. The digital infrastructure is what connects them,” he said.

Onigbanjo said the strategy would also link education with employment and entrepreneurship through programmes such as the Digital Training Academy, Technical and Vocational Education and Training and entrepreneurship initiatives.

He identified, “the NELFund loans, Student Venture Capital Grant and Tertiary Institution Staff Support as interventions designed to ease financial constraints facing students and educators.”

The coordinator said public portals and dashboards would also strengthen transparency by allowing citizens to monitor government commitments and assess the implementation of education programmes.

He explained that the strategy would be driven by five pillars, including data and interoperability, digital infrastructure, technology and procurement, teacher transformation and other measures aimed at strengthening education delivery.

On data management, he said the government would build on the Nigeria Education Data Infrastructure by adopting common data standards that would allow existing education databases to exchange information automatically while preserving institutional autonomy.

He said “priority would be given to data on schools, teachers, enrolment and education financing, with personal records protected under the Nigerian Data Protection Act.”

On infrastructure, he said the government would prioritise reliable electricity, broadband connectivity and digital devices for schools, particularly in rural and underserved communities, while providing for the maintenance of such facilities.

He added that the strategy would build on existing national connectivity initiatives, including Project BRIDGE and the Universal Service Provision Fund.

Onigbanjo said the government would also adopt vendor-neutral standards and transparent, performance-based procurement systems to encourage Nigerian developers to produce technology solutions aligned with the national curriculum.

He said the National Teachers’ Digital Competency Framework would establish standards for teachers’ digital skills, certification and career progression, supported by a national teacher professional development portal.

The strategy, he said, aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and the Federal Ministry of Education’s vision of using education to drive national development, innovation and global competitiveness.

He acknowledged the contributions of the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, state governments, development partners, the private sector, academia and civil society to the strategy’s development, particularly the Mastercard Foundation and the World Bank Group.

The strategy comes against the backdrop of persistent challenges in Nigeria’s education sector, particularly the large population of children excluded from formal education and shortages of qualified teachers in public schools.

A 2024 UNICEF report estimated that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, comprising 10.2 million primary school-age children and 8.1 million of junior secondary school age.

The Federal Ministry of Education, however, has cited an estimated 15 million out-of-school children in its recent interventions.

The teacher shortage also remains a major concern. Data reported from the Federal Ministry of Education’s digital education database showed that 31.8 million learners in public schools were served by 592,077 teachers, representing a learner-teacher ratio of approximately 54 to one.

The Universal Basic Education Commission has estimated that an additional 194,876 qualified teachers are needed in basic education.

The strategy also builds on the Federal Government’s rollout of the Digital National Education Management Information System (DNEMIS), launched in July 2026 to improve education data collection, planning and accountability.

As of its initial nationwide rollout, the platform had captured data from 124,548 schools, covering more than 40 million learners and 1.19 million teachers.

The government says the new EdTech strategy will provide a coordinated framework for using technology to address these challenges and ensure that investments in digital education translate into improved learning outcomes.

The post FG unveils digital plan to tackle teacher shortage, out-of-school children appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UN chief urges countries to rein in ‘merciless’ killer robots
description:
The United Nations chief Antonio Guterres has called on countries on Monday to impose binding rules on the use of “merciless” lethal autonomous weapons systems, often dubbed “killer robots,” on the battlefield.
Warfare is undergoing a radical transformation as armies seek to capitalise on artificial
content:
The United Nations chief Antonio Guterres has called on countries on Monday to impose binding rules on the use of “merciless” lethal autonomous weapons systems, often dubbed “killer robots,” on the battlefield.

Warfare is undergoing a radical transformation as armies seek to capitalise on artificial intelligence to boost their fighting abilities by identifying and striking targets more quickly and accurately.

Amid a chorus of warnings against handing the power of life and death to autonomous machines, country representatives have gathered for a conference at the UN in Geneva this week to debate whether to launch talks on binding rules for such weapons.

“I call on you to move towards negotiating a legally binding instrument to regulate autonomous weapon systems — including clear prohibitions and restrictions,” Guterres said.

“Seize this moment,” he said in a video message to the conference, urging countries to “take action to prevent the use and spread of these merciless weapons.

“We must never stop shielding civilians from the carnage and devastation of armed conflict, and preventing unnecessary suffering.”

Others have also warned of the dangers inherent in fully autonomous weapons systems.

Human Rights Watch said the meeting of the UN’s Review Conference of the Convention on Conventional Weapons would leave civilians “dangerously exposed” if it failed to act decisively.

The meeting brings together 128 countries to decide whether to open negotiations on legally binding rules.

“The need to regulate autonomous weapons has taken on new urgency” with developments in AI, said the head of the Weapons and Conduct of Hostilities Unit at the International Committee of the Red Cross, Laurent Gisel.

Russia’s representative attempted Monday to block access to the discussions by observer states and civil society, which campaigners said was to dodge criticism of its own alleged use of such weapons.

Russia has reportedly used fully autonomous drones to deadly effect in Ukraine, while Kyiv’s defence industry is pushing to develop autonomous “drone swarms.”

– ‘Carefully cultivated ambiguity’ –

While many states are in favour of tighter rules, countries that have the technology are reluctant to have their hands tied.

At the UN General Assembly last month, 163 states adopted a resolution calling for negotiations on rules governing autonomous weapons.

Five countries voted against — the United States, Russia, Belarus, Israel and North Korea, which last week boasted of a new AI-enabled torpedo system.

Nine abstained, including Iran, Saudi Arabia and China, which has maintained a “carefully cultivated ambiguity,” said Laure de Roucy-Rochegonde of the French Institute of International Relations.

Washington has proposed a five‑year process to develop a non‑binding instrument, while NGOs and the ICRC are advocating for a one‑year timeline.

In 2023, Guterres and ICRC President Mirjana Egger called on states to ban autonomous weapons before 2026.

The ICRC is calling for a ban on two categories of autonomous weapons: so‑called “unpredictable autonomous weapons” and those designed or used to directly target humans.

But given the opposition from leading international powers, observers caution that it looks unlikely that agreement will be reached this week to start talks on binding rules.

AFP

The post UN chief urges countries to rein in ‘merciless’ killer robots appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Most coastal nations now include ocean action in climate plans — Report
description:
More than 95 per cent of recently submitted climate plans by coastal and island countries include ocean-based measures to tackle climate change, but most still require external support in funding, technology, data and institutional capacity to meet their targets.
A new analysis by the World Resource
content:
More than 95 per cent of recently submitted climate plans by coastal and island countries include ocean-based measures to tackle climate change, but most still require external support in funding, technology, data and institutional capacity to meet their targets.

A new analysis by the World Resources Institute, titled Ocean-Based Climate Action in 2025 NDCs, found that ocean-related commitments in national climate plans, known as Nationally Determined Contributions, rose from 62 per cent in 2015 to 73 per cent in 2022 and more than 95 per cent in the latest submissions.

The report, however, warned that translating the commitments into measurable results would remain difficult without international cooperation and support, particularly for developing countries.

“Sixty-one per cent of the 1,281 ocean-related commitments analysed were classified as conditional or partly conditional, meaning countries could not deliver them with their existing financial, technical, and institutional resources. The challenge was more pronounced among developing economies, with all commitments from low-income countries classified as conditional or partly conditional. The proportion stood at 87 per cent for lower-middle-income countries and 92 per cent for upper-middle-income countries, compared with 35 per cent for high-income countries,” the report stated.

The analysis identified institutional coordination and governance, reliable data, technology, technical expertise and finance as major areas where governments needed assistance.

It said the support required went beyond direct project financing to include policy reforms, clearer institutional responsibilities, effective monitoring systems and stronger capacity in public institutions and regulatory agencies.

Citing research by the High-Level Panel for a Sustainable Ocean Economy, the report noted that ocean-based climate solutions could provide up to 35 per cent of the annual emissions reductions needed by 2050.

Such interventions could also protect coastal communities and sustain industries dependent on healthy marine and coastal ecosystems.

On the nature of the commitments, the study found that adaptation accounted for 69.9 per cent, while 22 per cent focused exclusively on reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Another 8.1 per cent combined mitigation and adaptation.

Adaptation measures included mangrove and wetland restoration, coastal protection, improved planning and monitoring, and responses to flooding and saltwater intrusion into groundwater.

In sub-Saharan Africa, 84.95 per cent of ocean-related commitments focused on adaptation, with fisheries and coastal zone management emerging as major priorities.

The report said this reflected the region’s need to reduce disaster risks, strengthen food security, protect coastal livelihoods and develop sustainable export industries.

“Stronger fisheries management and the protection of coastal ecosystems could support food production and the livelihoods of coastal communities, while investment in resilient ports and infrastructure could protect trade and economic activities from rising sea levels and extreme weather.

“Although mitigation accounted for a smaller proportion of ocean-related commitments, countries were increasingly looking beyond conservation to decarbonise maritime transport and energy industries. 51.8 per cent of the 282 mitigation-only commitments analysed concerned ocean industries, including shipping, offshore renewable energy, alternative fuels, and port decarbonization. The measures include improving vessel efficiency, adopting cleaner fuels, reducing emissions from ports, and expanding offshore wind energy,” the report stated.

The analysis also found that countries’ priorities varied by income level and geographical location.

“Adaptation accounted for 88 per cent of ocean commitments in low-income countries, 80 per cent in lower-middle-income countries, 62 per cent in upper-middle-income countries, and 57 per cent in high-income countries. Conversely, commitments with a mitigation component increased from 12 per cent in low-income countries to 43 per cent in high-income countries,” it stated.

The report said this focus was particularly important to Pacific Island economies, where shipping connects communities to markets and essential services, while dependence on imported fuels creates economic pressure.

It stressed the need for international cooperation, technology transfer and support tailored to countries’ development needs.

The findings come amid growing concerns over the gap between national climate commitments and the action required to limit global warming.

Citing the United Nations Environment Programme’s 2026 Emissions Gap Report, the analysis said current policies could result in about 2.8 degrees Celsius of warming this century, while full implementation of existing national climate commitments would limit the increase to about 2.6 degrees Celsius.

The report identified the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP31, as an opportunity to link national ocean priorities with practical implementation and financing.

It said discussions under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change’s Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue had highlighted the need for stronger cooperation to overcome implementation barriers.

The report also pointed to the COP31 Presidency’s Climate Implementation Bridge, which seeks to connect national priorities with project preparation, implementation capacity and financing partners.

It added that the Blue NDC Challenge, an initiative through which governments cooperate on ocean-related climate commitments, had brought together members whose plans account for 332 commitments, representing 25.1 per cent of the global total.

The post Most coastal nations now include ocean action in climate plans — Report appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Jigawa PDP governorship candidate promotes issue-based campaign
description:
From Mohammed Abubakar, Dutse
Ahead of the inauguration of his governorship campaign council, scheduled for Wednesday, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate for Jigawa State, Mustapha Sule Lamido, has expressed his commitment to promoting an issue-based campaign as the countdown
content:
From Mohammed Abubakar, Dutse

Ahead of the inauguration of his governorship campaign council, scheduled for Wednesday, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate for Jigawa State, Mustapha Sule Lamido, has expressed his commitment to promoting an issue-based campaign as the countdown to the 2027 general elections gets under way.

He has, therefore, urged party supporters in the state to recommit themselves to effectively mobilising votes for the party in all the elections, rather than resorting to name-calling and abuse of political opponents in the state.

He made the declaration at the commencement of the pre-campaign consultative stakeholders’ meeting with party faithful across the three senatorial districts in the state, with a view to galvanising support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Describing the forthcoming poll as a defining moment for the party, the state and the country at large, the scion of the Sule Lamido political family said the issue of Jigawa’s development must be paramount.

A statement from his campaign office on Monday said the first engagement brought together party stakeholders from the 75 wards in Jigawa South-West Senatorial District, where discussions centred on the party’s preparations for 2027 and its vision for the development and prosperity of the state.

The consultations were subsequently extended to Hadejia in Jigawa North-East Senatorial District, where leaders and stakeholders from 85 wards participated in discussions on political mobilisation, party unity and development priorities, and concluded with an engagement with stakeholders from Jigawa North-West Senatorial District.

Lamido said the engagements were designed to strengthen the party’s grassroots structures, consolidate support and build a common agenda for Jigawa ahead of the 2027 elections.

The PDP said its campaign would focus on issues affecting ordinary citizens, with emphasis on presenting policies and programmes capable of addressing the state’s development challenges, especially as they concern women and youths.

With consultations and mobilisation activities gathering momentum, the opposition party is positioning itself for a major electoral contest against the APC in its bid to take over the Jigawa State Government House in 2027.

Lamido said the meeting focused on strategies for taking the party’s campaign message to every part of Jigawa State, expressing confidence in the party’s determination to challenge the APC through democratic engagements.

He, however, stressed that the PDP would not resort to political hostility, personal attacks or inflammatory rhetoric in its quest to win the election.

“We reaffirm our commitment to reaching every part of Jigawa State in a peaceful, orderly and dignified manner, without rancour,” he said.

He advised supporters to promote the PDP and its candidates through constructive arguments, policy discussions and the presentation of alternative programmes, rather than insults, personal attacks or disrespect towards political opponents.

The candidate expressed appreciation to participants for their commitment and sacrifices, while acknowledging the continued support, goodwill and prayers of the people of Jigawa State.

title: ‘This Is Unacceptable’ – Obi demands immediate probe into Kwankwaso’s convoy attack
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called for an immediate investigation into the attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Kano State.
Obi also urged security agencies to arrest and prosecute anyone found responsible
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called for an immediate investigation into the attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Kano State.

Obi also urged security agencies to arrest and prosecute anyone found responsible for the incident, including those suspected of sponsoring the attack.

In a statement issued on Monday, Obi condemned the violence, which reportedly occurred in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State. Several members of Kwankwaso’s entourage were said to have sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised.

The NDC presidential candidate described the incident as unacceptable, warning that political differences should not be allowed to degenerate into violence, intimidation or destruction of property.

“I am deeply saddened by reports of the attack on the convoy of my brother and running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and members of his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State,” he said.

Obi stressed that every Nigerian has the constitutional right to participate in the democratic process without fear of being attacked because of their political affiliation.

He maintained that disagreements among political parties and their supporters should be resolved through dialogue and peaceful engagement rather than violence.

The former Anambra State governor called on the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to identify those involved in the incident and ensure they are brought to justice, regardless of their political influence or position.

He also expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State leadership of the NDC and others affected by the attack, while wishing those injured a speedy recovery.

“Nigeria belongs to all of us. We may belong to different political parties, but we remain one people with a common destiny. No political ambition is worth the life of any Nigerian,” Obi added.

title: COP31: AI benefits must outweigh environmental costs – UN
description:
The United Nations’ climate chief Simon Stiell has highlighted the “great potential and great peril” of artificial intelligence in the battle against global warming on Monday, as COP31 host Turkey launched an initiative aimed at tackling the issue.
Named after the Turkish Mediterranean city hosting
content:
The United Nations’ climate chief Simon Stiell has highlighted the “great potential and great peril” of artificial intelligence in the battle against global warming on Monday, as COP31 host Turkey launched an initiative aimed at tackling the issue.

Named after the Turkish Mediterranean city hosting the UN talks, the voluntary “Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge” seeks to tap the technology’s potential in finding climate solutions and assess its growing environmental risks.

The pledge has received 80 endorsements so far, including countries and companies, but only a small number of nations are among them for now.

“We have arrived at a technological moment of both great potential and great peril. AI and other frontier technologies are a double-edged sword,” Stiell said at the launch of the pledge.

“We cannot ask people to accept higher bills, more planet-heating pollution and deeper inequality today in exchange for promises of a better tomorrow. AI benefits must outweigh its growing costs,” Stiell said.

AI is being deployed in a broad range of applications, from improving weather forecasts to monitoring industrial emissions and optimising renewable energy.

But the data centres that power the technology consume huge amounts of energy and water, fuelling anger in communities whose utility bills have soared and raising concerns about their growing carbon footprint.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged AI companies in June to disclose their environmental impact and commit to powering every data centre with renewable energy by 2030.

A UN study has found that the facilities consumed more electricity than all but 10 countries in 2025, and could be ahead of all but five by 2030.

Their water consumption could meet the annual basic water needs of the entire population of sub-Saharan Africa by 2030, according to the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health.

About 30 per cent of the electricity consumed by data centres comes from coal, followed by renewables at 27 per cent, natural gas at 26 per cent and nuclear at 15 per cent, according to the International Energy Agency.

– ‘Creating momentum’ –

Only 10 countries have signed up to the COP31 pledge so far, with the United States, China and the European Union missing from the list.

Major AI players such as chip designer Nvidia, ChatGPT developer OpenAI and Claude’s Anthropic are also missing, but the pledge was signed by the World Business Council for Sustainable Development, a group whose members include Amazon, Google and Meta.

“CEOs and boards need to step up and align business and investment plans with the world’s agreed climate goals,” Stiell said.

Deputy Secretary-General of the UN’s International Telecommunication Union (ITU), Tomas Lamanauskas, which worked with Turkey on the pledge, stressed that Monday marked the launch of the initiative, with the hope of gaining more endorsements.

“Eighty is not a limit,” Lamanauskas told AFP. “I think it’s about creating momentum. … We’ll be working with others to come on board as well.”

Turkey’s Industry and Technology Minister Mehmet Kacir told the panel that the backing so far “demonstrates growing support for our shared ambition.

“We must both reduce AI’s environmental footprint and harness its potential to modernise industry, improve energy efficiency, strengthen climate resilience and accelerate green development,” Karcir said.

But a corporate campaigner at nonprofit group Beyond Fossil Fuels, Jill McArdle, called the AI pledge a “distraction” whose “promises are vague.”

“The AI pledge risks giving Big Tech a green stamp without requiring it to address the real climate impacts of its infrastructure,” McArdle said.

AFP

title: Denmark seeks NIMASA partnership to boost cadet employment, blue economy growth
description:
By Steve Agbota
The Danish Government has expressed readiness to explore opportunities for Nigerian maritime cadets to gain sea-based employment as ratings aboard Danish vessels through engagements with Maersk Shipping.
It has also indicated interest in partnering with the Nigerian Maritime Administ
content:
By Steve Agbota

The Danish Government has expressed readiness to explore opportunities for Nigerian maritime cadets to gain sea-based employment as ratings aboard Danish vessels through engagements with Maersk Shipping.

It has also indicated interest in partnering with the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) on the agency’s Blue Economy Acceleration Programme (N-BEAP) Hackathon, signalling prospects for stronger cooperation in maritime capacity development and blue economy innovation.

The Danish Ambassador to Nigeria, Jens Ole Bach Hansen, disclosed this during a visit to NIMASA, where he led a delegation to explore opportunities for strengthening maritime cooperation between both countries.

He explained that discussions were ongoing with Maersk Shipping on the possibility of engaging Nigerian cadets as ratings on Danish vessels, providing them with valuable onboard experience while they advanced their careers in the seafaring profession.

The ambassador also acknowledged the potential of NIMASA’s N-BEAP Hackathon and expressed the Danish delegation’s interest in the initiative as a platform for promoting innovation, developing technology-driven solutions and unlocking opportunities within Nigeria’s blue economy.

“Other areas identified for possible collaboration include maritime security, intelligence sharing, digitalisation, seafarer education, cadet training, institutional cooperation and maritime financing,” Bach Hansen said.

Responding, the Director-General of NIMASA, Dr Dayo Mobereola, welcomed Denmark’s continued interest in Nigeria’s maritime industry, describing the engagement as an opportunity to consolidate the longstanding relationship between both countries.

He expressed appreciation for Denmark’s hospitality during the agency’s recent visit in September and its support for Nigeria’s successful election into the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Council.

“Our priority is to translate the longstanding diplomatic relationship between Nigeria and Denmark into practical partnerships that deliver measurable benefits to both maritime industries. We look forward to strengthening collaboration in seafarer development, maritime innovation, technical capacity building and other strategic areas that will create sustainable opportunities for Nigeria’s maritime sector,” Mobereola stated.

Mobereola emphasised that the priority of the agency was to translate the goodwill and diplomatic engagements between both countries into concrete partnerships and measurable outcomes.

He therefore called for the establishment of a clear follow-up mechanism that would connect NIMASA with relevant Danish government institutions, maritime organisations, training establishments and private-sector operators capable of providing technical support and strategic partnerships.

According to him, direct engagement with these institutions would enable both parties to identify areas of mutual interest, develop practical implementation arrangements and ensure that proposals presented during previous engagements translated into sustainable benefits for the maritime industries of both countries.

He reaffirmed NIMASA’s readiness to work closely with the Royal Danish Embassy and relevant Danish institutions to advance the identified areas of cooperation.

The NIMASA DG expressed optimism that the renewed partnership would strengthen seafarer development, promote maritime innovation, enhance institutional capacity and create new opportunities for Nigeria’s maritime sector. He assured the delegation of the agency’s openness to additional areas of collaboration that would support the shared maritime development objectives of both countries.

title: N52,500 minimum pension: PenCom seeks private sector funding
description:
The National Pension Commission has called on the private sector to contribute to the sustainability of the Federal Government’s ₦52,500 minimum monthly pension for low-income retirees, disclosing that the government and pension industry have so far provided ₦400bn to the Pension Protection Fund.
Th
content:
The National Pension Commission has called on the private sector to contribute to the sustainability of the Federal Government’s ₦52,500 minimum monthly pension for low-income retirees, disclosing that the government and pension industry have so far provided ₦400bn to the Pension Protection Fund.

The Director-General of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, said the pension industry contributed ₦50bn, while the Federal Government provided ₦350bn, including payments to clear outstanding pension backlogs.

Speaking during an interview with ARISE NEWS on Monday, Oloworaran said wider private-sector participation was necessary to sustain the initiative and guarantee financial security for vulnerable retirees.

She said, “But in order for this to be sustainable, so that we can continue to support a minimum pension and ensure that vulnerable Nigerians have security in old age, the private sector must come through. And as of today, the industry has contributed 50 billion, the federal government another 350 billion, because they went and paid all the backlog.”

Oloworaran explained that PenCom had engaged an actuary to assess the financial implications of the initiative and project its long-term sustainability.

She said the minimum pension arrangement would also be reviewed in line with inflation and the available funding.

According to her, the Pension Protection Fund had ₦38bn before the current administration, while the government and pension industry had since provided additional funding.

She expressed confidence that the current funding could sustain the initiative for at least 10 years based on existing projections.

“Conservatively, we’re good for the next 10 years. Conservatively,” she said.

The PenCom boss disclosed that 54 per cent of beneficiaries who had received payments under the initiative were private-sector retirees.

She added that nearly 70 per cent of workers expected to qualify for the programme were in the private sector.

PenCom disputes claims of unpaid federal pensions dating back to 2004

On complaints about unpaid federal pensions, Oloworaran disputed claims that some retirees who left service in 2004 and 2005 were still owed their entitlements.

She explained that retirees who left service before the introduction of the Contributory Pension Scheme in 2007 were covered by the Defined Benefit Scheme, which is managed by the Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate, rather than PenCom.

“I vehemently stand by what I’m saying. That under the contributory pension scheme, you don’t have anybody owed that much. Even PTAD as well, nothing,” she said.

However, she acknowledged that pension payments remained a challenge in some states, noting that only 14 of the 36 states were paying pensions regularly.

“We have 14 states that are paying up. But 14 out of 36 states is a lot. And some states are doing very badly,” she said.

Oloworaran also discussed the PenCare Health Initiative, which provides eligible retirees with access to healthcare services.

She said beneficiaries would enrol through their Pension Fund Administrators, adding that the scheme currently covered one general health check annually but did not include major operations or serious illnesses.

“What we are doing is setting aside a critical illness fund so that people can use that. Of course, that will then have a limit. If it runs out, we won’t be able to pay for it,” she said.

The PenCom DG said the commission was also working to ensure that retirees received additional support through the initiative.

title: Misinformation threatens public trust, social cohesion, PR professionals warn
description:
• Call for ethical communication, accountability, inclusion in AI-driven world
• Urge PR practitioners to challenge falsehoods and give young people seat at the table
___________________________________________________________________________
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
Public relations profe
content:
• Call for ethical communication, accountability, inclusion in AI-driven world

• Urge PR practitioners to challenge falsehoods and give young people seat at the table

___________________________________________________________________________

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

Public relations professionals from different parts of the world have warned that misinformation and disinformation increasingly threaten public trust, weaken institutions and deepen divisions in societies. They called for greater ethical responsibility, transparency and accountability in public communication.

They also urged communication practitioners to leverage their influence to promote truthful information, strengthen social cohesion and ensure that people with disabilities and other marginalised groups are not excluded from access to information.

The experts spoke during a panel session titled “Misinformation and Social Cohesion: Rebuilding Trust through Responsible Public Relations” at the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja.

The panel featured the Chief Executive Officer of the Chartered Institute of Public Relations, United Kingdom, Mr Alastair McCapra; the Chief Executive Officer of Ardent Communications and President of the Public Relations Society of the Philippines, Ms Ana Pista; an Enterprise AI Governance Architect from Egypt, Dr Mohamed Hussien Abdelaziz; David Obinna Anyaele of the Abia State Disability Commission; and Australian communication expert Adrian Cropley.

The session was moderated by Peter Mutie, Chief Executive Officer of Peterson Communications Limited, Kenya.

Speaking on the growing threat of misinformation, Pista said the spread of false information fuelled division, weakened institutions and eroded public confidence, particularly as artificial intelligence continued to transform the communication landscape.

She said public relations professionals had a critical responsibility not only to correct disinformation but also to promote truthful communication, ethical practices, transparency and accountability.

Pista argued that professionalising public relations had moved beyond an industry aspiration to become a societal responsibility, given the profession’s influence in shaping narratives, public opinion and institutional reputations.

“With the power comes the responsibility to protect the truth,” she said, advocating stronger professional standards, ethics, education and responsible digital governance.

She added that responsible public relations should not seek to control people’s thinking but provide them with truthful information to enable them to think, decide and act responsibly.

On his part, Anyaele said responsible communication must go beyond the accuracy of information to address accessibility, warning that people with disabilities were often excluded when communication materials were not provided in formats they could understand.

He said a message could be factually correct but remain inaccessible to a deaf person without sign language interpretation or a blind person without audio alternatives.

Anyaele cited Nigeria’s more than 35 million persons with disabilities, warning that the failure to make public information accessible left millions vulnerable to exclusion.

“Responsible communication must be for all. There is nothing about us without us,” he said.

He maintained that communication processes and publications must be designed to accommodate everyone, stressing that exclusion from information was a form of injustice.

He commended the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for its efforts to make its communication mechanisms more inclusive and called on government institutions at federal and state levels to strengthen accessibility.

Anyaele also welcomed the participation of persons with disabilities at the WPRF, noting that the provision of sign language interpretation had helped make the conference more inclusive.

Contributing, Cropley cautioned against the tendency to dismiss every disagreement or expression of opinion as misinformation, saying communication professionals must distinguish between falsehood, legitimate criticism and differing perspectives.

He said rebuilding public trust required establishing the credibility of messages through facts, background information and proper context.

According to him, public relations should be about building relationships rather than merely controlling narratives, particularly in a post-truth environment where people increasingly questioned information from institutions and authorities.

Cropley said emotional intelligence and the ability to build meaningful connections would be critical to restoring confidence and bringing communities together.

On the ethical challenges confronting the profession, he said practitioners must understand how ethical principles applied within the specific organisational, national and cultural contexts in which they operated.

He also emphasised the need for continuous education and a stronger conversation around morality, arguing that responsible communication required more than simply adhering to written professional codes.

Abdelaziz identified the growing gap between what technology, particularly artificial intelligence, makes possible and what professional conscience permits as one of the greatest ethical challenges facing public relations.

He advocated a combination of emotional and moral intelligence to guide practitioners in determining what is right and wrong in their use of emerging technologies.

McCapra, in his contribution, warned of a widening disconnect between organisations and younger generations, particularly Generation Z, saying communication professionals must understand their expectations, concerns and relationship with technology.

He noted the apparent contradiction in the attitude of young people towards artificial intelligence, explaining that while they were among its biggest users, many also feared that the technology could undermine their career prospects and future employment.

He urged practitioners to listen before speaking, stressing that even open and transparent communication could fail to gain public acceptance if organisations did not understand their audiences.

Cropley, however, challenged communication professionals to be courageous enough to speak up when organisations engaged in questionable practices, rather than simply complying with instructions from their employers.

He said practitioners must be prepared to challenge wrongdoing, even when doing so could be uncomfortable or threaten their professional interests.

According to him, the growing influence of artificial intelligence should also push public relations professionals towards more strategic advisory and leadership responsibilities within organisations.

Pista also called for greater involvement of young professionals in shaping policies on ethics, disinformation and responsible communication.

She said younger generations needed to be heard and given meaningful opportunities to contribute to decisions that would shape their professional future.

“They should have a seat at the table because, at the end of the day, the future is theirs,” she said.

The panel discussion formed part of the knowledge conference and parliamentary sessions of the 2026 Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum, themed “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World”.

title: Jigawa needs a listening leader, says PDP gov candidate
description:
The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Jigawa State, Mustapha Sule Lamido, has said that Jigawa needs a listening leader, not a furious one.
Lamido made the remarks while speaking during a series of strategic stakeholders’ meetings held across the state’s three senatorial dist
content:
The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Jigawa State, Mustapha Sule Lamido, has said that Jigawa needs a listening leader, not a furious one.

Lamido made the remarks while speaking during a series of strategic stakeholders’ meetings held across the state’s three senatorial districts ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The meetings, which involved stakeholders from Jigawa South-West, North-East and North-West Senatorial Districts, were aimed at commencing preparations for the 2027 election campaign.

Speaking at the Gumel meeting held on Sunday, which was the third and final leg of the strategic stakeholders’ meetings across the three senatorial districts, the PDP governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections, Mustapha Sule Lamido, said the state was in dire need of a compassionate and listening leader.

Lamido stated that Jigawa did not need a leader who was always angry and furious with his people, but one who listened, understood their pains, and responded to their needs and aspirations.

He noted that only a leader who carried every part of the state along, without sectionalism, and who prioritised the welfare of the people could bring the desired development and prosperity to Jigawa.

Lamido said Jigawa did not need a sectional leader who looked after only a particular region.

“Jigawa today does not need a leader who is sectional or who looks after only a particular region, but one who puts Jigawa first in its entirety to ensure development in all ramifications,” he said.

He added that the state did not need a leader who was always furious, but one who listened to his people.

“Jigawa today does not need a leader who is always furious, but one who listens to the calls of his people and meets their wants and needs,” Lamido said.

Lamido alleged that there had been a decline in education, health, and many other sectors under the current leadership in the state.

“In my view, the style of this present government does not befit our people,” he said in Hausa.

He assured the people that a vote for the PDP was a trust that would bring benefits to the voter.

“Whoever gives the PDP his vote, it is as if he has given it as amana, and he will enjoy the benefit of the vote he gave.

“If you elect us, we promise that, Insha Allah, we will help you and do for you what will make you happy,” he assured.

On the party’s plans, Lamido disclosed that the party had officially commenced preparations for the 2027 campaign.

“Today, we officially commenced preparations for the 2027 election campaign with 75 wards across Jigawa South-West Senatorial District,” he said.

He added that the party needed unwavering commitment from its supporters to the progress, development and prosperity of the state during the forthcoming elections.

According to him, “We also deliberated on several important issues and discussed strategic plans towards achieving our collective goals in 2027.”

He, however, recalled how discussions with key stakeholders proceeded during the North-East Senatorial District meeting, held in Hadejia, where leaders from 85 wards attended.

Lamido said the target remained the progress, development and prosperity of the beloved state.

“This is the third and final leg of the strategic meetings that we are holding today (Sunday) in Gumel, the headquarters of Jigawa North-West Senatorial District,” he declared.

He thanked the party’s supporters and well-wishers and urged them to remain committed and united ahead of the elections.

Lamido also promised old members of the PDP who had remained loyal since the party lost power 12 years ago.

He therefore urged them to exercise more patience, saying that the party was with them and that they would soon rejoice if God granted it victory in the forthcoming elections.

In his address at the meeting, the Jigawa State Chairman of the PDP, Babandi Ibrahim Gumel, said the party was fully prepared and ready for the 2027 polls.

He commended Mustapha Sule Lamido for the strategic meetings and said the massive turnout across the three senatorial districts showed the level of acceptance of the party.

Gumel said the party would continue to engage stakeholders from all wards across the state to ensure victory in 2027.

title: Only 14 states pay pensions regularly – PenCom

content:
The National Pension Commission has disclosed that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states are paying pensions regularly, acknowledging that some state governments are performing poorly in meeting their obligations to retirees.

The Director-General of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, made this known during an interview with ARISE NEWS on Monday, describing pension payments as a continuing challenge in several states.

“We have 14 states that are paying up. But 14 out of 36 states is a lot. And some states are doing very badly,” she said.

However, she did not name the 14 states that are making regular pension payments or identify the states defaulting on their obligations.

₦400bn pension fund can sustain minimum payments for 10 years — PenCom

Oloworaran also said the ₦400bn provided by the Federal Government and the pension industry for the Pension Protection Fund could sustain the minimum monthly pension initiative for at least 10 years, based on current projections.

She said the government contributed ₦350bn, while the pension industry provided ₦50bn.

Speaking during the interview, she explained that the commission had engaged an actuary to assess the cost of the initiative and project its long-term sustainability.

“Conservatively, we’re good for the next 10 years. Conservatively,” she said.

Oloworaran, however, noted that the funding projections could be reviewed in response to inflation and the amount available to support the programme.

She said the commission was committed to ensuring that vulnerable retirees continued to receive financial support through the minimum pension arrangement.

The PenCom boss also disclosed that the Pension Protection Fund had ₦38bn before the current administration, adding that the Federal Government’s contribution included payments to clear outstanding pension backlogs.

She said 54 per cent of beneficiaries who had received payments under the initiative were private-sector retirees, while nearly 70 per cent of workers expected to qualify were in the private sector.

Police pension dispute

On the dispute involving retired police officers seeking to exit the Contributory Pension Scheme and return to a defined-benefit arrangement, Oloworaran said the commission was working with the police to develop a solution that would protect their retirement funds.

She disclosed that different options had been presented to President Bola Tinubu for consideration, adding that the priority was to ensure that police retirees received improved pension benefits.

“But what we want to do is put a structure in place. Where we are sure that nothing at all will happen to the funds for our police,” she said.

Oloworaran said the ultimate objective was to ensure that retired police officers received more money, regardless of the pension arrangement eventually adopted.

“And the ultimate result is more money in the hands of police. Whether you do it in the scheme or outside the scheme, it doesn’t matter,” she said.

She expressed hope that the dispute would be resolved before the end of the year, although she acknowledged that government bureaucracy could delay the process.

“I’m hoping, I mean, government is tough. A lot of bureaucracy here and there. I’m hoping before the end of the year, we would have resolved the police issue,” she said.

Tinubu had launched the ₦52,500 monthly minimum pension guarantee on November 10, 2026, for 173,209 eligible retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme, ending a 22-year delay in implementing the provision of the Pension Reform Act.

He also inaugurated the Pension Industry Healthcare Plan for Retirees (PenCare), which is designed to provide free essential healthcare services to low-income pensioners.

The initiatives were unveiled at a ceremony in Abuja, where he was represented by Senate President Godswill Akpabio.

title: Bayelsa West Stakeholders Begin Grassroots Mobilisation Ahead Of 2027
description: Political stakeholders in Bayelsa West Senatorial District have begun grassroots mobilisation and consultations ahead of the 2027 general elections, with a pledge to strengthen political support across the district.The stakeholders made the commitment at a meeting convened by the Minister of State f
content:
Political stakeholders in Bayelsa West Senatorial District have begun grassroots mobilisation and consultations ahead of the 2027 general elections, with a pledge to strengthen political support across the district.

The stakeholders made the commitment at a meeting convened by the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Heineken Lokpobiri, which brought together the Deputy Governor of Bayelsa State, Peter Akpe, and other political leaders from the area.

The meeting focused on building unity among political actors, strengthening engagement at the community level and securing support for candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the forthcoming elections.

Speaking at the gathering, Deputy Governor Peter Akpe said political leaders had been engaging with residents at the community, ward and unit levels to build support ahead of the polls.

He said the mobilisation effort was aimed at bringing party members together and strengthening their presence across the district.

Akpe also spoke of a target of securing large votes in each polling unit, while expressing confidence in the party’s chances in the coming elections.

In his remarks, Lokpobiri called on political stakeholders to demonstrate commitment to the mobilisation effort, stressing the need for collective action to achieve the party’s electoral objectives.

Another stakeholder, Fyneman Wilson, spoke about the political situation in Sagbama and the need for a change in representation ahead of the 2027 elections.

Bayelsa West Senatorial District comprises Sagbama and Ekeremor Local Government Areas.

The meeting comes as political activities and consultations begin to gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections, with stakeholders seeking to consolidate their support and strengthen grassroots engagement across the district.

title: AMAA 2026: Wale Ojo, Linda Ejiofor shine as ‘One Woman One Bra’ wins Best Film
description:
Nollywood actors Wale Ojo and Linda Ejiofor were among Nigeria’s biggest winners at the recently concluded 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards.
The 22nd edition of the awards was held on Sunday, November 15, 2026, at the Marriott Hotel in Ikeja, Lagos State.
It featured several films, actors, directors
content:
Nollywood actors Wale Ojo and Linda Ejiofor were among Nigeria’s biggest winners at the recently concluded 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards.

The 22nd edition of the awards was held on Sunday, November 15, 2026, at the Marriott Hotel in Ikeja, Lagos State.

It featured several films, actors, directors and other industry figures who took home awards across 26 nominated categories.

Ojo won the award for Best Actor in a Leading Role for Cameroon’s Lights Out (2025), while Ejiofor won Best Actress in a Supporting Role for The Herd (2025).

Her latest win follows her recognition for both Best Lead Actress and Best Supporting Actress at the 2026 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. There, she made history as the first person to win both categories in the same year.

Remarkably, the Kenyan-Nigerian co-produced film, One Woman One Bra (2025), won the top award, while The Color of Exile (2025) emerged as the most-awarded film of the night with four awards: Best Director, Achievement in Cinematography, Achievement in Sound and Best Actress in a Leading Role for Naky Savane.

Directed by Vincho Nchogu, One Woman One Bra won the coveted award for Best Film, Best Debut Feature Film by a Director, and the Ousmane Sembène Award for Best Film in an African Language.

According to Afrocritik, the film had its world premiere in the Biennale College Cinema section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival and won the Sutherland Award for Best First Feature at the 2025 BFI London Film Festival.

Founded in 2005 by the late Peace Anyiam-Osigwe, the AMAA Awards reward excellence in African filmmaking, diaspora cinema and technical mastery.

title: Suspected Thugs Attack Kwankwaso’s Convoy In Kano
description: There was a violent clash in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State after suspected thugs attacked the campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and the party’s Kano State governorship candidate, Comrade Aminu Abdussa
content:
There was a violent clash in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State after suspected thugs attacked the campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and the party’s Kano State governorship candidate, Comrade Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo.

Reports say that the incident occurred while the delegation was conducting a political mobilisation tour to seek public support, after completing engagements in Tofa, Rimin Gado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono and Bagwai local government areas.

Confirming the attack, the spokesperson for the NDC governorship candidate, Comrade Ibrahim Garba Shuaibu, said they had received intelligence reports while approaching Bichi that some people had blocked the road to prevent them from conducting the political rally.

According to him, upon arriving in the town, they noticed signs of stone-throwing, and shortly after passing the local government secretariat, a group of youths armed with dangerous weapons emerged and attacked their convoy.

Shuaibu added that the attack resulted in injuries to some of their supporters and damage to several vehicles, saying he personally saw about seven vehicles with smashed windscreens at the scene.

title: ‘Oil Tanker Set Ablaze In Hormuz Attack’
description: An oil tanker was set on fire by an attack in the Strait of Hormuz, which has been blockaded by Iran throughout the Middle East war, two maritime monitors said on Monday.The ship was exiting Hormuz near the Omani coast when an “unknown projectile” struck, causing a fire in the engine roo
content:
An oil tanker was set on fire by an attack in the Strait of Hormuz, which has been blockaded by Iran throughout the Middle East war, two maritime monitors said on Monday.

The ship was exiting Hormuz near the Omani coast when an “unknown projectile” struck, causing a fire in the engine room, UK Marine Trade Operations said.

Security monitor Vanguard identified the tanker as the Panama-flagged ON PHOENIX and said it was hit three nautical miles off Oman. Both agencies said all crew were safe.

Iran has heavily restricted traffic through Hormuz, insisting vessels use routes it has authorised. It has regularly targeted ships that transit without its authorisation.

AFP

title: ‘Provide Proof’, Akpabio Dares Amaechi Over Alleged Deduction From NDDC Contractors’ Payment
description: Senate President Godswill Akpabio has demanded proof from former Rivers State Governor and vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, supporting his allegation that he introduced a 50 per cent deduction from payments to contractors handling projects for the
content:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio has demanded proof from former Rivers State Governor and vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, supporting his allegation that he introduced a 50 per cent deduction from payments to contractors handling projects for the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC).

He disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Eseme Eyiboh.

Akabio’s reaction comes after Amaechi, a former Minister of Transportation, accused the Senate President of introducing the alleged deductions while addressing supporters at the ADC campaign rally held at the Tafawa Balewa Stadium in Bauchi State on Saturday.

The Senate President described the allegation as weighty and noted that Amaechi had yet to provide contract documents, payment records or details of identifiable transactions to substantiate the allegation.

His allegation followed what he described as recent comments by Akpabio against him in Port Harcourt.

He said, “An allegation delivered before an enthusiastic political audience does not, by that circumstance alone, acquire the status of a fact.”

The Senate President further urged the former governor to submit any credible evidence in his possession to the appropriate investigative authorities rather than use the allegation for political confrontation.

“If Amaechi possesses credible evidence of unlawful deductions involving NDDC contractors, the appropriate course is to identify the relevant transactions, disclose the supporting records and submit the material to competent investigative authorities and not the act of rabble-rousing,” he said.

On the Port Harcourt monorail project, which became controversial over its reported cost, incomplete implementation and failure to deliver the anticipated public transportation service, Akpabio said his record in office was equally open to public scrutiny, spotlighting Amaechi’s eight-year administration in Rivers State, which lasted from 2007 to 2015.

The Senate President also mentioned the Malaria-free Rivers State initiative, arguing that public officials should be prepared to account for expenditure, project delivery and value for money.

According to him, questions surrounding the projects should include the amount spent, the extent to which their original objectives were achieved and the institutional and contractual decisions that contributed to their outcomes.

“Public accountability does not begin and end with one’s political opponents. It extends to every public official entrusted with resources, authority and responsibility,” he stated.

According to him, the approaching 2027 general elections should not provide an excuse for making unsubstantiated allegations, adding that issues concerning the finances and administration of the NDDC deserved credible investigation.

The commission was established to address developmental challenges in the oil-producing Niger Delta region, particularly its infrastructure and environmental needs.

Akpabio maintained that the interests of the region’s residents should remain central to discussions about the commission, stressing the need for transparent procurement, completed projects and measurable developmental outcomes.

He added that Amaechi was entitled to raise concerns about public administration but had a responsibility to distinguish between allegations and claims backed by evidence.

“The credibility of a public allegation must rest not on the volume of its delivery, the status of its author or the occasion on which it is made, but on the quality of the evidence supporting it. Let the facts speak,” he added.

title: 2027: Oyo Accord gov candidate meets Ajimobi’s wife
description:
The Accord Party governorship candidate in Oyo State, Oriyomi Hamzat, has met with the wife of former governor Abiola Ajimobi, Ambassador Florence Ajimobi, ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Hamzat disclosed this in a post on Sunday, saying their meeting focused on the future of Nigeria and Oyo St
content:
The Accord Party governorship candidate in Oyo State, Oriyomi Hamzat, has met with the wife of former governor Abiola Ajimobi, Ambassador Florence Ajimobi, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Hamzat disclosed this in a post on Sunday, saying their meeting focused on the future of Nigeria and Oyo State as the next general elections approach.

He said their discussion also centred on the need for unity in support of President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition.

“Our conversation was centred on the importance of unity towards the realisation of Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s second-term ambition,” he said.

The broadcaster described the meeting as an opportunity for meaningful engagement despite political differences, stressing the need for mutual respect and a shared commitment to the development of the state.

“Moments like this remind me that beyond politics and our differences, there is always room for meaningful conversations, mutual respect and a shared commitment for the progress of our people,” he added.

Hamzat also reaffirmed his determination to contest the 2027 governorship election, describing his ambition as a collective effort rather than a personal political pursuit.

“My commitment to the service of Oyo State as the governor come 2027 remains unwavering, as this is not just my race; but our race,” he said.

He said his proposed administration would prioritise inclusive and people-centred governance, adding that his idea of “Governance with a Difference” would ensure that no one was left behind.

The Accord Party candidate also assured residents that he would continue to represent their interests in discussions and decisions concerning the state’s future.

“I will not step down, nor let down the trust you have placed in me,” he said.

Hamzat urged the people of Oyo State to remain hopeful about building a state where everyone counts.

title: Ondo Air Crash: NAF recovers black box, fixes memorial for Nov 26
description:
The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), commonly referred to as the black box, from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State.
The Service also announced plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony on Novembe
content:
The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), commonly referred to as the black box, from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State.

The Service also announced plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony on November 26, 2026, in honour of personnel and other victims who lost their lives in the NAF 931 aircraft accident.

The ceremony will take place at the National Military Cemetery in Abuja, providing an opportunity for bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the Air Force community to pay their last respects.

The Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed the developments in a statement on Sunday.

He said the memorial would serve as a formal expression of the Service’s respect and remembrance for those who died in the crash.

On the recovery operation, Ejodame confirmed that the Cockpit Voice Recorder, alongside other aircraft fragments and relevant evidence, had been retrieved from the crash site.

He explained that data recovered from the recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident.

According to him, the investigation is being conducted in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).

The Air Force spokesman reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to ensuring that the investigation meets the highest standards of professionalism, transparency and accountability, while supporting the independent technical processes required to establish the cause of the crash.

Ejodame also disclosed that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while efforts to identify the recovered remains were still ongoing.

He said the exercise had been particularly challenging due to the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth at which some of the aircraft wreckage had become embedded in the ground.

The NAF spokesman added that the Service was working with relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery operation and ensure appropriate remediation after the exercise.

He said the Air Force remained mindful of the grief experienced by bereaved families and was committed to providing them with sustained support.

The Service also acknowledged the cooperation of relevant agencies, host communities and other stakeholders who had assisted with the recovery and investigation efforts.

The Nigerian Air Force assured the public that it would continue to pursue a thorough investigation, responsible environmental management and a dignified remembrance of all those who lost their lives in the October 5 accident.

The post Ondo Air Crash: NAF recovers black box, fixes memorial for Nov 26 appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Why Atiku? The Answer is in The Solutions: by Paul Ibe
description:
Thank you for your open letter. Your central question—why Nigerians should expect an Atiku Abubakar presidency to deliver better outcomes—is legitimate. It deserves an answer grounded in policies and accountability.
You are right that Nigeria owes nobody the presidency. Neither longevity in politics
content:
Thank you for your open letter. Your central question—why Nigerians should expect an Atiku Abubakar presidency to deliver better outcomes—is legitimate. It deserves an answer grounded in policies and accountability.

You are right that Nigeria owes nobody the presidency. Neither longevity in politics nor persistence in seeking office creates an entitlement to lead. Atiku must earn the confidence of Nigerians.

Where I respectfully disagree is with the suggestion that familiarity with the same political establishment makes Atiku and President Bola Tinubu equivalent. Shared acquaintances do not establish identical convictions, competence or approaches to government. Treating them as interchangeable is like comparing apples and oranges while overlooking the differences that matter.

The useful comparison concerns what each proposes, how those proposals would work, and what they would mean for ordinary Nigerians.

That is where #AtikuSolutions—affordability, security and economic revival—should become the centre of this conversation.

Affordability: economic policy must make life liveable

For a mother deciding between food and medicine, the most meaningful economic indicator is what her income can buy. For a small business owner, it is whether electricity, transport and financing costs leave enough to remain in business.

Atiku’s proposed production subsidy addresses a major source of these pressures: energy costs.

His published proposal would provide preferentially priced domestic crude to qualifying Nigerian refineries, subject to verified production, domestic supply and conditions requiring the benefit to reach consumers. It envisages a budget ceiling, independent audits and sanctions for abuse. It also acknowledges that discounted crude carries a real cost to public revenue.

The intended connection is practical: lower the cost of producing fuel locally, ensure consumers receive the benefit, and ease the energy burden on households and businesses.

You ask how this would be financed. That question deserves precision. The crude discount represents revenue forgone; it must therefore be explicitly costed and accommodated within the budget. Published reporting also identifies details still requiring disclosure, including the discount rate, eligible volumes and annual ceiling. Those are proper subjects for scrutiny. We strengthen the proposal by answering them.

But a proposal with identifiable mechanisms and costs deserves examination on its merits. Dismissing it as an absence of ideas prevents precisely the policy debate you seek.

Security: protect lives and restore livelihoods

Your description of northern deprivation raises an essential point: a leader’s geographical origin does not guarantee development for people from that region.

A northern presidency is no substitute for effective government. Neither is a southern presidency. Nigerians everywhere need protection, functioning schools, accessible healthcare and opportunities to earn a living.

Atiku’s published security agenda includes decentralising security institutions, strengthening intelligence and border control, improving regional cooperation and addressing the conditions that sustain conflict. His longstanding economic programme also emphasises private investment, infrastructure and education.

The practical test of security policy is whether farmers can return to their land, children can attend school and traders can travel without fear.

Security and affordability are connected. When violence drives farmers away, food supply suffers. When transport routes become dangerous, distribution becomes more expensive. When businesses cannot protect their workers and investments, employment suffers.

Restoring security is therefore part of restoring the economy.

Economic revival: give enterprise room to grow

You ask where the new ideas are. An idea should be judged by whether it addresses the problem and can be implemented successfully.

Atiku’s economic approach places private enterprise at the centre of investment and job creation, with government providing security, infrastructure and credible rules. His published programme advocates wider private participation in infrastructure and stronger education and skills development. These are proposals against which his candidacy can be assessed.

For Nigerians, the questions are concrete: Can a manufacturer obtain dependable power? Can a farmer reach a market? Can a young entrepreneur access finance? Can an investor trust that the rules will remain predictable?

Economic revival requires answers across these areas. Affordable energy helps businesses survive. Security allows production to resume. Investment expands employment. Education equips people to participate.

That is the connection between priorities of #AtikuSolutions.

Accountability must accompany the programme

Your questions about wealth, allegations and public integrity should not be dismissed. Equally, allegations must be distinguished from findings established through due process. Neither political loyalty nor political hostility should determine the standard of evidence.

No candidate should receive immunity from scrutiny.

Your demand for clarity about implementation, financing and accountability is particularly valuable. Nigerians should insist on costed programmes, clear responsibilities, published milestones, transparent procurement and independent scrutiny. Supporting Atiku should strengthen those demands.

Nor should the lifestyle of an associate replace examination of the candidate’s programme. Concerns about political ostentation deserve to be heard, especially amid hardship. But the decisive questions concern who would exercise public responsibility, their competence and the standards governing their conduct.

Inclusion deserves a serious answer

Your concern about rotation also merits respect. Political balance matters in a diverse federation, and apprehensions about exclusion cannot simply be waved away.

Atiku must earn trust across regions through the substance of his commitments to inclusion, equitable appointments, development and devolution of power. Every Nigerian deserves a meaningful stake in the country, whoever occupies the presidency.

Your letter ends with a proposition I share: the presidency belongs to the Nigerian people.

They deserve a choice informed by evidence. They deserve to compare programmes, interrogate costs, examine records and demand measurable results.

Atiku’s experience gives Nigerians a record to scrutinise. His proposals give them an alternative to examine. Neither asks them to surrender their judgment.

The case for Atiku is that his approach to affordability, security and economic revival offers a credible direction that deserves serious consideration.

Let us debate that case with the rigour Nigeria’s circumstances demand.

The post Why Atiku? The Answer is in The Solutions: by Paul Ibe appeared first on Very Nigerian.
