title: US Watching Nigeria's January Election Closely, Says Nigeria Not Doing Enough To Stop Attacks - Check Below For Full Details
description: US State Department officials told a House hearing that Nigeria is taking religious violence more seriously after the CPC redesignation, but significant work remains ahead of the January 2027 election.
content:
United States State Department officials say the Tinubu administration is taking religious violence in Nigeria more seriously since the country was redesignated a Country of Particular Concern (CPC), but they maintain that significant work remains to end the attacks.

The officials made the disclosure at a congressional hearing of the Africa Subcommittee of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee held on Thursday, November 12, where they assessed Nigeria's efforts to protect vulnerable communities and address attacks on Christians and other religious groups.

They told the panel that despite some reported improvements since President Donald Trump returned Nigeria to the CPC list in November 2025, the Nigerian government still has much to do to end the violence, protect affected communities and ensure those responsible for the attacks are brought to justice.

The assessment came as US officials also confirmed that Washington is watching Nigeria's January 2027 presidential election closely, with American lawmakers and officials paying attention to how the polls are organised and executed.

Nigeria was redesignated a Country of Particular Concern over the handling of violence against religious communities, a move that pushed both governments into fresh engagement on security and human rights. In December 2025, the United States carried out strikes against terror targets in Nigeria's North-West following threats by the Trump administration to act if the killings continued.

Friday's reports quoted the officials as saying Nigeria is not doing enough to stop the attacks, even as Abuja insists it is taking steps to secure communities and hold perpetrators accountable.

The January 16 election is expected to draw unusual international scrutiny, with the opposition fielding several strong challengers, including Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde and other figures negotiating a possible alliance.

Foreign policy assessments quoted here reflect the views of US officials at the hearing and media reports of their remarks; the Nigerian government maintains it is addressing the security challenges.

title: INEC Boss Amupitan Denies Owning Pro-Tinubu X Account, Reports Matter To DSS, Police - Check Below For Full Details
description: INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan denied owning the @joashamupitan X account linked to pro-APC posts, saying the matter has been reported to the DSS and the Inspector-General of Police.
content:
Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Professor Joash Amupitan, has denied owning an X (Twitter) account that was linked to him and allegedly used to express support for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress.

Speaking at a dialogue in London, the INEC boss said the account, which bore the handle @joashamupitan, did not belong to him, insisting that he had never operated an account on the platform in his life.

"I never had an X account. I tried to get in touch with X, but there's no way if you don't have an account," he said. "I have my Yahoo mail. I check Yahoo mail. It was never my account. And that is the truth."

He disclosed that the allegation has been formally reported to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the office of the Inspector-General of Police, and that an independent report on the matter had been obtained.

"We have an independent report and the matter was also reported to the DSS as well as to the IG," he said.

Amupitan spoke on Thursday during a dialogue organised by Chatham House in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative, themed 'Nigeria's 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot'.

The controversy dates back to allegations that the X account bearing his handle had posted messages celebrating APC victories during the 2023 general election, raising questions about the political neutrality of the man who will oversee the 2027 polls.

INEC has consistently dismissed the allegation as fabricated, and in a statement of April 10, 2026, the chairman's media adviser, Adedayo Oketola, said fraudulent accounts had been created in the chairman's name to mislead the public and damage his reputation.

The INEC chairman also suggested the timing of the renewed allegation was significant, saying it emerged around a court ruling involving the African Democratic Congress, and argued that the only way to bring down an institution was to attack the person leading it.

He added that earlier accusations, including claims that he was a member of the President's legal team and that he lied about his educational background, were investigated by the security agencies and found to be unfounded.

Amupitan said some civil society organisations have also indicated interest in investigating the matter, and expressed confidence that the commission will deliver an election Nigerians will be proud of in 2027.

title: UNN Confirms Four Students Dead After Off-Campus Sign-Out Party, Declares Three-Day Mourning - Check Below For Full Details
description: The University of Nigeria, Nsukka confirmed four students and graduates died after a sign-out party at a lodge in Nsukka, with six others hospitalised; the school declared three days of mourning.
content:
The management of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) has confirmed the death of four of its students and graduates following an off-campus sign-out party at a lodge in the Hilltop area of Nsukka, Enugu State.

The Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simon Ortuanya, who addressed journalists on Thursday, November 12, said the university received a distress call at about 10pm on Wednesday, November 11, that some of its students and graduates were involved in an incident at a house party held at a lodge in the area.

According to the Vice-Chancellor, the university's security personnel moved to the scene immediately, and four persons lost their lives while six others were hospitalised, some of them in critical condition at the time of the briefing.

The institution said about ten of its students from different departments were involved in the incident.

Reports of suspected alcohol or substance use at the party have circulated widely, but the Vice-Chancellor cautioned that the actual cause of the deaths is not yet conclusive pending the outcome of investigations and medical reports.

The university has declared three days of mourning, during which all activities have been suspended, as the campus community comes to terms with the loss.

Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah has ordered a full investigation into the incident and called for a ban on sign-out parties in the state's tertiary institutions to prevent a recurrence.

The police, through the spokesperson of the Enugu State Command, SP Daniel Ndukwe, said officers responded to the scene and that an investigation into the circumstances of the deaths has commenced.

A statement attributed to the Pharmaceutical Association of Nigerian Students (PANS), UNN chapter, also clarified that the victims were not from the pharmacy department alone, confirming that the deceased comprised two males and two females.

Mindnewsng extends condolences to the families affected. As this is a developing story, findings from the investigation ordered by the authorities are awaited; claims about the cause of the incident remain unconfirmed pending official results.

title: Manchester United Agree Two-And-A-Half-Year Deal With Pochettino To Replace Michael Carrick - Check Below For Full Details
description: Manchester United have agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal with USA manager Mauricio Pochettino to replace the sacked Michael Carrick, with the Argentine taking charge after the international break.
content:
Manchester United have reached an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino for the Argentine to become the club's next head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract running until the summer of 2029.

Pochettino, the current manager of the United States men's national team, will replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday with the club 18th in the Premier League and without a win in their last ten matches.

Reports say United will pay a buyout of around £7 million to secure the release of the Argentine from his US Soccer contract.

The 54-year-old is expected to take charge of the squad after the current international break, with his first match in the dugout the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on November 22.

Before that, he remains in charge of the USA for their matches against Haiti, with the Americans in competitive action this weekend and again on Tuesday.

Carrick had been appointed in January 2026 on a deal until the end of the season after the sacking of Ruben Amorim, but a run of poor results, including just one win in ten matches, cost the former United midfielder his job.

Pochettino previously managed Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, and led the United States through the 2026 World Cup cycle.

An official announcement from Old Trafford is expected in the coming days.

title: Emefiele Trial: Witness Details Alleged Multi-Billion Naira Properties Acquired Through Proxies - Check Below For Full Details
description: An EFCC investigator told a Lagos court that former CBN Governor Godwin Emefiele allegedly acquired properties in Lagos, Delta, Ogun and Abuja through proxies - claims Emefiele denies.
content:
An investigator with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Alvan Gurumnaan, has told a Lagos State Special Offences Court in Ikeja that former Central Bank of Nigeria Governor, Godwin Emefiele, allegedly acquired multi-billion-naira properties through proxies while in office.

Gurumnaan, the seventh prosecution witness, gave the testimony during Emefiele's ongoing trial before Justice Rahman Oshodi. He said the properties allegedly linked to the former CBN governor were located in Lagos, Delta, Ogun and Abuja, with some already forfeited to the Federal Government through court orders.

The properties listed

The witness said the EFCC recovered more than $2 million in cash from the office of a lawyer, Ifeanyi Omeke, who allegedly admitted acting as a front for Emefiele and collecting money on his behalf.

Among the assets listed were twin duplexes in Lekki Phase 1, two mansions on Queen's Drive, Ikoyi, an 11-storey building under construction comprising about 94 luxury flats in Ikoyi, an industrial park under construction in Amuwo Odofin, a warehouse in Ogun State said to contain containers estimated at hundreds of billions of naira, and an estate of about 750 housing units in the Lokogoma District of Abuja.

The charges

Emefiele is standing trial alongside his co-defendant, Henry Omoile, over allegations of gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving transactions valued at $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. Emefiele faces a 19-count charge, while Omoile faces three counts of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts.

Defence objects, cites "trial by ambush"

The defence teams, led by Ojo Olalekan (SAN), challenged the admissibility of the testimony, arguing that the prosecution was introducing facts not contained in the proof of evidence served on the defendants - a move Emefiele's lawyers described as an attempt to subject them to a "trial by ambush". Justice Oshodi allowed the testimony while preserving the defence's right to cross-examine the witness.

The witness acknowledged that Emefiele denies the allegations, having done so in his extrajudicial statement to the EFCC. The case was adjourned for continuation of trial.

Editor's note: The claims in this report are allegations presented in court by a prosecution witness and remain subject to adjudication. The defendant has denied wrongdoing, and nothing in this report should be taken as a finding of guilt.

title: FG Grants Port Harcourt Airport 30-Year Concession To Boost Revenue, Efficiency - Check Below For Full Details
description: The Federal Government has signed a 30-year concession agreement for Port Harcourt Airport, approved by President Tinubu, with guarantees of no job losses for aviation workers.
content:
The Federal Government has granted a 30-year concession of Port Harcourt International Airport to Port Harcourt Airport Company Limited, in a deal designed to improve operational efficiency, boost revenue generation and maximise the airport's commercial potential.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this in Abuja during the signing of the agreement.

Why the concession matters

Keyamo explained that the Federal Government had long relied on profits from major airports to subsidise the operations of others recording losses.

"Some of our airports are being run at a loss. We make so much money from some of our primary airports, and most of those profits are ploughed into running other airports," Keyamo said.

The minister said the concession had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council, noting that the process was not a sudden decision but one that successive administrations had struggled to implement. Previous attempts were frustrated by resistance from labour unions and court cases involving the government.

Workers' welfare protected

Keyamo attributed the successful conclusion of the process to negotiations with aviation unions, saying the government secured their agreement before signing the deal.

He assured workers that the concession would not lead to job losses or a reduction in their conditions of service, adding that Tinubu had directed that the welfare of aviation workers must be protected throughout the process.

The move is expected to reduce the financial burden on the government while ensuring better management and improved performance of the nation's airports.
author: Mindnewsng

title: UNIJOS Names Patricia Lar As First Female Vice-Chancellor After Five Decades - Check Below For Full Details
description: The University of Jos has appointed Professor Patricia Lar, a medical microbiologist, as its first female Vice-Chancellor in the institution's five-decade history.
content:
The University of Jos, UNIJOS, has appointed Professor Patricia Lar as its first female Vice-Chancellor in the institution's five-decade history.

Lar, a professor of microbiology, medical microbiology and medical parasitology, was appointed by the university's Governing Council. In a statement issued on Thursday, the university's Deputy Registrar, Information and Public Relations, Emmanuel Madugu, confirmed the appointment, describing Lar as the first woman to lead the institution.

Madugu disclosed that the Governing Council ratified her appointment during a special meeting held on Thursday, where she was formally presented with her appointment letter. Lar will succeed Tanko Ishaya, the outgoing vice-chancellor, whose tenure had elapsed.

A distinguished career

Lar previously served as acting vice-chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University, Abuja, according to the News Agency of Nigeria.

Born in 1964 in Plateau State, she earned a bachelor's degree in microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University in 1986. In 1989, she obtained her second degree from the University of Lagos (UNILAG) College of Medicine, and earned a doctorate from the same institution in 1998.

She served as an associate professor from 2012 to 2015 and has been a full professor since 2015.

A milestone for Nigerian universities

Her appointment adds UNIJOS to the growing list of Nigerian universities led by women, a milestone many in the academic community describe as long overdue. Stakeholders within and outside the institution have congratulated Lar, expressing hope that her leadership will bring stability and renewed focus to the university.
author: Mindnewsng

title: Falling Crude Prices: FCCPC Presses Refiners, Marketers To Slash Petrol Prices - Check Below For Full Details
description: The FCCPC has put refiners and marketers on notice as Brent crude falls from a $115 peak to below $90, insisting savings must reach Nigerian consumers at the pump.
content:
The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, FCCPC, has intensified pressure on refiners and petroleum marketers to reduce petrol and diesel prices, following a 21.7 per cent decline in international crude oil prices.

Brent crude futures, which peaked at $115 per barrel in September, have fallen to below $90 this week. Yet Nigerian consumers still pay between N1,405 and N1,420 per litre in Abuja and N1,325 and N1,370 per litre in Lagos.

"No justification" for high prices

FCCPC Executive Vice Chairman and CEO, Tunji Bello, said the commission was closely monitoring domestic fuel prices to ensure the sustained fall in crude costs translates into tangible relief at the pumps.

"If the decline in crude prices is sustained, there is no justification for refiners and marketers to continue to keep petrol and diesel prices relatively high. We expect easing in wholesale petrol costs and for the resulting savings to reach consumers at the pump without undue delay," Bello said.

Marketers had attributed the surge in fuel prices over the past eight months to volatility following the US-Iran conflict in the Middle East and the resulting blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a transit route for at least a quarter of global oil traffic. Before the conflict began in late February, Brent closed at $72.48 and petrol sold for between N839 and N925 per litre.

Marketers push back

The Petroleum Products Retail Outlets Owners Association of Nigeria, PETROAN, through its National President Billy Gillis-Harry, said crude is only one of several factors: marketers must first sell off stock bought at higher cost, and dollar-denominated imports mean a weak naira keeps landing costs high even when crude falls.

The Petroleum Dealers Association of Nigeria, through its National Secretary Ibrahim Shehu Yahaya, added that crude reductions take days or weeks to flow through cargo pricing, refining and depot delivery, and that pump prices also include refining margins, transport, handling and taxes.

The FCCPC said it would collaborate with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority and other agencies to monitor prices, warning that it would take action within its mandate where there is evidence of anti-competitive conduct preventing consumers from benefiting from lower costs.

title: INEC Sets November 28 For Nationwide Mock Election Ahead Of 2027 Polls - Check Below For Full Details
description: INEC will conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28 to test its readiness and result-transmission capacity ahead of the 2027 general elections.
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has announced plans to conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28 as part of efforts to assess its preparedness for the 2027 general elections.

INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this on Thursday during a conference at Chatham House in London, where discussions centred on the theme, "Democratic trajectory beyond the ballot".

What the mock election will test

Amupitan explained that the exercise would simulate a presidential election across all the states, enabling the commission to test its electoral preparations, particularly its capacity to transmit election results.

"On the 28th of this month, we are planning a mock accreditation and voting across all the states in Nigeria, so that we simulate a presidential election and just be sure that we have gotten it right and that there will be transmission of result," Amupitan said.

Lessons from previous elections

He said the commission had reviewed lessons from previous elections and taken steps to address identified problems, citing recent off-cycle elections, including those in Anambra and Osun, as examples of improvements in the electoral process.

"Nigerians must trust me because I've done off-cycle elections. The last election in Osun State showed improvement. Every election is a lesson. The 2023 election was a great lesson for Nigeria. The one we had in Anambra was another. So we've learned certain things, and as a commission, we sat down to address some of those," he said.

Amupitan added that INEC was working to improve logistics so that voting and result declaration could be completed promptly, pointing to the Anambra election where results were declared the day after voting.

The mock exercise is expected to help INEC identify possible challenges and assess the effectiveness of its electoral processes ahead of the 2027 polls.

title: Meet KC Ohaebosim, First Nigerian-American To Become Lieutenant Governor In US - Check Below For Full Details
description: Wichita Democrat KC Ohaebosim has been elected Lieutenant Governor of Kansas, becoming the first Nigerian-American to hold the office anywhere in the United States.
content:
Wichita Democrat KC Ohaebosim has been elected Lieutenant Governor of Kansas, becoming the first Nigerian-American to hold the office anywhere in the United States.

The Chairman of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission, Abike Dabiri-Erewa, announced the milestone in a post on X on Friday, congratulating Ohaebosim on his victory in the November 3 midterm elections.

From Wichita to the statehouse

Ohaebosim previously served in the Kansas House of Representatives, representing a Wichita district, where he built a record on education, healthcare access and economic opportunity before launching his statewide campaign.

Born to Nigerian parents, his rise reflects the growing political influence of the Nigerian diaspora in the United States, where Nigerian-Americans have increasingly won seats in legislatures, city halls and, now, statewide executive offices.

Diaspora celebration

NiDCOM described the victory as a proud moment for Nigeria, noting that citizens of Nigerian descent continue to break new ground in mainstream American politics. Nigerians in the diaspora are among the most educated and civically engaged immigrant communities in the US.

Congratulatory messages have poured in from Nigerian officials and community groups on both sides of the Atlantic, with many describing the achievement as an inspiration to young Nigerians at home and abroad.

title: Gospel Singer Moses Bliss Donates N50m To Lawyer's Christmas Charity - Check Below For Full Details
description: Nigerian gospel singer Moses Bliss has donated N50 million to his lawyer, Pelumi Olajengbesi, to support his planned festive charity outreach to less-privileged Nigerians.
content:
Nigerian gospel singer Moses Bliss has donated N50 million to his lawyer, Pelumi Olajengbesi, to support his planned festive charity outreach to people in need.

Olajengbesi disclosed the donation in an Instagram post on Friday, thanking the gospel artiste for his generosity and support. According to the lawyer, he shared his plans with Bliss to assist less-privileged Nigerians during the festive season, and the singer responded with the multi-million-naira gift.

Christmas charity drive

The outreach, which the lawyer's firm has run in previous years, typically provides food items, clothing and financial support to vulnerable families during the Christmas period. The N50 million donation is expected to significantly expand the scale of this year's programme.

Fans of the singer, whose hit songs have made him one of Nigeria's most-streamed gospel artistes, praised the gesture, with many describing it as putting his faith into action during the season of giving.

Bliss has built a reputation for philanthropy alongside his music, supporting church projects and individual causes. Neither the singer nor the lawyer has disclosed how the funds will be distributed, but the lawyer said details of the outreach would be announced in due course.

title: ICPC Recovers N5.3bn From LG Accounts In Seven States, FCT - Check Below For Full Details
description: The ICPC has recovered over N5.3bn from local government accounts in seven states and the FCT, and is working with NITDA to put all 774 LGAs' finances online for public scrutiny.
content:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, ICPC, has recovered over N5.3 billion from local government accounts in seven states and the Federal Capital Territory following a review of their finances.

The commission said it was also working with the National Information Technology Development Agency, NITDA, to ensure that all 774 local government areas publish their financial records and operations online, in a bid to entrench transparency at the third tier of government.

Tracking the money

The recoveries followed the commission's system studies and review exercises, which examine how funds allocated to local councils are utilised. The ICPC said several councils were found to have kept funds outside approved channels, and the recovered amounts have been returned to the affected accounts for proper application.

Digital transparency push

The collaboration with NITDA is expected to give citizens direct visibility into council finances, reducing the information gap that has long shielded local government spending from public scrutiny. Anti-corruption advocates have long argued that most diversion of public funds happens at levels closest to communities, where oversight is weakest.

The commission urged council officials to embrace the open-books policy voluntarily, warning that continued opacity would attract investigation and possible prosecution.

title: TRCN Uncovers 250 Fake Certificates In Teachers' Recruitment - Check Below For Full Details
description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria has uncovered 250 fake teaching certificates in a recruitment exercise, prompting QR-coded certificates and stricter digital verification.
content:
The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria, TRCN, says it has uncovered 250 fake teaching certificates during a recruitment exercise, prompting the rollout of QR-coded certificates and stricter digital verification.

The Chief Executive and Registrar of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, said the move was aimed at flushing out quacks from Nigerian classrooms. She disclosed this while monitoring a recruitment exercise, noting that the discovery showed how far unqualified persons were willing to go to enter the teaching profession.

QR codes to the rescue

Under the new system, every genuine TRCN certificate will carry a QR code that schools, employers and state ministries can scan to instantly confirm the holder's registration status. The council says the digital database will make forged certificates immediately detectable.

Education sector analysts welcomed the reform but stressed that detection must be paired with enforcement - prosecution of offenders and audit of how the fake certificates passed through earlier screening stages.

Why it matters

Nigeria faces a well-documented learning crisis, with millions of children out of school and many in classrooms taught by unqualified instructors. Stakeholders say cleaning up teacher registration is a foundational step toward improving learning outcomes, and the TRCN has pledged continuous verification exercises across the states.

title: N639bn Unpaid Gas Debt Threatens Nigeria's Electricity Supply - Check Below For Full Details
description: Industry stakeholders warn Nigeria's electricity crisis may persist unless the Federal Government clears mounting gas supply debts, fixes weak transmission and attracts fresh investment.
content:
Nigeria's recent electricity crisis may persist unless the Federal Government addresses mounting debts in the power sector, inadequate investment in gas production and weak infrastructure, industry stakeholders have warned.

Stakeholders said the failure to establish a sustainable payment mechanism for gas suppliers was undermining electricity generation, with unpaid obligations to gas suppliers put at about N639 billion. Inadequate transmission infrastructure and poorly maintained distribution networks compound the problem, leaving generated power unable to reach consumers reliably.

The debt trap

Gas suppliers, who feed the thermal plants that produce the bulk of Nigeria's grid electricity, have repeatedly threatened to cut supply over unpaid invoices. When gas deliveries falter, generation drops and the national grid becomes vulnerable to instability - the familiar pattern behind the country's recurring national blackouts.

The liquidity crisis runs through the entire value chain: distribution companies collect insufficient revenue, pass less money to generation companies, and the generators in turn cannot pay gas suppliers. Government interventions have only partially bridged the gap.

What stakeholders want

Industry operators are pressing for a clear, enforceable payment framework for gas suppliers, accelerated investment in transmission infrastructure, and tariff and market reforms that restore the financial viability of the sector.

Until those structural issues are resolved, analysts warn, Nigerians should expect continued load-shedding and grid instability regardless of short-term fixes.

title: Kidnappers Demand N500m Ransom For FUNAAB Graduate, Three Others - Check Below For Full Details
description: Gunmen who abducted a FUNAAB graduate and three others from a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta have reportedly demanded N500 million for their release.
content:
The abductors of a graduate of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Adedoja Hannah, and three other victims have reportedly demanded a ransom of N500 million for their release.

The victims were reportedly seized on Tuesday night when gunmen invaded a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta, Ogun State, where they were working. The development was disclosed by a family source, who said the kidnappers established contact with the relatives and made the demand.

A growing pattern in Ogun

The incident adds to a string of abductions reported around Ogun State's farm settlements and peri-urban communities in recent months, raising fears among farmers and residents who depend on daily work in those areas.

Security agencies have repeatedly urged families not to pay ransoms, warning that payments fuel the kidnapping economy. Efforts to reach the Ogun State Police Command for an update on rescue operations were ongoing at the time of this report.

What we know so far

Friends and well-wishers of the victims have begun mobilising support and calling for intensified security operations around the Alabata corridor, which hosts several farms linked to the university community.

This is a developing story. Mindnewsng will publish verified updates on the victims' condition and police response as they become available. We appeal to the public to rely on official confirmation rather than unverified social media claims.

title: Protesters Block INEC Chairman Amupitan's Vehicle In London, Demand Resignation - Check Below For Full Details
description: INEC Chairman Prof. Joash Amupitan was heckled by Nigerian protesters outside Chatham House in London over allegations of irregularities in the preliminary voters register ahead of 2027.
content:
The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, was on Thursday heckled by Nigerian protesters in London who surrounded the vehicle conveying him outside Chatham House, where he was scheduled to speak.

The protesters hurled insults and demanded his resignation over allegations of irregularities in the preliminary voters' register ahead of the 2027 general elections. Video clips of the incident circulated widely on Nigerian social media, reigniting debate over the credibility of the commission's preparations.

The allegations, and INEC's response

The protest was organised by a coalition of Nigerian groups in the diaspora who claim the preliminary register contains anomalies, including duplicate and suspicious registrations. The commission has not publicly confirmed the specific figures cited by the protesters, and no independent verification has established the claims as presented.

Amupitan, who was appointed INEC chairman in 2025, has repeatedly pledged to deliver credible polls. In recent days he has also faced separate online claims about his personal social media activity, which he has denied, and he told reporters the commission would abide by court rulings on candidate disputes.

Why it matters

Nigeria's 2027 elections are already shaping up as fiercely contested, and public confidence in the voter register is central to the legitimacy of any outcome. The commission has announced digital verification initiatives and says it is cleaning the register ahead of the polls.

Observers note that protest pressure abroad has become a recurring feature of Nigerian electoral politics, with diaspora groups using international platforms to amplify domestic grievances.

Editor's note: The allegations mentioned in this report remain subject to official investigation. Mindnewsng reports them as claims made by those involved and does not present them as established fact.

title: Microsoft Battling To Restore Outlook After Global Outage - Check Below For Full Details
description: Microsoft says repairs to a major global Outlook outage are not going as expected, with email, Teams and Copilot hit worldwide as engineers seek alternative solutions.
content:
Microsoft admitted on Thursday that its efforts to repair a major global outage of Outlook were not going as expected, forcing the company to pursue alternative solutions as millions of users around the world - including in Nigeria - lost access to critical workplace services.

The hours-long disruption, which the technology giant attributed to elevated load on its infrastructure, affected not just email but also Microsoft Teams, the collaboration platform used by businesses, schools and government offices, as well as the company's AI assistant Copilot.

What went wrong

Microsoft said the outage was triggered by unusual traffic volumes that overloaded parts of the systems that keep Outlook online. Engineers worked through the night, but the company publicly conceded that standard recovery measures were not restoring full service as quickly as hoped.

The disruption rippled across time zones, with users reporting error messages, frozen inboxes and failed logins on both desktop and mobile apps. For many organisations, email remains the backbone of daily operations, and the outage forced some companies to fall back on phone calls and messaging alternatives.

Why it matters

The incident highlights how dependent modern work has become on a handful of cloud platforms. When one provider goes down, the impact is felt from corporate boardrooms to university lecture halls - and the timing, during peak working hours in Europe and Africa, made it worse.

Microsoft said it would continue updating users through its official status channels as engineers stabilised the affected systems. Users were advised to monitor official communication rather than reinstall apps, which does not fix a server-side problem.

This story is developing and will be updated as Microsoft confirms full restoration of service.

title: The 5-Hour Rule: How the World's Richest People Learn, and the 5 Books Elon Musk Recommends - Check Below For Full Details
description: The 5-Hour Rule is the quiet habit behind Elon Musk, Warren Buffett, Oprah Winfrey and Bill Gates: one hour a day, five days a week, devoted to learning. Here are the 5 books Musk has publicly recommended.
content:
When Elon Musk crossed the trillion-dollar net worth mark, the world scrambled for explanations - the companies, the risk-taking, the sheer volume of hours worked. But buried beneath all of it is a habit so quiet it barely makes headlines, one he shares with Warren Buffett, Oprah Winfrey and Bill Gates. It is called the 5-Hour Rule: one hour a day, five days a week, devoted entirely to learning. No meetings, no output - just reading, thinking and absorbing ideas.

The idea is simple and old. Benjamin Franklin reportedly set aside an hour a day for deliberate learning, and the habit has since been adopted by some of the most successful people in business, sports and politics. The rule is not about working harder; it is about learning faster.

How the 5-Hour Rule works

  • Read - consume books, articles and research in your field and beyond it
  • Reflect - think about what you read and how it applies to your life and work
  • Experiment - test the ideas in small, low-risk ways

The point is consistency, not intensity. One hour a day compounds into roughly 365 hours a year - the equivalent of nine full working weeks of pure learning.

The 5 books Elon Musk has publicly recommended

Musk has named several books over the years as formative. These five come up most often in his interviews and public statements:

  1. Superintelligence by Nick Bostrom - what happens when machines outthink us. Musk called it worth reading back in 2014, years before AI became dinner-table talk.
  2. Life 3.0 by Max Tegmark - how artificial intelligence could reshape work, society and what it means to be human.
  3. Merchants of Doubt by Naomi Oreskes and Erik M. Conway - how a handful of scientists muddied the truth on smoking, climate change and other major issues.
  4. The Big Picture by Sean Carroll - a physicist on the origins of life, meaning and the universe, and how they fit together.
  5. Lying by Sam Harris - a short case for dropping even the small, "harmless" lies.

Why the habit matters more than the list

The books are a starting point, not a secret formula. What separates the people who actually grow is the daily discipline of showing up to learn, even when there is no immediate payoff. The 5-Hour Rule works because it treats learning as non-negotiable - the same way most people treat lunch or sleep.

You do not need billions, rockets or a trillion-dollar net worth to start. You need one hour, five days a week, and a willingness to read, reflect and experiment. Start with one book from the list above, finish it, and then pick the next. The compounding does the rest.

title: AFCON 2027 Qualifiers - Nigeria Face Disaster, Benni v Pitso, Salah Fresh Start - Check Below For Full Details
description: AFCON 2027 qualifying resumes with decisive double-headers. Nigeria risk disaster after a 3-0 home loss to Guinea-Bissau; Egypt, Ghana, Senegal, Kenya and South Africa all face big tests.
content:
AFCON 2027 qualifying resumes this week with potentially decisive double-headers for several continental giants - including Nigeria and South Africa. For some, November offers a chance to move within touching distance of qualification; for others, another poor international break could be disastrous.

Can Nigeria avoid another catastrophe?

Nigeria's campaign is already in jeopardy after a wretched opening pair of fixtures left them three points off Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau. A humiliating 3-0 home defeat by the West Africans has given Eric Chelle's side little margin for error - especially with Tanzania automatically qualifying as co-hosts, leaving just one automatic qualifying berth in the group.

The Super Eagles now face the Taifa Stars twice - in Uyo and Dar es Salaam - knowing that further dropped points could leave them with too big a gulf to close. They must also navigate both fixtures without Victor Osimhen (again), while midfield duo Frank Onyeka and Raphael Onyedika are both absent. The hope is that Tolu Arokodare, in magnificent goalscoring form for Ajax Amsterdam, can finally make up for lost time and fire Nigeria back into contention.

Can Egypt restore harmony with Salah?

Hossam Hassan was unceremoniously dismissed on November 7, exactly four months after Egypt's unforgettable World Cup quarter-final defeat by Argentina. His increasingly contentious relationship with Mohamed Salah attracted heavy scrutiny, particularly after the forward was substituted against Angola and departed camp before the trip to South Sudan. New boss Ali Maher must establish a relationship with Salah, get the most out of a talented squad and restore stability - starting with a double-header against Malawi, where domestic hotshot Mahmoud Mamdouh earns a maiden call-up and Trezeguet returns.

Can returning Kudus ignite Ghana's campaign?

Like Nigeria, Ghana are in a tough spot after defeats by Cote d'Ivoire and The Gambia left them pointless after two games. Carlos Queiroz has departed, with women's coach Kim Bjorkegren holding the reins in an interim capacity for the double-header against Somalia. The comeback of Mohammed Kudus, who missed the World Cup through injury but has shown glimpses of form at Tottenham, should lift a squad that cannot afford another AFCON absence.

Is Vieira really the author of Senegal's revival?

Patrick Vieira's appointment replaced Pape Thiaw, but his latest squad suggests the transition could be more substantial than first thought. Edouard Mendy and Ismail Jakobs have retired internationally, while Sadio Mane and Idrissa Gana Gueye are absent for the fixtures against Sudan - Mane staying home as he awaits the birth of a child. Their absences open the door to an uncapped quartet, with Saudi-based Dion Lopy the chief beneficiary of Gana's absence.

Benni vs Pitso

Two of South Africa's most celebrated football personalities collide when Benni McCarthy's Kenya face Pitso Mosimane's South Africa in a compelling Group D double-header. Kenya are guaranteed to be at AFCON 2027 as hosts but must show readiness after a troubled international break in which McCarthy revealed players allegedly refused to train over unpaid allowances. Mosimane's side, evolving after the World Cup, began qualifying with two wins.

Other storylines to watch

  • Mali vs Rwanda: both sides took maximum points from their openers; Lassine Sinayoko has nine goals in 10 Ligue 1 games for Paris FC.
  • Cape Verde: consecutive defeats after World Cup heroics; coach Bubista left for RS Berkane; now face Liberia in must-win fixtures.
  • Amad Diallo: among 10 nominees for African Footballer of the Year; Ivory Coast's new boss Herve Renard could unlock the Manchester United winger against The Gambia.

CAF has also reversed its four-year AFCON plan and restored the two-year cycle - a reminder of how quickly the continental landscape keeps shifting.

title: Fury v Joshua Fight Faces Objections Over 3am Finish - Check Below For Full Details
description: Residents have raised objections to Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua finishing at 03:00 GMT in Cardiff on 11 December, citing noise, safety and traffic. Cardiff Councils licensing subcommittee meets on 25 November.
content:
The eagerly awaited Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua heavyweight clash is set for Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December - but residents have raised serious concerns over plans for the event to run into the early hours of the morning.

The all-British fight is expected to finish at 03:00 GMT the following day to align with prime-time viewing in the United States, prompting objections to the stadium's application to extend licensing hours.

What residents are objecting to

Cardiff Council has received several representations ahead of a licensing subcommittee meeting on 25 November, citing:

  • Anti-social behaviour and public safety
  • Noise and late-night disturbance continuing after the event ends
  • Traffic congestion and road closures
  • Impact on families with young children living near the stadium

One resident who lives directly opposite the stadium wrote that while they support the event, they want extra conditions including a dispersal plan with stewards in place until crowds clear, no amplified music outside the stadium after midnight, and street cleaning completed by 08:00 on 12 December.

Three others called for the application to be rejected outright, arguing that music, amplified sound, large crowds, shouting, vehicles and taxis could keep disturbance going well into the early morning. A parent with young children said a 03:30 finish would "cause absolute chaos" and leave the household with "exhausted, stressed children."

The stadium's request

The Principality Stadium normally operates a curfew until 01:00 when the roof is closed. It has now requested permission for licensed activities - including the sale of alcohol and the playing of music - to continue until 03:00 on 12 December, with the venue remaining open until 03:30.

Supporters and the business case

Not everyone is opposed. Some residents wrote in support, arguing the fight would bring a significant economic boost and attract tourists, particularly from the United States, to Cardiff. Pub owner Mike Catris described having the fight in the city as "overwhelmingly positive," calling any disruption "a small price to pay" for the money it generates for a struggling economy.

Why Cardiff and not Wembley or New York

Several venues were considered, including New York's Madison Square Garden. Focus shifted to the UK after Anthony Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn refused to budge on their contractual right to stage the fight on British soil. Wembley Stadium was touted, but its strict 23:00 event curfew proved a problem given Netflix's preference to broadcast during US prime time. Cardiff was chosen partly because the venue already has precedent for late-night boxing - Joe Calzaghe's 2007 super-middleweight unification win over Mikkel Kessler did not start until 02:00 local time to satisfy US network Showtime.

The application has been made under the Licensing Act 2003, with a 28-day consultation period. If objections are received, the council's licensing sub-committee must hear them and may modify the licence conditions or reject the application. The Principality Stadium has been asked to comment.

title: NAFDAC Uncovers Suspected Fake Parago Candies Hidden in Rice Warehouse - Check Below For Full Details
description: NAFDAC has uncovered a warehouse where suspected counterfeit Parago candies were allegedly concealed in cartons labelled as other products, including under a tarpaulin and inside a rice warehouse. The agency is yet to confirm quantities, location or arrests.
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has uncovered a warehouse where suspected counterfeit Parago candies were allegedly concealed in cartons bearing different product names.

The discovery was captured in a video on Thursday, showing NAFDAC officials inspecting the facility and uncovering the products hidden under a tarpaulin and inside cartons labelled as other goods.

How the candies were hidden

  • An official is heard explaining that the products were being concealed in cartons labelled "Toy with Candy", although the contents were identified as Parago.
  • The entire tarpaulin was reportedly filled with the suspected counterfeit candies.
  • The original carton of Parago was allegedly concealed in a store used for keeping rice - a facility meant to be a rice warehouse.

The official said the discovery revealed yet another method allegedly used to conceal the products from detection.

What NAFDAC has not confirmed yet

The agency is yet to provide further details on the quantity of products recovered, the location of the warehouse, the operators of the facility, or whether any arrests have been made.

The case adds to a string of recent NAFDAC enforcement actions against counterfeit goods, including the seizure of suspected fake Nivea and Listerine products in a Delta market and a raid on five shops in Aba where fake brand packaging worth about ₦200 million was seized.

NAFDAC urged consumers to buy only from trusted sources and to report suspicious products. Mindnewsng will update this report as more details emerge.

title: Canada Explains How Foreigners Can Apply for Citizenship Online, Sets Deadline - Check Below For Full Details
description: Canada has opened an online pathway for foreigners seeking citizenship. Eligible applicants fall into 3 groups based on age and family circumstances; others must apply on paper. Applicants get 60 days from account creation to submit or the account is permanently deleted.
content:
Canada has opened an online pathway for foreigners seeking citizenship, releasing details of who qualifies to use the digital application system and how the process works from start to finish.

The Canadian government has also provided an official website where eligible applicants can begin their applications. Importantly, not all foreigners can use this route - those who do not meet the conditions must apply on paper.

Who can apply for Canadian citizenship online

Eligibility depends on age and family circumstances. The government recognises three groups of applicants who may use the online system:

  1. Adults aged 18 and above who already hold permanent resident status and satisfy the requirements under subsection 5(1) of the Citizenship Act.
  2. Children below 18 who are permanent residents and have at least one parent who is either already a Canadian citizen or applying for citizenship at the same time (subsection 5(2) of the Citizenship Act).
  3. Minors under 18 who are permanent residents, in cases where neither parent is a Canadian citizen nor applying for citizenship simultaneously. These children must meet the requirements for minors under subsection 5(1) of the Citizenship Act.

Anyone who does not fall into one of these three groups must apply through the traditional paper-based route.

How to submit the application online

Once an applicant confirms they qualify, the next step is to create an account on the Canadian government's official citizenship application portal. The account is used to complete and submit the entire application digitally.

Critical rule: applicants have only 60 days from the date the account is created to finish and submit their application. If that deadline is missed, the government will permanently delete the account along with every application connected to it.

Anyone in that situation who still wants to pursue citizenship must start over by creating a fresh account. The government does permit the use of the same email address from the deleted account, so restarting does not require an entirely new identity on the platform.

Canada also updated citizenship oath waiver rules

Separately, Canada updated its guidelines on foreigners who can obtain a waiver from taking the citizenship oath. The government outlined the compassionate grounds under which adults and minors aged 14 to 17 can request an exemption, while children below 14 are automatically exempt from taking the oath.

For Nigerians and other Africans eyeing Canadian citizenship, the message is clear: check whether you qualify for the online route, and if you do, do not let the 60-day clock run out.

title: Mauritius Announces 15 Fully Funded Scholarships For Kenyan Students, Applications Close November 18 - Check Below For Full Details
description: Mauritius has announced 15 fully funded scholarships for Kenyan students under the Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme 2027 - covering undergraduate, MPhil and PhD studies. Applications close 5pm November 18 at Kenya Ministry of Education, Telposta Towers. Applicants must first secure admission to a Mauritian public institution by end of January 2027.
content:
Kenyans looking for a fully funded degree abroad have a fresh window of opportunity: the island nation of Mauritius has announced 15 fully funded scholarships for Kenyan students under its Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme for the 2027 academic year.

The offer, relayed through Kenya's Ministry of Education, covers undergraduate, Master's and PhD studies at Mauritian public higher education institutions - and the deadline is very close.

Key details

  • 15 fully funded slots for Kenyan students
  • Level: undergraduate, MPhil and PhD programmes
  • Applications must reach Kenya's Ministry of Education (Telposta Towers, Nairobi) by 5pm on Tuesday, November 18, 2026
  • Coverage: tuition and related support as provided under the scheme

How to qualify

Applicants must first secure admission to a Mauritian public higher education institution by the end of January 2027 - the scholarship is attached to confirmed admission, so the university application comes first.

Candidates are advised to apply directly to the institutions and the Ministry. No fees or intermediaries are involved in the official process - any agent demanding payment should be reported.

China is also offering 15

In the same week, Kenya's Ministry of Education also announced 15 fully funded Chinese government scholarships for the 2027/2028 academic year - bringing the total on the table to 30 fully funded slots for Kenyan students in one week.

For families weighing the cost of university, schemes like these can change everything - the advice from officials is simple: apply early, apply directly, and never pay a middleman.

title: Tinubu Rewards Flamingos With N100 Million Each After Historic FIFA U-17 World Cup Triumph - Check Below For Full Details
description: President Bola Tinubu has approved N100 million for each player of Nigeria's Flamingos after they became the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, beating Japan 2-1 in Morocco. Head coach Akeem Busari gets N100 million cash and the technical crew N50 million each.
content:
President Bola Tinubu has rewarded each member of Nigeria's victorious Flamingos with N100 million, held in five-year Federal Government savings bonds, after the teenage stars made history by winning the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco.

The reward was announced by First Lady Oluremi Tinubu, speaking on behalf of the President at a State House reception in Abuja. She explained that the money would be preserved in trust for the young players rather than handed to them immediately.

"Do you know what a savings certificate is? It is money, but it is in trust for you. You are still very young. Do you want to start handling N100 million now?" she told the squad.

The full reward package

  • N100 million each for every player, in five-year savings bonds
  • N100 million cash for head coach Akeem Busari
  • N50 million each for members of the technical crew

The announcement came a day after the Senate donated N100 million to the team, with Senate President Godswill Akpabio personally distributing the cash reward at a separate reception.

History makers

The Flamingos defeated Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat last Saturday, winning six consecutive matches to claim the title. Their victory made Nigeria the first African nation ever to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup - and the first African women's team to win a FIFA World Cup title at any level.

The First Lady also specially celebrated Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, whose decisive goals sealed the triumph, and urged state governments and private well-wishers to add their own recognition.

"You have elevated Nigerian football, inspired millions of young girls and opened a new chapter for women's football in Africa," she said.

According to officials, the bonds will mature when the players reach adulthood, paying each roughly N1.1 million monthly in the interim while keeping the principal safe.

title: Senate Summons MTN, Glo, Airtel Over Charges For Failed Calls, Orders Refunds - Check Below For Full Details
description: The Nigerian Senate has summoned the NCC and major telecom operators including MTN, Globacom, Airtel and 9mobile over airtime deductions for failed and dropped calls. Subscribers could get automatic refunds as the Senate Committee on Communications has four weeks to report back.
content:
The Nigerian Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) and the country's biggest telecom operators - MTN, Globacom, Airtel and 9mobile - to explain why subscribers are charged for calls that fail, drop or never connect.

The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Senate Chief Whip Tahir Monguno and presented by Deputy Majority Leader Lola Ashiru, who told the chamber that millions of Nigerians lose airtime to calls that never go through - and pay again each time they redial.

What the Senate ordered

  • An investigation into billing practices for failed, dropped and interrupted calls
  • Automatic refunds of airtime deducted on verifiably failed calls
  • Independent technical audits of operators' billing systems
  • Stricter enforcement of quality-of-service standards, with sanctions for offenders
  • An accessible complaints channel for subscribers seeking refunds

The Senate Committee on Communications, chaired by Senator Ikra Bilbis, must summon the regulator and operators and report back within four weeks. Senate President Godswill Akpabio warned that if the report is unsatisfactory, the Senate will take over the investigation as a Committee of the Whole.

Lawmakers stressed that the burden falls hardest on low-income earners, traders, students and small business owners who depend on mobile networks daily.

For subscribers, the message from the Senate is simple: no one should pay for a service that was never delivered.

title: Tragedy As UNN Graduates Reportedly Die During Sign-Out Celebration In Nsukka - Check Below For Full Details
description: Fresh graduates of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, reportedly died hours after celebrating the end of their final exams at an off-campus apartment in the Hilltop area. Reports differ on the number of victims and the cause remains unconfirmed as police investigate.
content:
A celebration meant to mark the end of years of hard work has turned into mourning at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), after fresh graduates reportedly died hours after their sign-out party.

The victims, said to be recent graduates who finished their final exams on Wednesday, were reportedly found dead on Thursday morning in an apartment around the Hilltop area, an off-campus residential zone popular with students.

What is known so far - and what is not

  • Reports from different newsrooms put the number of victims at six or seven; the figures have not been officially reconciled
  • The victims were reportedly identified as Pharmacy graduates, with five females and one male among those reported by one outlet
  • The cause of death is not yet known - no official confirmation has been issued
  • The Enugu State Police Command is yet to release an official statement; efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer were unsuccessful at the time of this report

The development has thrown the university community and the Nsukka area into shock, with students and residents seeking answers about what could have happened to classmates celebrated just a day earlier.

Videos and photographs circulating on social media have not been verified by this newspaper and should be treated with caution.

Mindnewsng will update this report as soon as the police or the university issue an official statement. We extend our condolences to the families affected.

Editor's note: This is a developing story. All figures are as reported by newsrooms on the ground and remain unconfirmed pending official police and coroner findings.

title: Strait of Hormuz Effectively Closed As Tankers Come Under Attack, Oil Price Hits $92 - Check Below For Full Details
description: Only about 3 ships a day are passing through the Strait of Hormuz against a normal 85, after Iran declared the waterway closed and tankers came under attack. Brent crude trades around $92 - a development with direct consequences for fuel prices in Nigeria.
content:
The Strait of Hormuz - the narrow waterway that carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil - remains effectively closed, with ship-tracking data showing just about 3 commercial crossings a day against a pre-crisis average of 85.

What is happening

  • Iran declared the strait closed to "hostile" shipping and now demands transit permits and tolls through a body it created, the Persian Gulf Strait Authority
  • Iran's Revolutionary Guard says several tankers caught fire after striking naval mines while using what it calls "unauthorised routes" - claims carried widely but not independently verified
  • Ships have been switching off tracking systems, making the true picture harder to verify
  • Iran says the strait will not reopen until the US meets seven conditions; Washington says it is ready to use force if necessary

Oil prices

Brent crude, the global benchmark, has been trading around $92 a barrel, swinging with every headline about attacks or peace hopes.

Why Nigerians should pay attention

Nigeria imports refined fuel and feeds its domestic market partly through supplies that price off this waterway. A sustained closure pushes up global crude and product costs, which flows into landing costs, pump prices and inflation - on top of the pressure already felt in 2026. It also matters for the Dangote refinery's economics and for naira stability as oil earnings shift.

Maritime insurers have raised war-risk premiums to severe levels, and any lasting resolution still depends on diplomacy that both sides describe as far from reach.

Editor's note: Claims from the warring parties remain unverified by independent maritime authorities. Mindnewsng will continue tracking the strait and what it means for fuel prices in Nigeria.

title: Kenya Discharges Last Ebola Patient, Begins Countdown To Ebola-Free Declaration - Check Below For Full Details
description: Kenya has discharged its final Ebola patient and begun closing isolation facilities, starting a 42-day countdown before the country can be declared Ebola-free. Health Minister Aden Duale said prevention measures remain in force until December 23.
content:
Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient and begun winding down quarantine and isolation facilities - a milestone that starts the formal countdown before the country can be declared free of the disease.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale announced the discharge in Nairobi, saying the remaining monitored contacts have also been released. The declaration of an Ebola-free status requires a standard 42-day window with no new cases - putting the expected date around December 23.

What it took

  • Rapid isolation and treatment capacity once the outbreak was detected
  • Contact tracing and monitoring of everyone exposed
  • Cross-border screening with neighbouring countries
  • Support from the Africa CDC, which publicly hailed Kenya's response

Minister Duale cautioned that prevention measures will remain in force until December 23, including surveillance at points of entry, until the official Ebola-free declaration.

Why it matters for Africa

Every win over Ebola matters far beyond one country. The virus has repeatedly crossed borders in past outbreaks, and Kenya - a regional travel and trade hub - moving quickly from outbreak to recovery shows the continent's response systems are getting faster and stronger. The Africa CDC praised the coordination that produced the outcome.

For travellers, businesses and families across East Africa, the message is reassurance: the system worked, and the finish line is in sight.

title: 'I no be Vincent': Zlatan Ibile dodges VeryDarkMan's 24-hour ultimatum amid raging feud - Check Below For Full Details
description: Zlatan Ibile has ignored VeryDarkMan's 24-hour ultimatum to publicly deny claims that his parents and three celebrities begged the activist privately. Instead, the Zanku crooner responded with cryptic posts and his viral line from Peruzzi's song INFERNO - and the online drama is far from over.
content:
The ongoing online war between rapper Zlatan Ibile and social media activist VeryDarkMan (VDM) has entered a new phase, after the "Zanku" crooner chose trolling over a direct response to the activist's 24-hour ultimatum.

Rather than issuing the public denial VDM demanded, Zlatan has kept his fans guessing with cryptic posts and laughing emojis, while continuing to push the song verse at the centre of the controversy.

The song line that lit the fire

Weeks ago, singer Peruzzi released his track INFERNO, featuring Zlatan and Shoday. Zlatan's verse contained a line that immediately caught attention: "I no be Vincent, I no fit masturbate."

The line is widely read as a reference to VDM, whose real name is Martins Vincent Otse - and who has spoken openly in the past about masturbation as part of his public commentary. Zlatan has never confirmed that the lyric was aimed at the activist, but few listeners needed the explanation.

VDM's ultimatum: 'Drop the names of the celebrities'

The drama escalated when VDM, in a video posted online, accused Zlatan of acting tough in public while sending intermediaries to beg him behind closed doors.

According to VDM, the rapper sent three celebrities to plead with him, and even claimed that Zlatan's parents joined a phone call with one of them to beg on their son's behalf.

"As a matter of fact, his parents were on a call with one of them to beg me that their son no fit chop, that their son is not feeling well, that this whole thing is messing him up," VDM said.

He then handed Zlatan a 24-hour ultimatum to publicly deny the claim - threatening to reveal the names of the celebrities involved and release phone recordings if the rapper stayed silent.

"Let him say it's a lie, make I drop the names of the celebrities," he added.

Zlatan's answer: cryptic posts and laughing emojis

When the deadline passed, Zlatan did not confirm or deny anything. Instead, per reports circulating on social media, he posted a cryptic "Zanku OT tested" message on X, dropped laughing emojis in comment sections, and kept promoting videos featuring his "I no be Vincent" verse.

It is not the first time the rapper has responded to the feud with riddles. In an earlier post on X, he wrote: "You can't complain about someone giving you a taste of your own medicine when you have run out of good medicine."

Why the two men are enemies

The bad blood between Zlatan and VDM traces back to the death of singer Mohbad in September 2023, a case that shook the Nigerian music industry. VDM repeatedly pressed Zlatan to speak publicly on what he knew about the circumstances surrounding the death, shared alleged audio recordings and issued public ultimatums. Zlatan largely stayed silent - and the silence became the foundation of the grudge VDM still carries today.

"That same Mohbad case make me no like Zlatan," the activist has said, while still acknowledging: "Zlatan is a great artist, I love his songs."

Davido, Burna Boy and the wider fallout

The feud pulled in bigger names. Davido was captured singing along enthusiastically to Zlatan's INFERNO verse during the welcome party for Zlatan's wedding in Marrakesh, Morocco - a moment that visibly angered VDM.

VDM responded by mocking Davido with a throwback clip, declaring he would rather "masturbate than kneel down and beg a woman". Burna Boy, watching the storm build, stepped in with a plea for calm, commenting: "Let it go, free am abeg."

VDM has also teased a diss track of his own, titled On My Knees - so if Zlatan thought silence would end this, the activist has made it clear the story is not finished.

Editor's note: The claims made by VeryDarkMan in this story are his own allegations and have not been independently verified by Mindnewsng. Zlatan Ibile has not confirmed that the INFERNO lyric was directed at VDM, and neither he nor Davido has publicly responded to the latest claims. This report will be updated as the situation develops.

title: British Army Lists Age Limits, Fitness Tests and Starting Salary for Infantry Soldier Role - Check Below For Full Details
description: The British Army has published the full entry requirements for its Infantry Soldier role: age 16-36, no formal qualifications needed, a three-part fitness test and a starting salary of 27,282 pounds. Here is everything Nigerians and other Commonwealth applicants should know.
content:
The British Army has published the complete entry requirements for its Infantry Soldier role, spelling out exactly what age, fitness level and educational background candidates need - information drawing fresh attention from Nigerians and other Commonwealth citizens considering a military career in the UK.

The requirements, broken down

  • Age: You can join between 16 and 36. At the time of your application you must be between 15 years 7 months and 35 years 6 months old. Junior Soldiers can start training at the Army Foundation College from age 16.
  • Education: No formal qualifications are required - the role is open regardless of academic background.
  • Starting salary: £27,282 per year from day one - roughly ₦55-60 million a year at current exchange rates (rates move daily).

The fitness test - three events, same standard for men and women

  • Mid-thigh pull: 76kg (Army Reserve: 50kg)
  • Seated medicine ball throw: 3.1 metres (Reserve: 2.7m)
  • 2km run: under 10 minutes 15 seconds, after an 800m warm-up

The standards are set by role, not by age or gender - the infantry sits in the highest bracket alongside the Guards, Paratroopers and Royal Armoured Corps. Candidates sit all three events at a 2-day residential assessment centre, which also includes cognitive tests, medical examinations and team exercises.

The Nigerian angle - and the timeline

The Army accepts applicants who are British, Irish or Commonwealth citizens - which includes Nigeria. But the recruitment process is thorough: expect 3 to 6 months from application to the start of training, including medical record checks (1-3 months), the 2-day assessment centre and background/security clearance.

Important context from their own recruits: you must already be in the UK legally to enlist - the Army does not recruit from overseas, so this path is for Nigerians already in Britain (or those with existing UK status), not a visa route by itself.

This article is for general information only and is not immigration or recruitment advice. Requirements are revised periodically - the official Army jobs site is the standard of record.

title: Nigerian-Born UK Opposition Leader Kemi Badenoch Warns Britain Risks Becoming 'A Welfare State With a Country Attached'
description: Kemi Badenoch, the Nigerian-born leader of Britain's Conservative Party, has renewed her stark warning that the UK risks becoming 'a welfare state with a country attached' - as she attacks Labour's Budget and proposes radical welfare reforms including barring GPs from signing young people onto sick notes.
content:
Kemi Badenoch - the Nigerian-born leader of Britain's Conservative Party - has issued the warning that is now dominating UK political conversation: “Britain is at risk of turning into a welfare state with a country attached.”

What she said and why it is trending now

Badenoch has used the phrase repeatedly, and it is resurfacing with full force around Labour's new Budget, which she dismissed as “not good enough, not strong enough, not bold enough - the UK is dropping.” Her argument: Britain is spending ever more on welfare and benefits while growth, work and productivity lag - a combination she says cannot continue.

  • She followed up with a concrete proposal: GPs should be barred from signing young people onto sick notes, part of a push to curb a rising youth jobs crisis and get Britain back to work.
  • Her line echoes a famous warning about the NHS - “an NHS with a country attached” - once made by a senior Labour health secretary himself.
  • She has also challenged the government directly on defence spending and energy bills, and congratulated the new prime minister with a pointed sign-off: “Britain cannot go on like this without becoming a welfare state with a country attached.”
  • Reports suggest her party is polling strongly in the wake of the Budget fight - one tabloid claimed an eight-point lead over rival Nigel Farage.

The Nigerian angle

Badenoch was born in Wimbledon, London, in 1980 and raised in Lagos - spending much of her childhood in Nigeria before returning to the UK as a teenager. She is the first Black person to lead a major UK political party, and the daughter of a GP father and professor mother. Nigerians online are watching with pride and amusement in equal measure: a Nigerian-raised politician now telling the British establishment that too much dependency is a trap - an argument her Nigerian audience knows all too well, coming from a country where the “japa” wave, remittances and subsidy debates dominate the same conversation.

The debate it has ignited

Supporters say she is saying out loud what is mathematically obvious: welfare spending plus weak growth equals a fiscal trap. Critics call it harsh rhetoric that punishes the sick and ignores poverty. Either way, the phrase has struck a nerve on both sides of the Atlantic - and it comes from a leader with Lagos roots.

This article is for general information only and is not political advice. Quotes are as reported by the publications cited; polling figures move frequently.

title: Elon Musk Is Heading for $1 Trillion - Here's What That Much Money Can Actually Buy
description: Elon Musk is already worth about $845-850 billion - and Tesla shareholders have approved a pay package that could push him past $1 trillion, the biggest in corporate history. Here is what a trillion dollars actually buys, put in terms every Nigerian will understand.
content:
Elon Musk is on track to become the world's first trillionaire - and it is no longer a distant fantasy. As of November 8, 2026, trackers value his fortune at about $845 billion (Bloomberg) to $850 billion (Forbes), and Tesla shareholders have already approved the biggest pay package in corporate history for him: a performance-based deal worth up to $1 trillion over a decade (about $878 billion after required payments, per Reuters).

How big is $1 trillion, really?

A trillion is a million million - 1,000,000,000,000. Stacked in $100 bills it would tower over 6,700 kilometres into space. But the more useful comparisons for Nigerians:

  • More than 25 of Nigeria's entire federal budgets. Nigeria's annual budget is roughly ₦54 trillion - about $36 billion. Musk's package is worth over 25 of those.
  • Bigger than most national economies. $1 trillion exceeds the annual GDP of countries like Switzerland and is in the same league as the Netherlands and Saudi Arabia - a single man's paper wealth rivalling mid-sized rich nations.
  • Worth more than 30 Aliko Dangotes. Africa's richest man is worth around $25 billion - Musk's fortune is about 30 times that.
  • Roughly 13 years of Nigeria's oil earnings. At recent output and prices, that is what $1 trillion looks like against the country's main export earner.
  • About 5,000 Dangote refineries. The $20 billion Lekki refinery - Africa's largest single industrial project - could be built 50 times over for the cost of one Musk pay award. Five thousand would still not spend it all.

He has not collected it yet

The trillionaire tag comes with strings: the Tesla award pays out only if Musk hits extraordinary performance milestones - including market value targets that would make Tesla by far the most valuable company on Earth. Forbes and Bloomberg trackers currently put his paper wealth just under $900 billion, so history's first trillionaire remains an if, not a when. It is also mostly stock, not cash - which is exactly why regulators and critics from Pope Leo to Norway's sovereign wealth fund attacked the deal as excessive.

The Naija takeaway

One man controlling wealth larger than dozens of national budgets is why the pay deal made global headlines - and why debates about executive pay, tax and inequality are not going away. For readers: be wary of any investment pitch or “Musk giveaway” message on WhatsApp or Facebook promising free money, crypto or Tesla shares - Musk gives away nothing through random DMs, and those are always scams.

This article is for general information only and is not financial advice. Net worth figures move daily with share prices; the package value depends on Tesla meeting multi-year performance targets.

Sources: BBC; Reuters (November 6, 2025 shareholder vote); Fortune; Euronews; Bloomberg Billionaires Index and Forbes real-time trackers (November 8, 2026); World Population Review.
